# Bitcoin CMA — Literature Review v2 (10–15 year horizon)

**Master working document.** Rich, retained detail lives here; `dashboard.html` is the distilled interactive view. Regenerate both with `python3 build_v2.py`.

- **Coverage:** 72 distinct approaches (20 from v1 + 52 added by a 12-lens divergent-breadth sweep), each scored on rigor / signal / robustness / data-ops and ranked into a tiered leaderboard, with a driver-cluster signal map exposing redundancy.

- **Outputs per approach:** appreciation (nominal + real), volatility, and correlation vs growth equities, value equities, nominal fixed income, TIPS, and GOLD — cited vs synthesized, anchored to the scripted baseline.

- **Gold twin:** `../../gold/cma_litreview/NOTES.md`.


---

## Empirical baseline (scripted — `empirical_anchor.py`)

- Full (2010-07…2026-05): BTC **+142%/yr nom**, **+137%/yr real**, vol **103%**
- Trailing 10y: BTC **+65%/yr nom**, **+60%/yr real**, vol **69%**
- Trailing 5y: BTC **+17%/yr nom**, **+11%/yr real**, vol **57%**


> The appreciation DECAY (142→65→17%/yr) dominates every forward CMA; a method's value is mostly the conditioning it adds (tails, regime, correlation), not its level forecast. BTC–gold correlation is ~0.

## Signal map — driver clusters (exposes redundancy)

Approaches grouped by the underlying variable they ultimately rest on. Many 'distinct' approaches reduce to the same driver — the marginal information is in spanning clusters, not counting approaches.


**Scarcity / supply-schedule extrapolation** — _Deterministic halving/21M cap or price-vs-time co-trend treated as the value driver — spurious non-stationary fits._
  - Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law
  - Cost-of-Production / Mining-Cost Floor
  - Power-Law Time Regression (Santostasi / Burger Corridor)
  - Energy-Value / Thermoeconomic Fair-Value (Joule Equivalence + Landauer Temperature)
  - Discrete Cycle-Amplitude Decay Extrapolation (4-Year Halving Peak-Multiple Compression)
  - Logarithmic-Regression "Rainbow" Fair-Value Corridor

**Adoption / network-value (Metcalfe & saturation)** — _Value rises with user/network growth on an S-curve; produces the decay shape but value-link is reverse-causal and exponent ad hoc._
  - Metcalfe's Law Network-Value (NVM)
  - Network Value-to-Transactions (NVT) Ratio
  - Adoption S-Curve / Logistic Demand Growth
  - Generalized-Metcalfe x Logistic-Saturation Fundamental Support (Wheatley-Sornette)
  - Demographic & Wealth-Transfer Flow-of-Funds Demand (Great Wealth Transfer, Life-Cycle Cohort, Savings-Rate)
  - Discrete-Access Step-Function Demand (ETF -> Wirehouse Models -> 401k/ERISA -> RIA TAMP)

**Monetary / global-liquidity & debasement macro** — _BTC as a claim on monetary base / global liquidity / fiscal debasement — one shared liquidity-beta factor._
  - Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge
  - Quantity Theory of Money / Velocity Equation of Exchange (MV=PT)
  - Global-Liquidity / Collateral-Multiplier Cycle Barometer (Howell / Alden Directional Liquidity-Beta)
  - Fiscal-Theory-of-the-Price-Level / Fiscal-Dominance Hard-Asset Bid
  - Cagan/Jermann Dynamic Money-Demand (Real-Balances, Adoption-Shock Structural)
  - Eurodollar / Shadow-Money BTC-as-Collateral (Snider)
  - Debasement-CAGR / Fiat-Half-Life Return Floor
  - Dynamic-Factor / Mixed-Frequency Macro Nowcasting (DFM + MIDAS, ML-augmented)
  - Equation-of-Exchange Velocity Network-Utility Valuation (Burniske MV=PQ)
  - Stablecoin-Float Liquidity-Onramp Demand Sink

**Store-of-value / monetary-TAM terminal-share** — _Back-out a return from an asserted terminal capture share of gold/reserve/money pools._
  - Store-of-Value / Gold-Parity TAM Substitution
  - Discounted-Utility / Monetary-Premium DCF (Moneyness Analogue)
  - Institutional Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions (LTCMA) for Bitcoin
  - Triffin / Dedollarization Neutral-Reserve Sovereign Share
  - Hyperbitcoinization Terminal Monetary-Base Share (Probability-Weighted Barbell)
  - Cross-Asset Relative-Value Ratio (BTC/Gold, Market-Portfolio Share, Hard-Money Basket, Multi-Pool Monetary TAM)
  - Structural Stock-Flow Demand-Clearing Engine (Inelastic-Supply Price-Multiplier)

**Equilibrium / structural no-cashflow theory** — _First-principles SDF / no-arbitrage / game-theoretic value — rigorous, regime-proof, but declines to forecast a level._
  - Equilibrium / Game-Theoretic Security-Utility Pricing
  - Consumption-CAPM / Rare-Disaster / ICAPM Hedging-Demand Equilibrium Premium
  - Rational-Bubble / OLG No-Arbitrage Equilibrium (Tirole/Blanchard-Watson; van Oordt; Biais; Schilling-Uhlig Martingale)

**Return-process, vol & tail risk engines** — _Model the return distribution's higher moments (jumps, fat tails, rough vol, EVT) — the risk-shape block, not drift._
  - Regime-Switching / Jump-Diffusion & Heavy-Tail Return Process
  - Fractal Long-Memory & Adaptive-Efficiency (MF-DFA / Hurst / ARFIMA)
  - Rough Volatility (Fractional-Brownian RFSV) for Bitcoin
  - ML Realized-Volatility & Vol-Term-Structure Forecasting (HAR-RV / GARCH / Hybrid)
  - Tail-Risk Implied Required Return (CVaR / Expected-Shortfall Pricing)
  - Extreme-Value-Theory Tail-Distribution (GPD / Peaks-Over-Threshold / Block-Maxima)

**Dependence / factor / macro-nowcast regressions** — _Cross-sectional or time-varying co-movement structure — conditions the correlation row._
  - Cross-Sectional Factor & Macro-Liquidity Regression
  - Cross-Asset Dependence-Structure Engine (DCC-GARCH + Copula tail-dependence)
  - Geopolitical-Risk-Index Conditional Safe-Haven Factor (GPR/EPU)

**Options/derivatives risk-neutral & carry microstructure** — _Read forward/vol/skew/carry off derivatives screens — short-tenor risk conditioning, no decade drift._
  - Options-Implied Risk-Neutral Forward & Vol Surface (Deribit DVOL / RND)
  - Market-Implied Futures Forward Curve & Basis
  - Variance/Jump Risk-Premium & SDF-Implied Physical Return (P-vs-Q, VRP, SVCJ)
  - Options-Skew / Convexity Risk-Reversal Signal
  - Derivatives-Microstructure: Perp Funding, Cross-Rail Basis Segmentation & Price Discovery (Crypto Carry)
  - Convenience-Yield / Theory-of-Storage Commodity Valuation

**On-chain cost-basis & supply microstructure oscillators** — _Reflexive transforms of past price / UTXO ledger — positioning timers with a realized-price floor._
  - On-Chain Cost-Basis Valuation (Realized Cap / MVRV / SOPR / Thermocap / HODL Waves)
  - Mining-Economics Dynamics & Security-Budget Sustainability (Hashprice, Hash/Difficulty Ribbons, Puell, Cost-Curve, Supply-Elasticity)
  - On-Chain Supply-Distribution & Flow Microstructure (URPD, Liveliness/Dormancy, Reserve Risk, Illiquid/Exchange-Flow, Entity-Cohort, LTH/STH)

**Bubble / narrative / attention reflexivity** — _Reflexive feedback (LPPLS hazard, SIR contagion, attention) — crash-hazard and boom-bust cadence conditioning._
  - Reflexive / Log-Periodic Bubble & Crash-Hazard (LPPLS / JLS)
  - Agent-Based / Sociophysics Generative Market (Chartist-Fundamentalist, Percolation, Ising/SOC)
  - Information-Entropy / Complexity-Plane Efficiency Valuation
  - Behavioral Attention & Text-Sentiment (Search/Wiki/Social NLP, Fear-Greed)
  - Narrative-Economics / Reflexivity Feedback-Loop (SIR Contagion + Garcia VAR)
  - Behavioral-Preference / Disagreement Overvaluation (Lottery-MAX, Miller, Scheinkman-Xiong)

**Demand-channel flow plumbing (ETF/treasury/access)** — _Map institutional inflow Q to price via impact/elasticity/access steps — bet on an unobservable inflow path._
  - Treasury-Company Reflexive Demand Channel (mNAV Flywheel + Convertible Vol-Arb Loop)
  - Square-Root Market-Impact Law (Metaorder Demand-to-Price Mechanism)
  - ETF-AUM Cointegration Elasticity & Inelastic-Markets Flow Multiplier

**Survival / absorbing-zero hazard** — _Price the -100% point-mass / Lindy survival explicitly — regime-agnostic tail wrapper._
  - Survival / Ruin-Probability (Absorbing-Zero Hazard)
  - Lindy / Age-Conditioned Survival Adoption Premium

**Allocation-implied & view-blending CMA construction** — _Invert holdings for an implied return or reconcile imposed views — consume a CMA rather than forecast one._
  - Portfolio Sizing / Risk-Budget Allocation
  - Bayesian Model-Averaging / Dynamic Model Averaging under Model & Parameter Instability
  - Implied-Equilibrium-Return Inversion (Black-Litterman / Risk-Parity / Kelly Back-Out)
  - Liability-Driven / Surplus-Optimization Implied BTC Hurdle (Endowment/LDI)
  - Entropy-Pooling / Fully-Flexible-Probabilities Stress-View CMA Construction (Meucci)

**Cross-asset / intra-crypto & geopolitical conditioning** — _Relative-value or exogenous-shock overlays (equity-beta, dominance, capital-flight, policy caps)._
  - Official-Sector Policy-Endogenous Return Caps (Repression Tax/Ban, Regulatory Capital, ECB Zero-Value)
  - Capital-Flight / Sanctions-Evasion / Remittance Transactional-Demand Floor
  - Equity-Beta-Implied / Public-Proxy-Implied Expected Return (Levered Nasdaq, MSTR mNAV, Miner NAV)
  - Intra-Crypto Relative-Value (BTC Dominance / ETH-BTC Rotation Overlay)
  - Liquidity-Risk & Higher-Moment Priced Factors (Amihud Illiquidity, Co-Skewness / Downside-Tail Beta)

**ML forecasting** — _Data-driven prediction that decays to random-walk-with-drift at decade horizon._
  - Machine-Learning Forecasting & Empirical Asset Pricing (DL/Trees/On-Chain ML/Gu-Kelly-Xiu/HMM)

### Recommended orthogonal ensemble

Build the house BTC CMA as a layered ensemble, not a single engine, because no method honestly produces the decade level. (1) LEVEL/SHAPE anchor: take the central 8-12% nominal from the cross-method decay consensus, mechanically shaped by the power-law/age decay (id 4) and cross-checked by cycle-amplitude decay (id 68) and the debasement-CAGR floor (id 31) as a bound — trim id 4's high central level down to the honest band. (2) MACRO/REGIME conditioning of the drift sign: global-liquidity direction (id 25) as the one robust replicated BTC-macro overlay, with FTPL (id 26) as a fiscal-dominance scenario lever. (3) VOLATILITY cell: HAR-RV/GARCH (id 42) for the ~57% floor, cross-checked by rough-vol (id 21). (4) CORRELATION row: DCC+copula (id 48) for the time-varying +0.56 equity / ~0 gold structure, cross-checked by the GPR safe-haven test (id 55) and factor regression (id 9). (5) TAILS: EVT (id 47) for VaR/ES plus the regime-switching/jump process (id 18) for the body fat-tails, the survival/absorbing-zero hazard (id 19) to make the -100% point-mass explicit, and LPPLS (id 17) for within-cycle crash-hazard. (6) RECONCILIATION: feed all of these as coherent views into Entropy-Pooling (id 71) under the rational-bubble identity E[r]=discount+crash-hazard (id 51) so the final return/vol/correlation/tail panel is internally consistent and non-normal. Use the LTCMA tuple (id 15) and barbell (id 30) only as external sanity brackets, never as the engine. The mutually-orthogonal core to actually combine: 4, 25, 42, 48, 47, 18, 19, 71.


### Signal notes

Signal map for a 10-15yr BTC CMA. Realized facts the ensemble must reproduce: appreciation decays 142->65->17%/yr (full/10y/5y), so the DECAY ANCHOR dominates and any method implying a flat/rising high return (S2F id 0 at ~78%/yr) is disqualified as an engine. Vol floor ~57%; equity correlation RISES to +0.56 in the ETF era; BTC-gold correlation ~0. Honest central output: ~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15. KEY STRUCTURAL TRUTH: because the level is a near-consensus decay anchor, a method's marginal value is the CONDITIONING it adds — tails, regime, correlation — NOT its level forecast. That is why the top of the ranking is dominated by risk-shape and dependence engines (18, 47, 48) and regime overlays (25, 51), while the most-cited 'valuation' families (S2F 0, rainbow 69, Metcalfe 1, NVT 2, cost-floor 3) sit at the bottom: they are spurious non-stationary co-trends (price-on-time or price-on-price) that broke post-2021 and add no tail/correlation/regime information. Three failure modes recur and should be treated as automatic downgrades: (a) spurious I(1) regression / cointegration that fails (0,1,2,6,24,67,69); (b) circularity where the 'driver' is endogenous to price (cost/energy 3,35; on-chain 8,65; flow-elasticity 67; demographics 56); (c) horizon mismatch — clean short-tenor risk machinery (options 10,37,38; ML 41; carry 39) extrapolated to a decade. Orthogonality is the scarce resource: the genuinely independent information blocks are the liquidity-direction macro factor (25), the higher-moment/tail engine (18/47), the dependence structure (48), the absorbing-zero hazard (19), the policy/flight conditioning (53/54), and the reconciliation layer (71/51). Everything in the scarcity, adoption, and monetary-TAM clusters is largely redundant with the shared decay anchor plus one liquidity beta, so include at most one representative from each as a cross-check. Net: combine ~8 orthogonal lenses, let the decay anchor set the level, and spend the modeling effort on the risk shape and correlation row where the methods actually differ and where the ETF-era regime shift is doing the real damage.

## Comparison table — approaches (with medium Explanation)


| Rank | Approach | Source | Explanation (medium) | Pros | Cons | Key drivers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regime-Switching / Jump-Diffusion & Heavy-Tail Return Process | Academia | This is not a price model but a model of Bitcoin's return-generating process. Rather than one decaying drift and a single ~57% volatility number, it specifies the full conditional distribution using four econometric tools: Markov-switching GARCH (returns flip between a calm low-vol and a turbulent high-vol regime), affine jump-diffusion / SVCJ (stochastic volatility with downward price jumps that arrive together with vol spikes), self-exciting Hawkes processes (a jump today raises the odds of the next, producing crash clustering), and heavy-tail laws (a power-law tail index ~2.1-2.5, heavier than equities' ~3). Its CMA contribution is the risk SHAPE, not the appreciation level: vol-of-vol, kurtosis, expected shortfall, expected maximum drawdown, and regime-conditional correlation. It must borrow its drift (~10-15% nominal) from adoption/TAM rows. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it implies vol is a mixture (~40-50% calm, ~80-110% turbulent), a realistic -55% to -75% peak-to-trough drawdown, and — most usefully — that diversification vanishes precisely in crisis regimes when BTC co-jumps with equities. The lesson: do not size Bitcoin off a single sigma. | • Targets the right object for a CMA's RISK side: it produces vol-of-vol, kurtosis, tail index, expected shortfall and expected-max-drawdown — exactly the inputs CVaR-based sizing and option pricing need, which a single sigma cannot supply<br>• Empirically dominant in-sample and out-of-sample: MS-GARCH and SVCJ specifications beat single-regime / pure-diffusion models on VaR backtests and option-pricing RMSE across multiple peer-reviewed studies — this is not a fringe view, it is the consensus econometric description<br>• Captures documented BTC stylized facts other approaches deny: fat tails (tail index ~2.1-2.5), volatility clustering, vol-of-vol, leverage/asymmetry, and synchronized price-and-vol crashes (correlated co-jumps)<br>• Honest about drawdown shape: the realized -77% to -93% cyclical drawdowns are tail events that a lognormal 57%-vol model assigns near-zero probability; this family reproduces them, making it the right lens for 'how bad is the bad case over 10-15yr'<br>• Regime framing reconciles the empirical-anchor instability (142%->65%->17% appreciation, 103%->57% vol across windows): those are not parameter drift to be averaged away, they are regime realizations, which argues directly for a path/scenario CMA over a point CMA<br>• Internally consistent with the options-implied row: the same SVCJ/jump structure that fits returns also fits the Deribit vol surface and DVOL, so the physical-measure CMA and the risk-neutral measure can be tied together | • Says almost nothing about the DRIFT: these are conditional-second-moment-and-tail models; the regime means are estimated noisily off a short, bull-dominated sample and have essentially no forward predictive content for 10-15yr appreciation. This family must borrow its appreciation number from elsewhere (decay/adoption/TAM rows)<br>• Severe parameter instability on BTC's short history: ~13-16 years, one micro-cap era, ~4 cycles. Jump intensity, regime means and transition probabilities are estimated on a handful of regime realizations, so standard errors are large and estimates are highly sample/window-dependent — false precision risk is real<br>• Horizon mismatch: most of these are fit on daily or high-frequency (5-min) data for VaR/option pricing at days-to-months horizons. Extrapolating a daily MS-GARCH/SVCJ to a 10-15yr unconditional distribution requires strong stationarity assumptions the data violates (the process is itself non-stationary and maturing)<br>• Identification fragility: separating a 'jump' from a high-vol diffusion draw, or a regime switch from a vol cluster, is statistically delicate; different filters (MCMC vs sequential learning vs threshold) give materially different jump counts and tail indices<br>• Weak BTC regime persistence specifically: studies note BTC's regimes are less persistent than equities', so the clean 'calm vs crisis' story is muddier — switching is frequent and noisy, weakening the regime-conditional CMA<br>• Maturation breaks the fit forward: ETF/institutional access is plausibly compressing the tail and dampening the leverage-feedback crashes that produced past -80% drawdowns (K33's argument), so a model calibrated on 2011-2022 extremes likely OVERstates forward tail risk — yet there is too little post-institutional data to recalibrate<br>• Not a standalone CMA: on its own it yields no appreciation and no cross-asset correlation forecast (most papers are univariate on BTC) — it is a risk-shape overlay, not a full row | • Regime state variable: an unobserved Markov chain (usually 2, sometimes 3 states) that switches the entire return distribution between calm/bull and turbulent/bear regimes, with its own mean, variance and transition probabilities (which the data also says are only weakly persistent for BTC vs equities)<br>• Stochastic volatility: vol modeled as a mean-reverting latent process (kappa, theta, vol-of-vol sigma_v) rather than a constant, so the CMA sigma is a distribution, not a scalar<br>• Jumps in returns AND in variance, with the two jumps correlated (SVCJ rho_J<0): a price crash and a vol spike arrive together, fattening the left tail beyond what diffusion plus return-jumps alone produce<br>• Self-excitation (Hawkes): jump intensity is path-dependent — a jump today raises the conditional intensity of the next jump, generating empirically-observed crash/squeeze clustering and volatility persistence<br>• Heavy-tail innovation law: power-law / alpha-stable / skewed-t tail with an estimated tail index alpha (BTC ~2.1-2.5, vs ~3 for equities) and large excess kurtosis, fit directly to extremes via EVT/peaks-over-threshold<br>• Leverage / asymmetry: negative shocks raise future vol more than positive shocks of equal size (EGARCH/GJR asymmetry, and the negative return-vol jump correlation) |
| 2 | Extreme-Value-Theory Tail-Distribution (GPD / Peaks-Over-Threshold / Block-Maxima) | Academia | EVT discards the body of BTC's return distribution and fits only the tail beyond a high threshold, where asymptotic theory says exceedances must follow a Generalized Pareto Distribution regardless of the parent. The single estimated parameter that matters is the tail-index xi: positive xi (BTC ~0.08 on gains, ~0.18-0.21 on losses) means a heavy Frechet tail — extreme moves are far more likely than a normal or even Student-t body implies. Because BTC returns cluster in volatility, the credible implementation is McNeil-Frey GARCH-EVT: GARCH-filter to near-i.i.d. residuals, then POT-fit the tail, then re-inflate by current conditional vol. Outputs are Basel-grade VaR, Expected Shortfall, and multi-horizon return levels (the worst loss expected once per n periods), including the actuary's 99.5% / 1-in-200 standard. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA, EVT does NOT give appreciation — it is the rigorous source for the tail/drawdown/ES and the high-quantile vol-of-the-tail inputs, replacing a naive Gaussian sigma with a data-driven extreme-loss distribution that survives stress design. | • Theoretically rigorous and asset-agnostic: the GPD/GEV limit holds for ANY heavy-tailed parent, so it does not assume normality and does not curve-fit the whole distribution — it is the actuarial/Basel standard for exactly the fat-tailed regime BTC inhabits<br>• Directly produces the CMA cells everything else punts on: VaR, Expected Shortfall, multi-horizon return levels and the 1-in-200 capital number — the drawdown/tail/stress inputs, grounded in BTC's actual extremes rather than a Gaussian sigma that understates crash risk by orders of magnitude<br>• Empirically validated for BTC: GPD passes Anderson-Darling/Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness-of-fit on BTC excess returns (IntechOpen 2024), and the dynamic-POT / GARCH-EVT variants pass formal VaR backtests and Model-Confidence-Set tests, beating GARCH with Student-t/skew-t/GED innovations out-of-sample (Ke-Yang-Tan 2022)<br>• Quantifies a real, distinctive BTC fact — its tail is heavier than FX and most equities (Gkillas-Katsiampa 2018) — that variance-based risk models systematically miss; the McNeil-Frey GARCH-EVT filter also captures volatility clustering, the dominant feature of crypto returns<br>• Falsifiable and parameter-light (one shape, one scale per tail); the tail-index is a stable structural descriptor far less prone to the spurious-regression failures of S2F/Metcalfe | • Says NOTHING about expected appreciation — it is purely a loss/tail-distribution estimator, so it cannot populate the central return cell of a CMA at all; any appreciation figure must be imported from another family<br>• Univariate by default — standard EVT/POT is silent on cross-asset CORRELATION (BTC vs equities/gold/TIPS/FI); recovering tail-dependence requires the heavier EVT-copula machinery, which is a separate, much harder estimation with its own fragility<br>• Threshold choice is subjective and the estimates are sensitive to it: too-low u biases xi, too-high u inflates its variance on a thin tail; xi confidence intervals on a ~15yr daily sample are wide, and the loss vs gain tail give materially different xi (0.18 vs 0.08), so the 'tail index' is not a single robust number<br>• Small extreme-sample / regime-instability: only a few hundred exceedances exist, the parent regime has shifted (pre-ETF vs post-ETF, declining realized vol), and a static xi assumes the tail process is stationary over a 10-15yr horizon it almost certainly is not; dynamic-POT helps short-horizon but does not solve long-horizon non-stationarity<br>• Square-root-of-time scaling of a daily tail to a multi-year horizon is invalid for heavy tails (it understates xi-driven aggregation), so the 10-15yr return-level / drawdown extrapolation is a heroic stretch the daily fit does not license<br>• Backward-looking: the worst realized extreme caps the empirical tail, so EVT can still under-price a never-before-seen catastrophic (exchange-collapse / protocol-failure / regulatory-ban) event — the left-tail mass a single-history fit cannot see | • Tail-index / shape parameter xi (BTC ~0.08 gains, ~0.18-0.21 losses; xi>0 = heavy Frechet tail, infinite higher moments once xi exceeds 1/k)<br>• Threshold choice u (POT) or block size (Block-Maxima) — the central bias/variance tradeoff; too low contaminates the tail with the body, too high starves the fit (mean-excess plot / Hill plot calibration)<br>• GARCH pre-filter (McNeil-Frey) to convert volatility-clustered returns into near-i.i.d. residuals so the EVT i.i.d. assumption holds; conditional vol then re-scales the static tail into a dynamic VaR/ES<br>• Confidence level / return period: 95%, 99%, Basel 97.5% ES, and the actuarial 99.5% (1-in-200) — the quantile at which the tail is read<br>• Scale parameter beta and exceedance count (sample of extremes only; BTC ~580-610 exceedances over a decade of daily data)<br>• Sample window and asymmetry (separate fits for the loss tail vs gain tail; BTC's gain tail can exceed the loss tail — upside-heavy) |
| 3 | Cross-Asset Dependence-Structure Engine (DCC-GARCH + Copula tail-dependence) | Academia | This is the CMA's missing correlation engine. Rather than a single scalar realized correlation, it models the full time-varying covariance and, crucially, the tails. The pipeline is GARCH (filter each asset's volatility clustering) -> DCC/ADCC (time-varying conditional correlations) -> EVT marginals (Generalized Pareto tails) -> copula (Gumbel/Clayton/Student-t/vine) to extract asymmetric upper- vs lower-tail dependence. Key inputs: the GARCH/EGARCH specification, the DCC decay parameters, the EVT threshold, and the copula family chosen by AIC/likelihood. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it does not produce appreciation or volatility-as-a-trend; it produces the dependence cells. The literature's consistent finding: BTC-gold dependence is near zero and regime-flipping (Gumbel parameter ~1.0 => independence), while BTC-equity correlation is positive and has risen, with some lower-tail (co-crash) dependence that is real but frequently not statistically significant. It refutes BTC as a reliable safe haven while confirming it is not a gold proxy either. | • Directly populates the correlation and co-tail half of the CMA — the only family in the review built to do this — instead of leaving those cells to a single scalar realized anchor<br>• Captures ASYMMETRIC and NONLINEAR dependence: a Gaussian/scalar correlation misses that BTC may co-crash with equities in the left tail while showing weaker upside co-movement; copulas make lambda_L vs lambda_U explicit<br>• Directly and falsifiably tests the 'digital gold' claim — the literature repeatedly finds BTC-gold tail dependence ≈ 0 (e.g. Gumbel parameter ~1.007 => independence; BTC-gold copula ~0.05, Kendall tau ~0.04), refuting naive safe-haven narratives with a measured statistic<br>• Time-varying (DCC/ADCC) output shows correlations are regime-dependent and rising with institutionalization, which a static CMA number hides — useful for stress/scenario design<br>• Produces portfolio risk outputs (VaR/CVaR) the rest of the CMA stack cannot, making it directly usable for risk-budgeting a BTC sleeve<br>• Econometrically disciplined and peer-reviewed: GARCH-EVT-copula is standard tail-risk machinery, not a crypto-native curve-fit | • It is NOT a return model — it produces no appreciation or expected-return estimate at all, so it can only ever fill the correlation/vol-structure cells of a CMA; the level half must come from another approach<br>• Dependence is badly non-stationary: DCC level and the best-fit copula flip across pre-2020 / COVID / ETF regimes, so an in-sample tail-dependence coefficient is a poor 10-15yr forward guide — the very time-variation it measures undermines extrapolation<br>• Heavy specification risk: results swing with the GARCH variant, EVT threshold, copula family, and estimation method; tail-dependence coefficients are notoriously imprecise on short, structurally-broken crypto samples, and several studies find BTC-equity lower-tail dependence is present in point estimate but NOT statistically significant<br>• Short / regime-broken sample: BTC has only ~3-4 cycles and the institutional era is <6 years, so EVT tail fits lean on very few true extremes — the estimates the CMA would trust most (co-crash tails) are the least reliable<br>• Many headline pairs (BTC-gold) come back as independence (Gumbel ~1.0), which is informative but means the engine often 'confirms zero,' adding little beyond the realized scalar for those cells<br>• Backward-looking by construction: it characterizes realized joint behavior, not forward structural change (ETF flows, macro-regime shifts) that will actually drive 10-15yr correlations | • GARCH/EGARCH/GJR univariate filtering of each asset's volatility clustering and leverage (the conditioning step before any dependence is measured)<br>• DCC/ADCC decay parameters (a,b) governing how fast conditional correlations move and the asymmetry term capturing higher correlation in joint downturns<br>• EVT marginal modeling: Generalized Pareto tail fit above a chosen threshold + kernel/empirical body (the semiparametric distribution feeding the copula)<br>• Copula family selection: Gumbel (upper-tail), Clayton (lower-tail), Student-t (symmetric heavy tails), Frank (no tail), or a vine of pairwise copulas — chosen by AIC/BIC/log-likelihood<br>• Lower- vs upper-tail dependence coefficients lambda_L, lambda_U — the asymmetry that distinguishes a diversifier from a co-crash asset<br>• Sample window / regime: pre-2020 vs COVID vs ETF era radically changes both DCC level and the fitted copula (dependence is non-stationary)<br>• Threshold and estimation choices (EVT threshold, copula estimation by IFM vs full MLE) to which tail-dependence estimates are sensitive |
| 4 | Global-Liquidity / Collateral-Multiplier Cycle Barometer (Howell / Alden Directional Liquidity-Beta) | Practitioner | Bitcoin is framed as the most liquidity-sensitive asset on the planet — a high-beta, demand-pure claim on Global Liquidity. The driver is not money-supply level but gross, collateral-augmented funding: central-bank money + private credit + a repo/shadow-money multiplier (~77-80% of global lending is collateral-backed), aggregating to Howell's ~$189T pool that cycles on a ~65-month debt-refinancing rhythm. The headline evidence is DIRECTIONAL: BTC aligns with global liquidity in 83% of 12-month windows (74% of 6-month), more than equities, gold or bonds, with liquidity leading BTC ~13 weeks. Crucially this beta DECAYS as the horizon shortens (corr 0.94 overall, 0.51 at 12mo, 0.36 at 6mo), where idiosyncratic and valuation forces take over. For a 10-15yr CMA the framework implies appreciation tracks the secular liquidity uptrend (fiscal-dominance money creation) times a liquidity-beta >1 that compresses toward gold's as BTC matures — yielding a decaying return with violent cyclical drawdowns, NOT a perpetual growth rate. Howell decomposes BTC as ~40-45% liquidity, ~25% gold-like, ~25% risk appetite — explicitly NOT pure digital gold. | • The DIRECTIONAL claim is the most robust empirical finding in BTC macro: an 83%/12mo hit rate with global liquidity, higher than equities/gold/bonds, is a real and replicated signal (Callahan/Alden) — and being directional (sign-of-change) it sidesteps the spurious-level-regression trap that sinks naive M2-elasticity and S2F<br>• The collateral-multiplier lens is conceptually richer than money-supply models: it captures repo/shadow-money creation (~77-80% of lending is collateral-backed) and gross funding conditions that M2 misses, which is genuinely where marginal risk-asset liquidity is set<br>• Honest about HORIZON: the framework explicitly documents its own decay (0.94 → 0.51 → 0.36 as windows shorten), so it does not over-claim short-term precision — and the ~65-month cycle gives a falsifiable PHASE call rather than a perpetual-uptrend assertion<br>• Driver decomposition (~40-45% liquidity / ~25% gold / ~25% risk) is unusually candid for a practitioner thesis — it explicitly REFUSES the pure-digital-gold framing and quantifies BTC as a blend, which matches realized behavior (high equity beta, ~0 gold correlation)<br>• Generates a realistic drawdown/amplitude profile (e.g. the -47% 2025-26 liquidity-downswing call) rather than a smooth compounding path — useful for the tail/loss-given-bear half of a CMA that level models ignore<br>• Practitioner adoption is deep and cross-checkable: CrossBorder Capital, Alden, CF Benchmarks and Onramp all publish liquidity-linked BTC work, and the framework has on-record cycle calls (peak Q3 2025) that can be scored ex-post | • DIRECTION ≠ MAGNITUDE: an 83% directional hit rate says nothing about HOW MUCH BTC rises — it cannot, by itself, produce an appreciation number. Any 10-15yr CMA is bolted on by assuming a secular liquidity uptrend AND a liquidity-beta, neither of which the barometer estimates; the headline stat is being repurposed beyond what it supports<br>• The 'global M2 / global liquidity' series is contested as data-tortured: critics (e.g. Sina vs Raoul Pal's model) show the fit relies on arbitrarily lag-shifting M2 forward 10-13 weeks and 'finding great matches between pockets of data' — overfitting with 'no idea about predictive accuracy.' The lead-time is itself a fitted parameter, not structural<br>• REVERSE CAUSALITY is unresolved: in 2025 BTC topped FIRST and liquidity peaked ~145 days later, suggesting BTC may LEAD liquidity (as a risk-appetite barometer) rather than follow it — which inverts the framework's premise that liquidity is the exogenous driver<br>• The collateral multiplier is asserted, not measured: Howell's own interviews give the $189T peak and the ~77-80% collateral-backed-lending stat but do NOT publish an itemized central-bank-vs-private-vs-collateral breakdown or a quantified multiplier coefficient — the mechanism is narrative, the aggregate a black box<br>• Documented post-2021/2025 BREAKDOWN: CF Benchmarks reports the M2-BTC R² collapsing from 0.71-0.90 to ~0.59 with a ~46% (~$66k) fair-value gap as M2 EXPANDED while BTC FELL — exactly the regime where the liquidity bid rotated toward gold (gold liquidity Z-score +2.82 vs BTC -1.31). The barometer can read wrong for quarters at a time<br>• The ~65-month cycle is calibrated on very few realized cycles and is converging with the halving cycle right now (Howell concedes this), making it nearly impossible to attribute BTC moves to liquidity-phase vs halving vs risk appetite — the decomposition (40/25/25) is judgmental, not estimated<br>• Silent on a calibrated covariance matrix: like the other monetary models it gives qualitative correlation views (BTC-gold negative short-run / positive long-run, the 'dog on a leash') but no stable coefficients vs growth eq, value eq, nominal FI, TIPS — all CMA covariance cells must be imported from realized data | • Global Liquidity as GROSS collateral-augmented funding: central-bank money + private-sector credit + a collateral-reuse/repo/shadow-money multiplier (~$188.8T peak; ~77-80% of global lending collateral-backed) — the level AND its rate-of-change<br>• The ~65-month (5-6yr) debt-refinancing liquidity cycle and its PHASE (peaked Q3 2025, downswing through ~2027) — the recurring driver Howell argues should REPLACE the 4-year halving cycle<br>• Directional liquidity-beta: BTC moves with liquidity 83% of 12mo / 74% of 6mo windows; liquidity LEADS BTC ~13 weeks (a tradable lead, not a level anchor)<br>• Horizon-dependent decay of the relationship: tight over 12mo (corr 0.51) and full-sample (0.94), but eroding to 0.36 at 6mo and toward noise intraday/monthly as idiosyncratic + valuation factors dominate<br>• Driver decomposition (Howell): ~40-45% global liquidity, ~25% gold-like behavior, ~25% pure risk appetite (NASDAQ-correlated) — BTC is a BLEND, not a pure liquidity or pure gold play<br>• Fiscal dominance / sovereign debt refinancing (~$70T+ annual rollovers) forcing central banks to monetize deficits — the secular tailwind under the cyclical wobble (the 'monetary inflation' thesis)<br>• Idiosyncratic break conditions: exchange collapses (Mt.Gox, FTX/Terra), and extreme on-chain valuation (high MVRV-Z) where profit-taking/panic overrides the liquidity signal<br>• The 'global M2' / global-liquidity measurement choice itself (8-economy M2 in USD vs collateral-inclusive gross liquidity) and any lag-shift applied — a load-bearing and contested input |
| 5 | Power-Law Time Regression (Santostasi / Burger Corridor) | Crypto-native | The power-law time model regresses log BTC price on log age (days since the 2009 genesis), yielding P proportional to t^n with a canonical exponent n~=5.69 and R^2~=0.961 over 2010-2026. Because annualized appreciation under this form equals n divided by current age, the model FORECASTS its own decay: ~33%/yr at today's ~17-year age, easing to ~18%/yr by 2040, which compounds to roughly a 27% nominal CAGR over a 2026-2041 window read off the central line. Parallel corridor bands (about -50%/+200% around fair value) supply a dispersion view; the model says nothing about volatility-as-a-statistic or cross-asset correlations, which must be imported from realized data (~55-60% vol, gold corr ~0). The recent peer-reviewed treatment is double-edged: the power law fails Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests (lognormal preferred) and its exponent swings ~3x with the time-origin choice, yet it still out-of-sample-beats ARIMA, ETS, and random-walk-with-drift at 12-24 months (p<0.05). For a 10-15yr CMA it is the most bullish entry, and its ~22-27% rests entirely on the historical exponent persisting through the ETF-era regime break. | • Internally encodes appreciation DECAY — unlike naive 'BTC compounds at 100%+' extrapolations, the power law mechanically slows returns as the asset ages (n/age), which is the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA<br>• Empirically tight in-sample: R²≈0.96 over ~12 orders of magnitude and ~15 years; visually compelling on log-log<br>• Recent peer-reviewed work (arXiv 2605.21316) finds that DESPITE weak statistical structure, the power law out-of-forecasts ARIMA, exponential smoothing and random-walk-with-drift at 12-24 month horizons (p<0.05) — so it has genuine, if modest, predictive content<br>• Parameter-light and falsifiable: a single exponent and intercept; deviations from the corridor are observable<br>• Gives an explicit fair-value band (not just a point), which maps naturally onto a CMA central case plus dispersion<br>• Author imposes a self-discipline ('do not use past ~2040'), acknowledging the model is an interpolation of an adoption S-curve, not eternal physics | • The headline structural claim is statistically weak: 8 of 11 Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests REJECT the power law (lognormal preferred), and the fitted exponent varies by ~3x (α̂≈5.65 to 16.5) across reasonable shifts of the time origin — violating shift-invariance and revealing the fit is not a robust law<br>• A 3-component sigmoid (multi-wave adoption) beats the power law in-sample on AIC/BIC — i.e., the power law is not even the best-fitting curve, it just generalizes better out-of-sample by being simpler<br>• Any monotonically rising series looks linear on a log-log plot; log-log axes massively compress error and flatter curve-fits — the 'tight fit' is partly an axis artifact (the core critique of the Burger corridor as retrofitting, not prediction)<br>• No economic anchor: t (calendar time) is not a value driver. The asserted Metcalfe causal loop (addresses~t^3, price~addresses^2) is the same family the academic literature largely rejects in naive form (spurious cointegration, non-stationarity), and Wheatley-Sornette's own generalized Metcalfe (exponent 1.69) is used to flag BTC as repeatedly OVER fundamental value, not to bless the trend<br>• Survivorship / single-path: the law is fit to the one realized BTC history; it cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass, so it overstates expected return by ignoring the left tail<br>• Post-2021 regime risk: ETF era, institutionalization and the maturity break mean the historical exponent may not persist; the corridor has already been quietly re-parameterized downward as upper bands over-predicted<br>• Says nothing about volatility-as-risk or correlations — useless for the portfolio-construction half of a CMA without external inputs<br>• Crypto-native marketing has weaponized it ('$1M floor by 2037') in ways the more careful authors did not intend; provenance must be separated from hype | • Time since genesis (t in days) — the sole regressor<br>• Fitted power-law exponent n≈5.6 and intercept A<br>• Asserted network/Metcalfe feedback loop linking addresses, price, and hash-rate as mutual power laws of time<br>• 1/t appreciation decay built into the functional form<br>• Corridor band multiples defining the fair-value dispersion<br>• Time-origin and fit-window choices (to which the exponent is highly sensitive) |
| 6 ⚠ | Entropy-Pooling / Fully-Flexible-Probabilities Stress-View CMA Construction (Meucci) | Practitioner | Entropy Pooling treats CMA-setting as a measure-change problem. You build a large panel of joint scenarios for BTC plus the correlation set (typically a fat-tailed historical bootstrap, so skew and crash mass are already present), each with a probability. Forward beliefs enter as linear constraints on those probabilities: mean/median (appreciation), volatility (a floor), the whole correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, VaR/quantiles, and tail co-dependence. EP solves for the posterior probabilities that satisfy all views with minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence from the prior, then a confidence c shrinks the result back toward the prior (Meucci 2008/2010). The output is a fully coherent distribution from which every CMA cell — appreciation (nominal/real), vol, each pairwise correlation, downside risk — is computed jointly, not bolted together. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it is the natural engine: impose the realized appreciation-decay path (142%→65%→17% to ~8-12% forward), a ~50-60% vol floor, deliberate left-tail mass, and ~0 BTC-gold correlation, and let EP reconcile them. It generates nothing on its own — garbage views in, garbage CMA out. | • Strictly more general than Black-Litterman/BMA: BL imposes only mean views under a Gaussian prior, whereas EP accepts views on volatility, the entire correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, quantiles/VaR and tail co-dependence on an arbitrary non-normal prior — exactly the moments that matter for a fat-tailed, skewed asset like BTC<br>• Internally coherent by construction: every CMA cell (appreciation, vol, all pairwise correlations, downside risk) is read from one posterior distribution, so the inputs are guaranteed mutually consistent — you cannot accidentally specify an appreciation/vol/correlation triple that has no valid joint distribution<br>• Minimal-distortion / least-spurious-structure property: KL-minimization changes the prior only as much as the views require, generalizing Bayesian updating (Caticha-Giffin), so unstated features of the fat-tailed prior (crash mass, skew) survive untouched<br>• Confidence parameter c lets you down-weight speculative long-horizon BTC views toward the historical prior, and opinion-pooling cleanly blends multiple analysts/scenarios — ideal when BTC views are genuinely uncertain<br>• No repricing needed and views can be inequalities/rankings, so it scales to large scenario panels and lax/qualitative beliefs ('decaying but still positive'); mature open-source implementations exist (Meucci MATLAB/R; fortitudo.tech Python; skfolio) | • Produces NO forecast of its own — it is a reconciliation engine, so the BTC appreciation/vol/correlation numbers are entirely the analyst's imposed views; it adds rigor and consistency but zero independent predictive content (garbage views in → coherent garbage CMA out). It cannot adjudicate the central question of *what* BTC's forward return is<br>• Garbage-prior risk: EP cannot create tail/crash mass the prior panel lacks. A BTC prior bootstrapped only from the survivorship-biased 2010-2026 path embeds BTC's good luck and under-weights absorbing-zero ruin; the posterior inherits that optimism no matter how the views are set<br>• View-conflict and order/partition dependence: imposing many moment views simultaneously (mean + vol floor + full correlation + skew + tails) can yield a posterior that satisfies constraints in a degenerate way (collapsing the effective number of scenarios). The need for Sequential Entropy Pooling (Vorobets) to get 'much better results for the same views' is itself an admission that the naive single-shot solution is fragile and grouping-dependent<br>• Confidence c and the prior are subjective and unobservable; there is no market-implied or data-driven way to pin them for a no-cashflow asset, so two honest analysts can produce very different BTC CMAs from the same engine — false precision risk<br>• Practitioner-only / not validated on crypto: there is no peer-reviewed application of EP to a 10-15yr Bitcoin CMA, no out-of-sample track record, and the method silently assumes the prior panel's dependence structure is a reasonable forward template — questionable across BTC's regime breaks (ETF era, institutionalization) | • Prior scenario panel: the choice and construction of the baseline joint distribution (historical bootstrap vs Monte-Carlo factor model; how much fat-tail/skew/crash mass is baked in) — EP cannot manufacture tail mass the prior lacks<br>• View set: which moments are constrained (mean/median, volatility, full correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, VaR quantiles, tail co-dependence) and the numerical targets imposed on each<br>• Confidence parameter c in [0,1]: opinion-pooling weight that shrinks the full-confidence posterior back toward the prior, governing how aggressively views override history<br>• Use of median/interquartile-range location and dispersion measures instead of mean/variance for fat-tailed, possibly infinite-variance BTC returns<br>• View ordering / partitioning: with many simultaneous moment views the naive single-shot EP can be suboptimal, so the grouping and sequence of constraints (Sequential Entropy Pooling) materially affects the posterior<br>• Effective Number of Scenarios (ENS): how much the views collapse the prior's diversity — a low ENS warns that the views are over-distorting the panel |
| 7 | Rational-Bubble / OLG No-Arbitrage Equilibrium (Tirole/Blanchard-Watson; van Oordt; Biais; Schilling-Uhlig Martingale) | Academia | Bitcoin has no cashflow, so the discounted-cashflow fundamental is ~zero and essentially the whole price is a rational bubble. The no-arbitrage logic (Blanchard-Watson, Tirole, van Oordt) forces a hard discipline a CMA can use: in equilibrium the bubble's EXPECTED return must equal the ordinary required return on risk capital - if it were higher the asset would eventually outweigh all wealth; if lower, nobody holds it. With stochastic bursting, price appreciates faster than the required return while it survives, but that excess exactly pays for a crash hazard, so unconditional E[r] = required return = discount rate + crash-hazard premium. Van Oordt adds a transactional-demand FLOOR (a PV of net transactional benefits) plus an additive bubble term needing ongoing net inflows; Biais et al. calibrate that only ~5% of BTC return variance is fundamental (95% extrinsic/sunspot) and that crash risk made up ~11pp of the early required return. Schilling-Uhlig bound it below: if the speculative condition fails, BTC is a martingale (expected real return = real rate) and can rationally go to zero. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this implies a modest expected return (an equity-like required return plus a crash premium survivors collect, NOT the realized 142%/65% survivor trail) with a fat left tail. | • Theoretically rigorous and internally consistent: it is the ONLY family that derives an explicit equilibrium expected-return IDENTITY (E[r] = required return = discount rate + crash-hazard premium) from first-principles no-arbitrage, rather than extrapolating a price curve - directly answering 'what return should a rational holder expect' for a no-cashflow asset<br>• Honestly bounds the upside: the no-arbitrage condition proves a rational bubble CANNOT deliver above-required-return expected appreciation indefinitely (else it outgrows all wealth), which is exactly the discipline a 10-15yr CMA needs against S2F/power-law/Metcalfe over-extrapolation - van Oordt explicitly rebuts the 'BTC grows to outweigh all wealth' critique<br>• Cleanly separates a defensible transactional-demand FLOOR from the speculative bubble term (van Oordt, Biais), so the CMA can be stress-tested by zeroing the bubble and seeing what utility-floor support remains<br>• Empirically calibrated, not just theoretical: Biais et al. Biais multiple-equilibria sunspot shift) that justifies the crash-hazard haircut other CMA rows apply by hand-waving<br>• Peer-reviewed, top-journal provenance (Econometrica, Journal of Finance, JME) with no asset-promoter conflict of interest - the opposite of the sell-side TAM pieces | • It is a POSITIVE (price-formation) theory, not a forecasting model: it pins expected return to an exogenous 'required return' it does not itself estimate, and it admits MULTIPLE equilibria and extrinsic volatility, so it yields a return IDENTITY and a tail structure but no unique point appreciation - any CMA number must be bolted on by choosing rho and h(t)<br>• The required-return identity says BTC's expected return is ~ordinary risk-required return, which sits FAR below realized history (142/65/17%/yr) - but that realized history is the survivor path, so the framework essentially says past returns are uninformative about forward expected returns, an uncomfortable, hard-to-calibrate stance<br>• Biais et al. find ~95% of return variance is extrinsic/sunspot - i.e. the model explicitly concedes that fundamentals explain almost nothing, so point forecasts inherit enormous uncertainty and the framework predicts perpetual high vol and crash risk rather than a clean expected return<br>• Crash hazard h(t) and loss-given-crash are essentially free parameters with little out-of-sample anchor; the bubble's EXPECTED return is pinned to this, not to realized history (Blanchard-Watson, Tirole, van Oordt)<br>• Crash hazard rate h(t) and loss-given-crash - the survival-conditioned appreciation is rho + h(t)*LGC; its level and growth set the lower bound below which negative bubbles are ruled out (van Oordt; Biais et al.)<br>• Net investment INFLOWS required to sustain the bubble term - rises with new-coin issuance and required return, falls with growth in transactional demand; a Ponzi-equivalent aggregate-cashflow condition (van Oordt)<br>• Extrinsic / sunspot volatility share - Biais et al. calibrate ~95% of return variance as non-fundamental, implying multiple equilibria and a coordination (sunspot) risk that can shift the asset off the positive-value equilibrium<br>• Speculative ('hodling') condition (Schilling-Uhlig): whether buyers hold coins back expecting appreciation; The heterogeneous cost curve (low-cost survivors at the bottom) plus a ~0.7 hashrate-price elasticity (asymmetric — fast up, sticky down) loosely bound drawdowns. The deliverable is a combined predictive density — a central forecast plus genuinely wide intervals that widen when the models disagree. Following Sharpe-Tint (1990), risk is the volatility of surplus (assets minus PV of liabilities); an asset is valued by its covariance with the liability, and earns inclusion only if its expected return clears a hurdle roughly equal to its beta-to-surplus times the surplus risk premium (the reverse-optimized "implied return"). Key inputs: the liability's risk drivers (real spending, wages, healthcare inflation, or the discount-rate curve), BTC's covariance with those drivers (empirically near zero), BTC's standalone volatility (55-100%), and the sleeve size. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the implication is sobering: because BTC hedges almost no real liability and its huge variance dominates surplus risk even at a 1-3% weight, the implied hurdle is high (plausibly mid-teens to 20%+ depending on liability and risk aversion). The framework therefore does not produce appreciation, vol, or correlation numbers directly; it produces a PASS/FAIL bar against whatever independent BTC return assumption you bring. Its honest verdict: only a tiny return-seeking sleeve, justified by raw return, not by liability hedging. | • Asks the correct question for an institution: not 'is BTC's Sharpe ratio attractive in isolation?' but 'does a BTC sleeve improve the probability of paying real liabilities?' — surfacing that BTC's diversification benefit is largely irrelevant to a spending/wage/healthcare liability it does not hedge<br>• Honest about volatility: by penalizing the variance of SURPLUS (not assets), it correctly inflates BTC's cost via its 55-100% vol, preventing the asset-only Sharpe optimizers (which BTC's high realized return flatters) from over-allocating — the framework structurally caps the sleeve at a token weight<br>• Produces a falsifiable decision bar (the implied hurdle) you can test any independent BTC CMA against, rather than a self-serving price target; it cleanly separates 'return-seeking' from 'liability-hedging' so BTC cannot masquerade as a hedge<br>• Methodologically grounded in 35+ years of accepted institutional practice (Sharpe-Tint surplus optimization, Leibowitz endowment-model dual-risk framework, LDI) — not a crypto-native curve-fit | • It is NOT a return forecaster: it consumes a BTC expected-return assumption and tells you whether it clears the bar — so it cannot, by itself, populate a CMA's appreciation cell. You still need an exogenous BTC return model, inheriting all that model's flaws<br>• Garbage-in on the covariance: the hurdle depends critically on BTC's covariance with the liability, which is estimated on a short, non-stationary BTC history and is regime-dependent (BTC's equity correlation has risen from ~0.26 to ~0.56). If BTC's correlation to the discount-rate/liquidity factor rises in a crisis exactly when funded status is stressed, the realized surplus damage exceeds the ex-ante hurdle<br>• No institution has actually published a liability-relative BTC hurdle — Grayscale, ARK and every existing approach in the set run asset-only mean-variance/Sharpe optimization against stocks and bonds, never against a liability covariance. Black & Litterman (1992) observed that market-cap weights, taken as a CAPM equilibrium, imply a unique vector of excess returns via Pi = lambda*Sigma*w (lambda~2.5-3 the market risk-aversion). Apply that to BTC's ~0.3-0.5% share of global investable assets and the implied excess return is tiny (<1%/yr). Kelly (1956)/Thorp give the same answer for a log-utility investor: f*=(mu-r)/sigma^2, so inverting a 1-2% holding at 55% vol gives mu-r = f*sigma^2 = only 0.3-0.6%/yr. HRP/risk-parity weights (Lopez de Prado 2016) are set without any return view at all; asking what return rationalizes them closes the loop. Two academic strands exist: Liu & Zhang's price-to-utility (PU) ratio, which proxies store-of-value utility via the UTXO staking ratio (coins idle >1 year) and flags BTC as rich or cheap to that utility, predicting long-horizon returns through mean-reversion; and Papadogiannis's unified-discounting identity, which models scarcity as a latent state variable mapped to pseudo-cashflows and discounted at an effective rate c_eff = cost-of-capital × belief-distortion. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out cleanly: an expected return emerges only by assuming the PU ratio normalizes AND the monetary-premium TAM grows along a decaying adoption S-curve. So the appreciation number (~10-13% nominal, echoing VanEck's 15% base) is really a TAM-penetration forecast in DCF costume; the framework's genuine value-add is putting BTC on the same algebraic footing as equities and gold. | • Honest about the absence of cashflow — instead of faking a dividend it explicitly models a utility/monetary-premium flow or a terminal scarcity value, which is the economically correct object for a non-productive asset<br>• Provides a falsifiable rich/cheap signal: the PU ratio is empirically shown to predict LONG-horizon BTC returns out-of-sample and to beat buy-and-hold and naive market-timing in backtests (Liu & Zhang)<br>• Grounds the proxy in classic monetary theory (medium-of-exchange / store-of-value / unit-of-account) and unique blockchain accounting (UTXO), rather than ad hoc curve-fitting<br>• The unified-discounting variant (Papadogiannis) restores algebraic comparability with equities/gold under one DCF identity, which is exactly what a CMA committee needs to slot BTC next to other building blocks<br>• Naturally accommodates appreciation DECAY: as the TAM penetration S-curve flattens and the PU ratio normalizes, implied forward returns fall toward a gold-like drift — the right shape for a 10–15yr CMA | • Garbage-in: the 'utility' proxy is a choice, not a fact. UTXO staking ratios, active addresses, and on-chain volume are gameable, regime-dependent, and only loosely tied to monetary value; the PU ratio's predictive edge is in-sample/backtest and over a short, bull-dominated history (2011–2020).<br>• It is TAM-penetration forecasting in DCF costume. The number that drives everything — Pr(adoption) and terminal share of gold/FX/reserves — is an unfalsifiable prior. Marketing 'academic' DCFs (ARK $1.2–2.4M by 2030; VanEck $2.9M by 2050 ~15% CAGR) are sensitive almost entirely to the penetration assumption, not the discounting math.<br>• Sibling naive models are REJECTED by the peer-reviewed econometrics. Stock-to-Flow regressions are spurious: S2F and price are both non-stationary (I(1)/trending), Engle–Granger cointegration fails its own preconditions, residuals are serially correlated, and the model broke post-2021 (predicted ~$100k in 2022; BTC crashed). Metcalfe/PM ratios likewise have little short-run predictive power and treat all users identically. The PU-ratio paper itself concedes traditional fundamental-to-market ratios fail short-term.<br>• The effective discount rate c_eff and belief-distortion K (Papadogiannis) are not independently observable — they are calibrated to fit observed price, so the framework can rationalize almost any valuation ex post (low falsifiability).<br>• No native volatility or correlation output. The family produces a fair-value level / expected return; vol and the correlation vector must be imported from realized data or asserted — so it contributes nothing to the risk side of a CMA on its own.<br>• Survivorship and reflexivity: 'utility' rises with price (more holders/activity when number-go-up), so utility-as-fundamental and price are mutually endogenous — undercutting the claim that one anchors the other. | • Utility/moneyness proxy growth — on-chain activity, active addresses, transaction value, and UTXO staking ratio (Liu-Zhang use staking ratio as the store-of-value proxy)<br>• Total addressable market (TAM) of the monetary functions BTC competes for — gold, offshore/store-of-value wealth, FX/settlement, central-bank reserves — and BTC's penetration share of each<br>• Effective discount rate c_eff = benchmark opportunity cost c times belief-distortion ratio K (Papadogiannis); a very high required return reflecting adoption/survival risk<br>• Probability of monetary adoption / survival — implicit Pr(BTC becomes a durable global store of value) that scales the terminal value<br>• Mean-reversion speed of the market-to-fundamental (PU) ratio — converts a level signal into an expected return<br>• Terminal resale / monetary-premium value at horizon end (no perpetuity of cashflows; value is entirely the terminal moneyness stock)<br>• Macro/liquidity regime — real rates and money-supply growth shift the convenience yield on a non-yielding monetary asset |

This breaks the 'floor' logic that the whole CMA rests on.<br>• The 'floor' is empirically breached in BOTH directions: price traded ~20-40% BELOW production cost for months in Oct-2022/FTX and again in Feb-2026 (price ~$70k vs cost ~$87k), while in bull runs price ran multiples ABOVE cost. So it is neither a floor nor a ceiling — at best a loose attractor.<br>• Hayes HIMSELF cautions against imputing an intrinsic value from it: 'extreme volatility and frequent market price fluctuations… could make identifying such an intrinsic value meaningless in application.' The naive model does not survive the modern regime.<br>• Indeterminate as a return forecast: the cost floor's future level depends on the hashrate AND efficiency paths, which are themselves driven by price and AI/data-center competition for chips and power (JPMorgan notes miners now decoupling toward AI) — so the 'forecast' smuggles in a price assumption.<br>• Tells you nothing about correlations, volatility, or risk premia — it is a level/anchor model, not a distributional CMA. Mapped forward, it implies appreciation dominated by the risk-free rate (~4-5%) plus a thin, shrinking premium — a low-double-digit ceiling, with volatility and correlations imported from other rows. | • Purely observable and model-light: reads off live, regulated screen prices - whatever you read today is regime-contingent and unstable<br>• Compresses toward the risk-free rate as the market matures and ETF arbitrage saturates: 2024's 20-30% collapsed to ~5% by 2026, so historical carry massively overstates forward carry<br>• No long-dated instruments means any decade-horizon use requires the same arbitrary extrapolation this approach was supposed to avoid - extrapolating a single-metaorder impact law to a 10-15yr cumulative-demand 'super-metaorder' is a heroic stretch the original authors never endorsed — impact decay, liquidity replenishment and regime change over a decade are not captured by a static sqrt(Q)<br>• Impact is largely TRANSIENT: only ~2/3 (and on Bitcoin, per Donier-Bonart, an 'uninformed' component leading to 'almost complete long-term decay') of peak impact persists, so naive use overstates the permanent price gain from a given flow — durable appreciation requires the demand to be 'informed'/persistent, an assumption the law cannot certify<br>• Parameters drift: Y, sigma and especially V (liquid float) are non-stationary; ETF custody and HODLing shrink V (amplifying impact) while deeper institutional books raise it — the net is ambiguous and the law gives no law of motion for V<br>• Silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on all cross-asset correlations (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) — every distributional and portfolio-construction cell must be imported from realized data; it populates at most the appreciation channel<br>• Reflexivity/endogeneity: sigma and V are themselves functions of price and flow, so the 'exogenous Q in, price out' framing is circular over long horizons; the same critique (price drives the inputs) that dogs S2F/NVT applies once you leave the intraday regime | • Cumulative net institutional demand Q over the horizon (the metaorder size) — the exogenous input the law converts to price; for a CMA this is the projected 10-15yr net inflow path, which the law itself does NOT forecast<br>• Square-root exponent delta ~ 1/2 (empirically anchored on Bitcoin; Donier-Bonart) — the concavity parameter that forces appreciation decay<br>• Order-unity prefactor Y (~0.5-1) calibrating impact magnitude per unit normalized flow<br>• Volatility sigma — impact scales linearly in sigma, so higher BTC vol amplifies the price move per dollar of flow<br>• Traded volume / liquidity V (the normalization) — deeper float and volume shrink impact; thinning liquid float (HODLing, ETF custody) raises it<br>• Latent-liquidity profile shape near price (locally linear vanishing of supply/demand -> sqrt; the LLOB/Walrasian micro-foundation)<br>• Permanent vs transient impact fraction (~2/3 of peak impact tends to persist; the rest decays) — determines how much of demand-driven price gain is durable vs mean-reverting |
| 71 | Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law | Crypto-native | Stock-to-Flow values Bitcoin purely on monetary scarcity: it regresses log market value on the log stock-to-flow ratio (existing supply divided by annual new issuance), the same hardness metric used for gold and silver. PlanB's original fit (value proportional to SF^3.3, R squared about 0.95) and the cross-asset S2FX version (pooling BTC, gold and silver, treating halvings as discrete phase transitions, R squared about 0.997) both produce dated price targets, e.g. the $288k 2020-2024 cluster. Because issuance halves every four years, SF roughly doubles each halving, so the model mechanically projects roughly 10x (S2F) to 17x (S2FX) per step, implying ~78%/yr between halvings forever. For a 10-15yr CMA this is the model's fatal flaw: it is demand-blind, the regression is spurious (both series are non-stationary and fail cointegration), and it broke out-of-sample after 2021 (predicted ~$98k, BTC closed ~$57k). It also says nothing about volatility or correlations. Honest forward use discards the literal targets, imposes BTC's realized appreciation decay, and yields only a low-double-digit nominal anchor. | • Fully deterministic supply input: the halving schedule and 21M cap are known in advance, so SF is the rare financial variable with zero forecast error — attractive for a long-horizon CMA skeleton<br>• Parsimonious and falsifiable: a single regressor produces explicit, dated price targets that can be checked (and have been)<br>• Captures a real economic intuition — that a credibly fixed, ungrowable supply supports a monetary 'hardness' premium (the same logic that makes gold a store of value); the Austrian/Mises critique even concedes SF can matter for a money's quality<br>• Cross-asset framing (S2FX) at least disciplines the BTC fit against gold and silver rather than fitting BTC in isolation<br>• Morillon & Chacon (2022), the first peer-reviewed treatment, find the in-sample fit is robust to early-assumption choices (not pure data-mining) and that dynamic out-of-sample accuracy improves over time | • Spurious regression / non-stationarity: both ln(price) and ln(SF) are non-stationary, trending series, so the high R² is the textbook artifact of regressing one trend on another. Without cointegration the coefficients and R² are statistically meaningless (Burger, Bitcoinwords/WORDS review; has been shown cointegration generally does not hold)<br>• SF is a near-deterministic step function of time, so S2F is effectively price-regressed-on-time in disguise — it cannot distinguish scarcity from any other variable that trended up over 2010-2020<br>• Demand-blind by construction: ignores adoption, liquidity, ETF flows, macro/real rates, regulation. Mises critique: scarcity (a subjective demand condition) is conflated with the mechanical SF ratio; price comes from marginal valuations, not a physical supply metric<br>• Out-of-sample failure: PlanB's S2F/S2FX predicted >$100k for 2021-2022; BTC closed Nov-2021 ~$57k and bottomed <$16k in 2022. The model has traded materially below trend since 2021 (off by ~$130k at points). 'Floor model' walk-back further eroded credibility<br>• Diminishing-returns problem: S2F implies a constant ~10x per halving forever (no decay), contradicting the clear empirical decay of BTC's growth rate (142%→65%→17%/yr) — the model is structurally too bullish at long horizons and its targets (e.g. $288k, $500k+, eventually multi-million) are unbounded<br>• Even when the fit 'works', Morillon & Chacon show an S2F-timing strategy underperforms buy-and-hold — no economic value added<br>• Says nothing about volatility or correlations — it is a price-level model only, so it cannot directly populate most CMA cells (vol, corr to equities/FI/TIPS/gold)<br>• S2FX 'phase transitions' have only ~4-6 data clusters; fitting a power law through 4 points (plus gold/silver) is gross overfitting and 'has not been replicated or reviewed' per PlanB himself | • Stock-to-flow ratio SF = circulating supply / annual new issuance (rises mechanically as block subsidy halves every ~210,000 blocks / ~4 years)<br>• Power-law exponent (~3.3 in original S2F) linking ln(SF) to ln(market value)<br>• Halving schedule — the deterministic, pre-programmed supply shock that doubles SF and drives ~10x value steps<br>• Cross-asset anchoring: gold (SF~62) and silver (SF~22) market values used to pin the regression line and justify a 'monetary scarcity' premium for BTC as SF approaches/exceeds gold<br>• Phase transitions / clusters (S2FX): treating each halving epoch as a regime with distinct properties, replacing time with SF as the independent variable<br>• Absolute scarcity / 21M hard cap as the terminal narrative (SF → ∞ as issuance → 0) |
| 72 | Logarithmic-Regression "Rainbow" Fair-Value Corridor | Crypto-native | The Rainbow chart fits log(BTC price) to a logarithmic function of time — log10(price)=a·ln(time)−b — so the fair-value line bends DOWN even on a log scale, baking in diminishing returns as the network matures. Nine color bands, spaced ~0.5×–5× around that line, label sentiment zones (deep-blue "fire sale" to dark-red "bubble"); they are read as over/under-valuation, not price targets. For a CMA you extrapolate the central line: because instantaneous appreciation ≈ ln(10)·a/t, the model itself forecasts decay — roughly mid-30s %/yr at BTC's current ~17yr age sliding toward low-20s %/yr by ~2040. The corridor width substitutes for a volatility/dispersion view. Key inputs are just the fitted coefficients a, b and the fit window — there is no demand, supply, macro or cashflow input. The honest read: the authors call it a "meme chart… not investment advice," it has been recalibrated downward after breaking its own lower band (2022), and any 10-15yr number is a curve-extrapolation, not a forecast. It implies a decaying-but-still-high-double-digit nominal CAGR; volatility and all correlations must be imported from realized data. | • Encodes appreciation DECAY more aggressively than naive extrapolations: the ln(time) form flattens the trend even on a log scale, the qualitatively correct shape for a maturing, no-cashflow asset's forward CMA<br>• Provides an explicit fair-value CORRIDOR rather than a point, which maps cleanly onto a CMA central case plus a dispersion/band view<br>• Parameter-light, transparent and falsifiable: two coefficients fit by OLS on public price data, R²≈0.95 in-sample; deviations from the band are observable in real time<br>• The single most widely cited, most accessible crypto-native fair-value band (Blockchaincenter, Bitcoin Magazine Pro, Coin Bureau, CoinGecko, Bitbo), so it shapes retail/practitioner expectations and is worth critiquing on its own terms<br>• Authors are unusually honest about limits — explicit 'meme chart / not investment advice / no scientific basis / cannot predict price with a rainbow' disclaimers, which is more candor than S2F or Metcalfe marketing | • No economic anchor whatsoever: calendar time is not a value driver. It fits a curve purely to past price — no supply, demand, adoption, macro, ETF-flow or cashflow input — so it is the most fundamentals-free model in the set (its own creators say it has 'no scientific basis')<br>• Retrofitting / recalibration is the fatal critique: when BTC broke the lower band in the Nov-2022 FTX crash, the curve was RE-FITTED downward (V2, again in 2023). A 'fair value' line that is silently re-parameterized whenever price escapes it is descriptive, not predictive — it can never be falsified because it is moved to fit<br>• Spurious-trend problem: log-price and ln(time) are both monotone trends; any rising series looks tight on a log-log/semi-log axis. The R²≈0.95 is an axis artifact (massive error compression), not evidence of a law — the same critique that sinks naive S2F/Metcalfe<br>• Survivorship / single-path: fit to the one realized BTC history; it cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass, so it overstates expected return by ignoring the left tail<br>• Lagging and band-breaking in BOTH directions: responds only to closing prices, overshoots tops/bottoms by 20-50%, and price has wicked outside both bands — so it is neither floor nor ceiling, just a loose attractor<br>• Says nothing about volatility-as-a-statistic or any cross-asset correlation; the corridor width is a price-dispersion band, not an annualized return vol, and every correlation cell must be imported from realized data<br>• Crypto marketing weaponizes it ('$1M by ~2037' style claims) in ways the careful authors disclaim; provenance of any forward number must be separated from the meme | • Time since genesis (ln of days/weeks since 2009) — the sole regressor<br>• Fitted log-regression coefficients a (slope on ln time) and b (intercept), e.g. V1 a=2.9065 / b=19.493; Coin Bureau V2-style a=2.6521 / b=18.163 (weeks); R²≈0.95<br>• 1/t appreciation decay AND log-scale flattening built into the ln(time) functional form (steeper deceleration than power-law-in-time)<br>• Band multipliers (~0.5× to ~5× the central line), evenly log-spaced, defining the corridor / dispersion<br>• Fit-window and time-origin choices, plus periodic DOWNWARD recalibration (V2 after the Nov-2022 FTX break) — the retrofitting lever<br>• Implicit adoption-S-curve narrative (diminishing returns as market cap expands) used to justify the flattening, but with no demand/macro variable |
