WHAT IT IS. This family forecasts Bitcoin's physical-measure (P) volatility process and its term structure, in contrast to the Q-measure options/DVOL surface (#11), which is limited to the ~6-month liquid-option tenor and prices risk-neutral variance, and in contrast to the descriptive regime-switching/jump-diffusion family (#19), which characterizes the distributional SHAPE but does not LEARN/forecast a vol path. Three pillars: (1) HAR-RV (Corsi 2009, J. Financial Econometrics 7:174-196): an additive cascade of daily/weekly/monthly realized-volatility components, estimated by OLS on high-frequency (typically 5-min) RV, that reproduces long memory, fat tails and self-similarity with no true long-memory parameter — 'remarkably good forecasting performance.' Extensions (Andersen-Bollerslev-Diebold HAR-CJ; HAR-RSV-J with signed semivariances) split continuous diffusive vol from discrete jumps. (2) GARCH-family (EGARCH/GJR/APARCH and score-driven GAS): conditional variance with leverage and heavy-tailed innovations, implying a long-run unconditional variance the forecast reverts toward. Catania & Grassi (2022, IJF 38:878-894) show conventional GARCH performs poorly on crypto and that time-varying skewness/score-driven dynamics improve forecasts across 600+ coins. (3) ML/hybrid: Huang, Sangiorgi & Urquhart (2024, JIFMIM 97:102064) find LSTM and CNN-LSTM beat GARCH at every 1-day-to-2-month horizon, with predictors spanning other cryptos, commodities, blockchain data, Twitter uncertainty and CO2. The LSTM-GARCH paper (Garcia-Lopez et al., Computational Economics 63:4, PMC10013303) feeds eGARCH/gjrGARCH parameters into LSTMs.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. RV is the observable; the HAR cascade encodes heterogeneous-horizon traders; jumps (bipower variation) are frequent in BTC and the jump term is statistically significant and improves accuracy; mean-reversion speed (GARCH alpha+beta persistence) sets the term-structure slope and the long-run sigma. Documented empirical facts: HAR-on-realized-variance beats daily-data GARCH, edge largest at short horizons; EGARCH/APARCH best among GARCH; BTC shows an atypical/inverse leverage effect.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The realized series decays 103% (full 2010-) -> 69% (10y) -> 57% (5y), with 2024-25 calm-window spot vol dipping toward ~40% and Kaiko reporting realized vol down ~75% from historical peaks by mid-2025 amid ETF 'strong hands.' This is exactly mean reversion to a falling long-run level — the family's core message. Failure modes are serious and I represent them faithfully: (a) HORIZON MISMATCH — every validated forecast is 1-day to ~2-months; a 10-15yr CMA is an out-of-model assertion of the unconditional sigma, and the best model differs by horizon. (b) FRAGILE ML EDGE — PMC10013303 found a plain MLP best, with NO Diebold-Mariano-significant gain over LSTM/GARCH, on only 6 pandemic months and at ~40x the compute; 'HARd to Beat' (arXiv 2406.08041) shows rolling-window choice can dominate model choice — classic overfit risk. (c) NON-STATIONARITY/REGIME BREAK — a model fit on 2017-2022 turbulence can mis-set the floor after ETF institutionalization; jump intensity is not a stable parameter. (d) CONDITIONAL != UNCONDITIONAL — a tranquil nowcast (~40%) is NOT the decade vol, because a 10-15yr window must average over recurrent 60-80% drawdown/jump episodes, mechanically lifting the unconditional sigma back toward 50-60%.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. Critically, this family produces essentially NO on-record multi-year vol forecasts — the academic papers stop at 1-2 months. The only decade-scale vol numbers in the broader literature come from sell-side narrative (e.g., CF Benchmarks projecting vol toward ~28% over a decade, in the SoV-TAM approach), which is NOT an RV/GARCH/ML output and which this family's mean-reversion logic actually undercuts: there is no RV/GARCH/ML evidence of a realized floor below ~57%, so a ~28% terminal is unsupported by the forecasting models themselves.

CMA BOTTOM LINE. Use this family for ONE thing: setting and defending the volatility cell. The defensible decade-average is ~50-60% (center ~55%), a mean-reverting path with a diffusive floor ~40-50% plus a jump premium, explicitly above gold (~15%) and equities (~18%). It is silent on appreciation (import the ~8-12% nominal cross-approach central) and on all correlations (import realized: growth ~+0.45, value ~+0.30, nominal FI ~+0.15, TIPS ~+0.25, gold ~0). Skeptical read: its real contribution is disciplinary — it kills the 'BTC vol will converge to gold/equity levels' claim while also refusing to over-extrapolate a calm-period 40% nowcast into the CMA.

### #15 · Consumption-CAPM / Rare-Disaster / ICAPM Hedging-Demand Equilibrium Premium

*Family: consumption-equilibrium-SDF · Source: Academia · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 59*


**Explanation:** This family prices Bitcoin from a structural SDF instead of a chart. Under Lucas/Breeden consumption-CAPM the equilibrium premium is risk-aversion times the covariance of BTC returns with consumption growth. Empirically that covariance is ~zero — Liu-Tsyvinski (2021) find BTC has no exposure to macro/consumption factors and the NY Fed (Benigno-Rosa 2023) find it ignores monetary/macro news — so the model predicts a LOW or NEGATIVE premium while realized returns are huge. Wilson (2024) names this the 'Bitcoin premium puzzle': the model is rejected even at risk aversion above 10. Barro-Rietz rare-disaster theory rescues part of it (high return = crash compensation), but Almeida et al. (2024) show only ~one-third of the BTC premium comes from bad-state returns; most is upside, so disaster risk is a minority driver and compresses as perceived crash probability falls. Merton ICAPM adds that BTC's weak inflation/recession hedge RAISES required return — inverting gold-parity. For a 10-15yr CMA the structural read forces appreciation DECAY toward a high-beta-equity-plus-shrinking-disaster-residual, with very wide error bands.


*Scores — rigor 5, signal 2, robustness 4, data-ops 2, orthogonality 4. Theoretically the most rigorous family in the set — it derives the premium from a structural SDF (risk-aversion x consumption-covariance + disaster compensation) and asks why a premium should exist. But it fails on its own terms for BTC (rejected at RRA>10, the 'premium puzzle'), so its predictive power for a 10-15yr level is weak — wide CIs, low-power Euler tests, no usable point forecast. Its real value is conditioning: it survives regime change well because the ~zero consumption/macro covariance is a structural fact independent of halving cycles or the ETF correlation shift, and rare-disaster decay matches the observed appreciation decay. Operationally awkward: disaster calibration is unidentifiable (no realized BTC consumption disasters) and the synthesized levels are judgment, not model output.*


**Key drivers:** Coefficient of relative risk aversion (RRA) in the representative-agent SDF — Wilson rejects the model even at RRA > 10; equity-premium-style calibrations need RRA ~3-4 with disasters; Covariance of BTC returns with aggregate consumption growth — empirically ~zero (Liu-Tsyvinski 2021; Benigno-Rosa 2023), which is what breaks the C-CAPM and creates the puzzle; Perceived rare-disaster probability and severity (Barro-Rietz) — crash/protocol-failure/regulatory-ruin tail; the disaster premium falls as this perceived probability declines with ETFs/institutionalization; Share of premium from bad states vs good states — Almeida et al. (2024) find only ~1/3 of BTC's premium comes from negative (-3 to -1 SD) returns, ~39% from large positive returns (the puzzle's right tail); Merton ICAPM hedging value — BTC's weak/negative inflation- and recession-hedge RAISES required return (risk amplifier), inverting the gold-parity logic; Money-in-utility / transactional-services term and illiquidity/holding-cost penalty (Schilling-Uhlig, Choi-Rocheteau endowment-economy variants); Rising BTC-equity (consumption-proxy) covariance over time — Wilson and others note stock-BTC correlation has been 'tightening'; as covariance rises, the structurally-justified premium and the beta both rise


**Pros:** Only family in the set that derives BTC's premium from a structural equilibrium SDF (risk-aversion x consumption-covariance + disaster compensation) rather than fitting price to time, supply, or network size — it asks WHY a risk premium should exist, not just what curve fits; Generates honest, often DEFLATIONARY guidance for a forward CMA: because BTC's consumption covariance is ~zero, the structurally-JUSTIFIED premium is small — a powerful counterweight to S2F/Metcalfe/power-law hype that mechanically extrapolate high returns; Rare-disaster mechanism naturally produces appreciation DECAY: as perceived crash/ruin probability falls with institutionalization and ETF adoption, the disaster premium compresses — the correct qualitative shape for a maturing asset; The ICAPM-hedging inversion is a genuine conceptual contribution: it explains WHY a poor inflation/recession hedge should command a HIGHER (not lower) required return, correctly flipping the naive 'digital gold safe-haven' story that the gold-parity approaches lean on; Peer-reviewed and falsifiable (Wilson 2024 B.E. J. Macro; Liu-Tsyvinski 2021 RFS; Almeida et al. 2024): the puzzle is documented with formal Euler-equation/GMM tests and option-implied premium decompositions, not assertion; Portfolio-coherent: an SDF framework outputs a premium AND, in principle, betas/covariances that slot directly into a mean-variance CMA, unlike level-only models (S2F, cost-of-production)


**Cons:** The model FAILS on its own terms for BTC — it cannot explain the realized premium at any reasonable risk aversion (rejected even at RRA > 10). It diagnoses a puzzle but does not produce a usable point forecast; the 'CMA' is the small structural premium PLUS a large unexplained residual the theory can't pin down; Consumption-covariance is measured with enormous noise and the GMM/Euler tests have 'extremely low power' (Wilson) and 'very wide confidence intervals' — so the framework cannot statistically reject almost any forward return, making it weak as a precise CMA generator; Rare-disaster calibration is fundamentally unidentifiable: with no realized 'BTC consumption disasters' in a ~15yr sample, the disaster probability/severity that rationalizes the premium is free-fit and unfalsifiable (the standard Barro-Rietz critique — 'peso problem' in reverse); Almeida et al. show disaster/bad-state risk is only ~1/3 of the BTC premium — most premium is UPSIDE (positive-return states), which a crash-compensation SDF does not naturally explain; the dominant driver looks like speculative/convenience demand, not consumption-risk insurance; Consumption data is low-frequency (quarterly), heavily revised, and a poor match for a 24/7 asset whose price is dominated by sentiment/flows — Chen et al. find BTC's pricing kernel is 'decoupled from the consumption kernel' (minimal impact from real-economy shocks), undermining the C-CAPM mechanism at the root; Silent on most CMA cells as published: the structural papers quote a premium (and the option papers a variance-risk premium) but do not publish forward volatility or a full cross-asset correlation matrix vs growth/value/FI/TIPS/gold — those must be imported; The ICAPM-hedging-amplifier and C-CAPM-low-premium conclusions point in OPPOSITE directions (one says high required return because bad hedge, the other says low premium because low covariance), so the family does not yield a single coherent number without the analyst choosing which mechanism dominates

METHODOLOGY. This family is the only structural-equilibrium strand in the BTC-CMA universe. It nests three classical models. (1) Lucas (1978)/Breeden (1979) consumption-CAPM: in a representative-agent exchange economy the equilibrium risk premium on any asset equals RRA x cov(asset return, consumption growth). (2) Barro (2006)/Rietz (1988) rare disasters: augment the endowment process with low-probability, high-severity consumption collapses; the equity (or BTC) premium becomes compensation for bad-state exposure and can be matched with modest RRA (~3-4) once disasters are present. (3) Merton (1973) ICAPM: with stochastic investment opportunities, required return depends on an asset's covariance with state variables investors want to hedge (inflation, recessions); an asset that hedges POORLY commands a HIGHER required return. Applied to BTC, money-in-utility (Schilling-Uhlig 2019) and search/holding-cost variants (Choi-Rocheteau 2021) add a transactional-services term and illiquidity penalty.

KEY RELATIONSHIP & THE PUZZLE. The load-bearing empirical fact is that BTC's consumption/macro covariance is ~zero. Liu-Tsyvinski (RFS 2021) find crypto 'has no exposure to most common stock-market and macroeconomic factors or to the returns of currencies and commodities' — only crypto-specific network/momentum/attention factors price it. Benigno-Rosa (NY Fed SR 1052, 2023) find BTC is 'unresponsive to both monetary and macroeconomic news' while the same news significantly moves stocks, exchange rates and precious metals. Plug a near-zero consumption covariance into C-CAPM and the model predicts a LOW or NEGATIVE premium. Yet realized BTC excess returns are enormous. Wilson (2024, B.E. J. Macro) formalizes this as the 'Bitcoin premium puzzle': using the three standard equity-premium methods (Mehra-Prescott model premium, Euler-equation tests, GMM RRA estimation), 'standard macroeconomic models predict a low or negative Bitcoin premium... the model is rejected even when the coefficient of relative risk aversion is above 10.' He notes 'stocks are more tightly correlated with consumption, so the model tends to predict a very low Bitcoin premium,' and the stock-BTC correlation 'has been tightening over time' — a structural break in late 2013 lowered the premium, but the puzzle 'is persistent... no downward trend since.'

QUOTES/FIT. Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024/2025) decompose the option-implied premium: BP averages ~66%/yr (1-month), BVRP ~14%/yr, Sharpe ~0.8 (~2x S&P 500). Critically, 'negative Bitcoin returns (between three and one standard deviations) account for only one-third of the total Bitcoin premium,' while large positive returns (20-60%) account for ~39%. This DAMAGES the pure rare-disaster reading: if BTC's return were mainly crash-compensation, the premium should concentrate in bad states as it does (more so) for the S&P. Instead BTC's premium is upside-dominated — pointing to speculative/convenience demand, not consumption-disaster insurance. They cite Chen et al. that BTC's pricing kernel is 'decoupled from the consumption kernel, with minimal impact from real-economy shocks like the COVID crisis.'

FAILURE MODES. (a) Identification: with no realized BTC consumption-disaster, the disaster probability/severity that rationalizes the premium is free-fit and unfalsifiable. (b) Power: Wilson's Euler/GMM tests have 'very wide confidence intervals' and 'extremely low power' — the framework cannot reject most forward returns, so it is a weak point-forecast generator. (c) Data mismatch: quarterly, revised consumption vs a 24/7 sentiment-driven asset. (d) Internal tension: the C-CAPM (low covariance -> low premium) and the ICAPM-hedging (poor hedge -> high required return) conclusions point in opposite directions; the analyst must choose which dominates.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This strand deliberately produces no dated price target — its contribution is to DOCUMENT that no structural risk-premium model can justify BTC's realized return, which implies a forward CMA should NOT extrapolate that return. The honest structural implication for a 10-15yr CMA is a SMALL justified premium (high-beta-equity-like, ~7-11% nominal) plus a shrinking disaster residual, with appreciation decaying as BTC's equity covariance rises and perceived disaster probability falls — and with very wide bands given the near-zero test power. The ICAPM inversion is the distinctive CMA contribution: it correctly flips the gold-parity 'safe-haven lowers required return' logic, treating BTC's weak inflation/recession hedge as a required-return amplifier rather than a discount, which is why this family assigns BTC a LOW gold correlation and refuses it gold's real-purchasing-power premium.

</details>

### #16 · Debasement-CAGR / Fiat-Half-Life Return Floor

*Family: monetary-debasement-floor · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 58*


**Explanation:** The mechanism is an identity, not a regression: if the unit of account (fiat) is diluted at rate d per year, any asset with a credibly non-dilutable supply must, over long horizons, appreciate in that unit at least at d to hold constant real share. The key input is the TRUE debasement rate — broad money + credit growth (~6-12%/yr, central ~7% per Lyn Alden), deliberately chosen over CPI (~2-3%) because money creation, not the consumer-price basket, measures denominator dilution. The "fiat half-life" reframes this: at ~7%/yr, fiat purchasing power halves in ~10yr, so the floor is ~7% nominal / ~4-5% real. Expected return = this floor PLUS a decaying adoption premium (the S-curve repricing as BTC monetizes), which compresses toward zero as adoption saturates. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this implies nominal appreciation drifting DOWN from history toward the high-single-to-low-double-digit floor plus a thin, shrinking premium — i.e. ~9-13% nominal, the floor being the durable component and the premium the part that decays out, consistent with realized 142%->65%->17% decay.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 5, orthogonality 3. Identity logic and the broad-money-over-CPI choice are genuinely sound and yield the right decaying shape, lifting rigor above average. But the "floor" is empirically falsified (BTC fell 16-32% while money grew, equity corr rose to +0.56), so signal and regime-robustness are weak; it adds no tail/correlation conditioning beyond a level anchor. Broad-money inputs are trivially available and stable, making data_ops excellent.*


**Key drivers:** Broad money + credit growth rate (the true debasement rate, ~6-12%/yr major economies, central ~7%, per Lyn Alden) — the floor itself; Choice of debasement measure: broad money/credit (~7%) vs CPI (~2-3%) vs interest-adjusted debasement (bond yield minus broad-money growth) — sets the floor level; Fiat half-life: time for purchasing-power to halve at the debasement rate (~10yr at 7%), the convex 'no bottom' framing; Credibility/fixity of the 21M cap as the non-dilutable numerator (the beta=1 assumption requires supply genuinely does not grow); Decaying adoption/monetization premium — the one-time S-curve repricing layered on top of the floor, which compresses toward zero as BTC's monetary share matures; Fiscal dominance / sovereign-debt growth as the reason debasement persists indefinitely ('fiat has no bottom'); Interest rates earned on fiat alternatives (if bonds pay >debasement, the relative case weakens — the practitioner caveat)


**Pros:** Anchors a cashflow-less asset to a real, measurable, persistent macro quantity (broad-money growth) that is far more stable and forecastable than price-trend extrapolation, S2F, or Metcalfe fits; Correctly uses the monetary-dilution measure (broad money ~7%) rather than CPI, capturing the denominator effect that CPI understates — a genuine analytical improvement over naive inflation-hedge framing; Naturally produces a DECAYING forward return: the durable floor (~7%) is modest and the adoption premium is explicitly transient, so unlike S2F/power-law it does not bake in perpetual triple-digit returns — the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA; Beta=1 minimalism is more defensible than the elasticity>1 (2.0-2.65) approaches: it avoids the spurious-regression trap of fitting a leveraged coefficient on two non-stationary trends; the floor is an accounting identity, not an estimated parameter; Portfolio-coherent with gold's debasement-hedge logic, so it slots BTC into a real-asset / debasement sleeve with a transparent, stress-testable single lever


**Cons:** The 'floor' is empirically NOT a floor: in early 2026 BTC fell ~16% YTD and ~32% over 12 months WHILE broad money kept growing — debasement continued but BTC dropped, directly falsifying the lower-bound claim over multi-year windows. It behaved as a high-beta risk asset, selling off into tightening, not as a debasement hedge; Source equivocation: the careful practitioners (Lyn Alden, Sam Callahan/Swan) actually argue RELATIVE outperformance vs bonds and warn 'valuations do matter… not an easy environment to gain real purchasing power' — they do NOT assert a literal absolute return floor. The hard 'no top/no bottom' floor is the maximalist crypto-native reading (Bitcoin Magazine sponsored post), which the underlying analysts stop short of; The beta=1 identity only holds if BTC's monetary share is constant; but share is volatile and can FALL (de-monetization), so the identity provides no floor on price in any finite window — only an asymptotic tendency that says nothing about a 10-15yr drawdown of 60-80%; Conflates flow (annual money growth ~7%) with a stock repricing: there is no arbitrage forcing BTC to track money growth year-by-year; the link is a narrative, not a no-arbitrage condition, so the 'floor' has no enforcement mechanism; The decaying-adoption-premium term is unmodeled — its size and decay path are pure assumption, so the whole excess-return estimate above the ~7% floor is judgmental, and the floor alone (~7%) may not even compensate for BTC's ~55-60% volatility (poor risk-adjusted floor); Silent on volatility and all correlations — a level/return-floor narrative only; every distributional CMA cell must be imported from realized data

CONSTRUCTION. The Debasement-CAGR / Fiat-Half-Life floor is the most minimalist member of the monetary-debasement family. Its load-bearing claim is an accounting identity rather than a regression: if the unit of account is diluted at rate d, an asset with a credibly non-dilutable supply must, over a long horizon, appreciate in that unit at least at d to hold constant real monetary share. The signature analytical move — due to Lyn Alden and echoed by Swan/Sam Callahan — is to measure d as TRUE monetary debasement (broad money + credit growth, ~6-12%/yr across major economies since 1960, central ~7%) rather than CPI (~2-3%). Alden's interest-adjusted-debasement metric (10y bond yield minus broad-money growth) ran ~-5% through the 2010s and spiked to ~-25% in 2020-21, illustrating how negative-real-monetary-yield regimes push capital into hard assets. The "fiat half-life" reframing (purchasing power halves in ~10yr at 7%) supplies the convex "fiat has no bottom" intuition popularized by the Bitcoin Magazine sponsored essay: because sovereign-debt dynamics make debasement perpetual, the denominator trends to zero, so a fixed-supply numerator has 'no top.'

DISTINCTNESS FROM #7 (M2 ELASTICITY). Both live in the monetary-substitution universe, but the mechanics differ sharply. The M2-elasticity approach estimates a cointegrating VECM with a leveraged long-run beta (~2.0-2.65: 1% money -> >2% BTC) and an error-correction pull to a money-implied fair value. The debasement-floor approach pins beta at 1 on the dilution channel (the identity), treats the raw ~7% broad-money rate as the floor, and pushes ALL excess return into a SEPARATELY decaying adoption/monetization premium. This is cleaner econometrically — it sidesteps the spurious-regression critique that plagues the leveraged-beta fits (regressing two non-stationary trends) — at the cost of being almost content-free as a return model: an identity that BTC 'should' trend with debasement enforces nothing in any finite window.

DECOMPOSITION FOR THE CMA. Expected nominal return = debasement floor (~7%, durable) + adoption premium (transient, S-curve, ->0). This produces the correct DECAY shape without the perpetual-triple-digit pathology of S2F/power-law. My synthesized central ~10-11% nominal / ~7-8% real sits below the trailing-5y realized 17% (the monetization premium is bleeding out) but above the bare floor while any adoption tailwind survives.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. The pure debasement-floor framework rarely publishes a clean annualized 10-15yr CMA — its proponents are deliberately vague ('no top'). The closest on-record numbers are: (i) Lyn Alden's input anchor (broad money 6-12%/yr, ~7% central), which implies a ~7% nominal floor; (ii) JPMorgan/Panigirtzoglou's debasement-trade work, but that is a $170k 6-12mo gold-equivalence tactical target (~+40%), explicitly NOT a structural long-horizon rate — repurposing it as a CMA is a category error; (iii) the Grayscale/Cerity/Relai 'debasement trade' commentaries, which assert directional tailwinds without annualized floors. So the family is rich in narrative, thin in dated multi-year point forecasts — itself a tell that the 'floor' resists falsification by staying unquantified.

FAILURE MODES (be brutal). The decisive one is empirical: in early 2026 BTC fell ~16% YTD and ~32% over 12 months WHILE broad money kept expanding. Debasement continued; the 'floor' did not hold. BTC sold off into tightening as a high-beta risk asset — the opposite of a debasement hedge. This is the textbook falsification: a multi-year window in which the asset went DOWN while the supposed driver went UP. Second, source equivocation: the careful practitioners (Alden, Callahan) actually argue RELATIVE outperformance vs bonds and warn explicitly that 'valuations matter' and real purchasing-power gains are 'not easy' — they stop short of the literal absolute floor that the maximalist Bitcoin-Magazine reading asserts. The hard floor is a crypto-native amplification the underlying analysts disown. Third, the identity only floors constant-share price; monetary share can FALL (de-monetization), so there is no enforcement and no bound on a 60-80% drawdown. Fourth, the ~7% floor is a poor risk-adjusted proposition against ~55-60% realized vol. Fifth, the shared-gold-driver logic is contradicted by the ~0 realized BTC-gold correlation and by gold holding while BTC fell in 2026 — the twin-hedge claim is asserted, not measured. Net: a conceptually appealing, denominator-aware improvement over CPI-based inflation-hedge framing, but as a CMA it supplies at most a soft ~7% nominal anchor plus a judgmental decaying premium, with no volatility/correlation content and a documented multi-year breach of its own floor.

</details>

### #17 · Narrative-Economics / Reflexivity Feedback-Loop (SIR Contagion + Garcia VAR)

*Family: narrative-reflexivity · Source: Academia · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 58*


**Explanation:** Bitcoin has no cashflows, so this school values the contagious STORY instead. Shiller (2019) models the 'Bitcoin narrative' as an epidemic: people are Susceptible, then Infected (believers), then Recovered/bored, governed by a contagion rate and a recovery rate. Like a disease, the believer share is hump-shaped — it rises, peaks when the susceptible pool thins, then decays — and crucially can RELAPSE in new waves (2013, 2017, 2021). Garcia et al. (2014) make the loop measurable: a VAR on price, social-media word-of-mouth, search and new users finds two self-reinforcing loops (word-of-mouth and new-user), quantifying Soros's reflexivity — price feeds attention feeds adoption feeds price. For a 10-15yr CMA the output is a SHAPE, not a number: each wave recruits a smaller pool of never-heard-of-it susceptibles, so peak amplitudes and trend appreciation DECAY while volatility stays high from the relapsing booms and busts. Inputs: contagion/recovery rates, the VAR feedback coefficients, and the shrinking susceptible reservoir. It rationalizes BTC's observed appreciation decay and persistent high vol better than scarcity models.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 4, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 4. Methodologically credible for SHAPE — the SIR/relapsing-wave structure is the cleanest mechanistic explanation for the appreciation decay (smaller susceptible pool each wave) and the persistent boom-bust vol the realized data shows, which is its strongest conditioning contribution. But it produces no native return level (all CMA numbers are bolted-on judgment), and its core inputs (social trace, word-of-mouth VAR calibrated on 2011-2013 data) are precisely what the ETF-era allocator buyer breaks, so it fails the regime-change and data-ops tests hardest. Signal is high on tails/cadence, low on level.*


**Key drivers:** Contagion (infection/transmission) rate of the Bitcoin narrative vs the recovery/forgetting rate — their ratio (an R0-like reproduction number) sets whether a fresh epidemic wave ignites and how high it peaks; Size of the remaining SUSCEPTIBLE pool — the stock of people who have not yet heard/adopted the story; it shrinks secularly across waves, so each successive epidemic is less explosive (the core decay mechanism); Reflexive feedback coefficients (Garcia VAR): price->search (~0.39), search->word-of-mouth (~0.24), word-of-mouth->price (~0.10); search->new-users (~0.16), new-users->price (~0.14) — the measured strength of the self-reinforcing loops; Word-of-mouth / social-media volume (Twitter mentions) as the contagion vector for the word-of-mouth loop; Search-volume (Google Trends) as both an attention amplifier and, per Garcia, an early WARNING — search spikes preceded large price DROPS; New-user / active-wallet growth as the adoption-loop vector (SIR variants map open wallets to the susceptible/infected pools); Recurring multi-year wave/relapse structure — narratives fade and re-ignite (mutate via new sub-stories: ETF, sovereign reserve, debasement), driving the boom-bust cadence rather than a smooth path; Exogenous shocks/triggers — crashes are attributed to outside stimuli the endogenous loop cannot self-predict (Garcia, Sornette-adjacent)


**Pros:** Directly explains the two BTC facts most CMA models can't: (a) the appreciation DECAY (each wave recruits a smaller susceptible pool, so peaks shrink) and (b) the persistent HIGH volatility / boom-bust cadence (relapsing epidemic waves) — the shape matches realized history without curve-fitting price on time; Empirically grounded and falsifiable, not numerology: Garcia et al. (peer-reviewed, J. R. Soc. Interface) actually MEASURE the feedback channels with a VAR, reconstruct price at rho=0.84, and correctly sign 9-10 of the 10 largest daily moves — real out-of-sample-ish content, and the search-spike-precedes-crash finding is a genuine leading indicator; Captures reflexivity/demand that supply-side models (S2F, cost-of-production) ignore entirely — price and belief are modeled as mutually endogenous (Soros), which is the actual driver of a no-cashflow speculative asset; Carries an Anthropic-grade pedigree (Shiller, Nobel laureate; Soros; ETH-Zurich complexity group) and a clear mechanism for why naive extrapolation fails — a useful skeptical counterweight to crypto-native hype models; Naturally produces a distribution with fat left tails and negative skew (waves end in busts), which is the right risk shape for portfolio construction even if the point return is imprecise


**Cons:** Produces NO native appreciation number. SIR/VAR describe the SHAPE and timing of waves, not a 10-15yr expected return; any CMA appreciation figure is bolted-on judgment about how fast peaks decay — the framework is silent on the level; Parameter instability and reverse causality: the contagion/recovery rates and VAR coefficients are estimated on short, regime-specific samples (Garcia's data is 2011-2013); Garcia himself cannot rule out price->wallet-creation (reverse causation), and the loops are calibrated pre-institutionalization. Post-ETF, the marginal buyer is an allocator who never tweets or opens a wallet, breaking the social-trace inputs; Crashes are exogenous by construction — both Garcia and the SIR setup attribute the bust to outside stimuli the model 'can provide no warning' for, so it cannot forecast the very drawdowns a long-horizon holder must survive (same blind spot as LPPLS); The proxies degrade over time: Twitter/X word-of-mouth, Google search, and on-chain wallet growth are increasingly noisy or gamed (bots, off-chain custody, ETF flows), so the contagion vectors that drove the 2011-2017 fits are weakening — the empirical engine is eroding precisely as the asset matures; Says nothing directly about cross-asset correlations or volatility-as-a-stat; those must be imported from realized data. It is a narrative-dynamics model, not a full distributional CMA; Risk of just-so storytelling: with enough sub-narratives (ETF, halving, debasement, AI-treasury) one can always claim a 'new wave' ex-post; the framework is more convincing as a descriptive lens than as a disciplined forward estimator

METHODOLOGY. This is a narrative-reflexivity family that fuses three strands. (1) Shiller's Narrative Economics (2019) imports the SIR epidemic model from epidemiology: a population is partitioned into Susceptible (haven't heard the BTC story), Infected (believers who spread it), and Recovered (heard it but no longer act on it / forgot). Transmission is governed by a contagion rate c and a recovery rate r; their ratio behaves like a basic reproduction number R0. The Infected share follows a hump-shaped curve — it rises while c-driven new infections outpace r-driven recoveries, peaks as the Susceptible pool thins, then declines. Critically, narratives can MUTATE and RELAPSE: a new sub-story (ETF, sovereign reserve, debasement hedge) re-infects the population, producing a fresh wave. Shiller's only explicit BTC claim is qualitative and visual — he overlays the Bitcoin price-attention run-up on the Ebola epidemic curve to argue the story, like a disease, follows an epidemic arc that ultimately decays. (2) Garcia, Tessone, Mavrodiev & Perony (2014, J. R. Soc. Interface) make the loop EMPIRICAL with a four-variable vector autoregression (VAR) on daily Bitcoin price, Twitter word-of-mouth (BTC tweets per million), Google search volume, and new-user/wallet growth. They identify two positive feedback loops in the absence of exogenous stimuli: a WORD-OF-MOUTH loop (price->search->word-of-mouth->price) and a NEW-USER loop (price->search->users->price), with estimated one-step coefficients price->search ~0.39, search->word-of-mouth ~0.24, word-of-mouth->price ~0.10, search->users ~0.16, users->price ~0.14. Impulse-response (10,000 bootstraps) shows search rises 2-4 days after price increases and word-of-mouth/users rise 1-2 days after search; the 4-day-lag VAR reconstructs price at rho=0.84 and correctly signs 9 or 10 of the 10 largest daily moves in their late sample. A notable asymmetry: large price DROPS are PRECEDED by search spikes — search is a leading bust indicator. (3) Soros (2014, J. Economic Methodology) supplies the philosophy: fallibility + reflexivity = the 'human uncertainty principle'; markets don't passively reflect fundamentals, they actively shape the beliefs and flows that become the fundamentals, so boom-bust loops are intrinsic, not anomalies.

CMA DERIVATION. No appreciation number falls out natively. The framework delivers a SHAPE: (a) appreciation DECAY, because each epidemic wave can only recruit from a shrinking pool of never-heard-of-it susceptibles, so peak amplitudes fall over time; (b) high, recurring VOLATILITY, because the relapsing-wave structure is intrinsically boom-bust; (c) negatively-skewed, fat-left-tailed returns, because waves end in exogenously-triggered busts the model cannot self-predict. To produce a CMA you must judgmentally map 'shrinking susceptible pool + weakening social-trace loops' onto a decay rate, then anchor to realized history. That yields my ~7-11% nominal / ~4-8% real, vol ~55-65%, equity-like correlations (~0.4-0.55 growth), and a gold correlation held near zero — because the contagion mechanism gives no debasement/safe-haven channel, only a risk-appetite/attention channel.

HISTORICAL FIT. The framework fits BTC's qualitative history well: the 2011, 2013, 2017 and 2021 cycles look like successive epidemic waves with declining log-amplitude, matching the realized 142%->65%->17%/yr decay. The Garcia VAR's in-sample sign accuracy is genuinely impressive for a social-data model.

FAILURE MODES / CRITIQUES (faithful). First, severe parameter instability and reverse causality: Garcia's data ends in 2013 and the authors cannot rule out price->wallet-creation; the loops are pre-institutional. Post-ETF, the marginal buyer is an allocator who never tweets or opens an on-chain wallet, so the contagion vectors (Twitter, search, wallets) are decoupling from the price they once drove. Second, crashes are EXOGENOUS by construction — the very drawdowns that determine a long-horizon holder's geometric return are outside the model's predictive reach. Third, just-so risk: with a steady supply of fresh sub-narratives one can always label a new wave ex-post, making the lens more descriptive than predictive. Fourth, the proxies are degrading (bots, off-chain custody, ETF flows). 

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None from the named primary authors — Shiller, Garcia and Soros deliberately avoid point price targets; Shiller's BTC commentary is famously skeptical (he has repeatedly called it a speculative bubble narrative, not endorsed a target). The closest empirical descendant, the 2024 'Do infectious diseases explain Bitcoin price fluctuations?' SIR study, forecasts active-WALLET counts (recovery rate from downtrends, infection rate from uptrends) to within ~3 days of price explosions and notes wallets correlate with price — but offers no 10-15yr appreciation figure. So the framework is best used as a SHAPE prior (decay + high vol + equity-correlation, gold-uncorrelated) and a skeptical check on monotone extrapolation, not as a source of a headline number.

</details>

### #18 · Equity-Beta-Implied / Public-Proxy-Implied Expected Return (Levered Nasdaq, MSTR mNAV, Miner NAV)

*Family: cross-asset-equity-implied · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 58*


**Explanation:** BTC has no cashflow, so the standard equity CMA blocks (CAPE, dividend yield, real GDP, buybacks) don't apply. This approach borrows the equity premium through beta. CAPM rearranged: E[BTC] = Rf + beta x ERP. BTC's realized beta to the Nasdaq-100 has been roughly 4.6 over the past decade (Sherwood), so naively E[BTC] = 4% + 4.6 x 5% ~ 27%/yr. But that beta is unstable (it went negative in 2025) and is structurally falling as ETFs, MSTR-style treasuries, and listed options institutionalize the asset. Decaying beta toward 1.5-2.5 lands the forward at ~11-16%; a further haircut for BTC's fat left tail / non-survivorship pushes the central case to ~8-12% nominal. The view is cross-checked against equities the market actually quotes on BTC: MSTR's +112% mNAV premium and miner NAV premia/discounts embed a market-implied forward BTC price, leverage, and vol. Implication for a 10-15yr CMA: a decaying-beta CAPM is one of the few frameworks that mechanically produces appreciation decay AND a high vol/high equity-correlation profile consistent with realized data.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 3, robustness 2, data-ops 4, orthogonality 3. Data-ops is strong: NDX beta, MSTR mNAV, and miner NAV are all liquid market-quoted series, easy to refresh in a CMA process.*

METHODOLOGY. Two coupled mechanisms. (1) CAPM-inverted equity beta. (2) Public-proxy / equity-market read. Rather than assume the beta, read it (and an embedded forward) off equities the market actually quotes on BTC. VanEck's Matthew Sigel ('Deconstructing Strategy', 2025) decomposes MSTR: a +112% mNAV premium to combined fair value of its BTC + software; the premium alone drives 96.56% of returns and 87.48% of vol and carries an 'approximate beta of 1.77 to BTC'; MSTR realized vol ~113% vs BTC ~55%. Critically Sigel states the premium reflects 'market expectations around Strategy's future Bitcoin holdings' decomposed into terminal BTC quantity x projected future BTC price x discount rate — i.e. the equity market is pricing an implied forward BTC view, which can be backed out. Bitcoin-miner equities (MARA, RIOT, CLSK, CIFR) give a second NAV-premium/discount read on embedded leverage.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The framework is internally consistent across CMA cells in a way scarcity/network models are not: a high-but-decaying beta simultaneously delivers (a) appreciation DECAY, (b) high realized vol (~55-60%), and (c) high, rising equity correlation (~0.55) — all matching the realized anchor (142->65->17%/yr; vol floor ~57%; equity corr rising; gold corr ~0). HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The beta is the Achilles heel. A CMA built on a number that changes sign is fragile; the decay-path assumption is unfalsifiable ex-ante. CAPM is also the wrong null for a fat-tailed, non-normal asset with large idiosyncratic risk (regulatory, custody, protocol) that CAPM ignores — so the single-equity-ERP it borrows is a category stretch, and the single-path realized beta cannot price BTC's catastrophic left tail. The proxies add reflexivity: MSTR's premium has ~1.77 beta to BTC, so reading a 'forward' off MSTR partly reads BTC's own price back to itself; miner NAVs are now muddied by HPC/AI-datacenter pivots (JPMorgan's late-2025 miner re-rating upgraded CLSK/CIFR on HPC, cut MARA/RIOT), decoupling them from pure BTC exposure. The academic anchor (Sanhaji & Chevallier, Econometrics 2023) validates that BTC's systematic beta is real, time-varying, and best measured with high-frequency 'realized' betas — but the authors frame it as a RISK-tracking (variance-explaining) tool for portfolio risk dashboards, NOT a device to invert into a forward expected return. That is the honest boundary: the literature supports measuring BTC's equity beta; inverting a dominant, unstable beta into a 10-15yr forward level is the practitioner's leap, not an academically blessed result.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. No firm publishes a clean CAPM-inverted 10-15yr BTC CMA. ### #19 · Rough Volatility (Fractional-Brownian RFSV) for Bitcoin

*Family: rough-volatility · Source: Academia · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 56*


**Explanation:** Rough volatility models Bitcoin's log-volatility as a fractional Brownian motion with a tiny Hurst exponent (H≈0.12-0.14 for BTC, vs ≈0.1 for equities). H<<0.5 means vol is strongly anti-persistent: shocks decay fast and the realized-vol path is jagged at every scale. The key inputs are the roughness index H (from how q-th moments of log-RV increments scale with lag), a vol-of-vol parameter, and a long-run vol level. The model's output is a TERM STRUCTURE of volatility and sharper realized-vol forecasts that beat AR/HAR — but it says NOTHING about expected return or correlation. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it is therefore a risk-only building block: it disciplines the volatility cell (and warns vol is mean-reverting around a high long-run level, not trending to zero), but appreciation and every cross-asset correlation must be borrowed from realized data. Its central caveat: Cont-Das and a 2025 BTC paper argue the measured 'roughness' may be a microstructure/estimation artifact, not a true property of spot vol — so even the one cell it informs is contested.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Methodologically sound and falsifiable (H is physically estimated, RFSV beats AR/HAR out-of-sample), but it is a risk-only block: silent on the decay-anchored return level and on the entire correlation row (gold/equity), so its 10-15yr CMA signal is low. Robustness is middling — fast mean-reversion to a high vol floor is genuinely regime-stable, but the measured roughness may be a microstructure/estimation artifact (Cont & Das), undercutting the one cell it informs. Data is cheap (daily RV from price) but operationally it touches only one cell.*


**Key drivers:** Hurst exponent H of log-volatility increments (≈0.12-0.14 for BTC realized vol per Takaishi 2020 / finite-sample work; ≈0.1 for equities per Gatheral et al.) — the single roughness parameter governing vol persistence and term structure; Vol-of-vol parameter ν (amplitude of the fractional-Brownian driver of log-vol); Long-run / unconditional volatility level toward which log-vol mean-reverts (the 'vol floor' the CMA inherits); Realized-volatility estimator and sampling frequency (5-min RV; the 1% finite-sample error band; choice of Δ materially shifts the apparent H); Multifractality of BTC log-vol: the generalized Hurst exponent is NOT constant across moment orders (Takaishi), which violates the single-H homogeneity assumption RFSV needs; Microstructure noise / spot-vol estimation error — the contested source of apparent roughness (Cont-Das 'fact or artefact'); Δ^{2H} scaling of the conditional log-vol forecast variance — drives the volatility term structure and the speed of mean reversion


**Pros:** Directly informs the one CMA cell it addresses — volatility — with a physically-estimated, falsifiable parameter (H) rather than an assumption; and the RFSV forecast empirically beats AR/HAR realized-vol forecasts (Gatheral et al.), so it has genuine out-of-sample skill on vol; Provides a TERM STRUCTURE of volatility and a fast-mean-reversion structure, which correctly implies that BTC's long-horizon average vol is anchored to a high unconditional level (a vol FLOOR) rather than drifting to zero — exactly the 'vol stays ~50-60%' shape a 10-15yr CMA needs; Estimated specifically on Bitcoin (Takaishi 2020; the 2025 finite-sample paper with H≈0.12-0.14; 'Cryptos have rough volatility and correlated jumps'), so it is not a blind transplant of an equity result; Explains a known statistical trap: RFSV-generated data LOOKS like long memory under classical tests even though it is not — so it warns against the competing long-memory/persistence family's spurious findings; Honest about scope: as a second-moment model it makes no over-reaching price-target claims (unlike S2F/Metcalfe/power-law), so it cannot be 'weaponized' into hype forecasts


**Cons:** Says NOTHING about expected return: RFSV is a pure volatility/risk process and produces no appreciation estimate at all — the most important CMA cell must be imported entirely from elsewhere, making it at best a partial building block; Says NOTHING about cross-asset correlation (growth/value equities, nominal FI, TIPS, gold) — the entire correlation row is silent, so it cannot inform the 'digital gold' axis or portfolio construction; The measured roughness may be a STATISTICAL ARTIFACT, not a real feature of spot volatility. Cont & Das (2022/2024) show realized vol ALWAYS looks rough (H<0.5) regardless of the true spot process, because microstructure noise and spot-vol estimation error manufacture apparent roughness — a frontal challenge to the whole approach; BTC-specific rejection: the 2025 paper 'Multifractality in Bitcoin Realized Volatility' (arXiv:2507.00575) could not even estimate a valid roughness index (the p-variation statistic stayed strictly negative) and concludes rough-vol models are 'structurally misaligned with the empirical features of Bitcoin volatility,' recommending multifractal random-walk / multifractal stochastic-vol models instead; Multifractality breaks the single-H assumption: Takaishi himself finds the generalized Hurst exponent is non-constant, so a single roughness number is a simplification of a richer, regime-dependent scaling — and H itself drifts with sampling frequency Δ; Even taken at face value it informs only volatility; it offers no view on the appreciation DECAY or the rising equity correlation that dominate a real BTC CMA

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Rough volatility begins with Gatheral, Jaisson & Rosenbaum (2018, Quantitative Finance; arXiv:1410.3394). Their empirical claim: across thousands of equity/index realized-vol series, the q-th absolute moments of log-vol increments scale as m(q,Δ)∝Δ^{qH} with H≈0.1 — far below the H=1/2 of a standard diffusion. They model log-volatility as a fractional Brownian motion with this small H (the RFSV model), where H<1/2 makes vol 'rough' / anti-persistent: it mean-reverts extremely fast and the path is jagged at every scale. Two consequences matter for a CMA. First, RFSV produces a TERM STRUCTURE of volatility: the conditional variance of future log-vol scales like Δ^{2H}, giving sharper realized-vol forecasts that beat AR and HAR benchmarks. Second — and decisively — RFSV is a model of the SECOND MOMENT only. It contains no drift on price, no expected-return parameter, and no cross-asset structure. It can populate the volatility cell of a CMA and nothing else.

BITCOIN ESTIMATES. Takaishi (2020, Finance Research Letters; arXiv:1904.12346) applies multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA) to Bitcoin log-volatility increments and finds the generalized Hurst exponent is below 1/2 — confirming rough, anti-persistent BTC vol. He adds a crucial wrinkle: the generalized Hurst exponent is NOT constant across moment orders, i.e. BTC log-vol is MULTIFRACTAL, with part of the multifractality coming from the fat-tailed distribution (revealed by shuffling). A 2025 finite-sample follow-up (arXiv:2511.03314, 'Multifractality and sample size influence on Bitcoin volatility patterns') sharpens the number: estimating H as Δ→0 via the ansatz H(Δ)=H₀·n/(n+a), it obtains H₀≈0.1262-0.1379 across three periods, with the parameter a≈3, and finds the 5-minute RV carries only ~1% relative error — concluding 5-min RV is adequate for H estimation. So the on-record BTC roughness index is H≈0.12-0.14, slightly above the equity ~0.1 but firmly 'rough.' The Digital Finance paper 'Cryptos have rough volatility and correlated jumps' (2025) corroborates roughness using 3+ years of 5-min data and adds that daily vol is best explained by roughness PLUS correlated jumps across cryptos.

KEY RELATIONSHIP TO A CMA. The model's honest contribution is the VOL FLOOR. Because rough vol mean-reverts very fast around a high unconditional level, the multi-year AVERAGE volatility is governed by that long-run level, not by the latest (possibly low) print. This is the cleanest theoretical case AGAINST the optimistic vol-compression theses (e.g. CF Benchmarks' ~28% terminal vol): fast anti-persistent reversion does not let vol drift to equity-like levels and stay there. It supports a 10-15yr vol band around realized ~55-60%. The model gives NO appreciation and NO correlation, which must be imported from the realized-decay baseline (nom 142%→65%→17%/yr; vol floor ~57%; equity corr rising to ~0.56; BTC-gold ~0).

FAILURE MODES / CRITIQUES (represented faithfully). (1) Roughness may be an ARTIFACT. Cont & Das, 'Rough volatility: fact or artefact?' (2022; arXiv:2203.13820) show via simulation that realized vol ALWAYS exhibits apparent H<0.5 regardless of the true spot-vol roughness — microstructure noise and spot-vol estimation error manufacture spurious roughness. Their follow-up filtering work (2024) reinforces that estimation error, not the volatility process, drives the H<0.5 finding. If true, the BTC H≈0.13 is measuring noise, not vol dynamics. (2) BTC-SPECIFIC REJECTION. The seed paper 'Multifractality in Bitcoin Realized Volatility: Implications for Rough Volatility Modelling' (2025; arXiv:2507.00575), using Bitstamp 1-min data 2017-2024, could NOT estimate a valid roughness index at all — the normalized p-variation statistic stayed strictly negative (max < -0.009) across all years and frequencies — and concludes rough-vol models are 'structurally misaligned with the empirical features of Bitcoin volatility,' recommending Multifractal Random Walk / Multifractal Stochastic Volatility instead. (3) MULTIFRACTALITY breaks the single-H homogeneity assumption RFSV needs (Takaishi's own non-constant generalized-Hurst result; the 2025 paper's spectral widths 0.06-0.42). (4) H drifts with sampling frequency, so the 'law' is not shift-invariant.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is a defining feature: the rough-volatility literature publishes NO multi-year price forecasts, NO appreciation targets, and NO correlation projections. It is exclusively a second-moment estimation exercise. Any practitioner who attaches a return path to it is bolting an external assumption onto a pure vol model. For our CMA the appropriate use is narrow and defensible: cite rough vol as theoretical support for a HIGH, MEAN-REVERTING volatility floor (~55-60% over 10-15yr, arguing against rapid compression), discount that support modestly for the artifact critique, and import every other cell from the realized-decay baseline.

</details>

### #20 · Agent-Based / Sociophysics Generative Market (Chartist-Fundamentalist, Percolation, Ising/SOC)

*Family: agent-based-generative · Source: Academia · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 56*


**Explanation:** This family asks the opposite question from every reduced-form BTC model: not "what equation fits price?" but "what minimal set of interacting agents makes the real return distribution appear by itself?" You simulate noise traders, chartists, and fundamentalists on an order book (Cocco-Marchesi for Bitcoin), or binary buy/sell 'spins' coupled locally and to global sentiment (Bornholdt's Ising market), or random percolation clusters of agents who trade as a herd (Cont-Bouchaud), and the macro stylized facts — truncated power-law tails (cumulative exponent ~2.9-3, the empirical "inverse-cubic" range), volatility clustering, and crashes — emerge endogenously. A single control parameter (social-coupling strength, per-cluster trade probability near the percolation threshold, or Ising temperature) tunes the system toward criticality, where bubbles and crashes self-organize. For a BTC CMA the key implication is humbling: these models target the distribution's higher moments (vol, kurtosis, tail, crash hazard), not its drift. They robustly justify a high vol floor and a fat left tail, but produce no native appreciation number and, being single-asset, no cross-asset correlations.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 4, data-ops 2, orthogonality 4. Mechanistically rigorous and peer-validated (Cocco-Marchesi reproduces BTC's return CDF and vol clustering from micro-interaction), and regime-robust because it derives tails/crashes from criticality rather than fitting halving-cycle artifacts. But it is silent on the CMA's central cell — drift — and on all cross-asset correlations, so its predictive signal for a 10-15yr appreciation/correlation matrix is weak. Severe identification problem and bespoke simulation/calibration make it operationally heavy for a CMA process; its real value is conditioning the vol floor and left-tail, not levels.*


**Key drivers:** Social-coupling / herding strength — the master control parameter (Ising coupling J, Cont-Bouchaud cluster trade probability a, sentiment-feedback gain) that tunes proximity to a critical point where power-law tails and crashes emerge; Agent-type mix and switching: relative populations of random/noise traders, chartists (trend-followers/momentum) and fundamentalists, and the endogenous switching between them that drives alternating-dominance cycles, bubbles and reversals; Network/lattice topology of who-influences-whom (regular lattice, scale-free, random percolation graph) — sets cluster-size distribution and how herds form; Proximity to the percolation threshold p_c / critical temperature T_c — the order parameter governing whether the market is in a disordered (Gaussian-ish) or ordered (herded, fat-tailed, crash-prone) phase; Self-organized-criticality feedback (margin calls / forced liquidations / leverage avalanches) that drives the system back to the critical state, producing scale-invariant avalanche (drawdown) sizes; Order-book / market-clearing microstructure and finite agent wealth/inventory constraints, which truncate the power law and shape realized volatility; Exogenous supply schedule (issuance/mining) entered only as a slow drift in coin count — NOT as a fitted appreciation driver


**Pros:** Only family in the set that DERIVES BTC's stylized facts endogenously — fat tails, volatility clustering, and crashes fall out of micro-interaction rather than being assumed or curve-fit, giving a genuine mechanism for the ~50-60% vol floor and heavy left tail a CMA needs; Provides a principled, mechanistic account of crash/bubble hazard via a tunable criticality parameter — directly relevant to sizing the drawdown risk a 10-15yr BTC holder must survive, which most reduced-form models ignore; Cocco-Marchesi (2017) demonstrably reproduces real Bitcoin statistical properties (autocorrelation of absolute returns, the return CDF) from a simple two-agent design — a real, peer-reviewed validation on BTC specifically, not just equities; Falsifiable on distributional grounds: the emergent tail exponent, vol-clustering decay, and crash-size distribution can be checked against realized BTC data (Cont-Bouchaud cumulative tail ~2.9-3 matches the empirical inverse-cubic law); Naturally accommodates regime change / structural breaks (ETF entry, leverage build-up) by changing agent populations or coupling — more flexible than a single fixed regression coefficient


**Cons:** Silent on appreciation — the CMA's single most important cell. These models target the return-distribution SHAPE (higher moments), not the drift; Cocco-Marchesi enters supply growth but does not output an expected-return path. Any 10-15yr appreciation number is bolted on from outside the framework.; Silent on cross-asset correlations — they are single-asset, closed-economy simulations of one order book / one lattice, so they say nothing about BTC vs growth equities, value, nominal FI, TIPS or gold. All correlation cells are n/a.; Severe calibration/identification problem: many free parameters (agent counts, coupling, switching rates, network topology) map to the same handful of stylized facts, so the model is badly under-identified — multiple very different parameter sets reproduce the same fat tails. INET-Oxford/PLOS work flags the absence of reliable operational calibration and weak out-of-sample validation as the field's central methodological weakness.; Stylized-fact matching is necessary but not sufficient: reproducing fat tails and vol clustering does NOT validate a model's forward predictions; some literature finds even those facts are hard to recover robustly under calibration, and the models are routinely critiqued as flexible enough to be near-unfalsifiable on dynamics.; Essentially never used to produce on-record multi-year BTC price/return forecasts — the family is explanatory/generative, not a desk forecasting tool. Repurposing it as a CMA point estimate is a category error.; Criticality/SOC claims for markets are contested: 'scale-invariant avalanche' findings are sensitive to estimation choices and have been challenged (the general critique that financial criticality is partly a fitting artifact), so the crash-hazard mechanism, while suggestive, is not settled science.

EPISTEMOLOGY (why this is genuinely distinct). The other 20 BTC-CMA approaches are reduced-form: they posit a driver (stock-to-flow, M2, active addresses, mining cost, time-since-genesis, an option surface) and fit price to it. This family inverts the logic. It specifies the MICRO rules of heterogeneous interacting agents and lets the MACRO return distribution — fat tails, volatility clustering, bubbles, crashes — emerge as a collective phenomenon. None of the reduced-form models derive the stylized facts; here they are the output. The unifying thread across the four canonical lineages is a tunable social-coupling control parameter that pushes the system toward a critical point, at which power-law tails and crash onset appear endogenously.\n\nTHE FOUR LINEAGES. (1) Order-book ABM — Cocco, Concas & Marchesi (2017, J. Econ. Interaction & Coordination), the first ABM built specifically for Bitcoin: random traders + chartists on an order book, supply growing at the real issuance rate. It reproduces BTC's autocorrelation of absolute returns and the return CDF. The 2019 IEEE Access extension adds mining and a fundamentalist class. (2) Percolation/herd — Cont & Bouchaud (2000, Macroeconomic Dynamics): random communication clusters of agents trade together; at/near the percolation threshold p_c the return distribution becomes an exponentially-truncated power law with cumulative tail exponent ~2.9-3, squarely in the empirical 'inverse-cubic' range, with the per-cluster trade probability a as control knob. (3) Ising/spin opinion dynamics — Bornholdt (2001, IJMPC): binary buy/sell spins with ferromagnetic local coupling FRUSTRATED against an anti-ferromagnetic coupling to global magnetization; this frustration produces metastable states, intermittency, power-law returns and clustered volatility. Sznajd and scale-free-network variants extend it. (4) Self-organized criticality — Bak, Tang & Wiesenfeld (1987, PRL): the sandpile that self-tunes to a critical state emitting power-law avalanches; applied to markets, leverage/margin-call cascades give scale-invariant drawdown sizes.\n\nWHAT IT DELIVERS FOR A BTC CMA — AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The honest, load-bearing point: this family is a DISTRIBUTION-SHAPE engine, not a drift engine. It legitimately informs the higher moments a CMA needs — a high, persistent volatility (vol clustering does not switch off with maturity), a fat LEFT tail, and an explicit crash/bubble hazard mechanism via criticality. It is the best mechanistic justification in the whole survey for refusing to compress BTC vol to equity-like levels and for treating the median 10-15yr outcome as well below the mean. But it is SILENT on appreciation (Cocco-Marchesi enters supply growth without forecasting return) and, being single-asset closed-economy simulations, SILENT on every cross-asset correlation. So appreciation (~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real) and correlations are imported from the realized-decay baseline and cross-approach central, NOT derived here.\n\nFAILURE MODES / SKEPTICAL READ. Calibration and identification are the Achilles heel: many free parameters (agent counts, coupling strength, switching rates, topology) collapse onto the same few stylized facts, so the models are badly under-identified — wildly different parameter sets reproduce the same tails. The INET-Oxford calibration-methods survey and the PLOS One 'Calibrating emergent phenomena' work both flag the absence of reliable operational calibration and weak out-of-sample validation as the field's defining weakness; some find even fat tails / sufficient kurtosis hard to recover robustly under calibration. Reproducing stylized facts is necessary but not sufficient — it does not validate forward dynamics, and critics reasonably call the family near-unfalsifiable on dynamics. The SOC/criticality-in-markets claim is itself contested ('scale-invariant avalanche' findings are estimation-sensitive and have been challenged as partly artifactual). ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS: essentially NONE. Unlike S2F ($288k-$500k+), Metcalfe ($1.5M/2035) or power-law-time ($1M/2037), the ABM/sociophysics literature does not publish dated multi-year BTC price targets — it is explanatory/generative, not a forecasting desk. That absence is itself the verdict: this family belongs in a BTC CMA as the source of the vol floor, fat-tail, and crash-hazard assumptions, NOT as the source of the central appreciation or correlation numbers.

</details>

### #21 · Fiscal-Theory-of-the-Price-Level / Fiscal-Dominance Hard-Asset Bid

*Family: monetary-macro-fiscal · Source: Academia · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 55*


**Explanation:** FTPL determines the price level from the government's budget identity: real debt = present value of primary surpluses. Run structural deficits with no credible path to surpluses and the price level must rise to inflate away nominal debt — a fiscal, not monetary, source of inflation. The fiscal-dominance overlay says deficit spending is now the primary liquidity engine; with no commodity supply constraint, that liquidity bids up scarce assets including Bitcoin, which is valued as a leveraged debasement claim (BTC tracks global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows). The distinctive twist is non-monotone: the same intractable deficits force heavy Treasury issuance that lifts long real yields and term premium, raising the opportunity cost of a yieldless asset and pressuring BTC even while the Fed cuts. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this nets a persistent debasement tailwind against an episodic real-rate headwind — implying low-double-digit nominal appreciation (decaying), high but not declining volatility, a rising equity correlation, and — unlike pure debasement framings — a meaningful positive sensitivity to TIPS/real yields rather than a clean gold proxy.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 4, data-ops 2, orthogonality 4. Core FTPL is peer-reviewed and structurally derived rather than fitted, but contested on identification, hence rigor 4 not 5. Predictive signal for a 10-15yr BTC level is weak: it emits no native appreciation number and launders an assumed liquidity beta, so the level forecast is analyst prior, not output. Its real value is conditioning — the non-monotone debasement-vs-issuance framing and sovereign-solvency lens survive halving/S2F/ETF regime breaks well (robustness 4). Operationally it needs fiscal/issuance modeling plus a judgment-set BTC beta, so it is not a clean drop-in CMA pipeline.*


**Key drivers:** Fiscal balance / primary surplus path — the FTPL valuation anchor: real debt = PV(primary surpluses); deteriorating surplus expectations devalue nominal debt and bid hard assets; Fiscal dominance regime — deficit spending exceeding private credit creation as the dominant liquidity driver (Alden/Callahan); interest payments on a large debt stock act as stimulus, so rate hikes can be inflationary not contractionary; Treasury issuance volume and maturity mix — heavy long-dated supply raises term premium and long real yields (KC Fed 2025: debt/GDP expansion lifts 5-10yr yields), the bearish leg; Long-term real yields / term premium — the opportunity-cost channel: higher real yields on guaranteed govt bonds compress the risk premium available to a non-yielding BTC; Global liquidity impulse — BTC as a high-beta liquidity barometer (83% directional hit rate over 12m); the bullish transmission of fiscal deficits into asset prices; Monetary-fiscal divergence — Fed easing (QE/buyer-of-last-resort) vs Treasury issuance; the net of the two determines whether the liquidity bid or the real-yield headwind dominates; Inflation vs real-yield split — whether fiscal stress shows up as inflation (FTPL price-level jump, BTC-bullish debasement) or as higher real yields/term premium (BTC-bearish), which is regime-dependent and the crux of the non-monotone view


**Pros:** Theoretically rigorous and peer-reviewed at the core: Cochrane's FTPL (Princeton UP, 2023) and the continuous-time stochastic GE formalization (arXiv 2403.01593) give a real macro foundation, not a fitted price curve — it cannot be dismissed as spurious S2F/Metcalfe numerology; Genuinely distinct from existing monetary rows: it endogenizes the price level via the fiscal budget rather than treating money supply as exogenous (rows #7/#8), and it is the only framing that models the fiscal-vs-monetary DIVERGENCE and reframes BTC's real-yield sensitivity through a sovereign-solvency lens; Non-monotone realism: by pairing a bullish debasement/liquidity leg with a bearish issuance/real-yield leg, it explains episodes (e.g. 2022 and high-yield 2025-26 regimes) where BTC fell DESPITE worsening fiscal deficits — something pure debasement/M2 models cannot accommodate; Empirically anchored bullish channel: BTC's ~83% directional co-movement with global liquidity over 12-month windows (Alden/Callahan) is among the strongest macro relationships for any asset class, lending the liquidity leg real signal; Correctly predicts the empirically observed TIPS/real-yield linkage: because the framework explicitly routes BTC through the real-yield/term-premium channel, it accommodates BTC's measured positive TIPS correlation (~0.30 trailing-5y) rather than asserting a gold proxy the data rejects


**Cons:** FTPL itself is contested: prominent economists (Buiter, McCallum) dispute its causal mechanism and identification (the budget identity holds under any theory of the price level, so attributing causation to fiscal policy is debated); the empirical FTPL literature is far from settled; Indeterminate as a CMA: the framework produces no native long-horizon BTC appreciation number. The output depends entirely on (a) how much of fiscal stress shows up as inflation vs real yields and (b) an assumed BTC liquidity beta — both analyst inputs, so the CMA launders a prior rather than generating a forecast; The two legs can offset to near-zero and the sign is regime-dependent: Cochrane's own mechanism is primarily INFLATIONARY (debt eroded by a price-level jump, not sustained higher real yields), whereas the bearish BTC leg requires the real-yield/term-premium channel to dominate — the framework does not pin which prevails over 10-15yr; Practitioner sources carry a long book and are not peer-reviewed: Alden/Callahan and the crypto-desk commentary are advocacy-adjacent (hard-asset thesis), and the 'liquidity flows into BTC' transmission is asserted from a short, bull-dominated sample that breaks down in shorter windows and at valuation extremes (their own caveat); Reflexivity/circularity in the bullish leg: 'fiscal dominance bids hard assets' is partly a restatement of the post-2020 regime in which both deficits and BTC rose together; isolating fiscal causation from the shared risk-appetite/liquidity driver is not established; Silent on volatility and most correlations as published numbers — vol, growth/value-equity, nominal-FI and gold co-movements must all be imported from realized data; the framework constrains only the appreciation sign and the real-yield linkage

Cochrane (grumpy-economist Substack) (2023) https://www.grumpy-economist.com/p/fiscal-theory-parables; CCN (Crypto education) (2026) https://www.ccn.com/education/crypto/bitcoin-traders-fed-rate-cuts-2026-fiscal-policy-risk-explained/


<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This approach has two layers that must be kept distinct. (1) The ACADEMIC core — Cochrane's Fiscal Theory of the Price Level (Princeton UP, 2023; 'Fiscal Theory Parables', 2023) and its continuous-time stochastic GE formalization (arXiv:2403.01593, 2024) — replaces the quantity theory's money-supply determinant with the government's intertemporal budget identity: the real value of nominal debt equals the present value of expected future primary surpluses, and the price level adjusts (like a stock price to its dividend stream) to enforce that equality. Cochrane's 'Twin Parables': debt issued WITH credible surpluses is non-inflationary (like equity with dividend promises); debt issued WITHOUT surplus credibility forces a one-time price-level JUMP that inflates the real debt away, plus higher nominal rates. Crucially, Cochrane's first-order mechanism is INFLATIONARY (real debt eroded by a price-level jump), not a sustained real-yield increase. (2) The PRACTITIONER overlay — Alden/Callahan's 'Full Steam Ahead: All Aboard Fiscal Dominance' (2025) and 'Bitcoin: A Global Liquidity Barometer' (2024) — argues that under fiscal dominance, deficit spending exceeds private credit creation as the dominant liquidity engine, that interest payments on a large debt stock make rate HIKES stimulative (widening deficits, keeping inflation elevated), and that absent commodity supply constraints this liquidity bids up scarce hard assets 'stocks, real estate, gold, and bitcoin.' BTC is the highest-beta, purest such claim (no earnings/dividends to confound it), tracking global liquidity ~83% of 12-month and ~74% of 6-month windows — the strongest such relationship among major assets.\n\nKEY RELATIONSHIP / WHY DISTINCT. The framework is genuinely non-monotone, which is its analytic contribution and the reason it is distinct from the existing M2-elasticity (#7) and quantity-theory (#8) rows that make money supply exogenous and monotone-bullish on debasement. Here, the SAME fiscal dominance that supplies the bullish debasement/liquidity bid also forces heavy Treasury issuance. The Kansas City Fed (2025) finds debt/GDP-raising Treasury supply lifts yields across maturities and raises the term premium, pronounced at 5-10yr. That raises long-term REAL yields, and — per the practitioner desk view ('Bitcoin's hard-money thesis is colliding with 5% Treasury yields', 2025; CCN 2026) — an allocator who can lock 5% guaranteed on a 30yr bond faces a higher opportunity cost of holding yieldless BTC. So BTC can FALL despite worsening deficits (observed 2022, and in high-yield 2025-26 episodes), which pure debasement models cannot explain. The crux for a CMA: whether fiscal stress manifests as INFLATION (FTPL price-level jump, BTC-bullish) or as higher REAL YIELDS/term premium (BTC-bearish) is regime-dependent and the framework does not pin it over 10-15yr. The honest net is a structural debasement tailwind minus an episodic real-rate headwind.\n\nHISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The bullish leg fits the 2020-2021 and 2023-2024 liquidity-expansion regimes well, and the 83% liquidity hit-rate is real signal. The bearish leg fits 2022 (BTC fell with bonds as real yields surged) and the 2025-26 high-yield collisions. Failure modes: (a) FTPL is contested at the source — Buiter and McCallum dispute its causal identification, since the budget identity holds under any price-level theory; attributing causation to fiscal policy is a modeling choice. (b) The two legs can offset to near-zero, and the framework cannot sign the net over a decade. (c) The practitioner transmission ('liquidity flows into BTC') is from a short, bull-dominated sample and is partly a restatement of the post-2020 co-movement of deficits and BTC, with the shared risk-appetite driver not cleanly separated (reflexivity). (d) Sources are advocacy-adjacent with a long book.\n\nON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. No firm publishes a quantitative 10-15yr BTC CMA from this framework. The strongest on-record statements are Alden's: she expects 'very large fiscal deficits to continue' for 'the next ten years' and BTC to 'finish higher,' with new highs above $100k in the 2026 cycle — but explicitly with a LOWER trajectory than before ('Before all this tariff kerfuffle, I would have had a higher price target') and 'slowing returns' as cycles tie to macro/liquidity rather than halvings. This is a decaying-appreciation, regime-conditioned view, NOT a fixed CAGR — which is the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA and supports a low-double-digit nominal anchor.\n\nCMA TRANSLATION. I synthesize ~9-12% nominal / ~6-9% real, vol ~55-60%, growth-eq ~0.45, value-eq ~0.30, nominal-FI ~0.10 (with a regime-dependent NEGATIVE beta during duration sell-offs), TIPS ~0.30 (the framework's signature high-real-yield-sensitivity cell), gold ~0.12. The distinctive output vs every gold-proxy/debasement row is that this framework predicts BTC's positive TIPS/real-yield sensitivity and adverse issuance-regime behavior rather than a clean gold linkage — and the realized data (TIPS 0.30, gold ~0) corroborates that read.
