### #30 · Options-Implied Risk-Neutral Forward & Vol Surface (Deribit DVOL / RND)

*Family: options-implied · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Conditioning overlay · Overall 51*


**Explanation:** This approach reads BTC's listed-options market rather than its price history. From the cross-section of strikes, Breeden-Litzenberger recovers a risk-neutral density of the terminal price; from the term structure (distilled into Deribit's 30-day DVOL index) you read the market's annualized volatility expectation. Its decisive limitation: under the risk-neutral (Q) measure the forward equals spot times cost-of-carry, so the drift is the financing rate, NOT a real-world expected return. The options surface therefore delivers a best-in-class volatility input and a no-arbitrage forward but is silent on 10-15yr appreciation. A return only emerges by grafting a pricing-kernel/P-density step onto it: Grith-Almeida-Miftachov (arXiv 2410.15195) recover an option-implied physical premium of ~66%/yr (Martin lower bound 65.6%, Chabi-Yo-Loudis 84.8%) — but only at a 27-day horizon on 2017-2022 data, a pre-ETF high-premium regime. For a CMA: trust it for vol (~55-60%, floored at realized ~57%); decay the stale short-dated premium hard for horizon and maturation to ~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real. It yields no cross-asset correlations.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 2, orthogonality 3. No-arbitrage RND/DVOL is methodologically clean and best-in-class for the vol and tail inputs, but under Q it drifts at the funding rate and is structurally silent on 10-15yr appreciation — the central CMA output must be imported, capping signal. Robustness is moderate: forward-looking and not sample-dependent, but liquid options end at ~6-13mo, so the long-horizon term structure is extrapolated, not observed. Data_ops suffers from no long-dated surface and the need to graft a separate P-measure kernel.*


**Key drivers:** Implied volatility surface (level, skew, term structure) across Deribit/CME strikes and expiries; Risk-neutral forward = spot x cost-of-carry (futures basis / perpetual funding rate); the Q-drift is the risk-free/financing rate, not expected return; Risk-neutral density (RND) shape from the second derivative of call prices vs strike (Breeden-Litzenberger) — fat right tail, lognormal-plus-jump; Variance risk premium: gap between implied (Q) and realized (P) variance, the wedge that must be modeled to get from price to physical return; Pricing kernel / risk-aversion needed to convert Q-density to P-density and thus recover an expected return (Almeida-Grith-Miftachov; Martin lower bound); Option liquidity and longest-available tenor — caps the horizon at which the surface is observable (months, not years)


**Pros:** Purely market-implied and forward-looking: aggregates the positioning of sophisticated option traders in real time, no backward-looking sample dependence; Best-in-class for the VOLATILITY input of a CMA — DVOL and the term structure give a clean, daily, tradeable estimate of expected vol, far better grounded than a historical stdev; No-arbitrage discipline: the forward and RND are internally consistent and replicable, immune to the spurious-regression problems that plague S2F/Metcalfe; Captures the full distribution (skew, kurtosis, crash risk), not just a point — useful for tail-aware / left-tail CMA scenario work; The RND-vs-realized comparison yields a defensible variance risk premium and, with a pricing-kernel assumption, an option-implied expected-return lower bound (Almeida et al. ~66%/yr at 1mo; Martin bound 65.6%) — a genuinely market-anchored premium number; Galaxy and desks use it precisely as a 'maturing into a macro asset' read: the surface's flattening/declining vol IS the decay signal a forward CMA needs


**Cons:** Fundamentally cannot produce an expected appreciation. The risk-neutral forward drifts at the risk-free/funding rate by construction; equating that to a CMA return implies ~0% real appreciation, which is economically wrong for the asset. Any appreciation figure must be imported from a separate model — the options surface is silent on drift. This is the central, disqualifying limitation for a return CMA.; Horizon mismatch is severe: liquid BTC options extend ~6 months (Deribit) to ~12-13 months (CME, through next December); there is NO 10-15yr option. Extrapolating a 30-day DVOL or a 6-month surface to a 10-15yr CMA is a heroic, unvalidated stretch — the term structure is estimated, not observed, at the relevant horizon.; The P-density / pricing-kernel step that rescues an expected return is fragile: estimates swing from ~44% to ~102%/yr across vol regimes (Almeida-Grith-Miftachov), are only 27-day horizon, and assume the short-dated risk premium persists — exactly the assumption a maturing-asset CMA should reject.; Variance risk premium is large and time-varying (1mo VRP collapsed from ~15% to ~2.5% around the 2024 halving), so even the vol read is regime-dependent and can overstate forward vol.; Risk-neutral != physical: short-dated RNDs are dominated by hedging/skew demand and crash insurance, not long-run fundamentals — using them as a 10yr distribution conflates options demand with macro expectation.; Liquidity/venue concentration (Deribit dominant, now Coinbase-owned) and thin deep-OTM long-dated strikes make the long end of any extrapolated surface noisy and manipulable.; Marketing risk: 'options imply $250k' headlines (Galaxy 2026) are wide risk-neutral ranges, NOT directional forecasts; the same surface assigns near-equal odds to $50k and $250k by end-2026. Treating the high tail as an expected value launders a vol read into a return claim.

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. The options-implied family has two distinct deliverables and it is essential not to conflate them: (1) the risk-neutral forward, which by no-arbitrage equals spot x cost-of-carry — i.e. the futures price / perpetual-funding-implied forward — and whose drift under Q is the risk-free/financing rate, NOT a real-world expected return; and (2) the implied-volatility surface, distilled by Deribit's DVOL into a single VIX-style 30-day annualized vol via variance-swap replication (select two expiries bracketing 30 days, build the smile from order-book depth of 2 BTC across 5 levels, discard ITM and sub-5%-delta wings, interpolate, EMA-smooth over 240 ticks). DVOL=90 => expected daily move ~4.5% (DVOL/sqrt(365)). The surface also yields a full risk-neutral density via Breeden-Litzenberger (second derivative of call price wrt strike); Hou/Hardle et al. (2019, arXiv:1901.04770) and the peer-reviewed Hou et al. (JFE 2020, SVCJ stochastic-vol-with-jumps) and Cao & Celik (Financial Innovation 2021) formalize this.

THE CENTRAL PROBLEM FOR A RETURN CMA. Options price risk, not direction. The risk-neutral measure embeds the market price of risk, so the Q-density's mean is the forward (carry), and the entire premium an investor actually earns is the Q-to-P wedge — invisible in option prices without an external pricing-kernel/risk-aversion assumption. Therefore THIS APPROACH CANNOT, BY CONSTRUCTION, OUTPUT AN EXPECTED APPRECIATION. Any 'options imply X% return' claim is either (a) reading the upper tail of a wide risk-neutral range as an expectation (the Galaxy 2026 '$250k' headline — the SAME surface assigns near-equal odds to ~$50k and ~$250k by EOY 2026, and Galaxy itself calls 2026 'too chaotic to call' and frames the $250k-by-2027 number as a SEPARATE, non-options long-run view), or (b) smuggling in a P-density from a different estimator.

THE ONE LEGITIMATE RETURN SIGNAL — and its limits. Almeida, Grith & Miftachov (2024, arXiv:2410.15195) do the honest thing: they estimate the Q-density from options (SVI vol surface -> RND) AND a P-density from realized returns, and back out the physical premium. They report a Bitcoin Premium averaging ~66%/yr, option-based lower bounds of 65.6% (Martin) and 84.8% (Chabi-Yo & Loudis), a variance risk premium ~14%, and a Sharpe ~0.8 (≈2x S&P). BUT every one of these is a 27-DAY HORIZON number on monthly options (3-120 days), and it swings from ~44% (low-vol regime) to ~102% (high-vol regime). Extrapolating a one-month, regime-conditional risk premium to a 10-15yr CMA is precisely the error a maturing-asset CMA must avoid. The variance risk premium is also unstable — Bitfinex/desk data show 1-month VRP collapsing from ~15% to ~2.5% around the April 2024 halving.

HORIZON MISMATCH. Liquid BTC options reach ~6 months on Deribit and ~12-13 months on CME (six consecutive months plus two December contracts, so through next December). There is no multi-year option; a 10-15yr CMA horizon is 10-20x beyond the observable surface. The long end of any extrapolated term structure is unobserved, thin in deep-OTM long-dated strikes, and venue-concentrated (Deribit dominant, now Coinbase-owned). So the 'CMA' is an extrapolation, not a measurement.

WHAT IT IS ACTUALLY GOOD FOR IN A CMA. The volatility input. DVOL and the term structure are the best available forward vol estimate and far superior to a historical stdev. The realized-vs-implied comparison (BVIX^2 ~0.72 risk-neutral vs BRV ~0.58 realized annual variance in Almeida et al.) gives a defensible VRP. And the surface's flattening / declining DVOL over time is itself the maturation/decay signal a forward CMA wants — Galaxy frames exactly this: 'options pricing and volatility trends indicate bitcoin is maturing into a more macro-like asset rather than a high-growth trade.'

MY SYNTHESIS LOGIC. For appreciation I refuse to report the carry-rate forward as a 'return' (that would imply ~0% real, absurd as a CMA). Instead I take the family's only honest return artifact — the option-implied physical premium — and apply the empirical-anchor decay (full-window 142% -> 10y 65% -> 5y 17% nominal) projected forward, landing ~10% nominal / ~7% real as a 10-15yr center. This is explicitly a judgment overlay, NOT an options output. For volatility I extrapolate the declining DVOL/term-structure to ~50% (below the 57% trailing-5y realized, far above equities). Correlations are NOT producible from a single-asset options surface at all, so all five are pure judgments anchored to the trailing-5y realized matrix with mild mean-reversion: growth-eq ~0.45, value-eq ~0.30, FI ~0.15, TIPS ~0.20, gold ~0.10 (realized gold corr has been ~0.03-0.05, near zero; the digital-gold co-movement the thesis wants simply is not in the data, and the options approach is silent on it).

BOTTOM LINE. As a CMA method, options-implied is the gold standard for the VOL and tail inputs and a disciplined source for a SHORT-HORIZON risk premium, but it is structurally incapable of delivering a 10-15yr expected appreciation or any cross-asset correlation. Used alone it would force a near-0% real return CMA; used as headline-tail readings it launders a vol signal into a fake forecast. Its proper role is to supply the volatility/distribution leg of a CMA whose return leg comes from a different (e.g. stock-to-flow-rejected, demand-adoption, or building-block-premium) model.

</details>

### #31 · Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge

*Family: monetary-substitution · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 50*


**Explanation:** This approach values Bitcoin as a high-beta claim on fiat money growth rather than on cashflows. Empirically, log BTC price and log broad money (US M2 or a synthetic global M2) are each non-stationary I(1) and appear cointegrated, with an estimated long-run elasticity near 2.65 (a 1% rise in M2 maps to ~2.65% in BTC) and a VECM error-correction term of about -0.12/month pulling price back to a money-implied fair value over a ~6-month half-life. The CMA is built mechanically: forecast trend money growth (~7-8%/yr global), multiply by a forward elasticity that must be decayed from ~2.0 toward gold-like ~1.1-1.5, and that product is expected nominal appreciation; the debasement thesis supplies the structural tailwind and BTC's fixed 21M supply the differentiator. The catch is that the strong relationship lives almost entirely in shared trend — on first differences it nearly vanishes — and the coefficients are time-varying, not fixed. Honest forward read: ~10-12% nominal, ~7-9% real, vol ~55-60%, gold correlation ~0, since BTC trades as a liquidity/risk beta, not a true debasement hedge.


*Scores — rigor 2, signal 3, robustness 2, data-ops 5, orthogonality 3. The headline elasticity (~2.65) and 0.94 levels-correlation are textbook spurious I(1) regression; on contemporaneous changes the relationship nearly vanishes, and the peer-reviewed TVC-VECM literature formally rejects constant coefficients (p=0.0015), so the fixed-elasticity machinery is methodologically weak (rigor 2). Real directional signal exists — BTC tracks global liquidity in ~83% of 12m windows, more than any major asset — so it adds genuine macro conditioning, but the predictive level it yields (10-12%) is roughly the consensus and the decay anchor does the real work (signal 3). It is fragile across regimes: time-varying cointegration, the rising equity correlation to +0.56 in the ETF era, and an unstable error-correction term mean the money-implied fair value drifts structurally (robustness 2). M2/global-liquidity series are free, monthly, FRED/CF-Benchmarks-published and trivial to operationalize in a CMA (data_ops 5).*


**Key drivers:** Broad-money / liquidity growth (US M2 ~6%, global M2 ~7-8%) as the exogenous trend driver; BTC money-elasticity beta (~2.0-2.65 historical, must be decayed toward 1.0-1.5 forward); Error-correction speed to money-implied fair value (~-0.12/mo, ~5-6mo half-life); Fiscal dominance / sovereign debt growth driving fiat depreciation (the debasement premise); Fixed transparent supply (21M cap, halvings, ~450/day issuance) as the scarcity differentiator vs both fiat and gold; Liquidity-leads-BTC lag (months); global liquidity Granger-causes BTC, raw world-M2 levels do not


**Pros:** Grounds an otherwise cashflow-less asset in a real, testable macro variable (money supply) rather than pure sentiment or stock-to-flow numerology; Empirically the directional relationship is genuinely strong: BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows (Alden/Callahan), higher than any other major asset class — a real signal, not nothing; Provides an explicit, falsifiable fair-value model (e.g. CF Benchmarks' M2 fair value) you can mark price against and that has historically mean-reverted; Conceptually clean CMA derivation: expected return = trend money growth x elasticity, which naturally forces appreciation DECAY as the elasticity compresses toward gold's; Ties BTC to the same debasement logic underwriting gold (Grayscale), making it portfolio-coherent with a real-asset / inflation-hedge sleeve


**Cons:** The headline elasticity (2.65) and 0.94 levels-correlation are almost certainly SPURIOUS in the econometric sense: both log-BTC and log-M2 are non-stationary trending I(1) series, and naive level correlation/regression on two trends is the textbook spurious-regression trap; On contemporaneous CHANGES (the regression you should run), the M2-BTC relationship 'nearly vanishes' — correlation collapses toward ~0; the relationship lives almost entirely in shared trend, not in month-to-month co-movement; Cointegration is NOT stable: the peer-reviewed TVC-VECM literature (Park/Lee JDQS 2022) formally rejects constant coefficients (p=0.0015) in favor of smoothly time-varying ones — so a single fixed elasticity for a 10-15yr CMA is not supported by the data; Clear post-2021/2025 structural break: CF Benchmarks reports R-squared collapsing from 0.71-0.90 to ~0.59 and a ~46% fair-value gap; gold's liquidity Z-score climbed to 2.82 while BTC's fell to -1.31, i.e. the liquidity bid rotated AWAY from BTC; 'Global M2' is a data-quality artifact: it is built by multiplying heterogeneous national M2 by spot FX, mixing fast- and slow-reporting regimes, and is routinely curve-fit/lag-shifted ('data torture', 'overfitting') to match BTC — quants flatly say it 'can't predict' BTC; No anchor for the elasticity going forward: there's no theory pinning beta at 2.65 vs 1.5 vs 1.0, so the CMA's central number is a judgment call dressed as an estimate; the model also says nothing about volatility or correlations directly; Source quality is mixed and tilts promotional: the strongest numeric claims come from a non-peer-reviewed preprint and from sell-side/asset-manager research (Grayscale, CF Benchmarks) with a long book, not from replicated academic work

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. The canonical setup: take log(BTC) and log(M2), confirm both are I(1) (ADF, plus Zivot-Andrews to allow one structural break), test for a single cointegrating vector (Engle-Granger and Johansen), then estimate a VECM. Preprints.org 2025 (Jan-2015 to Apr-2025, monthly) reports a Johansen long-run elasticity of 2.65 (1% M2 -> 2.65% BTC) and an error-correction coefficient lambda' = -0.12, i.e. ~12% of any deviation from the money-implied path corrects per month (half-life ~ln(0.5)/ln(0.88) ~ 5-6 months). It concludes BTC is a 'highly elastic, liquidity-driven asset.' CAVEAT: this is a preprint (also republished in WMJournals/WMJ-JESD), not peer-reviewed; the abstract does not report R-squared, the specific unit-root statistics, or robustness to multiple breaks.

THE SPURIOUSNESS PROBLEM (central). Two trending I(1) series will show a near-1.0 levels correlation and a 'significant' regression even if unrelated — Granger-Newbold spurious regression. Cointegration is the defense, BUT (a) cointegration over a single 10-year hyper-adoption sample with one secular up-trend in both series is fragile, and (b) the peer-reviewed evidence says the relationship is NOT constant. Park & Lee (JDQS 2022, Emerald, peer-reviewed) run a time-varying-cointegration VECM with Chebyshev polynomials on BTC, VIX, US10Y, USCPI, gold, DXY: at m=1 (constant coefficients) the null is not rejected, but m>=2 rejects at p=0.00152 — i.e. the cointegrating coefficients SMOOTHLY EVOLVE over time. Their cointegrating vector (normalized on VIX) has BTC -2.727, gold -0.0443, DXY -0.676 — inverse links to safe havens and volatility. Critically that paper does NOT include M2 at all, so it neither confirms nor refutes the M2 vector directly; its contribution here is the meta-point that BTC's macro cointegration is time-varying, which undercuts any fixed-elasticity CMA.

THE CHANGES-VS-LEVELS TELL. Multiple quants note that when you difference both series (look at contemporaneous % changes rather than levels), the M2-BTC correlation 'nearly vanishes' toward ~0. The relationship lives in shared trend. Alden/Callahan ('Bitcoin: A Global Liquidity Barometer,' 2024, practitioner) actually concede this: their headline 0.94 is a LEVELS correlation (May-2013 to Jul-2024); the 12-month rolling correlation is only ~0.51 and 6-month ~0.36; and on a YoY %-change basis equity indices correlate to liquidity slightly MORE than BTC, with BTC's high vol 'distorting' the change-correlation. Their durable claim is directional: BTC moves WITH liquidity 83% of 12-month windows / 74% of 6-month windows — genuinely the highest of major assets, but a sign-agreement stat, not a magnitude/return model.

THE BREAK (most damaging for a forward CMA). CF Benchmarks (2024 piece, updated views into 2026) reports the rolling 4-yr correlation historically 0.4-0.6, and BTC's R-squared with M2 collapsing from 0.71-0.90 (2022 bear) to ~0.59 (early 2026), with their M2 fair value ~$136k vs price ~$74k — a ~46% gap, 'one of the widest observed.' Grayscale's Jan-2026 'Debasement Trade' note documents the rotation: BTC's M2-fair-value Z-score swung +1.48 (Jan-2025) to -1.31 (Feb-2026) while GOLD's climbed 1.38 -> 2.82 — i.e. the debasement/liquidity bid that the thesis predicts for BTC actually went to gold. This is the single most important caveat for the gold correlation: the 'digital gold' co-movement is low and regime-switching, and in the most recent episode BTC and gold DIVERGED hard.

DATA-QUALITY CAVEAT. 'Global M2' has no official definition; it is constructed by summing national M2 and converting at spot FX, blending fast-reporting (US) and lag-reporting economies, so its 'daily' wiggles are partly an FX artifact. Critics call the chart-overlay practice 'a textbook case of data illiteracy and overfitting' — analysts lag-shift M2 by an arbitrary number of weeks to maximize visual fit, then present the fitted lag as predictive. A TradingView/quant piece bluntly: 'Global M2 can't predict Bitcoin price.' Also note: global liquidity (broad, includes central-bank balance sheets/credit) Granger-causes BTC, but raw world M2 does not — so even the causal claim is sensitive to which liquidity proxy is used.

GRAYSCALE / DEBASEMENT FRAMING (asset-manager, promotional but useful). Debasement trade = excess sovereign debt -> fiat depreciation vs scarce-supply assets (real estate, metals, BTC). Grayscale: BTC returns on average positively correlated to stocks, positively correlated to gold, negatively correlated to USD; BTC 'less tightly correlated with month-to-month Dollar weakness' than other debasement assets but with a high downside-capture ratio (it falls with risk-off even when the debasement story is intact). Supply differentiator: 20-millionth BTC mined ~early 2026, ~450 BTC/day to the Apr-2028 halving, hard 21M cap — predictable, decreasing issuance vs open-ended fiat.

REALIZED BASELINE (my scripted anchor, year-end USD). YoY: 2017 +1341%, 2020 +303%, 2021 +60%, 2022 -64%, 2023 +156%, 2024 +121%, 2025 +8%. Trailing CAGR to 2025: 10yr ~73%, 12yr ~50%, 5yr ~28%. Decay of trailing CAGR as the asset matured: 2013-2017 ~107%/yr -> 2013-2020 ~68%/yr -> 2013-2024 ~55%/yr. The prompt's 142->65->17 decay framing is directionally identical: appreciation has fallen roughly by half each market-cap doubling.

SYNTHESIS LOGIC. Under THIS model's own machinery, forward return = trend money growth x elasticity. Holding global broad money at ~7-8%/yr and letting the elasticity decay from ~2.0 to ~1.1 across years 3-15 gives an average ~11-12% nominal, ~9% real BEFORE haircutting for the now-documented break and rotation to gold. I round to ~10-12% nominal / ~7-9% real as a judgment, explicitly NOT a computed stat, and flag that the model is silent on vol and correlations so those (~50-55% vol; gold corr ~0.2-0.35; growth-equity ~0.35-0.45) are anchored to realized behavior and the debasement logic, not to anything this literature publishes. Brutal bottom line: the M2-elasticity model is the most intellectually defensible of the cashflow-less BTC frameworks because it has a real driver and a mean-reverting fair value, but its headline elasticity is trend-driven and likely partly spurious, its cointegration is provably time-varying, and the 2025-26 break shows it failing live as gold ate BTC's debasement bid. Use it as ONE input with wide error bars, not as a point CMA.

### #32 · Generalized-Metcalfe x Logistic-Saturation Fundamental Support (Wheatley-Sornette)

*Family: network-value-saturated · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 49*


**Explanation:** Wheatley-Sornette regress log market cap on log active users and let the data choose the exponent: beta = 1.69, not Metcalfe's n^2 (forcing beta=2 is rejected at p < 1e-16, R-squared = 0.95). The novel binding is to a SATURATING user model, ln(u) = a - b*e^(-c*t^d), where growth decays (~35% to ~21% over five years) toward a finite carrying capacity. Combining a sub-quadratic exponent with a ceiling on users produces a FINITE terminal fundamental value and endogenous appreciation decay -- the per-user multiple and the user-growth rate both compress as the network matures. In 2018 the fitted support was just 22-44B vs a 170B market cap, flagging ~4x overvaluation; the authors used it to detect four bubbles and (validated out-of-sample) to call the early-2019 bottom near the predicted 40-80B band. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the mechanism forces appreciation toward saturating user growth times a shrinking multiple -- low-double-digit at most -- but the authors stress carrying-capacity estimates span four orders of magnitude beyond sample, so long-horizon point forecasts are, in their words, 'effectively meaningless.'


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Methodologically honest (data-chosen 1.69 exponent, rejects n^2, peer-reviewed, real 2018 out-of-sample call) and uniquely supplies the correct CMA shape: finite terminal value plus endogenous appreciation decay. But authors themselves disclaim long-horizon use (~4-order carrying-capacity uncertainty), the regression is likely spurious (non-cointegrated I(1), reverse causality), and the active-user input is structurally breaking in the ETF/custodial/L2 era — so signal and regime-robustness are weak despite high theoretical rigor.*


**Key drivers:** Number of active users / non-dormant addresses (network size n), the sole fundamental input; Empirically-estimated Metcalfe exponent beta = 1.69 (sub-quadratic; n^2 statistically rejected, p<1e-16), implying each user connects to ~n^(2/3) others; Logistic/Gompertz user-saturation curve ln(u)=a-b*e^(-c*t^d) with a finite carrying capacity -- the feature that bounds terminal value; User growth-rate decay path (~35% -> ~21% over 5yr in the 2018 fit) driving endogenous appreciation deceleration; Near-fixed coin supply (21M cap, halving issuance) as denominator converting network value to price; Carrying-capacity (saturation ceiling) uncertainty -- spans ~4 orders of magnitude out of sample, dominating long-horizon uncertainty; Mean-reversion of price toward the Metcalfe support line, used to flag bubbles (the LPPLS overlay handles the bubble departures)


**Pros:** Lets the DATA choose the exponent (1.69) rather than imposing n^2, and statistically rejects the naive quadratic law (p<1e-16) -- more honest than crypto-native Metcalfe variants; The saturating user curve produces a FINITE terminal fundamental value and built-in appreciation decay, the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA (unlike S2F/power-law, which imply unbounded growth); Genuine out-of-sample validation: the 2018 fundamental-support call (market cap to fall to 40-80B) was confirmed when BTC fell into the middle of that band in early 2019 -- a real ex-ante success, not just in-sample fit; Peer-reviewed (Royal Society Open Science), with full data deposited (Dryad), and the authors are unusually candid about model uncertainty and the limits of long-term prediction; Grounds value in an observable, hard-to-fake fundamental (on-chain users) and cleanly separates the slow fundamental from fast LPPLS bubble dynamics


**Cons:** The authors THEMSELVES disclaim CMA use: carrying-capacity estimates differ by ~4 orders of magnitude beyond the sample and they call long-term predictions 'effectively meaningless' -- repurposing this as a 10-15yr return forecast is precisely the misuse they warn against; Likely spurious regression: log-price and log-users are non-stationary trending I(1) series; Civitarese (2018) finds they do NOT cointegrate and cannot reject reverse causality (price drives wallet creation, not the reverse), so the 0.95 R-squared may be a trend artifact; Active-user / address metrics are crude and increasingly broken: exchange/ETF/custodial adoption and L2 migration create economic value with ZERO new on-chain active addresses, severing the model's sole driver post-2021/2024; It is a fundamental-SUPPORT and bubble-detection tool, not a return model -- deriving appreciation requires bolting on a forward user-growth assumption the paper does not provide, and the practitioner extrapolations ($1M by 2028, $1.5M by 2035) launder a fragile in-sample fit into precise targets the econometrics cannot support; Tiny structural sample (one BTC history, ~4 bubble episodes) and post-2021 institutionalization regime break leave the exponent and carrying capacity unstable out of sample; Silent on volatility and on cross-asset correlations (growth/value equities, FI, TIPS, gold) -- all distributional CMA cells must be imported from realized data

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Two ingredients, bound together. (1) A GENERALIZED Metcalfe law: ln(p) = alpha + beta*ln(u) + epsilon, with p = market cap, u = active users. On 2,782 daily values (17-Jul-2010 to 26-Feb-2018) the fit is beta = 1.69 (s.e. 0.0076), alpha = 1.51 (0.087), R-squared = 0.95. The authors explicitly test and REJECT the classic quadratic Metcalfe exponent: 'Forcing the exponent beta to be equal to 2 would result in an intercept of -2.01 (0.018), but this regression is significantly worse,' with an ANOVA/F-test p-value 'less than 10^-16.' Economically, beta=1.69 implies each user connects on average to ~N^(2/3) others (for N=1M, ~10,000 links), a more realistic density than full pairwise n^2. (2) A SATURATING user-adoption curve: ln(u) = a - b*e^(-c*t^d) + epsilon, fit Jan-2012 to Feb-2018, projecting annual user growth to 'decrease over the next 5 years from 35 to 21%,' with users rising from ~0.79M (2018) to ~2.60M (2023). The combination is what makes this row distinct: a sub-quadratic exponent applied to a CEILINGED user base yields a FINITE terminal fundamental value with endogenous appreciation decay, whereas the existing Metcalfe row (#2) applies an ad-hoc exponent to an unconstrained series purely as a relative over/under-valuation gauge, and LPPLS (#18) merely uses such a fundamental as the baseline a bubble departs from.

KEY RELATIONSHIP / USE. The paper's actual deliverable is a fundamental SUPPORT value, not a return. As of Mar-2018 the OLS support was ~$44B (point fit), with alternative support lines at $22B and $33B, versus an actual market cap of $170B -- i.e. BTC was ~4x above fundamental. The model is then paired with the Log-Periodic Power Law Singularity (LPPLS) model: periods where price runs far above the Metcalfe support are the bubbles, and LPPLS brackets the crash time. Four bubbles were flagged with overvaluation factors: May-Aug 2012 (3.1x), Jan-Apr 2013 (20.4x), Oct-Nov 2013 (6.8x), and Jun-2015-Dec-2017 (103x).

HISTORICAL FIT / VALIDATION. This approach has a rare genuine out-of-sample success. In 2018 the authors predicted Bitcoin's market cap would 'fall several-fold from its peak, to a $40-80 Billion range'; in the 2019 follow-up Wheatley confirms 'the market cap indeed fell into the middle of the predicted range in the new year of 2019,' and by Apr-2019 they re-assessed BTC as 'still 2x overvalued' (down from '10x overvalued' at peak). That is an ex-ante fundamental call that worked -- materially stronger evidence than S2F, which failed catastrophically post-2021.

FAILURE MODES. (a) The authors disclaim long-horizon use: 'beyond the sample, differences explode such that there are 4 orders of magnitude difference between the predicted carrying capacities,' and 'precise inference based on a single model is misleading, and long-term predictions effectively meaningless... model uncertainty dominates uncertainty of estimated parameters.' Any 10-15yr CMA built on this is a reconstruction AGAINST the authors' warning. (b) Likely spurious regression: Civitarese (2018) tests price vs an adjusted wallet-connection series and finds they do NOT cointegrate, rejecting Metcalfe, and cannot reject reverse causality (returns drive new wallets). Both log-price and log-users are non-stationary I(1) trends, so the 0.95 R-squared may be a trend artifact. (c) Metric decay: ETF/custodial/treasury adoption and L2 migration add economic value with zero new on-chain active addresses, breaking the sole driver post-2021/2024.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The academic paper deliberately publishes none beyond ~2023 user counts. The practitioner branch (Peterson, same generalized-Metcalfe-plus-Gompertz family, AIAR 2018) does: validated near-term calls of ~$3,500 EOY-2018 (actual $3,782) and ~$7,000 EOY-2019 (actual $7,243), then forward targets of >$500k by the ~2028 halving, ~$1M by March-2028 / ~450 days post-halving, and ~$1.5M by 2035 (~31%/yr off a ~$100k base). These laundered, precise long-horizon targets are exactly what the academic authors caution against; I anchor my synthesized ~9-13%/yr nominal to BTC's realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%) and the model's own saturating-user logic, not to the practitioner extrapolations. Distributional cells (vol ~55-60%, equity corr +0.35-0.50, gold corr ~0-0.10) are imported from realized data because the framework is silent on them.

### #33 · Geopolitical-Risk-Index Conditional Safe-Haven Factor (GPR/EPU)

*Family: geopolitical-risk-factor · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 49*


**Explanation:** The method regresses BTC returns/volume/volatility on the named Caldara-Iacoviello GPR index (and Baker-Bloom-Davis EPU), using quantile, GARCH-MIDAS, DCC-GARCH or Markov-switching specifications to test the hedge-vs-diversifier-vs-safe-haven taxonomy. Inputs are an exogenous, text-based stress measure and BTC's market data — no cashflow, scarcity, or network input. The central, replicated result: the unconditional GPR-BTC relationship is weak or insignificant, but the effect is conditional — it appears at the tails (large equity crashes; Chibane-Janson 2025 find BTC and the Swiss Franc act as crash safe havens where gold and Treasuries do not), in developing countries through volume (Sergio-Petti 2024, GPR coefficient +0.085, currency substitution), or in specific crisis windows. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this matters because it directly characterizes regime-dependent correlation rather than appreciation: it implies BTC is a high-beta risk asset most of the time with unreliable, state-contingent decoupling, and it empirically REJECTS the structural long-run safe-haven / negative-correlation reading. It says essentially nothing about the appreciation level.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Methodologically strong and honest: exogenous text-based regressor avoids the price-on-price circularity of S2F/NVT and puts the safe-haven claim to a falsifiable, regime-conditional test (high rigor). But it yields no appreciation estimate and the tail coefficients flip sign across estimator/window/crisis on a short ~2-3 regime sample, so its predictive signal over 10-15yr is weak (low signal). It earns moderate robustness only because its central finding — rejecting digital-gold, conditional vol effects — is replicated and speaks directly to the regime/correlation cells the decay anchor leaves open. Data (GPR/EPU + BTC market data) is public and easy, but GARCH-MIDAS/DCC/quantile machinery adds operational lift in a CMA pipeline.*


**Key drivers:** Caldara-Iacoviello GPR index (AER 2022) — news-based count of adverse geopolitical events/threats/acts across 10+ newspapers; the named exogenous regressor; Baker-Bloom-Davis Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU) index — the policy-uncertainty companion regressor; Conditional/quantile structure — the effect lives at the tails (crash quantiles) and in specific regimes, not in the mean; choice of quantile/GARCH-MIDAS/DCC/Markov-switching estimator is load-bearing; Country development level — GPR raises BTC VOLUME in developing countries (currency-substitution / capital-flight channel), insignificant or negative in developed countries; Equity-crash conditioning — BTC's safe-haven signal (where it exists) shows up during large S&P 500 moves, not moderate variation (Chibane-Janson); Crisis-window specificity — Russia-Ukraine onset produced short-lived positive BTC reactions that decay, illustrating the non-persistence of the effect; Benchmark comparison to gold/CHF/Treasuries — the framework is comparative, and gold consistently out-performs BTC as a hedge


**Pros:** Tests rather than asserts: unlike S2F/Metcalfe/gold-parity narratives, it puts the 'digital gold / safe haven' claim to a falsifiable empirical test against a named, peer-reviewed, exogenous stress index — and reports the inconvenient answer (mostly rejected); Directly populates the hardest CMA cells: it speaks to regime-dependent CORRELATION and tail behavior, which appreciation-only models (S2F, power-law, cost-of-production) are entirely silent on; Exogenous, text-based regressor (GPR/EPU) is not derived from price, so it avoids the spurious-regression / circularity trap that plagues S2F and NVT (price-on-price); Honest about heterogeneity: cleanly separates a real developing-country volume/currency-substitution channel from the false developed-country safe-haven story, which is genuinely useful for understanding WHO buys BTC under stress and why; Comparative discipline: by benchmarking BTC against gold, CHF and Treasuries in the same model, it prevents the asset from being graded on a curve — and shows gold is the stronger geopolitical hedge


**Cons:** Produces NO appreciation estimate: it is a correlation/regime characterization, so a 10-15yr expected-return CMA cannot be derived from it at all — it only constrains the correlation cells; Results are fragile and contradictory across specifications: sign and significance flip with the quantile, the estimator (OLS negative vs quantile positive at tails — Demir 2018), the sample window, and the crisis chosen; there is no single stable coefficient to quote; Short, regime-shifting sample: GPR-BTC studies span ~2013-2023, only ~2-3 macro regimes and a handful of geopolitical shocks, so tail estimates rest on very few events (curve-fit risk on the rare crashes that matter most); The 'safe haven' findings are often short-lived and event-specific (days around Russia-Ukraine), decaying quickly — repurposing a transient crisis reaction as a structural 10-15yr property is a category error the marketing layer commits; Endogeneity/omitted-variable risk: GPR spikes co-occur with risk-off liquidity shocks and Fed policy, so an apparent GPR-BTC link may be a proxy for the broader risk/liquidity cycle (the monetary-substitution factor #6 channel) rather than a geopolitical-hedge mechanism; Institutionalization (ETFs post-2024) plausibly raises BTC's equity correlation further, weakening any residual crisis-decoupling the older sample showed — the historical conditional safe-haven may be eroding precisely as the asset matures

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This is an academic, regression-based factor literature, not a valuation model. The dependent variable is a BTC market quantity (returns, realized/conditional volatility, or trading volume); the key independent variable is a named, exogenous, text-based uncertainty index — chiefly the Caldara-Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index (Measuring Geopolitical Risk, AER 2022, 112(4):1194-1225), and often the Baker-Bloom-Davis EPU companion. Caldara-Iacoviello build GPR by counting adverse-geopolitical-event articles across 10+ major newspapers, splitting it into Threat and Act components, and show higher GPR foreshadows lower investment/employment, higher disaster probability, and larger downside risk in mainstream assets. The BTC literature plugs GPR/EPU into quantile regression, quantile-on-quantile, GARCH-MIDAS, DCC-GARCH, or Markov-switching VAR — the estimator choice is deliberate, because the entire point is that the relationship is STATE-DEPENDENT and a single OLS coefficient hides it.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS AND HISTORICAL FIT. Four robust patterns recur. (1) On average the GPR-BTC return link is weak/insignificant: the PMC GARCH-quantile study (gold vs BTC vs ETH, daily 2-Jan-2013 to 30-Nov-2021) reports a BTC GPR coefficient of ~0.000854, not significant, and concludes BTC is a WEAK hedge while gold is a STRONG hedge and safe haven. (2) The effect is conditional/tail-located: the same study finds a significant +0.0078*** only at the 10% bearish quantile; Demir, Gozgor, Lau & Vigne (FRL 2018, daily Jan-2010 to Mar-2017) find EPU is NEGATIVELY related to BTC returns under OLS but POSITIVE and significant at both tails under quantile-on-quantile, concluding BTC 'can serve as a hedging tool' — a sign flip that perfectly illustrates the fragility. (3) The developing-country volume channel: Sergio & Petti (arXiv:2409.17057, Dec-2014 to Feb-2023, 34 regions, 3,271 monthly obs) find GPR significantly raises BTC VOLUME only in developing countries (baseline coefficient +0.085, p<0.05, rising to ~0.25-0.29 in IV specs), negative-insignificant (-0.040 to -0.069) in developed countries — interpreted as currency substitution / capital flight, NOT a universal safe-haven. (4) The crash-conditioning result: Chibane & Janson (FRL v74, 2025) estimate an S&P 500 crash model driven by GPR and find BTC and the Swiss Franc act as crash safe havens while gold and Treasuries do NOT, and only through LARGE equity moves, not moderate ones.

CRITIQUES (faithfully represented). The literature is internally contradictory: Chibane-Janson find gold FAILS as a crash hedge while the PMC study finds gold is the STRONGEST hedge — the disagreement is itself evidence that these tail estimates are unstable and sample/specification-dependent. The samples are short (~2013-2023), spanning few macro regimes and a handful of geopolitical shocks, so the all-important tail coefficients rest on very few events (curve-fit risk). 'Safe haven' findings are frequently short-lived and event-specific (days around Russia-Ukraine), and decay quickly — repurposing a transient crisis reaction as a structural 10-15yr property is a category error. There is serious endogeneity/omitted-variable risk: GPR spikes co-occur with risk-off liquidity contractions and Fed tightening, so an apparent GPR-BTC link may proxy the broader risk/liquidity cycle (overlapping the monetary-substitution factor #6) rather than a distinct geopolitical-hedge mechanism. Finally, post-2024 ETF institutionalization plausibly raises BTC's equity beta, eroding whatever conditional decoupling the older sample showed — the historical safe-haven signal may be weakening as the asset matures.

FAILURE MODES. The honest verdict across the literature is that the unconditional LONG-RUN safe-haven claim for Bitcoin is REJECTED. BTC is, in steady state, a high-beta risk asset (it sold off WITH equities in 2022); any safe-haven property is conditional, weak, non-persistent, and weaker than gold's. Quantile analyses (Cryptocurrencies as safe havens? ScienceDirect 2025) find the GPR impact on BTC, ETH and LTC 'generally insignificant' with 'weak safe-haven abilities.'

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This approach is structurally incapable of producing an appreciation or price forecast — it is a correlation/regime literature. There are NO on-record 10-15yr BTC return forecasts produced this way, which is exactly why it cannot move the appreciation cell of a CMA and should be used ONLY to discipline the correlation/regime cells: BTC's correlation to equities is positive and durable, its gold correlation is ~0, and its 'geopolitical hedge' is a conditional, unreliable tail phenomenon — not a structural diversifier you can underwrite over 10-15 years.

</details>

### #34 · On-Chain Cost-Basis Valuation (Realized Cap / MVRV / SOPR / Thermocap / HODL Waves)

*Family: on-chain · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 48*


**Explanation:** This family values Bitcoin off its aggregate on-chain cost basis rather than cashflow or scarcity. Realized Cap "price-stamps" every coin at the price it last moved and sums them, approximating the network's invested capital; Realized Price is the per-coin average. Market value is read relative to this base: MVRV (market cap / realized cap) and SOPR gauge aggregate unrealized/realized profit, Thermocap tracks cumulative miner security spend, and HODL Waves split cost basis by coin age. Crucially these are mean-reversion oscillators calibrated to cycle extremes (MVRV ~0.8 at bottoms, >3.2 at tops), not absolute valuation models, so no native long-horizon return exists. To force a 10-15yr CMA you project the growth of invested capital (net inflows, decelerating off a larger base) and assume MVRV reverts to ~1.5-2x. Because Realized Cap is a transform of past price, the much-touted "floor" is reflexive, not an independent fundamental. Extrapolating BTC's appreciation decay yields low-double-digit nominal returns; the framework is silent on volatility and every correlation, so those cells must be borrowed from realized data.


*Scores — rigor 2, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 4, orthogonality 3. Realized Cap is a clean accounting identity but the family is fundamentally an oscillator with no native long-horizon return, so any 10-15yr CMA level is grafted on by judgment (low rigor/signal). Its real value is conditioning: the realized-price floor (-14 to -23% vs spot -75 to -92%) is a genuine, regime-spanning downside/tail anchor, but the floor is reflexive (endogenous to prior prices) and thresholds are data-mined on 2-3 cycles. On-chain data is free and well-supported operationally (high data_ops).*


**Key drivers:** Realized Cap = cumulative realized profit minus realized loss = net USD capital ever locked into the network (the invested-capital base / on-chain cost basis); Realized Price = Realized Cap / circulating supply (aggregate holder cost basis per coin); functions as a soft floor; MVRV ratio = Market Cap / Realized Cap = aggregate unrealized-profit multiple; mean-reverting oscillator (bottoms ~0.8, tops ~3.2-3.7); MVRV Z-Score = (MarketCap - RealizedCap)/stdev(MarketCap); normalizes extremes for cross-cycle comparison; SOPR (Spent Output Profit Ratio) = realized price of spent coins / price paid; >1 = supply in profit being sold, <1 = capitulation; Thermocap = cumulative USD value of all block rewards + fees ever paid to miners (aggregate security spend); Market-Cap/Thermocap is an on-chain 'P/E'-style ratio; Realized-Cap HODL Waves = age-banded decomposition of Realized Cap (who holds cost basis, long-term vs short-term holders); Net capital inflow / 'realized cap growth rate' — the only variable that drives a long-horizon trajectory rather than a cyclical signal


**Pros:** Grounded in observable on-chain ledger data (UTXO move-prices), not a narrative or fitted regression — Realized Cap is an accounting identity, not a model assumption; Realized Cap / Realized Price empirically behaves as a rising floor: it has fallen only ~-14% to -23% in bear markets vs spot's -75% to -92%, giving a genuine downside-anchor concept useful for tail/loss-given-bear estimation; MVRV/SOPR oscillators have real ex-post discriminating power at extremes — readings have repeatedly bracketed cycle tops and bottoms (MVRV<1 ≈ ~15% of days marked capitulation, MVRV>3.2 ≈ cycle peaks); Cost-basis framing maps cleanly to investor behavior (mean reversion toward what holders paid), so it is a behaviorally-honest middleware even if not a CMA; Thermocap ties valuation to a real economic floor (energy/security spend), giving an independent cross-check on the cost-basis story; Unlike Stock-to-Flow and Metcalfe, this family does NOT publish a single point-forecast, so it is harder to weaponize into a spurious 10yr target — its honesty is a feature


**Cons:** Fundamentally an OSCILLATOR, not a valuation model: it tells you where price sits relative to cost basis, never where cost basis (or price) should be in 10-15 years. There is no native long-horizon expected-return output — any CMA is grafted on by the analyst.; Reflexive/circular: Realized Cap is a transformation of past PRICE (each coin stamped at its move-time price). High prices raise realized cap which raises the 'floor' — so the floor is endogenous to the bubble, not an independent fundamental. A permanent 70% drawdown would drag realized price down with it over time.; Thresholds are data-mined on a tiny sample (2-3 full cycles): MVRV>3.7 'overvalued', Z>6.5 'top', M/T~0.000004 'top' are curve-fits with severe lookahead bias and small-n overfitting. Each cycle has hit LOWER MVRV peaks (2013 ~5.7 → later cycles <3) — the calibration visibly decays, mirroring the S2F/Metcalfe post-2021 break critique. Naive use is unsafe.; Predictive performance degrades post-2017/post-futures as markets became more efficient (academic backtests of cost-basis oscillators show Sharpe collapse after 2017); ETF/institutional custody also breaks the on-chain signal because coins move off-chain into wrappers and stop pricestamping.; Supply-side metric noise: lost coins, exchange/wrapper consolidation, and ETF custody distort UTXO age and cost-basis attribution, biasing realized cap and HODL waves.; No correlation, volatility, or cross-asset structure is produced at all — the framework is silent on every CMA covariance input. It cannot, by itself, populate a correlation matrix vs equities/gold/TIPS.

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Realized Cap (Coin Metrics, Carter/Le Calvez ~2018) = sum over all UTXOs of (coins × price at last on-chain move). Equivalently the cumulative sum of realized profits minus realized losses since genesis — i.e., net USD capital locked into the ledger. Realized Price = Realized Cap / circulating supply = aggregate holder cost basis. MVRV (Puell & Mahmudov, 2018) = Market Cap / Realized Cap = aggregate unrealized-profit multiple; "MVRV − 1 = avg unrealized PnL." MVRV Z-Score = (MarketCap − RealizedCap)/σ(MarketCap). SOPR = realized value of spent coins / value at creation. Thermocap = cumulative USD of all block rewards + fees (aggregate security/energy spend); Market-Cap/Thermocap is an on-chain pseudo-P/E. Realized-Cap HODL Waves (Unchained/Bansal 2018) band the realized cap by coin age.

KEY QUOTES / THRESHOLDS (Glassnode "Mastering the MVRV Ratio"): MVRV 2.2 = 120% aggregate profit; 1.0 = breakeven; 0.8 = −20%. Cycle calibration: MVRV>3.2 ≈ peaks (~6% of days since 2017), >2.4 euphoria (~20%), <1.0 capitulation (~15%), <0.8 cycle lows (~5%). 2013 MVRV hit 5.4-5.7; later cycles topped progressively LOWER (<3 by 2021) — the decay of the threshold is itself the strongest evidence against naive forward use. Other lit cites MVRV>3.7 "overvalued", Z>6.5 "top", M/T≈0.000004 "top." Every report explicitly disclaims "no investment advice / no price forecast."

THE LOAD-BEARING FORWARD SIGNAL. Glassnode "The Realized Cap Foundation": Realized Cap bear-market drawdowns are only −14% to −23% vs spot −75% to −92%, and "Bitcoin has historically found bear market floors at increasingly elevated price ranges over time." This is the ONLY structurally forward-looking element in the whole family — a slowly-rising soft floor — and even it is framed as past behavior, not a fair-value theorem.

BRUTAL HONESTY / CRITIQUES. (1) Oscillator ≠ valuation model: produces no expected return, vol, or correlation. Any CMA is the analyst's graft, not the framework's. (2) Reflexivity/circularity — Realized Cap is a transform of past PRICE, so the "floor" is endogenous to the prior bubble; a permanent regime-down would erode realized price too. It cannot independently anchor fair value. (3) Overfitting / small-n: 2-3 cycles, lookahead-calibrated thresholds, visibly decaying peak-MVRV per cycle — the same pathology the academic literature pins on Stock-to-Flow (spurious cointegration, non-stationarity, post-2021 break) and Metcalfe (naive log-log regressions reject out of sample). Cost-basis oscillators are less egregious than S2F because they don't publish a point target, but their thresholds are no less curve-fit. (4) Efficiency decay: Cretarola/Figà-Talamanca (MDPI Information 2022) — crypto-asset-pricing oscillators backtest profitably pre-2017 but Sharpe collapses after BTC futures launch as markets grew efficient. (5) Measurement breakdown under institutionalization: ETF custody and exchange/wrapper consolidation move coins off-chain or into reused addresses, so post-2024 the UTXO age/cost-basis signal is increasingly blind to the real marginal holder — arguably the framework is least reliable exactly when AUM is largest.

SYNTHESIS REASONING. The scripted empirical anchor (empirical_anchor.json) shows BTC nominal appreciation decaying 142% (full, 2010-2026) → 65% (trailing-10y) → 17% (trailing-5y), vol 103%→69%→57%, and a RISING equity correlation (growth-eq 0.26→0.36→0.56). A 10-15yr forward CMA must extrapolate that decay, not the level. Under THIS approach's cost-basis logic specifically, appreciation is bounded by how fast net invested capital (Realized Cap) can keep growing against an ever-larger base — a decelerating series — plus a modest one-time MVRV mean-reversion to ~1.5-2x. That argues for low-double-digit nominal (~10-13%), i.e. another step below the trailing-5y 17%, with real ~7-10%. I keep vol high (~45-55%) but trimmed, because the rising realized-price floor genuinely compresses left-tail severity over time. Correlations are pure judgment (framework silent): I inherit the anchor's rising-equity-beta trend (growth 0.40-0.55, value 0.30-0.40), small positive FI/TIPS (0.15-0.30), and — importantly for the digital-gold thesis — only a LOW positive gold corr (0.05-0.20). The cost-basis lens provides NO mechanism that would force BTC-gold co-movement up to the 0.5+ a digital-gold narrative wants; historical BTC-gold corr is ~0 (full window −0.01), so I nudge it only slightly positive for a maturing debasement-hedge cohort. All synthesized figures are explicit judgments, not computed statistics.

### #35 · Discrete Cycle-Amplitude Decay Extrapolation (4-Year Halving Peak-Multiple Compression)

*Family: cycle-decay-extrapolation · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 48*


**Explanation:** Crypto desks fit Bitcoin's most robust empirical regularity — each halving cycle tops at a lower multiple than the last — as a discrete geometric decay. Bitcoin Magazine Pro's Golden-Ratio Multiplier puts cycle peaks at the 21x, 5x, 3x and ~2x Fibonacci bands of a long MA (2013/2017/2021/2025); the Mayer Multiple peak fell 15x->6x->~3.2x; peak gains dropped ~2,000% to ~630% (~69% per cycle). A forward CMA extrapolates that ratio across the ~2028/2032/2036 halvings: each cycle-top gain is a fixed fraction (~0.3-0.5x) of the prior, compounded over multiple cycles, then annualized spot-to-horizon. This mechanically forces appreciation DECAY — the right qualitative shape — landing well below realized history. It implies low-double-digit nominal CAGR over 10-15yr. The honest weakness: it is curve-fitted on only 3-4 cycles, says nothing about volatility-as-stat or correlations, and the underlying four-year cycle may itself be dissolving as ETF/treasury demand (~9,000 BTC/day) dwarfs halving issuance (~450 BTC/day) and the supply shock shrinks (block reward now 0.85% of supply).


*Scores — rigor 2, signal 3, robustness 2, data-ops 4, orthogonality 2. Encodes the correct qualitative shape (appreciation decay) and lands near the honest central band, but it is a geometric curve-fit on only 3-4 cycle tops with zero out-of-sample validation, mechanically tying the forecast to a 4-year halving regime that ETF/treasury demand may already be dissolving. Convergent multi-metric decay evidence lifts signal, yet rigor and regime-survival are weak (same small-n failure mode that broke S2F/Pi-Cycle). Inputs are public and cycle-indexed, so it is trivially easy to maintain in a CMA, but it adds no tail/correlation conditioning beyond a level that the decay anchor already supplies.*


**Key drivers:** Halving cycle index (discrete ~4yr unit) — the independent variable; each halving epoch is one step of the geometric series, NOT continuous calendar time; Cycle-top peak multiple of a long MA: Golden-Ratio Fibonacci bands (21x->5x->3x->~2x) and the Mayer Multiple peak (15x->6x->~3.2x); Inter-cycle decay ratio of peak gains (~69% lower gain each cycle; ~2,000% -> ~630%; alt framing ~50x->20x->7x => ~0.35-0.4x retention); Behavioral profit-taking acceleration: LTH-MVRV peaks compressing (36.2 -> 12.58, ~2.9x reduction); holders now distribute after ~2x moves vs ~4x prior, even 30-50% spikes; 2-Year MA Multiplier envelope (Bitcoin Investor Tool): accumulate < 2yr MA, distribute near 2yr MA x5 — bounds the cycle amplitude; Halving timing regularity (~520-530 days from halving to peak) used to date the projected cycle tops; Shrinking supply-shock magnitude (block subsidy now ~0.85% of supply, ~94% mined) and ETF/treasury flow dominance (~9,000 vs ~450 BTC/day) — the forces eroding the very pattern being extrapolated


**Pros:** Anchors directly to Bitcoin's single most robust empirical regularity — diminishing returns — and encodes appreciation DECAY by construction, which is exactly the shape a credible 10-15yr CMA needs (unlike S2F/Metcalfe/gold-parity, which imply constant or accelerating returns); Multiple independent metrics agree on the decay: Golden-Ratio bands (21->5->3->2), Mayer Multiple peaks (15->6->3.2), LTH-MVRV peaks (36.2->12.58), and raw peak gains (2000%->630%) all compress monotonically — convergent evidence, not a single fitted line; Discrete, geometric, cycle-indexed form is genuinely different from the continuous power-law (P~t^n, 1/age decay) — it ties the slowdown mechanistically to the halving schedule and to observable holder behavior (faster profit-taking) rather than to abstract calendar time; Transparent, falsifiable and refreshable from public data (price, moving averages, on-chain MVRV); each projected cycle-top multiple is an explicit, checkable number; Forward projections it produces (e.g. ~$175k-220k cycle top vs ~$327k needed to match the prior cycle) are sober relative to S2F/power-law millions — the method self-limits the bull case


**Cons:** Curve-fit on a tiny sample — only 3-4 completed halving cycles define the entire decay series; extrapolating a geometric ratio from 3 points across 2-3 FUTURE cycles is severe small-n overfitting with no out-of-sample validation, the same flaw that broke S2F and the MVRV/Pi-Cycle top indicators post-2021; The pattern it extrapolates may already be dissolving. ETF + treasury demand (~9,000 BTC/day) dwarfs halving issuance (~450 BTC/day, a ~20x imbalance), the supply shock has shrunk to 0.85% of supply (~94% mined), and Bernstein/Fidelity argue institutional flows have SUPERSEDED the halving — so the 4-year cycle that the whole method is indexed on may no longer exist (the 2024-25 cycle is already called a 'first major break'); The decay ratio is unidentified and chosen ad hoc: is next-cycle gain 0.30x, 0.35x or 0.50x of the prior? The framings disagree (69% gain-reduction vs the 21->5->3 band sequence vs 50x->20x->7x), and the 10-15yr CAGR is highly sensitive to which ratio you pick — the central number is a judgment dressed as a measured law; Says nothing about volatility-as-a-statistic or about ANY cross-asset correlation (growth/value equities, FI, TIPS, gold) — it is a price-amplitude model only, so most CMA cells must be imported from realized data; Reflexive / endogenous metrics: Mayer and MVRV are transforms of past price, so the 'multiples' are not independent fundamentals; a regime shift (e.g. a permanent lower-vol grind) breaks the calibration, and the bands have already been quietly re-parameterized downward; Pure timing/amplitude heritage: the 2-Year MA Multiplier and Golden-Ratio tools were built as cycle-TIMING oscillators (when to buy/sell), not forward return forecasters — repurposing them as a decade-CMA decay extrapolator is a category stretch the careful authors do not fully endorse

METHODOLOGY. This is the crypto-desk formalization of Bitcoin's most durable empirical regularity — diminishing returns — into a DISCRETE, geometric, halving-cycle-indexed decay of cycle-top amplitude. It is distinct from the continuous power-law (#5, P~t^n with 1/age decay): there the independent variable is calendar age and the slowdown is smooth; here the independent variable is the halving cycle index (a ~4-year integer unit), the slowdown is a step-function geometric series, and the mechanism is tied to the halving schedule and to observable holder behavior rather than abstract time. The list previously captured the underlying tools (2-Year MA Multiplier, Golden-Ratio/Mayer/MVRV) only as timing OSCILLATORS; this entry is their use as a forward-CMA decay EXTRAPOLATOR.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / NUMBERS. The decay shows up in four convergent metrics, all from Bitcoin Magazine Pro and adjacent desks: (1) Golden-Ratio Multiplier — cycle tops printed at the 21x band (2013), 5x (2017), 3x (2021), and ~2x/1.6x (2024-25), each a Fibonacci-spaced fraction of a 350-day MA. (2) Mayer Multiple peaks fell 15x (2013) -> 6x (2021), with a linear trendline implying ~3.2x for the current cycle. (3) Long-Term-Holder MVRV peaked 36.2 (2017) -> 12.58 (2021), a ~2.9x reduction, with Supply-Adjusted Coin-Days-Destroyed showing holders now take profit after ~2x moves vs ~4x prior, even on 30-50% spikes — a behavioral micro-foundation for the decay. (4) Raw peak gains: ~2,000%+ last cycle -> ~630% this cycle (~69% reduction); an alternative framing is ~50x -> ~20x -> ~7x. Halving-to-peak timing is ~520-530 days, used to date the projected tops.

ON-RECORD FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Bitcoin Magazine Pro projected a ~$175k-220k cycle top (1.6x-2x bands on a ~$70k 200-week MA, or a 3.2x Mayer Multiple), explicitly noting BTC would need ~$327k 'a stretch that looks increasingly unlikely' to match the prior cycle's magnitude. The Nasdaq 'Mathematically Forecasting Peak' framing uses the diminishing-multiple logic to derive next-cycle peaks; consensus diminishing-returns 2030 levels cluster ~$150k-300k (vs the $1M Wood/Saylor digital-gold ceiling, which is NOT a cycle-decay output). Crucially, none of these primary sources publish a 10-15yr ANNUALIZED CMA — they publish per-cycle top levels. The annualized number is my synthesis: extrapolating a ~0.35-0.45x inter-cycle gain-retention ratio across the ~2028/2032/2036 halvings and annualizing spot-to-horizon lands ~9-13% nominal (center ~11%), consistent with the realized-decay path and the honest cross-approach central of 8-12%.

HISTORICAL FIT. In-sample the decay is the best-fitting single regularity in BTC's history — monotone across every metric, every cycle, with no exceptions through 2021. That is its strength relative to S2F (which broke spectacularly post-2021) and naive Metcalfe.

FAILURE MODES — be brutal. (1) Tiny sample: 3-4 cycles define the entire series; extrapolating a geometric ratio across 2-3 FUTURE cycles is the same small-n overfitting that discredited S2F, Pi-Cycle and MVRV-Z tops. (2) The pattern may already be dead: post-2024, ETF+treasury demand (~9,000 BTC/day) dwarfs halving issuance (~450 BTC/day, ~20x imbalance); the block subsidy is now 0.85% of supply with ~94% mined, so the supply shock is negligible; Bernstein (Chhugani) and Fidelity argue institutional flows have SUPERSEDED the halving and the 2024-25 cycle is the 'first major break.' If the 4-year cycle dissolves, the index this method runs on ceases to exist and the extrapolation is meaningless. (3) Ratio indeterminacy: 0.30x vs 0.45x retention swings the CAGR by several points — the central number is judgment, not a measured law. (4) Reflexivity: Mayer and MVRV are transforms of past price, not independent fundamentals; the bands have already been re-parameterized downward. (5) Silence on vol-as-stat and on all correlations — the method populates only the appreciation cell natively; vol (~55%) and the correlation vector (growth ~0.50, value ~0.35, FI ~0.18, TIPS ~0.30, gold ~0.05) are imported from realized data. NET: a useful DECAY-SHAPE discipline and a sober antidote to S2F/power-law millions, but it must NOT be treated as a precise long-horizon law, and its own seed sources concede the cycle it indexes may be ending.

### #36 · Portfolio Sizing / Risk-Budget Allocation

*Family: portfolio-sizing · Source: Asset manager · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 47*


**Explanation:** This family declines to forecast Bitcoin's return at all. Instead it sizes BTC as a small satellite by its marginal contribution to total portfolio risk — volatility times correlation times weight — and solves for the weight that keeps BTC's share of portfolio risk at a tolerable level. The key inputs are BTC's standalone volatility (assumed to decay as it matures), its low-but-rising correlation to a 60/40, and a reference risk anchor: BlackRock benchmarks a BTC sleeve to a single Magnificent-7 stock and shows a 1% weight contributes ~2% of portfolio risk, 2%=>~5%, 4%=>~14%, which caps the 'reasonable' band at 1-2%. CoinShares frames it as ~3.6-4% per +100-120bps of added risk budget. For a 10-15yr CMA the family contributes only the risk envelope, not the return: expected appreciation must be imported from another approach. Its implicit CMA view is high volatility (~55-60%) decaying slowly, near-zero gold correlation, and a sleeve sized so even total loss is survivable.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 4, orthogonality 2. Methodologically the cleanest framing here — it refuses to fabricate a return and sizes on estimable risk inputs, satisfying scripted-analysis discipline (high rigor, easy data ops from a covariance matrix). But as a standalone CMA it produces no return forecast, so its predictive signal for a 10-15yr appreciation figure is weak — the ~8-12% number is admitted judgment, not output. Robustness is mid: vol-decay is an unverifiable assumption and the load-bearing correlation input is non-stationary (0 to ~0.56 post-ETF), which directly erodes the diversification premise the sizing relies on, though risk-budgeting itself degrades gracefully rather than breaking like S2F.*


**Key drivers:** BTC standalone annualized volatility (and its assumed decay path as the asset matures) — the dominant input; BTC's correlation to the existing 60/40 (low but rising and unstable, especially post-2021/post-ETF); The allocation weight itself, solved so BTC's marginal risk contribution hits a target (e.g. 2-5% of total portfolio risk); A reference risk anchor — BlackRock benchmarks to a single Magnificent-7 stock (~4% of portfolio risk); Investor's chosen incremental risk budget (CoinShares: +100bps annualized risk => ~3.6% weight); Rebalancing rule (CoinShares: quarterly, funded equally from stocks and bonds); Survivability / max-drawdown tolerance — the allocation is sized so a -100% BTC outcome is bearable; Expected return is deliberately NOT a driver — the method is return-agnostic by construction


**Pros:** Honest about what is knowable: BTC's risk (vol, correlation) is far more estimable than its 10-15yr return, so sizing on risk rather than a fabricated return forecast is methodologically cleaner than S2F/Metcalfe/DCF-style models; Naturally caps tail damage — a 1-2% sleeve makes even a total loss a survivable drag, which suits an asset with genuine ruin risk; Empirically grounded and reproducible: risk contributions are computed from a covariance matrix on real return data, satisfying the scripted-analysis discipline; Asset-manager versions (BlackRock, CoinShares, Grayscale) are institutionally vetted and widely adopted as the de facto framing for advisor allocations; Framework-agnostic to the bull/bear return debate — usable by skeptics and believers alike since it doesn't require endorsing a price target; Directly answers the practical question an allocator actually asks ('how much?') rather than the unanswerable one ('what's fair value?')


**Cons:** It is NOT a return model — it cannot, by itself, produce the expected-appreciation figure a CMA requires; you must bolt on a return assumption from another family, so as a standalone CMA approach it is incomplete; Garbage-in on volatility and correlation: estimates are dominated by a short, regime-unstable sample (BTC ETPs only since ~2015), and the assumed vol-decay path is an unverifiable assumption that drives the whole answer; Correlation is the load-bearing input and it is non-stationary: BTC-S&P rolling correlation jumped from ~0 to ~0.5-0.7 post-2021/post-ETF, eroding the diversification premise the sizing relies on — the 'low correlation' that justifies a 2% slot may not persist; Risk-budgeting tacitly assumes a positive (or at least non-negative) Sharpe; if BTC's forward return is poor, an 'optimally risk-sized' allocation still loses money — right-sizing the risk does not make the bet good; Mean-variance / risk-parity optimizers are notoriously sensitive to input error and routinely corner-solution into BTC when fed high historical returns, so backtested 'optimal' weights overstate the case (in-sample overfitting); Asset-manager sources have a conflict of interest (BlackRock IBIT, Grayscale, CoinShares all sell BTC products) — the 1-2% 'reasonable' framing is marketing-adjacent, not peer-reviewed; Says little about gold specifically: treats BTC's near-zero gold correlation as a feature without resolving whether BTC competes with or complements a gold sleeve in the same risk budget

DEFINING FEATURE: This family answers 'how much?' not 'what return?'. Its CMA contribution is a risk-budget envelope, not an appreciation estimate — a critical distinction for the lit review. Any appreciation/correlation numbers attributed to it are either (a) empirical inputs it consumes or (b) my own bolt-on judgments, never native model outputs.\n\nBLACKROCK INVESTMENT INSTITUTE, 'Sizing Bitcoin in Portfolios' (Dec 2024): The flagship asset-manager statement. Method = risk budgeting / risk contribution. A 1-2% BTC allocation lifts BTC's share of TOTAL portfolio risk to ~2-5%, 'in line with the average Magnificent Seven tech stock, which contributes ~4% of portfolio risk' in a 60/40. A 2% weight 'produces a similar amount of risk as the Magnificent Seven.' Beyond 2% the risk share rises disproportionately: a 4% BTC allocation = ~14% of portfolio risk. Explicitly NO expected-return figure published. Volatility framed qualitatively via price swings ($67k->$17k in 2021/22; $43k->$103k in 2024). Caveat (their own): the allocation only makes sense if you 'believe it will become more widely adopted' and can 'bear the risk of rapid price plunges.' CONFLICT NOTE: BlackRock issues IBIT — the largest spot BTC ETF — so the '2% is reasonable' framing is product-aligned, not peer-reviewed.\n\nCOINSHARES, 'Bitcoin Risk Budgeting for Portfolios' (2021): Most explicit risk-budget mechanics. Baseline 60/40, add BTC by detracting equally from stocks AND bonds, quarterly rebalance. Linear risk-contribution scaling: +100bps annualized risk => ~3.6% BTC weight; +120bps => 4%; +200bps => 5%. Backtest from Oct-2015 (BTC ETP availability); results 'consistent across 1-5yr windows.' Authors flag that future vol will likely fall and 'both expected future volatility and historical volatility should be taken into consideration' — i.e. they themselves caution against extrapolating historical vol, which is exactly the decay assumption my synthesized vol (~45-55%) honors. CONFLICT NOTE: CoinShares is a crypto asset manager.\n\nKAJTAZI & MORO, MDPI Risks/JRFM 2021, 'Bitcoin and Portfolio Diversification: A Portfolio Optimization Approach': The peer-reviewed mean-variance counterpart (could not fetch full text — 403; characterized from prior knowledge of this widely-cited paper). Finds adding a small BTC weight improves the efficient frontier (raises returns more than risk) across US/EU/China portfolios, with the diversification benefit coming from LOW correlation rather than from BTC's own return — and warns the optimizer's BTC weight is sensitive to the (high, historical) return input. This is the academic caution against in-sample corner solutions.\n\nKUMAR, MOHAN & NIVEDITHA, SAGE 2025, rolling-window DCC-GARCH (data Jan-2018..Oct-2022; S&P500, CAC40, NSE50): Core finding for the GOLD comparison central to the digital-gold thesis — 'Gold is the better safe haven; Bitcoin exhibits weak safe-haven characteristics but can be used as a diversifier and hedge.' BTC-S&P correlation: positive-but-insignificant 2018-19, negative/significant briefly in 2019, negligible during the Mar-2020 crash, strong-safe-haven only transiently in the Ukraine episode. Upshot: BTC's diversification value is real but REGIME-DEPENDENT and weaker than gold's. No explicit BTC-gold correlation reported.\n\nPOST-2021 CORRELATION BREAK (load-bearing critique): Multiple trackers (Phemex, Nasdaq, Newhedge) show BTC-S&P rolling correlation climbing from ~0 pre-2021 to ~0.5 post-ETF and ~0.74-0.94 in stress windows. METHODOLOGY. Jeffrey Snider (Alhambra Partners; "Eurodollar University") is a practitioner macro analyst, not an academic, and his BTC view is a corollary of his eurodollar framework rather than a standalone valuation model. The core claim: the operative global dollar system is the private, offshore, ledger-money "eurodollar" network, which since 2008 has been chronically short of money and — critically — short of PRISTINE, rehypothecatable collateral (on-the-run Treasuries/T-bills). This produces a "deflationary collateral path," and the binding macro problem is currency/credit INELASTICITY, not debasement. Bitcoin enters as "ghost money": a natural, market-driven response to monetary shortfall, explicitly analogized to medieval bills of exchange during the Great Bullion Famine. The distinctive, non-redundant feature versus every other entry in the digest is the CONTRARIAN SIGN: the dollar is NOT collapsing, "money printing" is "more PR than policy," bank reserves are inert, and the inflationist premise underwriting the M2-elasticity, gold-parity, and debasement-hedge theses is — in Snider's view — simply wrong.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / QUOTES. From "Monetary Wrongness Has Authored a Crypto Response" (RealClearMarkets, 2021), Snider frames crypto as a response to "the central bank response to an otherwise severe and constraining monetary shortage," and dismisses the debasement fear: those inflationary outcomes "never happen." He cites the 2017→2018 episode directly — when "the dollar instead caught its Euro$ #4 bid, renewed acute shortage, Bitcoin's price sunk like a rock" — which is the framework's one durable, falsifiable empirical regularity: BTC is WEAK during acute dollar/collateral shortages. He calls bubbles "a minor if ugly detail in an otherwise very familiar, ultimately successful longer-term story." In "Bitcoin, El Salvador, And…The Eurodollar's Ghost" (2021) he is openly skeptical of BTC as an imminent eurodollar replacement: "Cryptos are (long run, not short run) ghost money… the eurodollar, the true reserve, isn't going anywhere for quite a long time." This is the load-bearing nuance: the framework is bearish-to-neutral on BTC's near/medium-term monetary role and constructive only on a multi-decade ghost-money S-curve.

THE COLLATERAL CHANNEL. The "BTC-as-collateral" leg that makes this approach distinct (a haircut/rehypothecation, collateral-QUALITY premium) is largely LATENT for bitcoin. Snider's collateral analysis is about Treasuries; BTC is essentially not accepted as pristine repo collateral in size, and its volatility makes the haircut prohibitive. So the most novel mechanism is a possibility, not a current price driver — and a fair CMA cannot lean on it.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The framework's central macro call was persistently, decisively WRONG on 2021-2022: Snider forecast deflation/disinflation and a dollar shortage precisely as US CPI peaked near 9%. Because the deflationary-collateral premise is the model's beam, a CMA built on it inherits that fragility. Austrian critics (DyingEconomy.com) argue the causality is inverted — "the world's problem since 1971 has not been too little money but too much credit," deflation is "the market's belated attempt to liquidate malinvestment," and post-2020 inflation falsified the shortage thesis. Mainstream readers note BTC's behavior is at least as consistent with a plain high-beta-risk-asset story as with a bespoke eurodollar mechanism. The honest read: Snider supplies a mechanism and a sign, not a number; the sign (dollar strength, BTC weak in shortages) has mixed-to-poor recent fit.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None numeric. Snider is structurally forecast-averse and publishes NO BTC price target, return, vol, or correlation. The only on-record multi-year claim is qualitative directional: crypto survives long-run as ghost money ("ultimately successful longer-term story"), but the eurodollar remains the true reserve "for quite a long time," and BTC should sink during dollar-shortage episodes. There is therefore no published CMA to cite — all numeric cells are "n/a (source silent)," and the synthesized grid is anchored to the realized decay baseline with the framework supplying only the contrarian haircut (appreciation toward the LOW end, ~6-10% nominal) and the disorder-driven high-vol (~55-65%) and high-equity-correlation (+0.45 to +0.60) tilts, which the mechanism genuinely predicts. The BTC-gold correlation stays near zero — and, unlike the digital-gold theses, that is CONSISTENT with Snider's framing of BTC and gold as parallel symptoms of one monetary shortage rather than substitutes.
