### #38 · Convenience-Yield / Theory-of-Storage Commodity Valuation

*Family: convenience-yield · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 46*


**Explanation:** This framework borrows the commodity theory of storage. The cost-of-carry identity says a futures price equals spot grossed up by financing and storage, minus a convenience yield — the intangible benefit of holding the physical asset now. For Bitcoin, storage is roughly zero, so the convenience yield is essentially the negative of the annualized futures basis net of the risk-free rate. Backing it out gives BTC's only quasi-'dividend': estimates of ~2.35%/yr (Hilliard-Ngo) to ~5.4% (Kim), attributed to short-sale constraints and governance/voting rights. The structural step plugs this into a Gibson-Schwartz two-factor model where the spot is geometric and the convenience yield mean-reverts, jointly pricing futures and options. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this is sobering, not bullish: the convenience yield is small and, crucially, frequently NEGATIVE (an 'inconvenience yield' during stress — BTC traded at -95% annualized convenience during COVID). So this channel implies BTC behaves like a volatile industrial commodity with a modest, unstable carry — it cannot justify high appreciation, only a low-single-digit holding-utility component embedded in a high-vol price process.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Theoretically strong (Gibson-Schwartz, Hilliard-Ngo out-of-sample option support) so rigor is high, but it is a relative-pricing/forward-curve tool that treats spot drift as exogenous — it cannot produce a 10-15yr appreciation number, so empirical signal for the level CMA needs is weak. The backed-out convenience yield is small, frequently negative (-1.4% full sample, -9.5% COVID, range -165% to +90%) and basis-dependent, so it breaks down across regimes (low robustness). Data is live futures/options (available) but option-implied estimation is operationally heavier than a simple proxy. Its genuine contribution is conditioning — a defensible high-jump-vol case and the strongest evidence-based argument for low gold correlation — not the appreciation level.*


**Key drivers:** Annualized futures-spot basis (the observable input): cy ≈ r + storage − (1/(T−t))·ln(F/S); for BTC storage≈0, so cy is mainly the negative of the basis net of the risk-free rate; Short-sale constraints in spot BTC markets — the primary documented source of positive convenience yield (Kim): hard-to-borrow spot makes prices 'downward sticky', creating a holding premium; On-chain governance / voting rights — holding spot (not a derivative) confers protocol-vote optionality; Kim finds the holding benefit rises ~+5.6% when an important network proposal is pending; Mean-reversion speed and long-run mean of the convenience yield in the Gibson-Schwartz OU process (κ, α) — governs how the carry evolves and how the forward curve is shaped over the horizon; Inventory / scarcity state: like industrial metals, BTC's convenience yield is more volatile and more often negative when 'inventory' (exchange balances / liquidity) is low or during crisis (theory-of-storage state dependence); Jump intensity and jump size (Hilliard-Ngo): BTC's return process has significant jumps; the convenience-yield estimate is conditional on a jump-diffusion spot dynamic, not pure GBM; Funding/leverage demand: in crypto the basis is dominated by perpetual-funding and leverage demand (contango), so the 'convenience yield' partly reflects positioning/segmentation, not pure holding utility (BIS crypto-carry critique)


**Pros:** Gives BTC a genuine, observable, market-priced quasi-dividend — the convenience yield is backed out of live futures/option prices, not asserted; it is the closest thing a cashflow-less asset has to a yield, and it plugs cleanly into a CMA as expected return ≈ rf + risk premium − cy; Theoretically rigorous and well-established: Gibson-Schwartz (1990) is a 1,000+-citation commodity-pricing standard, and Hilliard-Ngo show the jump-diffusion-plus-convenience-yield model significantly outperforms practitioner Black-Scholes on Deribit BTC options — so the commodity framing has real out-of-sample option-pricing support; Honest about magnitude: unlike scarcity/Metcalfe narratives, this framework produces a SMALL number (~2-5%), implicitly conceding BTC has no large structural carry — a useful discipline that argues AGAINST the 65-140% appreciation extrapolations; State-dependence is informative: the finding that BTC's convenience yield is more volatile and often negative in low-inventory/crisis regimes (like an industrial metal, unlike gold) is a direct, evidence-based rebuttal of the naive 'digital gold' thesis and helps set correlation/regime expectations; Decomposes the basis into economic primitives (financing, storage, convenience) rather than treating it as a black-box momentum/sentiment signal — more structural than the crypto-carry positioning family


**Cons:** It is a valuation/relative-pricing tool, NOT a return forecaster: the convenience yield prices the forward curve and options consistently with spot, but says almost nothing about the spot's own expected drift (μ). A CMA needs the appreciation rate, which this framework treats as exogenous — so it cannot produce a 10-15yr appreciation number on its own; The estimated convenience yield is small AND frequently negative ('inconvenience yield'): full-sample mean ≈ −1.4%, COVID mean ≈ −9.5%, range −165% to +90% annualized (Aharon et al.). A 'dividend' that is often negative and wildly unstable is a poor structural building block and contradicts the 'positive holding benefit' framing; The basis is contaminated by leverage/funding demand and market segmentation, not pure holding utility: BIS crypto-carry work shows the BTC basis is dominated by perpetual-funding and arbitrage-capital constraints (contango from leverage demand), so what gets labeled 'convenience yield' is partly a positioning/financing artifact — backing out a structural holding benefit from it risks mislabeling noise; Estimates are fragile and disagree by ~2x across studies (2.35% vs 5.4%) depending on data window, exchange, and whether option-implied or futures-implied; the convenience yield is not a stable parameter; Silent on every other CMA cell: the literature publishes no appreciation, no annualized volatility figure, and no cross-asset correlations (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) — all distributional and correlation inputs must be imported from realized data; Theory-of-storage assumes meaningful 'inventory' and storage economics; BTC's storage cost is ~0 and 'inventory' (exchange balances) is a weak, manipulable analogue, so the commodity mapping is partly metaphorical and the convenience yield loses its classical interpretation

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. The approach imports the commodity theory of storage (Kaldor 1939, Working 1949, Brennan 1958; formalized in continuous time by Gibson-Schwartz 1990). The cost-of-carry identity is F(t,T) = S(t)·exp[(r + w − cy)(T−t)], where r is financing, w is storage, and cy is the convenience yield — the flow of non-pecuniary benefits from holding the physical asset rather than a forward claim. Inverting: cy = r + w − (1/(T−t))·ln(F/S). For Bitcoin storage w≈0, so the convenience yield is essentially the negative of the annualized futures basis adjusted for the risk-free rate. The structural valuation embeds cy in a two-factor stochastic process (Gibson-Schwartz): spot S follows geometric Brownian motion while cy follows a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dδ = κ(α−δ)dt + σ_δ dW, with the two innovations correlated. This jointly prices the entire forward curve and options. Hilliard-Ngo (2022) extend the spot to a JUMP-diffusion and show, on Deribit option data, that the jump-diffusion-with-convenience-yield model 'significantly outperforms Practitioner Black-Scholes,' concluding 'Bitcoin behaves more like a commodity than a currency.'

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & MAGNITUDES. Three studies pin the number, and they disagree by design because they use different instruments and windows: (1) Hilliard-Ngo estimate an average annual convenience yield ~2.35% from option/jump-diffusion fitting. (2) Kim (2022, FRL) finds the BTC spot trades at a 5.4% premium to futures — the convenience yield — sourced to short-sale constraints ('spot prices are downward sticky') and on-chain voting rights, with the holding benefit rising an additional +5.6% when an important network proposal is pending. (3) Aharon et al. (2023, COVID paper) compute cy directly from cost-of-carry and find it is frequently NEGATIVE: full-sample mean −1.4%, pre-COVID +1.6%, during-COVID −9.5%, with an astonishing range of −165% to +90% annualized. Critically, they show BTC's convenience yield is more volatile in low-inventory periods and behaves like an INDUSTRIAL metal, whereas gold's convenience yield is far more stable (mean −2.0%, range −26% to +16%).

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT, AND WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR A CMA. This is the only framework in the digest that gives BTC a genuine market-priced quasi-dividend. But as a CMA building block its honest message is deflationary, not bullish. The convenience yield prices the forward curve; it does NOT forecast spot drift. The CMA contribution is a small carry term in E[return] ≈ rf + risk premium − cy, and because cy averages roughly zero-to-slightly-negative over a full cycle, it neither powers nor explains the historical 65-140% appreciation. So this lens implicitly endorses a LOW, decaying appreciation (I synthesize ~8-11% nominal), a HIGH jump-driven volatility (~55-62% — the framework needs jumps, so vol-compression skepticism is well-grounded), and — most usefully — a LOW gold correlation: the industrial-metal carry profile co-moves with the cycle (toward equities, realized ~0.56), not with gold's safe-haven profile. The theory-of-storage evidence is thus an evidence-based REBUTTAL of 'digital gold,' aligning with realized BTC-gold ≈ 0.

FAILURE MODES & CRITIQUES (faithfully). First, it is a relative-pricing tool masquerading as valuation — it cannot output appreciation, which is exactly the cell a CMA most needs. Second, the 'convenience yield' is contaminated: the BIS 'Crypto carry' work (2023) argues the BTC basis is dominated by perpetual-funding/leverage demand and arbitrage-capital segmentation (contango from leverage demand), so backing out a structural 'holding benefit' from the basis risks relabeling a financing/positioning artifact as economic utility. Third, the number is unstable and often negative — a 'dividend' ranging −165% to +90% is not a usable structural parameter. Fourth, theory-of-storage presupposes meaningful inventory and storage economics; BTC's storage≈0 and 'inventory' (exchange balances) is a weak, gameable analogue, so the commodity mapping is partly metaphorical. Fifth, the literature is silent on volatility-as-a-statistic and on every cross-asset correlation, so the distributional half of the CMA must be borrowed wholesale from realized data.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. No author has used the convenience-yield/theory-of-storage framework to publish a multi-year BTC price or return forecast. Hilliard-Ngo, Kim, Gibson-Schwartz, and Aharon et al. are all relative-pricing/option-pricing/empirical papers, not capital-market-assumption documents. (Provenance note: the seed misattributed the Quantitative Finance paper to 'Hofmann, Maier & Reinerth'; the verified authors are Jimmy E. Hilliard and Julie T. D. Ngo, QF 22(11), 2079-2091.)

### #39 · Derivatives-Microstructure: Perp Funding, Cross-Rail Basis Segmentation & Price Discovery (Crypto Carry)

*Family: derivatives-microstructure · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 46*


**Explanation:** Bitcoin's derivatives complex emits three measurable signals. Perpetual-swap funding (paid every 8 hours to keep the perp pinned to spot) proxies leveraged long demand; its base is ~11%/yr but it spikes to triple digits in manias. The cross-rail wedge is the ~2.6%/yr gap between ETF-option-implied carry and CME-futures carry, persisting because segmented margin/collateral rails block cross-margining and starve arbitrage capital (limits-of-arbitrage). Price discovery — Hasbrouck information share — locates where the efficient price forms; post-ETF it has shifted toward CME. The pivotal academic result (Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov) is a warning, not a return: carry reaches 40-60%/yr, is unexplained by fundamentals, reflects a volatile convenience yield from trend-chasers plus scarce arbitrage capital, is NOT a risk premium on spot, and HIGH carry predicts CRASHES (a non-additive drift). For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this framework therefore mainly CONSTRAINS others: it forbids adding basis/funding to expected spot return, raises the volatility/tail estimate via forced-liquidation cascades, and says nothing structural about gold.


*Scores — rigor 5, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Top-tier peer-reviewed microstructure foundation (BIS/Mgmt Science, Hasbrouck JF 1995) earns a 5 on rigor, and its rigorous negative result usefully disciplines carry-as-drift errors. But signal for a 10-15yr spot return is weak (2): it generates NO native appreciation forecast and explicitly shows carry does not predict positive returns. Robustness is mid (3) given short, regime-unstable samples (perps 2016+, ETF 2024+, 386-obs wedge) that may compress, though the vol/tail conditioning is durable. Data_ops mid (3): funding/basis data exist but Hasbrouck shares and cross-rail wedge require nontrivial assembly. Value is conditioning the vol/tail cells, not anchoring the level.*


**Key drivers:** Perpetual-swap funding rate (8-hour rebalancing payment): base ~0.01%/8hr ≈ 10.95%/yr, spiking to 200%+ annualized in bull manias; proxies leveraged-long demand and trend-chasing convenience yield; Dated-futures / cash-and-carry basis level (crypto carry): up to 40-60%/yr, highly time-varying, unexplained by observable fundamentals; Cross-rail basis WEDGE: ~2.58% mean / 2.52% median annualized gap between IBIT-ETF-options-implied carry and matched CME-futures carry (Mallory 2026, 386 obs); SD ~4.7%; Limits-of-arbitrage / market segmentation: inability to cross-margin spot BTC, CME futures, and ETF-options across distinct collateral systems; scarcity of arbitrage capital due to regulatory/margin frictions; Marginal-trader composition: small trend-chasing leveraged longs (perp demand) vs. constrained arbitrageurs (cash-and-carry shorts) — the demand/supply imbalance that sets carry; Hasbrouck (1995) information share / Gonzalo-Granger component share: WHERE the efficient price is formed (CME futures vs spot ETFs vs offshore perps); transaction size as a leadership determinant; Crash-risk / convenience-yield channel: high carry co-moves with the price of crash-risk insurance and PREDICTS future crashes — the non-additive-drift caveat; Forced-liquidation / excess-volatility mechanism: mark-to-market losses on short futures before convergence trigger liquidation cascades, amplifying realized vol


**Pros:** Built on genuinely high-quality, peer-reviewed microstructure scholarship (BIS / Management Science; Hasbrouck JF 1995) and current ETF-era data — not crypto-native numerology like S2F or Metcalfe; Supplies a rare, rigorous NEGATIVE result that protects a CMA from a real error: it proves the futures basis / funding 'yield' is NOT additive to expected spot return (high carry predicts crashes, not gains), directly disciplining carry-as-drift approaches; Directly informative for the volatility and tail cells of a CMA: documents excess futures volatility, forced-liquidation cascades, and a measurable crash-risk-insurance linkage — mechanisms that justify keeping the vol floor high; Falsifiable and refreshable: funding rates, the cross-rail wedge, and information shares are all computable in near-real-time from public/exchange data, so the regime read can be updated continuously; Illuminates the marginal-buyer/seller structure (trend-chasing leveraged longs vs. constrained arbitrageurs), which underpins BTC's rising equity/risk-asset correlation better than supply-only models


**Cons:** Not a primary return model: this framework produces NO native long-horizon appreciation forecast for spot BTC — the appreciation number must be borrowed from another approach, so it can only constrain/adjust, not anchor, a CMA; The headline carry result is explicitly that carry does NOT predict positive spot returns (it predicts crashes), so naive practitioners who add 'basis yield' or 'funding income' to BTC's expected return are committing exactly the error the literature refutes — high abuse potential; Short, regime-unstable samples: perpetuals (2016+), spot ETFs (2024+), and the cross-rail wedge (2025-26, 386 obs) all post-date most of BTC's history; the segmentation wedge may compress sharply as CME moves to 24/7 trading and rails integrate, so today's ~2.6% is not a structural constant; Price-discovery findings are method- and period-dependent and contradictory: Hasbrouck IS studies variously crown CME futures (Kapar-Olmo), the spot market (Baur-Dimpfl; Corbet et al.), or 'no single price setter' — there is no settled answer to WHERE price is formed; Cross-asset correlation content is thin: the literature is essentially silent on BTC vs. gold/TIPS/value-equity correlations, so those CMA cells get almost no structural guidance from this approach; A cash-and-carry / basis-harvest STRATEGY return (a real ~5-15%/yr market-neutral yield) is a fund product, not a property of BTC the asset — conflating the two would mis-specify a long-only BTC CMA

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

WHAT IT IS. This is a microstructure family that reads Bitcoin's derivatives complex as three distinct objects, deliberately separating them from approach #17's treatment of the dated-futures basis as a simple carry/yield input. (1) PERPETUAL FUNDING: the perp swap has no expiry; an 8-hour funding payment keeps it pinned to spot. Offshore base is ~0.01%/8hr (≈10.95%/yr), but in bull manias funding has spiked above 0.2%/8hr (>200% annualized). Funding is a near-real-time gauge of leveraged-long demand. (2) CROSS-RAIL WEDGE: Mallory (2026, arXiv:2605.29309) recovers an ETF-implied forward from put-call parity on IBIT options, maps ETF shares to BTC via BlackRock's daily holdings file, benchmarks against BRRNY, and compares the implied carry to matched CME-futures carry. Across 386 date-bucket obs the mean wedge is 2.58%, median 2.52%, SD 4.72% (annualized). She attributes it to 'friction resulting from inability to cross margin spot bitcoin and CME futures' — segmented collateral systems that 'do not recognize offsetting risk,' a clean limits-of-arbitrage result. (3) PRICE DISCOVERY: Hasbrouck (1995) information share and Gonzalo-Granger component share locate the efficient price. Findings are method/period-dependent — Kapar-Olmo (2019, daily) crown CME futures; Baur-Dimpfl and Corbet et al. crown spot; recent multi-market work (20 spot, 26 futures venues) finds CME futures lead with transaction size as the key determinant; post-ETF commentary describes discovery 'moving to Chicago' as CME underpins ETF hedging and moves toward 24/7 trading.

THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT (and the reason this is a distinct CMA entry). Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov, 'Crypto Carry' (BIS WP1087 2023; Management Science 2026), show crypto carry — the cash-and-carry return, long spot/short futures — reaches up to 40-60%/yr, varies strongly, and 'cannot be explained by observable fundamental factors.' Their interpretation: a 'highly volatile crypto convenience yield' from 'trend-chasing and attention by smaller investors seeking leveraged upside exposure… in boom periods,' plus 'the relative scarcity of arbitrage capital taking the other side.' The CMA-critical finding: carry is NOT a compensation for spot risk, and 'a high crypto carry predicts future price crashes and a rise in carry typically goes hand in hand with a rise in the price of crash risk insurance.' This is the non-additive-drift caveat: you cannot add the futures basis or funding 'yield' to BTC's expected spot return — if anything, an elevated basis is a bearish forward signal for spot. That directly refutes the common practitioner move of treating BTC's persistent contango as a structural tailwind.

HOW IT FEEDS A 10-15yr CMA. It does NOT produce a primary appreciation number; treating it as one is a category error. Its three contributions are: (a) a GUARDRAIL — forbid carry-additive drift; the basis/funding is a microstructure premium for leverage/insurance, not spot expected return; (b) a VOLATILITY argument — documented 'excess volatility of crypto futures relative to spot,' forced-liquidation cascades (short-futures mark-to-market losses before convergence), and the crash-risk-insurance linkage all argue for keeping the vol estimate at/above the realized ~57% floor rather than compressing it; (c) a CORRELATION-STRUCTURE story — the marginal buyer is a leveraged trend-chaser funded via perps, which mechanistically ties BTC to risk-on/liquidity regimes and supports a positive, possibly rising, equity correlation (realized 5y +0.56). On gold the framework is silent and supplies no co-movement mechanism, so it leaves BTC-gold at ~0.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTICISM. (1) Regime instability: perpetuals date to ~2016, spot ETFs to 2024, the cross-rail wedge to 2025-26 — none spans a full BTC history, and CME's move to 24/7 plus rail integration could collapse the ~2.6% wedge, so it is not a structural constant. (2) Strategy-vs-asset conflation: the cash-and-carry basis harvest is a real market-neutral fund yield (~5-15%/yr historically), but that belongs to a delta-hedged STRATEGY, not to long-only BTC — importing it into a BTC asset CMA double-counts. (3) Price-discovery is unsettled and contradictory across studies; 'where price is formed' has no canonical answer. (4) Thin cross-asset content: the literature gives almost no guidance on gold/TIPS/value correlations.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY: none. By construction this family publishes basis/funding/wedge levels and information shares, not multi-year BTC price targets. Its honest CMA footprint is a constraint layer, not a forecast — which is precisely its value: it is the one approach in the digest that actively PREVENTS an overstated appreciation by ruling out carry-additive drift, while reinforcing a high vol floor and a risk-on equity correlation.

### #40 · Variance/Jump Risk-Premium & SDF-Implied Physical Return (P-vs-Q, VRP, SVCJ)

*Family: options-risk-premium-extraction · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 45*


**Explanation:** The option market prices BTC under the risk-neutral measure Q; a CMA needs the physical measure P. This family bridges the two. The variance risk premium (Q-variance minus P-variance) is the carry an option seller earns; for BTC it is far larger than equities (Almeida et al.: BVRP ~0.14 vs SPX ~0.02; Alexander & Imeraj first measured the BTC variance-swap VRP off Deribit, building the BVIN index). Martin's (2017) SVIX inequality and the Chabi-Yo-Loudis bound then turn the risk-neutral variance of the whole option surface into a model-free LOWER BOUND on the physical expected excess return, giving an SDF-implied return without a structural model. An SVCJ model (Hou et al. 2020) adds structure: it isolates a priced jump-risk premium from unpriced diffusion and shows BTC price jumps are anti-correlated with volatility jumps. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the key inputs are the current option surface, the persistence/decay of the VRP, and the jump-premium term. The honest caveat: every published number is a 27-day conditional premium (~66%/yr annualized), not a decade forecast — extrapolating it requires aggressive decay assumptions the authors never make.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 3. Theoretically strong (model-free SDF bounds, clean VRP/jump decomposition) so rigor is high, but the 27-day horizon is fatally mismatched to a 10-15yr CMA — the level is pure judgment, not method output, gutting signal. NCC validity for a single speculative asset is doubtful and the bound is regime-fragile, so robustness is low. Deribit-only, young, fragmented option data makes it operationally heavy. Its genuine contribution is second-moment (vol/tail) conditioning, not the return level.*


**Key drivers:** Variance risk premium (VRP) = risk-neutral expected variance (option-implied) minus physical realized variance; BTC BVRP ~0.14 annualized one-month vs SPX ~0.02 — the persistent option-selling carry; Risk-neutral variance of the full option surface (Martin SVIX-style equal-strike weighting) that feeds the model-free lower bound on the physical premium; Martin (2017) negative-correlation-condition lower bound and Chabi-Yo & Loudis higher-order bound translating Q-variance into a floor on the physical equity-style premium (BTC ~65.6% / ~84.8% at one month); SVCJ jump parameters: jump intensity, jump size/volatility, and the priced jump-risk premium vs unpriced diffusion (Hou et al.); anti-correlation of price jumps and volatility jumps; Volatility regime / clustering of the risk-neutral density (Almeida et al. find two vol regimes: high-vol BP lower bound ~78%, low-vol ~44%) — the premium is state-dependent; Persistence and decay path of the VRP and jump premium over the holding horizon — the (untested by the authors) bridge from a 27-day premium to a multi-year CMA; Skew/asymmetry of the risk-neutral density: BTC premium is far more upside-driven than SPX (positive returns contribute ~39-52% of BTC premium vs ~25% for SPX)


**Pros:** Directly answers the question other option-based approaches dodge: it produces a PHYSICAL (P-measure) expected return, not just a risk-neutral forward or RND — the only forward-looking, market-implied estimate of BTC's expected return on this list; Model-free lower bounds (Martin SVIX, Chabi-Yo-Loudis) require minimal assumptions — no return-distribution shape, no growth model — and Martin shows the SPX bound is empirically near-tight (time-series average ~5%, matching realized), lending credibility to the method when applied to BTC; Cleanly separates compensated from uncompensated risk: the VRP isolates the variance-selling carry and the SVCJ decomposition isolates the priced jump premium from unpriced diffusion — a genuinely richer risk picture than vol-only models; Grounded in actual traded option prices (Deribit), refreshable in real time (BVIN/BVRP stream every 15 seconds), so the input is observable and auditable rather than a fitted historical regression; State-aware: the clustering/regime finding gives a conditional premium (high-vol vs low-vol), which is more honest than a single static number and maps onto a CMA scenario framework


**Cons:** Horizon mismatch is fatal for a CMA: every published estimate is a 27-day (one-month) conditional premium annualized to ~66%/yr. These are short-horizon risk-compensation snapshots, NOT 10-15yr expected returns — the authors never forecast a decade, and naively annualizing the option-implied premium massively overstates a long-horizon CMA; The Martin/Chabi-Yo bounds are LOWER bounds that rely on the negative-correlation condition (NCC) between the SDF and the market return; this condition is well-motivated for the broad equity market but is far less obviously valid for a single speculative asset like BTC, so the 'lower bound' interpretation may not hold; Thin, young, fragmented option market: BTC options (mostly Deribit) have a short history (~2017+), wide spreads, limited deep-OTM strikes, and venue concentration — the risk-neutral variance and tail integrals that the bounds need are noisily estimated, and Almeida et al. concede the first-moment premium is 'a noisy measure'; VRP harvestability is asserted by the carry magnitude but not established as a stable, investable long-run premium; the VRP spikes around large moves (Alexander-Imeraj) and became correlated with equity/gold VRP in the pandemic, so the diversifying carry is regime-dependent and can vanish exactly when needed; Says almost nothing directly usable for the correlation cells of a CMA: the paper notes BTC 'largely fluctuated independently of traditional macro-financial markets' and mentions gold only once in passing — no structural BTC-vs-growth/value/FI/TIPS/gold correlation is produced; SVCJ jump-premium estimates are model-dependent (the opposite of the model-free bounds) and sensitive to identification of jumps vs diffusion in a 24/7, microstructure-noisy market

METHODOLOGY. This family answers the one question option-pricing approaches (#11 single-Q-forward/RND, #19 return-process shape) explicitly decline: what is BTC's PHYSICAL (real-world, P-measure) expected return implied by the option surface? It chains four ideas. (1) The variance risk premium (VRP = E^Q[variance] - E^P[variance]) is the carry an option/variance-swap seller earns; Alexander & Imeraj (2021) first measured it for BTC, building a CBOE-VIX-style implied-vol term structure off 15-minute Deribit quotes (now the live BVIN index) and finding the BTC VRP large and spiking before big moves. (2) Martin's (2017) SVIX lower bound and the Chabi-Yo-Loudis higher-order bound convert the risk-neutral variance of the WHOLE option surface into a model-free floor on the physical expected excess return — no distributional assumption needed. Martin showed the SPX bound averages ~5% and is empirically near-tight, which is the credential the whole approach leans on. (3) An SVCJ model (Hou, Wang, Chen & Haerdle 2020, J. Financial Econometrics) adds structure, separating a PRICED jump-risk premium from unpriced diffusion and documenting that BTC price jumps are significantly anti-correlated with volatility jumps. (4) Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024) tie it together for BTC.

KEY NUMBERS (Almeida et al., 27-day horizon, annualized). BTC return premium ~66%/yr; Martin lower bound ~65.64%, Chabi-Yo-Loudis ~84.78% (vs SPX one-month bound ~5% — BTC ~13x). BTC VRP (BVRP) ~0.14 vs SPX ~0.02 (~7x). Risk-neutral variance ~0.72, realized ~0.58, average implied vol ~82%. BTC annualized Sharpe ~0.8 vs SPX ~0.5. A signature finding: BTC's premium is upside-skewed — positive returns (20-60%) contribute 39-52% of the premium vs ~25% for SPX, and negative returns (-60% to -20%) only ~20-28% — so unlike equities (where the premium is compensation for mildly-bad states), much of BTC's premium is paid for the right tail. A clustering algorithm on the risk-neutral densities finds two volatility regimes: high-vol Martin bound ~78.16% / Chabi-Yo ~102.27% with risk-neutral variance 0.86; low-vol ~43.99% / ~54.51% with variance 0.46. Interestingly BVRP is HIGHER in the low-vol regime (~0.17) than high-vol (~0.12).

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The bounds are model-free and refreshable, which is the strength. But four critiques bite for CMA use. First, HORIZON: every number is a one-month (27-day) conditional premium. The authors never forecast a year, let alone a decade; the ~66% is the compensation demanded right now for one month of BTC risk, mechanically scaled by ~82% implied vol. Annualizing it into a CMA is a category error — as vol mean-reverts and option markets deepen, the implied premium compresses proportionally. Second, the Martin/Chabi-Yo bounds require the negative-correlation condition between the SDF and the asset return; well-motivated for the aggregate market, much shakier for one speculative asset, so the 'lower bound' may not bound. Third, DATA: BTC options are young (2017+), venue-concentrated (Deribit), wide-spread, and thin in deep-OTM strikes — exactly the strikes the tail integrals need; Almeida et al. themselves call the first-moment premium 'a noisy measure,' and Alexander-Imeraj warn the variance-swap formula underestimates fair value when BTC fluctuates excessively. Fourth, the diversification/correlation story is weak for a CMA: the paper says BTC 'largely fluctuated independently of traditional macro-financial markets' and mentions gold only once — noting BTC's VRP 'became highly correlated with the VRP of equity and gold during the pandemic.' That is a second-moment, crisis-specific comovement (everyone bids vol protection together), NOT a return correlation, and certainly not support for a digital-gold return link.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is the cleanest source of all in one respect: the academic literature using this method publishes NO multi-year BTC return forecast and NO CMA. Almeida et al. produce a 27-day conditional premium; Alexander-Imeraj produce a vol-index term structure and VRP series; Hou et al. produce option prices and jump parameters; Martin produces a one-month equity-premium proxy. Any 10-15yr number is a downstream construction, not something these authors endorse. That restraint is itself a finding: the most rigorous, forward-looking, market-implied method on this list deliberately refuses to extrapolate to a decade — a useful rebuke to the S2F/power-law/gold-parity families that confidently project multi-million-dollar targets. For the CMA, the right use is to take the SIGN and ORDERING (BTC premium >> equity premium; BTC vol >> equity vol; jumps priced; premium upside-skewed) and the refreshable VRP/vol inputs as sanity checks, then impose the realized appreciation-decay discipline to land a defensible ~9-13% nominal forward, NOT the ~66% the raw option surface prints today.

</details>

### #41 · Triffin / Dedollarization Neutral-Reserve Sovereign Share

*Family: monetary-macro-reserve · Source: Official sector · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 45*


**Explanation:** The mechanism is geopolitical, not statistical: the Triffin dilemma plus dollar-reserve weaponization create latent demand for a neutral, seizure-proof, fixed-supply reserve asset, and Bitcoin is pitched as gold's digital analogue — benchmarked to central banks' ~1,000t/yr gold-buying pace. The CMA inputs are (1) a terminal Bitcoin share of the ~$12.3T official FX-reserve pool, (2) an explicit sovereign-adoption probability, and (3) a flow-to-marketcap multiplier. Crucially the reserve pool is SMALL versus BTC's existing ~$2T cap: even a wildly-bullish 5% allocation across ALL FX reserves implies only ~$130k-$410k (1x-10x flow multiplier). For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this caps the standalone reserve contribution at a modest premium and concentrates upside in a low-probability tail — because surveys put current central-bank endorsement at ~0% (93% no intent). Probability-weighting the scenarios yields ~10-14%/yr nominal, consistent with BTC's realized appreciation decay (142%→65%→17%), not its history.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 3, orthogonality 4. Mechanism is economically real and the reserve-pool TAM is genuinely distinct/bounded, giving high rigor and a self-limiting (non-runaway) contribution. But empirical signal over 10-15yr is weak: reserve-manager surveys show ~0% adoption and BTC fails the official sector's own reserve criteria (vol, liquidity, carry), so the base case is near-zero and adds little to the decay-anchored level. Robustness is moderate (geopolitical driver is regime-orthogonal but adoption could inflect either way); data is available (reserve pool, CB gold flows, surveys) but the key inputs are judgment probabilities, not estimable parameters.*


**Key drivers:** Total official-sector FX-reserve pool (~$12.3T; USD ~57%, gold ~20% at market) and the addressable de-dollarization slice; Terminal Bitcoin reserve SHARE captured by the horizon (scenario lever, e.g. 1-5% of FX reserves; El Salvador ~14% of its own reserves, Brazil RESBit proposal 5%); Explicit sovereign-adoption PROBABILITY — the load-bearing tail parameter (surveys: ~0% current, 93% no intent); Triffin dilemma / fiscal-dominance erosion of confidence in the dollar as global reserve unit; Dollar weaponization / sanctions (2022 reserve freeze) driving demand for a neutral, seizure-resistant, non-state-issued asset; Gold's central-bank accumulation pace (~1,045t/yr 2024) as the benchmark for reserve-diversification velocity; Flow-to-marketcap multiplier (incremental reserve demand on a thin, illiquid float — debated 1x to ~10x+); Reserve-asset qualification criteria: volatility, liquidity, trust/transparency, legal/custody, cross-border usability (Bitcoin fails several today per CB surveys); BRICS / emerging-market settlement de-dollarization and IMF counter-pressure (El Salvador forced to strip mandatory legal-tender status)


**Pros:** Targets a genuinely DISTINCT and large pool (official reserves + sovereign treasuries, ~$12.3T) that is largely orthogonal to the private-gold TAM and M2 frameworks, so it is additive rather than double-counting; Mechanism is economically real and on-record: the Triffin dilemma is a textbook reserve-currency tension, dollar weaponization measurably accelerated gold diversification (CB buying >1,000t/yr three years running), and a credibly neutral, seizure-resistant fixed-supply asset is exactly what a sanctioned surplus sovereign would want; Naturally a DECAYING/bounded contribution: the reserve pool is finite and small versus BTC's existing market cap, so the framework does not imply runaway returns — even a 5% all-reserve allocation only implies ~$130k-$410k, disciplining the bull case; Has real institutional sponsorship lending it credibility as a scenario (Deutsche Bank Research 2025 'room for both gold and Bitcoin by 2030'; CoinShares strategic-reserve rationale; 1-2% allocation recommendations from BlackRock/JPMorgan/WisdomTree), and live sovereign data points (El Salvador, US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, Brazil RESBit proposal); Probability-weighting makes it usable as an honest CMA tail input rather than a single hype target — the structure forces you to multiply a generous share by a tiny adoption probability


**Cons:** The decisive empirical fact KILLS the base case: reserve-manager surveys show ~0% of central banks hold digital assets and 93% have NO intention (OMFIF GPI 2025, ~$5T reserves surveyed; UBS 2025: ~80% expect continued USD dominance). The thesis prices a transition that the actual decision-makers overwhelmingly reject — so the adoption probability is genuinely near-zero, not merely low; Bitcoin fails core reserve-asset criteria TODAY on the official sector's own terms: too volatile (~57% realized vs gold ~15%), too illiquid at sovereign size, no yield (negative carry), unproven track record, custody/legal/accounting opacity, and not used in cross-border trade — the Czech National Bank found 'no miraculous stabilising force' in diversification tests, and Rogoff (2026) calls it appealing-in-theory but unsuitable until it demonstrates gold-like stability; The 'neutral reserve' logic is self-undermining: the same volatility that makes BTC a poor reserve asset is required to deliver the high returns the bull case needs, and a stable enough BTC to qualify as a reserve asset would by construction have a LOW forward return — the thesis cannot have both; Active official-sector COUNTER-pressure: the IMF forced El Salvador to strip Bitcoin's mandatory legal-tender status as a $1.4B loan condition; BRICS de-dollarization statements are explicitly gradual and currency-/settlement-focused, not BTC-reserve adoption — incumbents will defend currency sovereignty (DB: policymakers will ensure digital assets 'do not threaten the sovereignty of their currencies'); Sizing is small and flow-multiplier-dependent: the reserve pool is modest versus BTC's existing ~$2T cap, so absent a large (and unproven) illiquidity multiplier the standalone reserve contribution to price is minor — most published 'reserve' price targets (e.g. $2.9M/2050) smuggle in heroic share AND multiplier assumptions; The anchor report is qualitative, not a CMA: Deutsche Bank publishes NO reserve-share number, price target, volatility forecast, or correlation — repurposing 'room for both by 2030' as a quantitative long-horizon assumption is a category error; Digital-gold premise is empirically unsupported for correlation: realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0, so even if BTC absorbs some of gold's reserve role, it does not co-move with gold — undercutting the 'BTC = digital gold reserve' framing the thesis leans on

WHAT MAKES THIS DISTINCT. Unlike #6 (private investable-gold TAM) and #7/#8 (M2 / quantity-theory monetary substitution), this approach targets the OFFICIAL SECTOR specifically: ~$12.3T of central-bank FX reserves (USD ~57%, gold ~20% at market per NY Fed Liberty Street, 2024) plus sovereign treasuries. The driver is geopolitical, not statistical — the Triffin dilemma (the reserve issuer must run external deficits to supply world liquidity, eroding confidence in its own unit) and dollar weaponization (the 2022 freeze of Russia's reserves) generate latent demand for a politically NEUTRAL, seizure-resistant, non-state-issued, fixed-supply reserve asset. Bitcoin is pitched as gold's digital analogue and explicitly BENCHMARKED to gold's central-bank accumulation pace: ~1,045 tonnes in 2024, the third straight year above 1,000t (World Gold Council), itself a measurable de-dollarization signal.

METHODOLOGY. Bottom-up and scenario-based: (1) size the addressable reserve pool; (2) assume a terminal Bitcoin SHARE by the horizon (1-5% of FX reserves is the practitioner band; live anchors: El Salvador holds ~7,474 BTC ≈ 14% of ITS OWN reserves, Brazil's RESBit proposal floats 5%); (3) apply an explicit sovereign-adoption PROBABILITY; (4) treat the result as incremental demand flow on top of BTC's existing ~$2T market cap, optionally with an illiquidity flow-multiplier; (5) divide by near-fixed supply and annualize. The load-bearing — and most honest — feature is that the share must be multiplied by a probability that the surveys put near zero.

THE DECISIVE SKEPTIC ANCHOR. OMFIF's Global Public Investor 2025 (surveying institutions representing ~$5T of reserves) found ZERO central banks hold digital assets, 93% have NO intention, and only 7% are even monitoring; 82% don't use and don't plan to use DLT. The UBS 2025 reserve-manager survey (~40 central banks) found ~80% expect continued USD dominance. The cited disqualifiers are exactly the reserve-asset criteria: volatility (~57% vs gold ~15%), illiquidity at sovereign size, negative carry, custody/legal/accounting opacity, and absence of cross-border trade use — the Czech National Bank's diversification tests found 'no miraculous stabilising force.' Kenneth Rogoff (Project Syndicate, Feb 2026) concedes the neutral-asset appeal is 'growing' but judges BTC unsuitable until it shows gold-like stability. And the official sector is actively HOSTILE at the margin: the IMF made a $1.4B loan to El Salvador conditional on stripping Bitcoin's mandatory legal-tender status (effective May 2025), and BRICS de-dollarization communiqués are explicitly gradual and local-currency/settlement-focused, not BTC-reserve adoption. Deutsche Bank itself (the bull anchor) cautions policymakers will ensure digital assets 'do not threaten the sovereignty of their currencies.'

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The flagship official-sector-adjacent piece — Deutsche Bank Research, 'Bitcoin vs. Gold: The Future of Central Bank Reserves by 2030' (Laboure & Siazon, Sep 2025) — is QUALITATIVE: 'room for both gold and Bitcoin to coexist on central bank balance sheets by 2030,' citing BTC's falling 30-day volatility (historic low in Aug 2025 even above $123,500) as a maturation signal, but it publishes NO reserve-share %, price target, vol forecast, or correlation. Practitioner reserve-scenario numbers exist but are crypto/sell-side, not official: a widely-circulated '$2.9M by 2050' reserve-asset scenario (~16%/yr off ~$100k), CoinShares' strategic-reserve rationale (no point CMA), and 1-2% reserve-allocation recommendations from BlackRock, JPMorgan and WisdomTree. My own implied-price check shows why the channel is bounded: 1-5% of $12.3T FX reserves as incremental flow on a ~$2T cap implies only ~$107k-$410k across a 1x-10x flow multiplier — i.e., absent heroic multiplier assumptions the standalone reserve contribution is modest.

FAILURE MODES. (1) The base case is empirically dead — ~0% endorsement means the adoption probability is near-zero, not low. (2) Self-undermining vol logic: the volatility that powers the bull return is precisely what disqualifies BTC as a reserve asset; a BTC stable enough to qualify would have a low forward return. (3) Digital-gold correlation is asserted, not measured (realized BTC-gold ~0), so the gold-benchmark framing lacks the co-movement it implies. (4) Sizing is multiplier-dependent and the pool is small versus BTC's cap. NET: I treat this as a genuine but LOW-PROBABILITY TAIL-SHARE overlay — it adds a modest premium and concentrates upside in a small-probability sovereign-FOMO tail, landing the probability-weighted 10-15yr nominal CMA at ~10-14%/yr (real ~7-11%), vol ~55-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15 — consistent with BTC's realized appreciation decay, NOT its history, and explicitly NOT a base-case reserve-transition bet.

### #42 · On-Chain Supply-Distribution & Flow Microstructure (URPD, Liveliness/Dormancy, Reserve Risk, Illiquid/Exchange-Flow, Entity-Cohort, LTH/STH)

*Family: on-chain-supply-microstructure · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 44*


**Explanation:** The thesis: because issuance is fixed and falling, what matters for price is how the EXISTING stock is distributed and whether it is flowing toward "strong hands" (illiquid, dormant, accumulating cohorts) or back to "weak hands" (exchanges, liquid float). URPD locates the cost-basis walls price must climb through; CDD/Liveliness/Dormancy and Reserve Risk measure whether long-term holders are spending or accumulating conviction; liquid/illiquid supply and exchange netflow quantify the float actually for sale; the 155-day LTH/STH split separates seasoned-holder cost basis from speculative flow. A supply-shock CMA reasons: if illiquid supply keeps absorbing more than issuance while ETF/treasury demand persists, a shrinking sellable float forces price up. But these are timing tools, not return models — none publishes a multi-year appreciation, and the realized appreciation-decay path (142%→65%→17%/yr) must discipline any extrapolation. The load-bearing risk: ETF/custody migration (~1.3M BTC, ~7% of supply, in wrappers) breaks every on-chain flow signal, since the marginal buyer never touches the chain.


*Scores — rigor 2, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 3, orthogonality 2. Metrics are clean accounting transforms of the UTXO ledger (rigor not zero), but they are short-horizon positioning oscillators with no native long-horizon return output — the 9-13% level is grafted on by judgment, exactly the supply-squeeze over-extrapolation the literature warns against. Signal/robustness are weak for a 10-15yr CMA: cost-basis metrics are reflexive transforms of past price, Reserve Risk's HODL-bank denominator is endogenous to bull markets, and ETF-era off-chain custody (~7% of supply) degrades the on-chain flow read precisely as the method matures. Data is freely derivable from the chain but entity-clustering vendor dependence and the off-chain blind spot keep data_ops middling. Its real value is conditioning (URPD walls, float/illiquid tilt for tails/path), not the level.*


**Key drivers:** URPD cost-basis histogram shape: concentration 'walls' (supply clusters that act as support/resistance) vs thin 'air-pockets' price moves through quickly; ATH- vs percent-partitioned binning; Age-weighted spend flow: Coin-Days-Destroyed, Average/Median Spent-Output Lifespan (ASOL/MSOL, Tu-Xue), Blummer Liveliness/Dormancy (CDD ÷ all coin-days created) — measures whether old coins are moving (distribution) or sitting (HODL); Reserve Risk oscillator = current price ÷ cumulative HODL-bank (opportunity cost of NOT selling, accumulated from coin-days); low = high conviction + low price = attractive entry; Spend-propensity float: entity liquidity L = cumulative outflows/inflows (illiquid L≲0.25 / liquid 0.25–0.75 / highly-liquid ≳0.75); Illiquid-Supply-Shock ratio = illiquid ÷ (liquid+highly-liquid); Exchange reserve / netflow (inflow−outflow) and Exchange-Whale-Ratio (top-10 inflows ÷ total inflows) as proxies for sell-side pressure / supply available to market; Entity-clustered cohort behavior: Accumulation-Trend-Score (size-weighted balance change across wallet cohorts), whale-cohort (1k+ BTC) accumulation vs distribution; 155-day LTH/STH split: cohort realized price (on-chain cost basis) and cohort MVRV — separates seasoned-holder conviction from short-term speculative flow; Structural demand sinks (spot ETFs, corporate treasuries, sovereign reserves) draining liquid float faster than issuance — the supply-squeeze premise


**Pros:** Grounded in observable UTXO-ledger data (move-prices, coin-ages, entity-clustered flows), not a fitted curve or narrative — URPD, CDD and liquid/illiquid classification are accounting transforms, not regression assumptions; Captures information aggregate cost-basis scalars (#9) cannot: the DISTRIBUTION of cost basis (URPD walls/air-pockets) and the directional FLOW of supply (toward illiquid strong hands vs back to exchanges) — genuinely orthogonal microstructure detail useful for tail/path-of-return and support-level work; Reserve Risk and the illiquid-supply ratio have real ex-post discriminating power: Reserve Risk has historically marked cyclical undervaluation (low) and blow-off tops (high); rising illiquid supply has preceded several supply-squeeze rallies — leading rather than coincident signals; Cohort separation (155-day LTH/STH, whale Accumulation-Trend-Score) maps cleanly to behavioral reality — seasoned holders and whales drive supply availability differently from speculators — making it a behaviorally honest middleware; Exchange netflow/reserve gives a near-real-time read on sell-side pressure and the actually-tradeable float, a discipline pure-scarcity (S2F) and pure-price (power-law) models entirely lack; Unlike S2F/Metcalfe, the careful versions do NOT publish a single hard price target, so they are harder to weaponize into a spurious decade forecast — their reluctance to forecast long-horizon is itself a feature


**Cons:** Not a return model — every metric is a short-horizon TIMING/positioning oscillator with no native long-horizon expected-return output; a 10–15yr CMA is entirely grafted on by the analyst via a supply-squeeze assumption, exactly the over-extrapolation the literature warns against; Reflexive/circular: URPD and the LTH/STH/Reserve-Risk cost bases are transforms of PAST PRICE (coins stamped at move-time price), and Reserve Risk's denominator (HODL-bank) is endogenous to the bull market — high prices manufacture the very 'conviction floor' the model treats as fundamental; Severe ETF-era degradation, metric-specific: ~1.3M BTC (~7% of supply) sit in ETF custody and trade off-chain; daily on-chain transactions fell ~500K (Dec-2023) to ~250K (2025) at NEW highs. Exchange-reserve depletion no longer cleanly means cold-storage demand; illiquid supply is contaminated by custodial consolidation; the marginal buyer never touches the chain — breaking flow signals; Documented in-sample failures: Clemente's Sept-2021 'Illiquid Supply Floor $39K, never below again' was breached to ~$16K in 2022; his $53–57K supply-imbalance targets were undershot. In 2024–25 Reserve Risk, MVRV-Z, Pi-Cycle and related top-indicators failed to mark the cycle — the calibration visibly decays each cycle; Exchange-flow noise: market makers, OTC desks and institutional custodians move large BTC for reasons unrelated to immediate buy/sell intent, so netflow 'does not predict price movements with certainty'; whale-ratio and netflow are easily misread; Tiny sample / curve-fit risk: thresholds (illiquid L≲0.25, Reserve-Risk bands, 155-day cutoff) are calibrated on 2–3 cycles with lookahead bias; academic work finds on-chain metrics add only ~12–18% forecasting improvement and have weak, unstable out-of-sample predictive power for returns; Produces NO volatility or cross-asset correlation output whatsoever — the entire framework is silent on every CMA covariance cell; vol and the correlation vector vs equities/gold/TIPS must be imported from realized data

A genuinely shrinking, illiquid float can amplify squeezes AND air-pocket crashes (URPD thin zones), so vol stays high; floor held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized. Multiples of equity/gold vol. | ~0.45–0.55 (judgment; framework silent, so I inherit the rising trailing-window equity beta — 5y growth-eq corr 0.56 — and hold it elevated, since the ETF/institutional flows that drive accumulation and illiquid-supply growth ARE the same risk-on flows driving growth equities; the off-chain migration that degrades these metrics also tightens the equity link). | ~0.30–0.40 (judgment; below growth, tracking the anchor's value-eq corr ~0.37 at 5y). | ~0.15–0.25 (judgment; modestly positive via shared liquidity/rate-cycle sensitivity of the marginal institutional holder). | ~0.20–0.30 (judgment; slightly above nominal FI, real-rate sensitivity of a long-duration risk asset). | ~0.05–0.15 (judgment). <details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This approach is the DISTRIBUTION-and-FLOW counterpart to approach #9's aggregate cost-basis scalars. Where #9 collapses the UTXO set into single numbers (Realized Price, MVRV, SOPR, Thermocap), this family keeps the cross-section and the directional flow. Five distinct lineages, each with its own author and its own ETF-era failure mode:

(1) URPD (Renato Shirakashi, popularized by Glassnode). A histogram: each bar sums the BTC whose last-move price fell in that bucket (ATH-partitioned into 100 bins 0→ATH, or percent-partitioned ±2% steps around spot). It exposes "walls" (cost-basis concentration that acts as support/resistance) and "air-pockets" (thin zones price traverses fast). This is purely descriptive — a map of where holders are anchored.

(2) Age-weighted spend FLOW. Coin-Days-Destroyed weights each spent coin by its dormancy. Tu & Xue (2017, arXiv:1712.10287) formalize Average/Median Dormancy (ASOL/MSOL) and link CDD to traded-pool size via Little's Law — explicitly a turnover/velocity measure, NOT a price forecaster (the abstract makes no predictive claim). Tamas Blummer's Liveliness = ΣCDD / Σ(all coin-days ever created), a 0–1 ratio that trends up when old coins move (distribution) and down when they sit (HODL); Dormancy is its inverse cousin. Hans Hauge's Reserve Risk distills conviction into an oscillator: price ÷ cumulative "HODL-bank" (the running opportunity cost of holders choosing NOT to sell). Low Reserve Risk = high conviction + low price = historically attractive; high = blow-off top. It is a cyclical timing oscillator, self-described as such.

(3) Spend-propensity FLOAT. Rafael Schultze-Kraft (Glassnode CTO) classifies every entity by liquidity L = cumulative outflows/inflows: illiquid (L≲0.25), liquid (0.25–0.75), highly liquid (≳0.75). Will Clemente & Willy Woo's Illiquid-Supply-Shock ratio = illiquid ÷ (liquid+highly-liquid) models the probability of a supply squeeze. Glassnode reported illiquid supply ~3.2x liquid+highly-liquid in 2022 (~78% of supply illiquid).

(4) Venue FLOW. CryptoQuant exchange reserve (coins on exchange wallets) and netflow (inflow−outflow); rising inflow = sell pressure. Exchange-Whale-Ratio = top-10 inflows ÷ total inflows.

(5) Entity-cohort behavior. Glassnode's Accumulation-Trend-Score (size-weighted balance change across cohorts) and whale-cohort (1k+ BTC) accumulation/distribution; plus the 155-day LTH/STH split — coins become statistically unlikely to move after 155 dormant days, so cohort realized price and cohort MVRV separate seasoned-holder cost basis from speculative flow.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The unifying CMA story is the supply squeeze: fixed/falling issuance + supply flowing into illiquid/dormant/accumulating hands + structural ETF/treasury/sovereign demand ⇒ shrinking sellable float ⇒ upward price pressure. But this is a TIMING narrative, not a return model. No metric outputs a multi-year expected return, vol, or correlation.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS produced this way. The honest record is poor. Will Clemente's Sept-2021 "Illiquid Supply Floor" model declared ~$39K a floor BTC "may never drop below again" — BTC bottomed near $16K in 2022, a clean falsification. His Aug-2021 supply-imbalance targets ($53–57K) also undershot. These are the clearest cases of converting a flow metric into a forward price claim, and they failed. The careful publishers (Glassnode docs, Tu-Xue) explicitly decline long-horizon forecasts.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. Pre-2017 these signals tracked cycles well. Post-futures and especially post-ETF, fit decays. The 2024–25 cycle is the decisive test: Bitcoin Magazine and 21shares document that Reserve Risk, MVRV-Z, Pi-Cycle and the top-indicator cohort failed to mark the cycle, and on-chain transactions fell ~500K→250K/day AT new highs. Mechanism of degradation: ~1.3M BTC (~7% of supply) migrated into ETF custody trading off-chain; exchange-reserve depletion no longer cleanly signals cold-storage demand; illiquid supply is contaminated by custodial consolidation; the marginal buyer never pricestamps the chain. Exchange netflow is further muddied by MM/OTC/custodian movement unrelated to intent. Academic work (data-source-diversity studies) finds on-chain metrics add only ~12–18% forecasting improvement with weak, unstable out-of-sample power.

CMA BOTTOM LINE. Treat this family as path/tail/support-level color, not a CMA generator. My synthesized ~9–13% nominal / ~6–10% real is a decay-disciplined judgment anchored to realized 142%→65%→17%, deliberately below scarcity bulls because the float metrics are reflexive (built from past price), have over-promised squeezes, and are precisely the signals most broken by the off-chain ETF migration. Vol ~55–60% (squeeze + air-pocket two-sidedness). Gold corr ~0.05–0.15: the strong-hands/HODL framing reads as digital-gold but the data shows ~0 — the load-bearing contradiction, held at band bottom.

### #43 · Liability-Driven / Surplus-Optimization Implied BTC Hurdle (Endowment/LDI)

*Family: liability-driven · Source: Asset manager · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 44*


**Explanation:** This is a liability-RELATIVE optimizer, not a return model. Following Sharpe-Tint (1990), risk is the volatility of surplus (assets minus PV of liabilities); an asset is valued by its covariance with the liability, and earns inclusion only if its expected return clears a hurdle roughly equal to its beta-to-surplus times the surplus risk premium (the reverse-optimized "implied return"). Key inputs: the liability's risk drivers (real spending, wages, healthcare inflation, or the discount-rate curve), BTC's covariance with those drivers (empirically near zero), BTC's standalone volatility (55-100%), and the sleeve size. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the implication is sobering: because BTC hedges almost no real liability and its huge variance dominates surplus risk even at a 1-3% weight, the implied hurdle is high (plausibly mid-teens to 20%+ depending on liability and risk aversion). The framework therefore does not produce appreciation, vol, or correlation numbers directly; it produces a PASS/FAIL bar against whatever independent BTC return assumption you bring. Its honest verdict: only a tiny return-seeking sleeve, justified by raw return, not by liability hedging.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 2, orthogonality 3. Sharpe-Tint surplus optimization is theoretically sound and asks the institutionally correct question, structurally penalizing BTC's 55-100% vol and near-zero liability hedge to cap the sleeve — high rigor. But it is explicitly not a return forecaster: it consumes an exogenous BTC appreciation assumption and cannot populate a CMA's level cell, so its standalone predictive signal for BTC over 10-15yr is weak. Robustness is middling because the hurdle hinges on a non-stationary BTC-liability covariance that can spike precisely in stressed-funded-status regimes; data_ops is poor since it requires a separate return model plus liability-driver covariances few CMA processes maintain.*


**Key drivers:** Liability risk drivers: the present value and volatility of the obligation being funded (real spending rule for an endowment; wage/benefit accruals and the discount-rate curve for a pension; reserves for an insurer); Covariance of BTC returns with the liability's drivers (empirically near zero for real-spending/wage/healthcare/rate liabilities) — the single most important input, since it determines whether BTC hedges or adds surplus risk; BTC standalone volatility (55-100%), which dominates the asset's marginal contribution to surplus variance even at small weights; Sleeve size / weight of BTC in total assets (the marginal-risk contribution and thus the hurdle scale with weight); Surplus risk aversion (lambda) and the surplus/funded-ratio Sharpe ratio — the 'price of risk' multiplying the marginal risk contribution to set the hurdle; Funded status / horizon: hurdle rises as funded status improves (less risk budget) and as the plan de-risks toward termination; an open endowment with a perpetual real-spending liability has more room than a closed pension


**Pros:** Asks the correct question for an institution: not 'is BTC's Sharpe ratio attractive in isolation?' but 'does a BTC sleeve improve the probability of paying real liabilities?' — surfacing that BTC's diversification benefit is largely irrelevant to a spending/wage/healthcare liability it does not hedge; Honest about volatility: by penalizing the variance of SURPLUS (not assets), it correctly inflates BTC's cost via its 55-100% vol, preventing the asset-only Sharpe optimizers (which BTC's high realized return flatters) from over-allocating — the framework structurally caps the sleeve at a token weight; Produces a falsifiable decision bar (the implied hurdle) you can test any independent BTC CMA against, rather than a self-serving price target; it cleanly separates 'return-seeking' from 'liability-hedging' so BTC cannot masquerade as a hedge; Methodologically grounded in 35+ years of accepted institutional practice (Sharpe-Tint surplus optimization, Leibowitz endowment-model dual-risk framework, LDI) — not a crypto-native curve-fit


**Cons:** It is NOT a return forecaster: it consumes a BTC expected-return assumption and tells you whether it clears the bar — so it cannot, by itself, populate a CMA's appreciation cell. You still need an exogenous BTC return model, inheriting all that model's flaws; Garbage-in on the covariance: the hurdle depends critically on BTC's covariance with the liability, which is estimated on a short, non-stationary BTC history and is regime-dependent (BTC's equity correlation has risen from ~0.26 to ~0.56). If BTC's correlation to the discount-rate/liquidity factor rises in a crisis exactly when funded status is stressed, the realized surplus damage exceeds the ex-ante hurdle; No institution has actually published a liability-relative BTC hurdle — Grayscale, ARK and every existing approach in the set run asset-only mean-variance/Sharpe optimization against stocks and bonds, never against a liability covariance. The framework is well-established in general but UNAPPLIED to BTC on the record, so all numbers here are derived, not cited; Sensitive to subjective inputs (risk aversion lambda, sleeve size, choice of liability proxy) that swing the hurdle widely; a generous endowment-spending liability and high BTC return assumption can flip the verdict, so it can be reverse-engineered to justify a predetermined allocation; Says nothing native about BTC's own appreciation, volatility, or cross-asset correlations — all distributional CMA cells must be imported from realized data or another model, just like the cost-of-production and NVT frameworks


> **⚠ Adversarial verifier — numbers unreliable.** CITATION FIXES: (1) Remove the fabricated MSCI quote 'high volatility inflates beta, raising the required hurdle rate substantially' — replace with the actual MSCI language: hurdle = beta x portfolio expected return; implied returns proportional to marginal contribution to risk. The flaw is purely the magnitude of the synthesized hurdle and the fail verdict built on it.

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. The framework inverts the CMA question. Sharpe and Tint (1990, 'Liabilities — A New Approach', JPM 16(2):5-10) replaced asset-return variance with SURPLUS variance as the risk measure: define surplus S = A − k·L (assets minus a liability-importance-weighted PV of liabilities), and optimize U = E(surplus return) − lambda·Var(surplus return). The pivotal change is that an asset is now valued by its covariance with the liability, not merely its standalone moments. An asset whose returns are driven by the same factors as the liability (e.g., TIPS for an inflation-linked spending rule) REDUCES surplus volatility and is attractive even at a low standalone return; an asset uncorrelated with the liability (BTC) cannot reduce surplus volatility and is confined to the return-seeking sleeve, where it must clear a return hurdle to compensate for the surplus variance it adds.\n\nTHE HURDLE. Operationally the bar is the reverse-optimized 'implied return.' MSCI ('Earning a Place in the Portfolio,' 2023) states it cleanly: hurdle ≈ beta-to-portfolio × portfolio expected return, with implied returns 'proportional to the marginal contribution to risk of that component.' In surplus space, substitute 'surplus portfolio' and 'surplus return premium' for portfolio/return. BTC's hurdle is driven by two compounding facts: (1) its covariance with a real-spending/wage/healthcare/discount-rate liability is ~zero (BTC's realized TIPS correlation ~0.30, FI ~0.19, gold ~0 — none high or stable enough to hedge a liability), so it earns no hedging credit; and (2) its 55-100% standalone vol makes its marginal contribution to surplus variance very large even at 1-3% weight. As MSCI notes, 'high volatility inflates beta, raising the required hurdle rate substantially.' The result: an implied hurdle plausibly in the high-teens-to-20%+, which I synthesize at ~14-22% nominal / ~11-19% real.\n\nKEY RELATIONSHIP / VERDICT. The framework's value to a BTC CMA is comparative, not generative. Set the hurdle (~14-22%) against the cross-approach central forward BTC return (~8-12% nominal, the decayed extrapolation of 142%->65%->17%/yr). The forward return is BELOW the surplus hurdle for a real liability. Therefore a BTC sleeve is surplus-DILUTIVE for the median pension or endowment once you (a) penalize its vol in surplus terms and (b) deny it hedging credit it does not earn. It survives only as a tiny raw-return-seeking bet justified by return alone — which is exactly what the asset-only optimizers (Grayscale's ~5% Sharpe-maximizing weight) miss, because they optimize asset Sharpe, not funded status.\n\nHISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. Surplus optimization is battle-tested in pension/LDI and endowment practice (Leibowitz-Bova-Hammond 2010 formalize the endowment's dual return-seeking/liability-aware risk view; Cambridge Associates' LDI handbooks operationalize funded-status risk). Its failure modes when applied to BTC: (1) covariance instability — BTC's correlations are estimated on a short, non-stationary history and rise in crises (equity corr 0.26->0.56), so realized surplus damage can exceed the ex-ante hurdle precisely when funded status is already stressed (correlation-goes-to-one risk, a 'dragon risk' in Leibowitz's terms); (2) input subjectivity — lambda, sleeve size, and the liability proxy swing the hurdle, so the model can be reverse-engineered to bless a predetermined allocation; (3) it forecasts nothing about BTC itself, inheriting an exogenous return model's flaws.\n\nON-RECORD FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY: none. This is the distinctive finding. Despite the framework being standard institutional practice, NO asset manager, consultant, pension, or endowment has published a liability-relative BTC hurdle. Every BTC portfolio study on the record — Grayscale's 'Crypto in Diversified Portfolios' (~5% asset-only Sharpe-max weight, ~95% vol, ~0.36 avg correlation inputs), ARK, 21Shares, and all prior rows in this digest — runs asset-only mean-variance against stocks and bonds. None flips to a liability-covariance hurdle. So the framework is genuinely distinct from everything covered, but every output here is DERIVED from the general surplus mechanics applied to BTC's realized moments, not cited from a BTC-specific publication. That absence is itself informative: the institutions most bound by liabilities (DB pensions, insurers) have not found a liability-relative case for BTC, consistent with the steep implied hurdle this framework produces.

### #44 · Options-Skew / Convexity Risk-Reversal Signal

*Family: options-skew-convexity · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 44*


**Explanation:** The signal is the 25-delta risk reversal (call IV minus put IV) and the steepness of the left/right IV-smile slopes. Deribit Insights backtests (Apr-2019 to Dec-2022) show that, unlike equities where you buy crash protection, in BTC systematically SELLING the risk reversal delivers the best risk-adjusted returns — robust across deltas, surviving exclusion of the March-2020 crash, and explained by BTC's spot-vol correlation being negative only ~65% of the time plus persistently rich call wings. That is a harvestable convexity/insurance-supply premium, not a price forecast. The disciplining academic result (Wang et al. 2024, J. Int. Money & Finance) is that both IV slopes predict realized VOLATILITY weekly but NOT returns — BTC options carry volatility, not directional, information. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this means skew informs the volatility and tail/correlation cells and offers a carry overlay, but supplies NO appreciation number; the central estimate must be borrowed. It usefully caps naive bullishness: a market that won't pay up for directional convexity is not pricing structural drift.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 3. Methodologically strong and honest: forward-looking market-priced data, peer-reviewed evidence that skew forecasts realized vol but NOT returns — a rare falsifiable negative result that guards against directional over-extrapolation. But signal for a 10-15yr CMA is weak: it produces no appreciation forecast by construction and the entire surface lives at days-to-3-month tenors, so any decade view is fully imported. Robustness is poor — the harvestable short-RR premium is explicitly regime-dependent and decaying as institutions mature the market. Data_ops is constrained: Deribit options data is short-maturity, requires surface modeling, and offers no long-horizon read for a standard CMA process. Its genuine value is conditioning the vol/tail cell, not the level.*


**Key drivers:** 25-delta risk reversal level and its z-score vs history (25d-call IV minus 25d-put IV); Left and right slopes of the implied-volatility smile (skew steepness); Spot-vol correlation (negative ~65% of the time in BTC, vs persistently strongly negative in equities) — drives why short-RR pays; Net-buying-pressure / dealer-inventory and option supply-demand imbalance (call wings trading rich/cheap); Realized positive vs negative skewness of returns (jumps) that the slopes mean-revert against; Variance / volatility risk premium magnitude and its regime (higher in low-vol clusters per Almeida et al.); Market maturation / institutional participation, which the practitioner source expects to erode the short-RR premium over time


**Pros:** Grounded in live, forward-looking, market-priced data (Deribit options) rather than backward price extrapolation or on-chain proxies — it reflects what risk-takers actually pay for convexity right now; Delivers exactly the CMA cells most models miss: a genuine implied-volatility and tail-risk view, plus an empirically harvestable carry strategy (short RR) with real desk adoption; Honest and self-disciplining: the peer-reviewed finding that skew forecasts realized vol but NOT returns is a rare falsifiable, NEGATIVE result that guards against the directional over-extrapolation plaguing S2F/Metcalfe/power-law models; Captures asymmetry/jump structure the lognormal/normal models ignore — left vs right slope separately price crash vs melt-up convexity; The short-RR / variance-premium edge is documented across multiple independent sources (Deribit practitioner backtest + Almeida et al. + Bitcoin-VIX VRP literature), not a single curve-fit


**Cons:** Produces NO appreciation forecast by construction — Wang et al. find the slopes have zero predictive power for returns, so the entire directional CMA must be imported from another framework; using skew to set expected return is a category error; Short maturities only: the entire surface lives at days-to-3-months tenors, so any 10-15yr extrapolation is heroic — there is no 10yr BTC option to read a decade view from; The harvestable edge is explicitly regime-dependent and decaying: Deribit itself warns the short-RR premium 'will likely become less profitable' as institutions mature the market and supply/demand normalizes — so even the carry result is non-stationary; Short-vol / short-RR carries severe negative-skew tail risk (sell crash insurance, blow up on the next March-2020/FTX gap) — strong Sharpe masks fat left-tail that a 10-15yr holder must survive; the backtest leans on a survivorship single path; Data depth is thin and venue-concentrated (Deribit ~ the whole liquid BTC options market; sample only ~2019+), and the variance-risk-premium estimates flip sign by regime, undermining a stable structural number; Says nothing directly about cross-asset correlations to equities/FI/TIPS/gold — those must be borrowed; the framework is asset-internal

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

WHAT THE APPROACH IS. The Options-Skew / Convexity Risk-Reversal signal isolates the SHAPE of BTC's implied-volatility smile — not its level (which is approach #11, the DVOL/RND vol-surface model). Two objects: (1) the 25-delta risk reversal, RR = IV(25d call) - IV(25d put), the market price of upside vs downside convexity; (2) the left and right slopes of the smile (skew steepness). Both are read off Deribit, which is effectively the entire liquid BTC options venue. The practitioner claim and the academic claim point in different but complementary directions, which is why this is a distinct entry.

THE PRACTITIONER EDGE (Deribit Insights, 'Finding edge in four years of volatility regimes,' ~2023). Backtesting Apr-2019 to Dec-2022, Deribit finds that systematically SELLING the 25d risk reversal produces the best risk-adjusted returns — the OPPOSITE of equity markets, where investors persistently overpay for downside puts. The result is robust across delta targets and survives excluding the March-2020 'Black Thursday' crash. Mechanism: BTC's rolling 60-day spot-vol correlation is negative only ~65% of the time (vs near-always-negative in equities), and call wings have traded persistently rich (a positive-skew/melt-up insurance demand). A short-RR harvests that. An overlay combining short-RR with spot BTC found ~75-80% allocation to the strategy was Sharpe-optimal. Crucially, Deribit itself flags decay: as institutions mature the market 'these strategies will likely become less profitable.'

THE DISCIPLINING ACADEMIC RESULT (Wang et al., 2024, J. Int. Money & Finance / ORL, 'Implied volatility slopes and jumps in bitcoin options market'). Using Deribit tick data, they derive a theoretical link between left/right IV slopes and negative/positive price jumps, and find empirically that jumps have REVERSAL impacts on the slopes even controlling for net-buying-pressure and realized skewness. The CMA-critical conclusion: 'Both left and right slopes of the implied volatility curve lack the predictive capability for returns, whereas they notably forecast realized volatility on the weekly frequency, which is in line with the evidence of more volatility-informed and less directional-informed trading in the bitcoin market.' This is the sharp NEGATIVE finding the seed brief highlights — skew is a VOLATILITY signal, not a RETURN signal. It is exactly the kind of falsifiable, demand-side discipline a single DVOL/RND point (approach #11) does not contain.

SUPPORTING RISK-PREMIA LITERATURE. Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024, arXiv 2410.15195, 'Risk Premia in the Bitcoin Market') decompose the BTC premium and find it is substantially driven by a large, regime-dependent VARIANCE risk premium (higher in low-vol clusters), with negative returns between 1-3 sd contributing only ~one-third of the total premium — unlike the S&P where mild-down returns dominate. This supports reading BTC's option premium as a volatility/variance phenomenon, not a directional-skew phenomenon. Alexander & Imeraj (2021, 'The Bitcoin VIX and Its Variance Risk Premium,' J. Alt. Investments) build a CBOE-VIX-style BTC implied-vol index from 7M+ Deribit prices and document a positive variance risk premium (implied > realized), the structural source of the short-vol/short-RR carry.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. Notably, NONE. This framework produces NO published multi-year directional BTC price/appreciation forecast — and that absence is a feature, not a gap. Because the peer-reviewed evidence says skew cannot forecast returns, no credible author uses it to set a 10-15yr appreciation number. The only forward-looking 'forecasts' are (a) realized-volatility predictions at weekly horizon and (b) the practitioner expectation that the short-RR premium itself will compress as the market institutionalizes. Anyone projecting a decade BTC price off the smile is misusing the tool.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTIC'S READ. (1) Maturity wall: no 10-15yr options exist, so any long-horizon read is extrapolation from <3-month tenors. (2) Negative-skew tail: the short-RR/short-vol edge is selling crash insurance — high Sharpe, fat left tail; a single FTX/March-2020 gap can erase years of carry, and the backtest is one survivorship path. (3) Regime non-stationarity: the variance risk premium flips magnitude by vol regime (Almeida et al.) and Deribit expects the edge to decay — so even the harvestable part is unstable. (4) Venue/sample concentration: Deribit ~= the market; data only ~2019+. (5) Asset-internal: silent on cross-asset correlations, which must be imported.

NET ROLE IN A BTC CMA PANEL. Use this approach to populate the VOLATILITY and TAIL/convexity cells (forward realized vol ~55-60%, implied richer by a positive VRP) and as a carry-strategy overlay — and, most importantly, as a SKEPTIC that refuses to read a structural directional premium out of option prices, thereby capping the over-bullish supply-scarcity and gold-parity models. The appreciation and correlation numbers are imported from the realized-decay baseline (~8-12% nom, gold corr ~0), not generated here.

</details>
