WHAT MAKES THIS DISTINCT. Unlike #5 (one-way terminal-share-of-gold sizing, gold's own return not a building block, no reversion anchor) and #6 (BTC-on-M2 elasticity), this family makes a cross-asset RATIO the forecast primitive and uses the comparator's OWN return as numeraire. The cleanest decomposition: E[BTC nominal return] = (1 + reversion of the BTC/gold ratio toward a fair band) x (1 + gold's own expected return) - 1. Gold's appreciation is thus an explicit input, and a mean-reversion/Z-score anchor (which #5/#6 lack) supplies the pull-back force.

THE FOUR SUB-MODELS, with on-record multi-year forecasts.
(1) BTC/gold ratio + Z-score (Bitcoin Magazine Pro / The Block / CCN): ratio measured in oz-gold-per-BTC. Jan-2026 ~17.6-20, down ~50% from ~40 in Dec-2024 as gold rallied to ~$5,100; bull markets >30-35, risk-off <20. WisdomTree's model-implied 'fair' ratio is ~21. A sub-2 Z-score flagged BTC cheap-vs-gold in Mar-2020 (BTC then +1,170% over the next year) and Nov-2022 (BTC +~150% over the next year). Scripted: ratio 17.6->21 over 12.5y + 5% gold = ~6.5%/yr BTC; 17.6->30 + 6% gold = ~10.6%/yr.
(2) WisdomTree hard-money basket — explicit on-record 2030 forecasts. Basket = global M2 x H (hard-money share of M2; gold historically 10% calm to >30% inflationary, median ~15%) x B (BTC's share of the gold+BTC basket; ~8% at snapshot, modeled rising to ~15% by 2030). Three M2 regimes: deflationary 3% -> BTC ~$120-135k / gold $3,000; base 5%, H~15%, B~15% -> BTC ~$250k / gold ~$4,000 by 2030; inflationary 7%, H toward 20%+, B faster -> BTC >$500k (~35% CAGR) / gold >$5,500. This JOINTLY forecasts gold, the signature feature.
(3) CoinShares four-pool TAM 2025 — on-record to 2039. Pools (May-2025): Global M2 $217.3T, CB FX reserves $18.2T, corporate treasuries $17.8T, gold $16.5T; total $269.8T (up ~21% from $170.3T in 2022). Per-pool capture rates run on a Verhulst S-curve over a fixed 2009-2039 horizon. Reference points: 1% of all pools -> ~$104k; 2% M2 + 5% gold -> $189k; 2% M2 + 20% gold -> $261k; and crucially the BASELINE (3.5% overall share) -> only ~$62k/BTC by 2039. Off ~$110k spot that baseline is a NEGATIVE ~-4%/yr return — the single most honest, least-cited number in the entire BTC-CMA literature, and it comes from a long-BTC issuer's own model. CoinShares flags pool overlap (gold inside CB reserves; treasuries inside M2) as overstating TAM.
(4) Doeswijk-Lam-Swinkels Global Market Portfolio (RAPS 2020) — the falsifiable bar. The invested global multi-asset market portfolio realized ~4.45% real / 11.2% vol (1960-2017). BTC added in 2017 would have weighed just 0.09% (HY bonds were 21x bigger). Today BTC (~$2.2T) is ~0.3-0.8% of ~$175-261T investable wealth. Scripted: BTC to 1% of a grown $330T portfolio in 12.5y = ~3.3%/yr; to 2% = ~9.2%/yr; to 0.5% = -2.3%/yr. This variant cannot be inflated by narrative — it pins BTC to its equilibrium weight in ALL wealth.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The reversion premise is the weak link: the BTC/gold ratio fell 50% in 2025 with NO mechanical pull-back, and with only 3-4 cycles the 'fair' band (21) is curve-fit, not structural. Deeper still — using a ratio as the primitive and gold's return as numeraire REQUIRES BTC and gold to be co-moving substitutes, yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). Dividing two near-uncorrelated assets does not produce a stable reverting ratio; the ratio's swings are mostly BTC's own equity-beta noise. The level-pinning (WisdomTree basket = M2 LEVEL x shares) reintroduces the same non-stationary trend-on-trend spuriousness that sinks #6. And provenance is conflicted: WisdomTree (BTCW) and CoinShares (BTC ETPs) are long-BTC issuers; their bullish scenarios are where the optimism hides.

THE PUNCHLINE FOR A 10-15YR CMA. Run to its own discipline, this family is far MORE humbling than gold-parity hype: ratio-reversion + gold return clusters ~6-11%/yr, market-portfolio-share to 1-2% gives ~3-9%/yr, and CoinShares' baseline is outright negative. Synthesized central ~7-11% nominal / ~4-8% real, vol ~50-60%, BTC-gold corr ~0.05-0.20 (I credit a small premium for shared debasement narrative but reject the high co-movement the ratio framing assumes). The framework's value is less as a point estimate than as a falsifiable discipline — and its honest verdict is that most of the gold-substitution upside is already in the price.

</details>

### #52 · Behavioral Attention & Text-Sentiment (Search/Wiki/Social NLP, Fear-Greed)

*Family: behavioral-attention-sentiment · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 40*


**Explanation:** The mechanism is reflexive: a burst of search/social attention pulls marginal buyers in, lifting price, which generates more attention — Kristoufek (2013) documents 0.88 (Google) / 0.83 (Wikipedia) co-movement and bidirectional causality, with a 10% search shock moving price ~2% over two periods then fading. Above trend, attention amplifies rallies; below trend it amplifies sell-offs (bubble dynamics). NLP strands (Gur 2025, FinBERT-LSTM on 650k+ headlines) add an asymmetry: negative news moves price and volatility far more than positive. The Fear & Greed composite operationalizes this as a contrarian oscillator. The decisive input for a CMA is the empirically short half-life: predictability is days-to-weeks (search) or minutes (tweets), and transaction costs erase the alpha. Because attention is a finite, saturating resource, its return contribution decays as adoption matures — implying a 10-15yr appreciation anchored to the realized decay baseline (142%→65%→17%/yr), NOT extrapolated from attention-fuelled past surges. The family is best for the volatility and short-horizon timing cells of a CMA, not long-run drift.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 4, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Replicated co-movement and honest self-limiting horizon give it moderate rigor, but reflexive circularity and zero native long-run drift make its 10-15yr signal weak — it must import a level from elsewhere. It scores well on robustness because attention-feedback is regime-invariant (survives halving breaks and the ETF shift) where S2F/Metcalfe do not, and its legitimate value is the vol and tail/timing conditioning cells, not the drift. Data-ops is middling: sentiment/Fear-Greed series exist but are noisy, vendor-dependent, and need NLP plumbing for a slow CMA.*


**Key drivers:** Retail search attention: Google Trends search-volume index and Wikipedia pageviews for 'Bitcoin' (Kristoufek's two phenomena-of-the-Internet-era series); Machine-read text tone: FinBERT/CryptoBERT/LLM sentiment scores over X (Twitter), Reddit, and financial-news headlines (polarity, intensity, volume of mentions); Reflexive attention-price feedback loop: bidirectional Granger causality (attention->price AND price->attention), with above-trend/below-trend asymmetry driving bubbles and crashes; Negative-news asymmetry: price and volatility respond markedly more to negative sentiment than positive/neutral (Gur 2025; FinBERT-LSTM + GARCH amplification); Composite Fear & Greed Index: 0-100 contrarian oscillator weighting volatility 25%, volume/momentum 25%, social media 15%, BTC dominance 10%, Google Trends 10% (Alternative.me); Attention saturation / S-curve maturation: the marginal pool of new searchers shrinks each cycle, so the attention return-contribution decays toward zero (the load-bearing assumption for a long-horizon CMA); Sentiment extremity (distance from neutral) as a volatility/uncertainty predictor independent of direction (Extremity Premium, arXiv 2602.07018)


**Pros:** Honest about its own horizon: the careful literature explicitly limits the signal to days-to-weeks momentum/volume/volatility and does NOT claim long-run forecasting — Kristoufek frames BTC as having 'no fundamental value,' so the family avoids the over-extrapolation that sinks S2F/Metcalfe; Measures a real, observable driver of a no-cashflow asset: when value is purely speculative, attention and sentiment ARE the marginal demand, and the 0.83-0.88 co-movement and bidirectional causality are genuine, replicated findings; Best-in-class for the volatility and tail/timing cells of a CMA: the Fear & Greed extremity result (arXiv 2602.07018, N=2,896, replicates on ETH and 6 of 7 cycles) and the negative-news GARCH amplification give a defensible, falsifiable handle on when BTC vol spikes; Contrarian Fear & Greed has a plausible (if marginal) ex-post edge: buying sub-25 readings beat buy-and-hold ~1,145% vs ~1,046% (2018-2025) and sub-10 readings averaged +48% 90-day returns — a real, if small-sample, mean-reversion signal; Cheap, transparent, real-time and model-light: search/pageview/sentiment series are public and refreshable daily, with no curve-fit price-history dependence


**Cons:** Produces NO long-run expected return by construction — predictability decays in ~15 minutes (tweets) to ~2 weeks (search); any 10-15yr appreciation number must be imported from a separate model, making this family unusable as a standalone CMA drift source; Pure reflexivity / circularity: attention and price each cause the other, so the high correlation is a feedback artifact, not an exogenous valuation anchor — you cannot tell whether sentiment forecasts price or merely co-moves with it (Kristoufek concedes bidirectional causality; Reddit/Twitter studies cannot reject reverse causality); Alpha is not exploitable net of costs: 'considering reasonable transaction costs makes it impossible to generate abnormal profits' from sentiment trading (Lou et al., ScienceDirect 2019); the Fear & Greed contrarian edge is small-sample (<10 sub-10 readings) and may not survive the institutional/ETF regime that did not exist pre-2021; Non-stationary, regime-dependent and manipulable: bot-driven social volume, sentiment concentrated in the bubble period, and a shrinking retail-attention base post-ETF (the marginal buyer is now an institution that never searches 'Bitcoin') break the historical attention-price link; Silent on cross-asset correlations and on real (inflation-adjusted) returns: the literature publishes essentially no BTC-vs-gold/equity/FI correlation from a sentiment lens, so most CMA cells must be borrowed from realized data

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This family is a behavioral-demand lens for a no-cashflow asset, merging four candidate signals into one approach: (a) Google Trends search volume and (b) Wikipedia pageviews as retail-attention proxies; (c) machine-read TEXT tone from FinBERT/CryptoBERT/LLM classifiers over X, Reddit and news; and (d) the composite Crypto Fear & Greed Index. It is distinct from existing digest row #9 (Cross-Sectional Factor & Macro-Liquidity Regression), which uses an attention PROXY as one numeric regressor (the Liu-Tsyvinski investor-attention factor) but never parses linguistic content nor adopts a published sentiment composite as the lens. Here, attention/sentiment IS the framework, not a control.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & HISTORICAL FIT. Kristoufek (2013, Scientific Reports 3:3415) is the seminal anchor: weekly Google Trends vs price correlation 0.8786, daily Wikipedia 0.8271 (both p<0.01). The causality is explicitly BIDIRECTIONAL (Granger both ways) — attention drives price and price drives attention — and a 10% search shock produces ~2% cumulative price movement over ~2 periods, after which the effect vanishes. The pivotal qualitative finding is an above-trend/below-trend ASYMMETRY: above the trend, rising interest pushes price higher; below trend, rising interest pushes price LOWER — i.e., attention amplifies whichever direction the market is already moving, a textbook bubble-and-crash reflexivity. Kristoufek frames Bitcoin as having "no fundamental value" with a market "of speculative traders," which is exactly why an attention lens is appropriate AND why it cannot anchor a long-run level.

Gur (2025, Journal of Forecasting, doi 10.1002/for.70068) modernizes the text strand: FinBERT-based sentiment over 650,000+ financial-news headlines, best model FinBERT-LSTM, with a robust asymmetry — Bitcoin's price (and GARCH volatility) responds far more strongly to NEGATIVE news than positive/neutral. This is a daily/short-horizon directional-and-volatility result, not a multi-year forecast. The Fear & Greed Index (Alternative.me) operationalizes the composite: volatility 25%, volume/momentum 25%, social media 15% (a text-processing algorithm scraping X mentions and engagement velocity), BTC dominance 10%, Google Trends 10%, scaled 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), used contrarian.

FAILURE MODES (faithful critiques). (1) NO LONG-RUN DRIFT. The decisive limitation: predictability decays in ~15 minutes at the trade level (Twitter; consistent with daily-level efficiency) and ~2 weeks at the search level. There is no mechanism for 10-15yr appreciation — any CMA drift number is imported. (2) REFLEXIVITY/CIRCULARITY. Because attention and price each cause the other, the high correlation is a feedback artifact; reverse causality cannot be rejected. (3) ALPHA NET OF COSTS IS ~ZERO. Lou/Aslanidis et al. (Finance Research Letters, ScienceDirect 2019): "considering reasonable transaction costs makes it impossible to generate abnormal profits" from sentiment trading; predictability is concentrated in the bubble period and driven by social sentiment, not macro news. (4) REGIME BREAK / NON-STATIONARITY. Bot-amplified social volume, and a shrinking retail-attention base post-ETF (the marginal buyer is now an institution who never Googles "Bitcoin"), erode the historical link. (5) SILENT ON CORRELATIONS AND REAL RETURNS — most CMA cells must be borrowed from realized data.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Essentially none, which is itself the finding. The careful academic literature deliberately refuses long-horizon point forecasts; Kristoufek makes "no claims about long-run price-level forecasting." The only multi-year evidence is BACKWARD-LOOKING strategy backtests, not forward CMAs: buying when Fear & Greed fell below 25 returned ~1,145% over 2018-2025 vs ~1,046% buy-and-hold (a thin ~100-bp-of-total edge over seven years), and sub-10 readings averaged +48% / median +48.5% over the subsequent 90 days with no negative 90-day instances — but on fewer than ten sub-10 observations, so the small-sample caveat is severe and the institutional-era out-of-sample is untested. The Extremity Premium working paper (arXiv 2602.07018, 2026; N=2,896, Feb-2018-Jan-2026) is the most rigorous recent contribution and pointedly forecasts UNCERTAINTY/spreads, not direction or level: extremity (distance from neutral) predicts excess uncertainty beyond realized vol (within-quintile p<0.001, Cohen's d=0.21, Granger F=211, placebo p<0.0001, replicating on ETH and 6 of 7 cycles).

CMA IMPLICATION. Treat this family as the VOLATILITY-and-timing engine of a Bitcoin CMA, never the appreciation engine. For drift, I anchor to the realized decay (142%->65%->17%/yr) and the family's own saturating-attention logic to push the 10-15yr forward to ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real — at/just below the trailing-5y rate, since the marginal attention pool shrinks as BTC institutionalizes. Vol stays ~55-60% (the family's best-supported cell, via negative-news GARCH amplification and the extremity premium). Correlations are borrowed from realized data (growth-eq ~0.50, value ~0.35, FI ~0.20, TIPS ~0.25, gold ~0.05); the family supplies no digital-gold axis, so I keep BTC-gold near zero and reject any safe-haven reading — reflexive, sentiment-driven crash behavior makes BTC LESS gold-like, not more.

### #53 · Dynamic-Factor / Mixed-Frequency Macro Nowcasting (DFM + MIDAS, ML-augmented)

*Family: macro-nowcasting · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 39*


**Explanation:** Borrowed from central-bank GDP nowcasting (IMF, BBVA/Camacho-Domenech), this method extracts one or two common latent factors — chiefly a global-liquidity/risk-capital factor and a real-activity factor — from a large panel of mixed-frequency macro and financial series using a Kalman-filter state-space DFM that handles ragged-edge data (series that report on different lags) natively. Bitcoin's return is regressed onto these factors to estimate its loading and a term structure of macro sensitivity; MIDAS weighting links high-frequency conditions to lower-frequency BTC aggregates without parameter proliferation. A 10-15yr CMA falls out by forecasting the factors forward under their estimated mean-reverting AR/VAR dynamics and multiplying by a decaying BTC loading. The implied appreciation is trend money/liquidity growth times BTC's (compressing) beta. The crucial caveat: DFMs are nowcasting/short-horizon tools — beyond ~4-8 quarters their forecasts collapse to the unconditional factor mean (a random walk with drift), so the framework is far stronger on volatility-regime and correlation structure than on a precise decade-ahead point return.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 2. Methodologically sound state-space machinery (Kalman/ragged-edge, endogenous mean-reversion gives the right decay shape) earns high rigor, but it is a nowcasting tool with a fatal horizon mismatch: beyond ~4-8 quarters it collapses to trend-liquidity-times-an-assumed-beta, adding little over a naive debasement assumption at 10-15yr. Signal/robustness are low because the liquidity beta is unstable and regime-dependent (post-2020 spike, ETF-era correlation shift) and the headline correlation is partly spurious trend. Data-ops is heavy: assembling and maintaining a large mixed-frequency panel plus DFM estimation is operationally burdensome for a CMA process.*


**Key drivers:** Global liquidity / broad-money factor (global M2, central-bank balance sheets, dollar funding) — the dominant common factor BTC loads on; Financial-conditions / financial-stress factor (NFCI, GFSI, credit spreads, equity realized vol) — GARCH-MIDAS finds Global Financial Stress Index a top long-term BTC-vol driver; Real-activity factor (ISM/PMI, Global Real Economic Activity / Kilian index, industrial production) — best single long-term BTC-volatility predictor in the crypto MIDAS literature; Real rates and the dollar (DXY, 10y TIPS yield) as the discount-rate / risk-appetite channel for a no-cashflow asset; BTC's time-varying factor loading (beta to the liquidity factor) and its assumed secular compression as the asset institutionalizes; Factor AR/VAR persistence and unconditional means — the mean-reversion that mechanically imposes appreciation decay at long horizons; Ragged-edge data-flow handling (Kalman filter) — the technical feature that lets daily/weekly/monthly series with different release lags enter one model; MIDAS lag-polynomial weights linking high-frequency macro conditions to lower-frequency BTC return/vol aggregates


**Pros:** Solves the mixed-frequency / ragged-edge data-flow problem no other BTC-CMA approach addresses: the Kalman filter ingests daily, weekly and monthly series with different release lags into one coherent state-space, so the factor estimate uses all information actually available at each date; Decay is endogenous, not hand-imposed: because the latent factors revert to their unconditional means under estimated AR/VAR dynamics, BTC's projected appreciation mechanically slows at long horizons — the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA, derived rather than asserted; Grounded in a genuinely strong empirical regularity: BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows (higher than any major asset class per Alden/Callahan), and the crypto GARCH-MIDAS literature shows real-activity and financial-stress factors significantly improve out-of-sample BTC volatility forecasts vs plain GARCH, especially in bear markets; Methodologically battle-tested: DFM/MIDAS nowcasting is the workhorse at the Fed, ECB, IMF and BBVA for GDP, with decades of validation, dimension-reduction discipline, and ML-augmented scalable variants (IMF WP/2022/052) — far more rigorous plumbing than S2F/Metcalfe curve-fits; Naturally produces the full CMA object: not just a point return but a factor-implied volatility regime (long-term GARCH-MIDAS component) and a correlation structure (BTC and equities co-load on the same liquidity factor), which most level-only BTC models cannot populate; Honest about uncertainty: the state-space form yields proper forecast-error bands and decomposes each release's contribution, so the analyst sees how fragile the long-horizon estimate is


**Cons:** Fatal horizon mismatch: DFMs are nowcasting / very-short-horizon tools. Beyond ~4-8 quarters their forecasts collapse to the unconditional factor mean — a random walk with drift — so a 10-15yr BTC return is essentially just 'trend liquidity growth times an assumed beta', and the elaborate factor machinery adds almost no information at that horizon over a naive debasement assumption; BTC's factor loading is unstable and regime-dependent: the beta to liquidity spiked post-2020, the BTC-equity correlation jumped in the ETF era, and the relationship 'on changes' (vs trend) is far weaker than the headline ~0.83 directional or ~0.94 levels correlation — which is itself partly the spurious-trend artifact that plagues the M2 cointegration approach (#7); Short BTC history (~15 years, ~3-4 liquidity cycles) is grossly insufficient to identify factor dynamics, the loading's secular decay path, or the unconditional means the long-horizon forecast reverts to — the very parameters that drive the CMA are the least well estimated; The crypto MIDAS literature is almost entirely about VOLATILITY, not expected RETURN: GARCH-MIDAS papers (Conrad-Custovic-Ghysels; Walther et al.) forecast BTC vol well but publish no multi-year return CMA, so the appreciation number is an analyst extension the peer-reviewed work does not actually deliver; ML augmentation (random forests, elastic-net preselection) improves nowcast accuracy but worsens interpretability and overfits a tiny sample at long horizons; it cannot manufacture signal that isn't in ~180 monthly observations; Liquidity / real-activity factors are themselves hard to forecast 10-15 years out — central-bank balance sheets, fiscal dominance and the dollar regime are deeply uncertain — so the 'exogenous' driver feeding the CMA is no more knowable than BTC itself; Says nothing structural about catastrophic BTC-specific tail risk (protocol failure, regulatory ban); the factor model prices BTC as a macro beta and ignores idiosyncratic left-tail mass, overstating the central forward return

Here the factor framework is HONEST where the digital-gold narratives are not: BTC and gold load only weakly on a common factor, and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). A liquidity/risk-asset factor model implies BTC co-moves far more with equities than with gold, so I keep gold correlation at the bottom of the band and explicitly reject any structural gold-substitution co-movement - the data and the model agree it isn't there. |

**Sources:** Dawn Holland, Iulia Ruxandra Teodoru, et al. / International Monetary Fund (2022) https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2022/english/wpiea2022052-print-pdf.pdf; Maximo Camacho and Rafael Domenech / BBVA Research, Universidad de Valencia (2019) https://www.uv.es/rdomenec/Camacho_Domenech_Nowcasting_and_Forecasting_with_DFM_2019.pdf; Christian Conrad, Anessa Custovic, Eric Ghysels (2018) https://www.mdpi.com/1911-8074/11/2/23/htm; Thomas Walther, Tony Klein, Elie Bouri (2019) https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1042443119302446; Sam Callahan and Lyn Alden / Lyn Alden Investment Strategy (2024) https://www.lynalden.com/bitcoin-a-global-liquidity-barometer/; Jaehyung An et al. (factor-augmented sparse MIDAS for nowcasting) (2023) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.13362


<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This approach lifts the central-bank GDP-nowcasting stack and points it at Bitcoin. The core object is a mixed-frequency dynamic factor model in state-space form: a large panel of macro/financial indicators (global M2 and central-bank balance sheets monthly; financial-conditions/stress indices and equity realized vol weekly/daily; ISM/PMI and Global Real Economic Activity monthly; real rates and the dollar daily) is assumed to be driven by a small number of common latent factors plus idiosyncratic noise. A Kalman filter estimates the factors and — critically — handles the 'ragged edge': at any date some series have reported through last week while others lag two months, and the filter treats the gaps as missing states rather than discarding data (Camacho-Domenech 2019; IMF WP/2022/052). MIDAS is the partial-model cousin: instead of compressing to factors, it links a high-frequency regressor to a lower-frequency target through a parsimonious lag polynomial (Almon/Beta weights), avoiding parameter proliferation. ML-augmented variants (IMF 2022; factor-augmented sparse MIDAS, arXiv 2306.13362) add elastic-net preselection or random forests to pick predictors and capture nonlinearity, improving nowcast accuracy especially around COVID. For BTC you extract a 'global liquidity / risk-capital' factor and a 'real-activity' factor, regress BTC return (DFM) or BTC volatility (GARCH-MIDAS) onto them, and read off a time-varying loading and a term structure of macro sensitivity.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The empirical anchor is strong and genuinely distinguishes this from numerology: Callahan/Alden (2024) find BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows and ~74% of 6-month windows, with a ~0.94 levels correlation May-2013..Jul-2024 — higher directional consistency than any major asset class. On the volatility side the peer-reviewed crypto MIDAS work is unusually clean: Conrad, Custovic & Ghysels (2018) and Walther, Klein & Bouri (2019) both find that a long-term volatility component driven by Global Real Economic Activity (Kilian index) and the Global Financial Stress Index dominates, that S&P 500 realized vol loads negatively on long-term BTC vol, and that these mixed-frequency specifications beat plain GARCH out-of-sample, especially in bear markets.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The decisive caveat is horizon. DFM/MIDAS are nowcasting and very-short-horizon forecasting tools; their comparative advantage is squeezing today's release flow into a current-quarter estimate. At long horizons the latent factors revert to their unconditional means under the estimated AR/VAR dynamics, so the multi-year forecast collapses to a random walk with drift — i.e., 'trend liquidity growth times beta'. The elaborate ragged-edge machinery that makes the nowcast superb adds essentially nothing to a 10-15yr point return. Worse, the parameters that DO drive a decade CMA — BTC's secular loading-decay path and the factors' unconditional means — are the least identifiable from ~15 years and only 3-4 liquidity cycles. The headline 0.94 levels correlation is partly the same spurious-trend artifact that undermines the M2-cointegration approach (#7): on contemporaneous CHANGES the relationship weakens markedly. And the loading is regime-unstable — it spiked post-2020 and the BTC-equity correlation jumped in the ETF era — so projecting it forward is guesswork dressed in a Kalman filter. ML augmentation cannot rescue this; it overfits a tiny sample at long horizons.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Pure peer-reviewed DFM/MIDAS work on BTC publishes volatility forecasts, NOT a multi-year return CMA — so a 10-15yr appreciation number is an analyst extension the literature does not itself deliver (an honesty point worth flagging). The closest on-record liquidity-factor RETURN projections are practitioner and explicitly short-horizon: Alden/Callahan's probability-weighted global-liquidity model implies ~+56% over 1yr (~$110k) and ~+104% over 2yr (~$144k) — 1-2yr liquidity-cycle calls, not a decade assumption. CF Benchmarks' CMA, which folds a macro-liquidity (global-M2 risk-capital) overlay into a three-model framework, is the nearest thing to a published forward CMA in this family: base case 30.1%/yr to a $1.42M 2035 target, vol declining toward ~28%, equity correlation 0.52->0.15, bonds 0.14->0.22, gold ~0.06 unchanged. I treat the 30.1% as over-optimistic (it leans on aggressive terminal adoption, not on factor mean-reversion) and the ~0.15 equity correlation as aspirational — the factor logic actually predicts equity correlation stays meaningfully positive because BTC and equities share the liquidity factor. The defensible synthesized read: ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, equity correlation ~0.40-0.55 and structurally the model's strongest claim, gold correlation ~0 — where this framework is admirably honest that BTC is a liquidity-driven risk asset, not digital gold.

</details>

### #54 · Stablecoin-Float Liquidity-Onramp Demand Sink

*Family: liquidity-onramp-stablecoin · Source: Official sector · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 38*


**Explanation:** The thesis: BTC can only be bought with on-ramped dollars, and the dominant on-chain dollar is the stablecoin. Aggregate stablecoin market cap is therefore the crypto-native "dry powder" that caps how much marginal bidding can occur; the Stablecoin Supply Ratio (BTC cap / stablecoin cap) operationalizes it — low SSR = ample buying power, high SSR = exhausted. Official-sector work hardens the macro side: reserve-backed stablecoins are now a real marginal buyer of T-bills (a 2σ inflow cuts 3-month yields 2.5-3.5bp, 5-8bp when bills are scarce — BIS WP 1270), and their growth raises safe-asset demand and pressures r-star (Richmond Fed). To get a 10-15yr CMA you must forecast stablecoin-float growth, a BTC-absorption multiple per new dollar, and SSR mean-reversion — none native to the framework. The fatal empirical wrinkle (NY Fed): stablecoin inflows FOLLOW large BTC up-moves with a lag, so the float reflects demand rather than gating it. For a CMA this means stablecoins are a coincident liquidity barometer, not an independent appreciation engine; usable only for regime/timing, anchoring forward returns to BTC's realized appreciation decay.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 4, orthogonality 3. Genuine official-sector rigor (BIS WP 1270 IV-identified, Richmond Fed GE) but it lands on T-bill yields/r-star, not BTC price — the BTC-return leap is unsupported, and NY Fed shows the float LAGS BTC moves, making forward forecasting circular. No native return/vol/correlation; any CMA level is bolted-on judgment, adding little over the decay anchor. Robustness is weak as an exogenous driver but the SSR float is highly auditable, high-frequency, and trivial to operationalize, earning strong data_ops.*


**Key drivers:** Aggregate dollar-stablecoin market cap / float (~$200-250bn 2025) as the crypto-native dollar liquidity base and 'dry powder' reservoir; Stablecoin Supply Ratio (SSR = BTC mktcap / stablecoin mktcap) and its mean-reversion band — the proximate timing instrument; Net stablecoin minting/burning and exchange-deposit inflows (velocity toward exchange addresses signals rotation into BTC); Short-dated US Treasury (T-bill) supply/scarcity — gates the macro safe-asset price impact (state-dependent: 2.5-3.5bp ample, 5-8bp scarce per BIS); Reserve-backed vs crypto-backed stablecoin mix — reserve-backed raise Treasury/dollar demand and press r-star; crypto-backed reduce it (Richmond Fed); Regulatory regime (GENIUS Act) mandating safe reserve backing — channels stablecoin growth into Treasury demand and legitimizes the float; Lag structure: BTC price up-moves LEAD stablecoin inflows by several days (NY Fed) — the float is largely a coincident/lagging mirror of demand, not exogenous


**Pros:** Grounds BTC bidding in an observable, high-frequency, crypto-native quantity (stablecoin float / SSR) rather than price extrapolation or scarcity numerology — and the float is auditable on-chain in near-real-time; Has genuine official-sector empirical backing for the MACRO link: BIS WP 1270 establishes a causal, IV-identified, state-dependent effect of stablecoin flows on T-bill yields, and Richmond Fed gives a coherent general-equilibrium safe-asset/r-star channel — far more rigorous than S2F/Metcalfe; SSR is a falsifiable, mean-reverting timing tool with some ex-post record of bracketing buying-power extremes; ties BTC to a concrete on-ramp constraint (you cannot bid without on-ramped dollars); Connects BTC to the broader dollar/safe-asset complex, giving a portfolio-coherent macro narrative (debasement on-ramp + Treasury demand) distinct from the broad-M2 barometer and the eurodollar-collateral channel


**Cons:** Causation runs the WRONG way for a demand driver: NY Fed shows stablecoin inflows FOLLOW large BTC up-moves with a multi-day lag, so the float is a coincident/lagging mirror of demand, not an exogenous 'sink' that gates it — using it to forecast forward returns is largely circular; Not a return model at all: it yields no native expected appreciation, volatility, or correlation; any 10-15yr CMA is bolted-on (float-growth × absorption multiple × SSR drift), none of which the literature estimates; The macro evidence is about T-BILL YIELDS, not BTC price: BIS WP 1270 and Richmond Fed never forecast BTC return — the BTC-pricing leap is the approach's own, unsupported by the cited official-sector work; Structural leakage and regime change: stablecoins increasingly fund non-BTC uses (cross-border payments, DeFi, T-bill yield, ETFs that never touch on-chain dollars), so float ≠ BTC dry powder; the ETF/institutional marginal buyer often bypasses stablecoins entirely, breaking the gating link; Tiny calibration window (2021-2025) spanning few cycles; SSR 'bands' drift and the indicator is among the on-chain cohort with unstable out-of-sample performance

METHODOLOGY. The approach fuses two layers. (1) A practitioner micro-instrument: aggregate dollar-stablecoin market cap as crypto-native "dry powder," operationalized via the Stablecoin Supply Ratio (SSR = BTC market cap / stablecoin market cap, CryptoQuant/Glassnode). Low/falling SSR = abundant stablecoin buying-power relative to BTC (bullish capacity); high SSR = exhausted. The bull narrative: BTC can only be bid with on-ramped dollars, and the dominant on-chain dollar is the stablecoin, so the float is the binding capacity constraint; new minting and stablecoin flows to exchange-deposit addresses are read as a leading rotation signal. (2) An official-sector macro layer establishing that the float is now systemically large: BIS WP 1270 (Ahmed & Aldasoro, 2025) uses daily 2021-2025 data and an IV strategy to show a 2σ stablecoin inflow lowers 3-month T-bill yields 2.5-3.5bp, rising to 5-8bp during bill scarcity (RRP drain, debt-ceiling episodes), concentrated in short maturities; ~$200bn AUM by Mar-2025, ~$40bn of T-bills bought in 2024 (rivaling the largest government MMFs). Richmond Fed EB 26-10 (Azzimonti & Quadrini, 2026) adds a GE result: reserve-backed stablecoins raise safe-asset/dollar demand and press the natural rate r-star DOWN, while crypto-backed reduce Treasury demand; under GENIUS-Act-style reserve mandates the dollar is reinforced, not threatened.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & HISTORICAL FIT. The "dry powder" pattern has visual support: 2020-2021 stablecoin supply grew ~$20bn→$120bn+ as BTC ran $10k→$69k; major BTC rallies have been preceded by float expansions. The SSR has bracketed buying-power extremes ex-post. BIS provides the cleanest causal evidence in the whole crypto-macro literature for the float→T-bill-yield link.

THE FATAL WRINKLE (faithfully represented). The NY Fed update (Anadu et al., 2025, Liberty Street; SSRN 5227592) directly tests the direction and finds capital flows INTO all stablecoins FOLLOW large BTC price increases (top-5% return days), measured over an ~8-day window — i.e., BTC up-moves LEAD stablecoin inflows, and riskier offshore/crypto-backed coins get the biggest inflows while US-based asset-backed coins' inflows are "barely statistically significant." This inverts the gating premise: the float largely MIRRORS demand with a lag rather than supplying exogenous demand. For a forward CMA this is decisive — a lagging coincident indicator cannot drive expected returns; it is at best a regime/timing overlay. Compounding this, the official-sector sources price T-BILLS, never BTC: the leap from "stablecoins move bill yields" to "stablecoins set BTC's 10-15yr return" is entirely the approach's own and is unsupported by the cited work.

FAILURE MODES. (a) Reverse causality / circularity (NY Fed). (b) Leakage: stablecoins increasingly fund cross-border payments, DeFi collateral, T-bill yield-harvesting and (post-2024) sit beside ETF rails where the marginal institutional BTC buyer uses cash equities plumbing that never touches an on-chain dollar — so float ≠ BTC dry powder, and the gap is widening. (c) Tiny window (2021-2025), few cycles, drifting SSR bands, unstable out-of-sample like the broader on-chain-indicator cohort. (d) Mis-specification risk: total float conflates demand-sink and store-of-yield uses.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None of the official-sector sources produce a multi-year BTC price/return forecast via this channel — by design, they forecast yields and dollar demand, not BTC. Practitioner SSR commentary is explicitly a timing/mean-reversion signal, not an annualized CMA. So unlike S2F ($288k-$500k+) or power-law ($1M+), this family has produced NO credible on-record multi-year BTC appreciation forecast — which is itself informative: its proponents treat it as a liquidity barometer, not a return engine. Synthesized CMA therefore anchors to the realized-decay baseline (~8-12% nominal, vol ~55-60%, equity corr ~0.45-0.55, gold corr ~0-0.15), treating the stablecoin float as a coincident liquidity-regime overlay rather than an independent appreciation driver.

### #55 · Machine-Learning Forecasting & Empirical Asset Pricing (DL/Trees/On-Chain ML/Gu-Kelly-Xiu/HMM)

*Family: ml-forecasting · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 38*


**Explanation:** These models learn a flexible mapping from predictors (technicals, macro factors, on-chain metrics, latent regimes) to next-period Bitcoin returns, letting nonlinear interactions emerge rather than imposing a line. Gu-Kelly-Xiu (2020) is the canonical empirical-asset-pricing version: trees and neural nets beat linear models, but the monthly out-of-sample R-squared is only ~0.3-0.4% in equities, with momentum, liquidity and volatility as dominant signals. For Bitcoin specifically, futures studies find ML directional accuracy near 56% intraday — barely above an ARIMA/coin-flip benchmark — and random forests that hit 87% in-sample collapse out-of-sample (overfitting). Bayesian Hidden Markov models add value by detecting bull/bear/calm regimes (predictors: momentum, VIX, Treasury yield), and TFT-style deep nets flag gold and the dollar as top macro drivers. The key implication for a 10-15yr CMA: edge is short-horizon and directional, decaying to random-walk-with-drift at long horizons. ML therefore cannot supply a decade appreciation level — only regime/correlation texture layered on the realized-decay baseline.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 3, orthogonality 2. Methodologically the most disciplined family here — strict OOS splits, SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano tests, economic-significance metrics — so rigor is high. But for a 10-15yr CMA level its predictive signal is near-zero: the documented edge is intraday-to-monthly (~56% directional, ~0.4% monthly OOS R2) and collapses to random-walk-with-drift at decade horizon, supplying no independent appreciation level. Robustness is weak because the noise-dominated, regime-shifting crypto data is exactly where these models overfit and degrade out-of-sample. Data is available but on-chain/feature pipelines and retraining add operational friction, and the framework's only durable CMA contribution is regime/tail conditioning (HMM), not the level.*


**Key drivers:** Predictor/feature set: technical (lagged returns, momentum, volatility), macro (VIX, US Treasury yield, USD index, gold, oil), and on-chain (active addresses, hashrate, NVT, exchange flows); Model class and its inductive bias: tree ensembles (RF/XGBoost/LightGBM) for tabular feature interactions vs sequence DL (LSTM/GRU/TFT) for temporal structure vs Bayesian HMM for latent regimes; Nonlinear predictor interactions — the documented source of ML's edge over linear models (Gu-Kelly-Xiu); Forecast horizon — the single most important driver of realized edge: predictability is concentrated intraday-to-monthly and decays toward random-walk at multi-year horizons; Latent regime state (bull/bear/calm) and the transition probabilities governing it (non-homogeneous HMM); Training-window stationarity / regime stability — performance is highly sensitive to whether the test period resembles the training period; Sample size and signal-to-noise — DL needs large data; crypto is noise-dominated, amplifying overfitting; Structural breaks (ETF/institutionalization) that degrade on-chain feature informativeness as the marginal buyer leaves the chain


**Pros:** Brutally honest about long-horizon limits: unlike S2F/Metcalfe/power-law, this family's own evidence says the edge is short-horizon and directional and degenerates to random-walk-with-drift at long horizons — which is the correct, conservative prior for a 10-15yr CMA (argues AGAINST extrapolating supra-decay returns); Genuinely out-of-sample and statistically disciplined: Gu-Kelly-Xiu and crypto follow-ups use strict train/validation/test splits, SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano tests, and economic (not just statistical) performance metrics — a higher evidentiary bar than the in-sample R-squared bragging of scarcity models; Captures nonlinearity and regime structure that linear/parametric models miss: HMMs cleanly separate bull/bear/calm regimes, and trees/NNs surface real nonlinear interactions, giving useful texture for the correlation and volatility-clustering side of a CMA even when they fail on the level; Identifies which drivers actually matter empirically (momentum, liquidity, volatility, VIX, Treasury yield, gold, USD) rather than asserting a single narrative driver — useful for building defensible correlation views; Model-agnostic and refreshable: can ingest new features (on-chain, ETF-flow, macro) and be re-estimated as regimes shift, with explicit overfitting diagnostics


**Cons:** Not a long-horizon model at all: the documented edge is intraday-to-monthly; at the decade horizon relevant to a CMA, learned predictors collapse to the unconditional random-walk-with-drift, so they supply NO independent appreciation level — the CMA still has to come from the realized-decay baseline; Severe overfitting / data-snooping risk in noise-dominated crypto data: random forests reaching 87% in-sample accuracy degrade to ~56% out-of-sample (barely above an ARIMA or coin-flip benchmark); with enough trials a beautiful backtest produces no real edge — the 'Training Set Delusion'; Tiny effective edge even when real: Gu-Kelly-Xiu's best monthly out-of-sample R-squared is ~0.4% in equities; for BTC, directional accuracy clusters near 50-56%, and transaction costs/non-stationarity routinely erase the gross edge; Non-stationarity and structural breaks break the models: crypto volatility, liquidity and behavior shift swiftly; ETF/institutionalization is documented to degrade on-chain feature informativeness (marginal buyer no longer touches the chain), so a model trained pre-ETF mis-specifies the post-ETF regime; Black-box / unstable feature importance: TFT calls gold the top driver, futures studies call SVM most robust, HMMs call momentum/VIX dominant — no consensus signal, and importances are sample-dependent, so the framework cannot be relied on to populate stable CMA correlations; Silent on equilibrium value: ML learns conditional means from history and has no anchor for a no-cashflow asset's fair value, so it cannot discipline whether BTC is over/undervalued at the horizon — it can only extrapolate the empirical drift it was trained on

The digital-gold linkage is not empirically supported by realized correlation. |

(Journal of Forecasting 44:1666-1698) (2025) https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/for.3258; Constandina Koki, Stefanos Leonardos, Georgios Piliouras (Research in International Business and Finance 59) (2022) https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0275531921001756; Akyildirim, Goncu, Sensoy et al. (PMC8296834) (2021) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8296834/; Jiahui Wang, Chen Zeng, Nan Li, Qiao Wang (SSRN 5797242) (2025) https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/5797242.pdf?abstractid=5797242&mirid=1; Hajar Novinsalari, Ahmet Şensoy (SSRN 5614913) (2025) https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5614913


<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This family pools five learned-predictor strands that share a core property absent from the existing 20 approaches: they impose almost no functional form and let the data choose a nonlinear conditional-mean (or regime) function. (1) Gu-Kelly-Xiu (2020, RFS 33:2223-2273) is the canonical empirical-asset-pricing-via-ML template — estimate E[r|z] over a large characteristic set with penalized regressions, random forests, gradient-boosted trees and neural nets, then compare strictly out-of-sample. Their headline equities results: trees and neural nets dominate (monthly OOS R-squared ~0.33-0.40%, vs near-zero/negative for OLS), with momentum, liquidity and volatility the dominant signals; a NN-sorted long-short decile earns Sharpe 1.35 (VW) / 2.45 (EW), and NN S&P timing earns Sharpe 0.77. (2) Deep sequence models — Köse et al. (2025, J. Forecasting 44:1666-1698) run LSTM/GRU/CNN/TFT plus XGBoost/LightGBM/SVR on BTC vs global macro; the Temporal Fusion Transformer wins and ranks GOLD the single most relevant feature, USD index second. (3) Tree/SVM ensembles on microstructure — Akyildirim/Goncu/Sensoy (PMC8296834) test six ML models on CME BTC-futures mid-price direction at 5-60min: SVM most robust (~56% OOS), random forest 87% in-sample collapsing OOS (classic overfit), ARIMA ceiling ~56% — i.e. ML barely clears a naive benchmark. (4) On-chain-feature ML feeds active addresses, hashrate, NVT and exchange flows into classifiers. (5) Bayesian/non-homogeneous Hidden Markov regime models — Koki, Leonardos & Piliouras (2022, RIIBAF 59) find a 4-state NHHM gives the best one-step-ahead forecasts for BTC/ETH/XRP, with momentum, VIX and US Treasury yield the most common predictors, cleanly separating bull/bear/calm regimes.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & CMA PAYLOAD. The shared, brutally honest message: documented edge is short-horizon and directional, and degenerates toward a random-walk-with-drift as the horizon lengthens. This is exactly the opposite of the S2F/Metcalfe/power-law/gold-parity family, which extrapolates supra-decay returns. For a 10-15yr CMA, the implication is a NEGATIVE result — ML supplies no defensible decade appreciation level beyond the unconditional drift, so the CMA defaults to the realized-decay baseline (~8-12% nominal). What ML DOES contribute is texture: regime structure (HMM bull/bear/calm, fat tails, vol clustering — supporting a high ~55-60% vol floor rather than smooth convergence to gold-like vol) and a learned cross-asset dependence set (VIX/Treasury-yield/USD/gold) that supports a high equity correlation (~0.45-0.55) and a modest, predictor-driven — not co-movement-driven — relationship to gold.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. In-sample fit is often spectacular and almost entirely illusory: the 'Training Set Delusion' (Wang, Zeng, Li & Wang, 2025, SSRN 5797242) documents that BTC return/vol ML models are pervasively overfit; the broader literature applies SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano tests precisely because naive backtests are contaminated by data-snooping. Non-stationarity is fatal — crypto volatility, liquidity and news-response shift swiftly, so a model trained in one regime mis-specifies the next. The most important structural break is institutionalization: post-ETF, the marginal buyer no longer touches the chain, degrading on-chain feature informativeness; a pre-2024-trained on-chain-ML model is arguably mis-specified today. Novinsalari & Sensoy (2025, SSRN 5614913) find ML on BTC ETFs beats 50% accuracy and claim weak-form-EMH violations, but such edges are intraday/short-horizon and typically die to transaction costs — they do NOT scale to a decade view. Feature importance is unstable across studies (TFT says gold; futures study says SVM/microstructure; HMM says momentum/VIX), so the framework cannot reliably pin CMA correlations.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. Notably, this family produces essentially NO credible on-record multi-year point forecasts — which is itself the finding. Reputable academic ML work confines itself to short horizons (intraday to one-month) and reports R-squared/accuracy/Sharpe, not 10-15yr price targets. Where multi-year ML 'predictions' appear, they are practitioner/ainvest-style ($X by date) extrapolations of a short-horizon model run forward, which the academic literature's own horizon-decay result discredits. Gu-Kelly-Xiu is explicitly a measurement of conditional risk premia, not a long-run forecast. The honest CMA use of ML is therefore as a discipline that rejects long-horizon extrapolation and anchors to the empirical drift plus regime/correlation structure — not as a source of a decade appreciation number.

</details>

### #56 · Structural Stock-Flow Demand-Clearing Engine (Inelastic-Supply Price-Multiplier)

*Family: supply-demand-clearing · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 38*


**Explanation:** The model treats Bitcoin issuance as a vertical supply line and clears it against a CES demand curve each period. The only supply that matters is the LIQUID float (total minus lost coins and strategic-reserve HODLings). Two exogenous inputs drive price: a daily withdrawal flow (BTC/day pulled into ETFs/treasuries/sovereign reserves) that shifts the vertical line left, and a demand-shift multiplier (10X-40X) that scales demand. Because supply cannot respond to price, withdrawals against a thinning float push the clearing price up nonlinearly, going 'hyperbolic' once liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC. Key inputs: initial liquid supply, daily withdrawal rate, demand-shift parameter, CES elasticity, and (v2) a fiat withdrawal-sensitivity term that throttles coin removal as USD price rises. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it implies a wide, scenario-dependent appreciation range whose central case (~mid-teens to ~40% nominal CAGR) sits far below BTC's ~100% historical CAGR but well above most cross-approach centrals — and it warns that volatility RISES, not falls, as scarcity binds, the opposite of the institutionalization-dampens-vol thesis.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 2, orthogonality 3. Theoretically the most honest family here — it actually solves for a clearing price from inelastic supply x flow rather than extrapolating price history, which is structurally correct and earns it a real edge on regime robustness (no halving/S2F-trend dependence). But signal is weak: the headline output hinges on an ad-hoc, unestimated demand-shift multiplier (10-40X) the authors themselves warn against overinterpreting, plus a severe advocacy conflict of interest that engineers the bullish sovereign-withdrawal input — so its level forecast adds little over the decay anchor and its main contribution is the inelastic-float regime/tail conditioning. Data_ops is poor: liquid-float, lost-coin, and withdrawal-flow estimates are noisy, contested, and not cleanly maintainable in a recurring CMA process.*


**Key drivers:** Initial LIQUID float: total supply minus lost coins (~17%+) minus HODLed/strategic-reserve coins; authors estimate ~40-50% already removed from liquid supply, leaving the clearing-sensitive base near ~2M BTC at the 'hyperbolic' threshold; Daily withdrawal rate (BTC/day) from liquid supply into ETFs/corporate treasuries/sovereign reserves/cold storage — the left-shift of the vertical supply line (scenarios span 0 to 4000 BTC/day); Demand-shift multiplier (D / A', e.g. 10X, 20X, 30X, 40X over the horizon) scaling the CES demand curve — captures institutional/sovereign adoption and credit-funded demand; CES demand elasticity (ε, ~ -2.10 conservative down to ~ -0.86 most-inelastic) — controls how fast the clearing price accelerates as the float thins; Perfectly inelastic (vertical) supply curve set by the fixed halving issuance schedule — the structural 'price-multiplier' premise; Fiat-denominated withdrawal sensitivity (v2): coins withdrawn per day FALL as USD price rises, the built-in damping that produces appreciation DECAY rather than runaway hyperbola; Epstein-Zin recursive-utility intertemporal preference (v2) — separates risk aversion from elasticity of intertemporal substitution in the demand block; Lost-coin / HODL-wave estimates feeding the liquid-vs-illiquid split (acknowledged as highly uncertain)


**Pros:** Genuinely endogenizes the clearing price from first-principles supply-demand intersection rather than extrapolating price history (S2F/power-law) or regressing on a single trend (Metcalfe/M2) — it is the only family here that SOLVES for price from flow x inelasticity; Peer-reviewed (JRFM, two papers 2025) with a transparent, fully parameterized and reproducible model (Analytica implementation + Figshare data posted), so every lever (float, withdrawal, demand-shift, elasticity) is auditable and stress-testable; Correctly captures a real, observable structural fact: Bitcoin's supply is perfectly issuance-inelastic, so a demand/flow shock has nowhere to go but price — the CoinShares evidence (≈4500 BTC/day ETF demand vs ≈921 minted; OTC holdings -74%, exchange balances -29% since 2020) shows the float really is thinning; Naturally produces appreciation DECAY in the honest version: the v2 fiat-withdrawal-sensitivity term throttles BTC removed as USD price climbs, and the authors explicitly flag that a steady multi-thousand-coin daily drain 'may not continue as price increases' — the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA; Triangulates within an order of magnitude of independent frameworks (MicroStrategy Bitcoin24, power-law, ARK) at the 2036 horizon, lending some convergent credibility to the central (not tail) scenarios; Makes a falsifiable, non-consensus VOLATILITY claim — that vol RISES as liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC (inelastic supply meeting inelastic demand), contradicting the institutionalization-lowers-vol narrative and giving a CMA a defensible high-vol floor


**Cons:** Severe conflict of interest: co-author Dennis Porter runs Satoshi Action Education/Fund (board + employment) and Rudd consults for it — a Bitcoin-policy advocacy nonprofit lobbying US states/governments to ADOPT strategic Bitcoin reserves, which is precisely the 'sovereign withdrawal' input that drives the model's bullish output. The model assumes the outcome its authors lobby for.; The demand-shift multiplier D is set 'in an ad hoc way' by the authors' own admission — there is no empirical estimation of the demand curve, so the headline scenarios ($1M 2027, $2M 2027, $5M 2031) are assumption-driven, not derived; the authors caution explicitly 'against overinterpretation of the projections on the upper end'; 'Hyperbolic' runaway price is conceded as possibly a 'first-generation model artefact' of the fixed-elasticity CES form — a model that produces multimillion-dollar tails because a vertical supply curve meets an inelastic demic curve is structurally rigged toward explosive output and may simply be mis-specified; Withdrawal-rate exogeneity is the load-bearing fiction: in reality net flows are price-RESPONSIVE (high prices entice lost/dormant coins and HODLers to sell, adding liquid supply), so the assumed steady multi-thousand-coin daily drain is the thing most likely to break exactly when the model says price accelerates; Calibrated only to the post-April-2024 halving with ~1-2 years of ETF data — no out-of-sample validation, tiny sample, and the liquid-supply / lost-coin estimates (~40-50% removed) are highly uncertain and could be wrong by a wide margin, which the authors acknowledge; Ignores Layer-2/Lightning, off-chain and custodial netting, and the demonetization-of-other-assets channel by construction — the float and demand measures are partial, and ETF/custodial concentration can hold coins that are economically liquid but appear 'withdrawn'; Says little directly about cross-asset CORRELATIONS — it is a price-path/clearing model, not a distributional CMA, so correlations to equities/FI/TIPS/gold must be imported from realized data

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Rudd & Porter (JRFM 2025, two papers) build a discrete, forward-simulating market-CLEARING engine. Each period they intersect a perfectly inelastic (vertical) supply curve — fixed by the halving issuance schedule — with a constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) demand curve, and read off the equilibrium clearing price. The innovation vs descriptive on-chain gauges is that supply is the LIQUID float, not total coins: they net out lost coins (~17%+ via HODL waves, plus Satoshi's stash) and strategic-reserve/long-term HODLings, estimating ~40-50% of total supply already removed from liquid circulation. Two exogenous inputs move the system: a daily WITHDRAWAL rate (BTC/day pulled from liquid supply into ETFs, treasuries, sovereign reserves, cold storage), which shifts the vertical line leftward, and a DEMAND-SHIFT multiplier D/A' (10X-40X over the horizon) scaling the CES curve. Paper 1 (18(2):66, Jan 2025) calibrates to the April-2024 halving (ε about -2.10, L_Min=0.04, T*=8yr logistic) and a Dec-2024 $102k recalibration. Paper 2 (18(10):570, Oct 2025) upgrades the demand block with Epstein-Zin recursive utility (separating risk aversion from intertemporal substitution) and a FIAT-denominated withdrawal-sensitivity term (coins removed per day fall as USD price rises), then Monte-Carlos across five variables (demand level, intertemporal preference, withdrawal sensitivity, initial liquid supply, daily withdrawal).

KEY RELATIONSHIP. Because supply is vertical, price acceleration is nonlinear: as the float thins, the clearing point slides into the inelastic region of demand and small withdrawals move price a lot. The papers state 'hyperbolic' appreciation appears once liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC; the v2 Monte Carlo finds such paths 'relatively rare,' concentrated where liquid supply is near/below 2M and withdrawal sensitivity is low.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS (produced THIS way). Paper 1: conservative path reaches $1M by ~June 2028 at 4000 BTC/day (autumn 2028 at 2000/day); a 10X demand shift with ZERO withdrawals still yields >$600k; CAGR tops 40.2% (2000 BTC/day + 30X demand). Bull scenario: $1M early 2027, $2M late 2027, $5M early 2031. Paper 2: 50% probability BTC > $5.17M and 75% > $4.81M by April 2036, with a stated range from 'low single millions to low tens of millions.' The authors cite BTC's 13yr historical CAGR (99.5%) for context and a v2 bull 2036 CAGR of 43.6% (D=40, 2000 BTC/day). They triangulate to MicroStrategy Bitcoin24 (baseline CAGR 29.2%, bull 37.5%, $13M by 2045) and a power-law 2036 fit (~$2.1M), claiming surprising convergence near $2-3M for 2036.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The model is calibrated, not validated out-of-sample — only ~1-2 years of post-halving ETF data, with highly uncertain lost-coin/liquid-supply inputs. Five self-disclosed limitations: (1) fixed-elasticity CES 'may oversimplify'; the forecasts are 'only a narrow slice from the very large space of possible demand curves'; (2) reliance on uncertain lost-coin estimates; (3) no Layer-2/Lightning dynamics; (4) credit-funded demand shocks could spike D unpredictably; (5) — most damning — the hyperbolic growth 'may be an artefact of our first-generation model.' The demand multiplier D is set 'in an ad hoc way.' The deepest economic flaw is exogenous, price-insensitive withdrawal: in reality high prices entice dormant coins and HODLers back to market, ADDING liquid supply exactly when the model says price runs away — the assumed steady multi-thousand-coin drain is the input most likely to break.

CONFLICT OF INTEREST (load-bearing for skepticism). Co-author Dennis Porter is on the board of and employed by Satoshi Action Education/Fund, a 501(c)(3) that lobbies US state and federal governments to ADOPT strategic Bitcoin reserves; Rudd reports a consulting/advisory relationship with it. The 'sovereign/institutional withdrawal' input that drives the bullish output is precisely the policy outcome the authors advocate — the model assumes the result its authors lobby for. This does not invalidate the clearing MECHANISM (which is the most economically coherent of the BTC valuation families — it genuinely solves a market rather than regressing on a trend like S2F/Metcalfe/M2), but it means the published demand-path scenarios and price targets should be treated as advocacy-aligned, not neutral estimates.

CMA IMPLICATION. The honest, transferable content is the inelastic-float clearing mechanism plus the v2 decay term — keep those, discard the asserted demand path and disowned hyperbola. A credible 10-15yr extrapolation of BTC's realized decay (142->65->17%/yr) under price-responsive (not exogenous) flows lands appreciation near low-double-digits (synthesized ~9-14% nominal), modestly above the cross-approach central because the thinning-float mechanism is real (CoinShares: ~4500 BTC/day ETF demand vs ~921 minted; OTC -74%, exchange balances -29% since 2020). Uniquely, the model argues vol RISES with scarcity (supply-shock corners), supporting a high vol floor (~55-65%) rather than the institutionalization-compression view. It is silent on cross-asset correlations, which must be imported from realized data; the demonetization-of-gold framing is a sizing narrative, not a measured gold correlation (realized ~0).

### #57 · Behavioral-Preference / Disagreement Overvaluation (Lottery-MAX, Miller, Scheinkman-Xiong)

*Family: behavioral-overvaluation · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 37*


**Explanation:** Value is set by who holds the asset and what they believe, not by cashflow or scarcity. Lottery/prospect-theory investors overpay for extreme positive skew, so high-MAX/high-PT coins are overpriced and subsequently underperform (a one-SD rise in PT value cuts next-week return ~0.71%; high-minus-low MAX spreads exceed ~1.5-3%/week). Separately, Miller (1977) and Scheinkman-Xiong (2003) show that when opinions diverge AND shorting is blocked, price reflects only optimists plus a resale-option bubble, with high volume and volatility. The forward-CMA signal is a decay rule: the overvaluation premium erodes as the holder base institutionalizes and as short/margin/options infrastructure deepens. Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu (2025) show the crypto disagreement premium literally vanishes once a coin's margin trading is switched on. Because these effects concentrate in small, illiquid, hard-to-short coins — not Bitcoin, which now has CME futures, IBIT options and inverse ETFs — the family implies BTC's behavioral premium is mostly gone, so a 10-15yr BTC CMA should extrapolate decayed, near-risk-asset returns, not historical levels.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 3, data-ops 2, orthogonality 3. Peer-reviewed, mechanism-based, falsifiable theory (rigor 4), but it is a weekly cross-sectional anomaly that produces no BTC level and concentrates in small illiquid coins — Bitcoin is exactly where the effect is weakest, so direct 10-15yr predictive signal is poor (signal 2). It does carry one genuinely valuable, regime-aware contribution: an infrastructure-conditional DECAY mechanism explaining why BTC appreciation eroded as shorting/options/holder-base institutionalized, which survives and even anticipates regime change (robustness 3). Data ops are awkward: requires high-frequency cross-coin MAX/PT/disagreement/short-constraint inputs and bespoke judgment to graft onto a CMA, with no off-the-shelf level output (data_ops 2).*


**Key drivers:** Lottery/MAX demand: maximum recent daily return as a positive-skew proxy; high MAX = overpriced = lower future return (negative cross-sectional relation); Cumulative-prospect-theory (PT) value of the historical return distribution (probability weighting of tails + loss aversion); high PT value = overpriced; Divergence of opinion / disagreement, proxied by abnormal trading volume (Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu) or forecast dispersion (Miller); Short-sale constraints — the binding condition that lets optimists set the price; relaxing them (margin, futures, options, inverse ETFs, borrow) removes the overvaluation; Resale-option / speculative-bubble component (Scheinkman-Xiong): holders pay above own valuation expecting to sell to a more optimistic future buyer; scales with overconfidence and trading frictions; Holder-base composition / institutionalization: lottery-seeking retail vs diversified rational marginal holder; Limits to arbitrage (illiquidity, transaction costs, coin size) — the anomaly amplifies where arbitrage is costly and is largest in small/low-price coins, minimal in BTC


**Pros:** Peer-reviewed, mechanism-based, and falsifiable: the lottery/MAX (Financial Innovation 2021; JIFMIM 2021, 2024), prospect-theory (JIFMIM 2022), and disagreement (Financial Management 2025) papers report signed, significant cross-sectional effects, grounded in Miller (JF 1977) and Scheinkman-Xiong (JPE 2003) classics; Supplies a genuine, infrastructure-conditional DECAY mechanism absent from factor-regression and LPPLS approaches: the overvaluation premium shrinks as shorting/margin/options deepen and the holder base institutionalizes — directly relevant to why BTC's realized appreciation decayed 142->65->17%/yr; Contrarian and disciplined: it predicts LOWER (not higher) forward returns for the most hyped, lottery-like, hard-to-short assets — a useful antidote to S2F/Metcalfe/power-law extrapolation that the academic literature rejects; Explains BTC's high volatility and large trading volume as equilibrium outcomes of disagreement + resale-option speculation, not anomalies to be assumed away (Scheinkman-Xiong); Empirically self-validating on BTC: Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu show the disagreement premium DISAPPEARS once margin trading activates, and BTC already has deep two-sided infrastructure (CME futures since 2017, IBIT options since Nov-2024, inverse ETFs), so the framework's own logic says BTC's behavioral premium is largely spent


**Cons:** It is a CROSS-SECTIONAL anomaly, not a level/CMA model: it ranks coins and predicts relative under/over-performance over weekly horizons, not an absolute 10-15yr BTC appreciation, volatility, or correlation. Any CMA number is grafted on, not produced.; The alphas concentrate in small, illiquid, low-price, costly-to-arbitrage coins and depend on harvesting extreme returns there; Bitcoin — the most liquid, most institutionalized, least short-constrained coin — is precisely where the effect is weakest or absent, so the family barely applies to BTC specifically; Self-defeating over the CMA horizon: the mechanism predicts its own erosion. As short/margin/options/borrow infrastructure deepens (already largely true for BTC), the overvaluation premium decays toward zero, leaving no exploitable behavioral return for a long-horizon BTC holder; Short, bull-dominated samples (2014-2020/2021) and weekly horizons; out-of-sample persistence at 10-15yr horizons is untested, and frictions/transaction costs may make the cross-sectional alphas unharvestable in practice; Silent on the entire risk side of a CMA: it offers no native volatility magnitude, no correlations to equities/FI/TIPS/gold — those must be imported from realized data; Direction-asymmetric for BTC: if anything, removing short constraints and lottery demand argues BTC was historically OVERvalued and forward returns should be lower, not a basis for any positive premium

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Two intertwined behavioral channels, both deriving expected returns from preferences/beliefs rather than fundamentals. (A) Lottery/MAX + cumulative prospect theory (CPT). Investors over-weight small-probability large gains (Tversky-Kahneman probability weighting) and are loss-averse, so they overpay for positive-skew payoffs. Empirically: a one-SD rise in a coin's PT value reduces its next-week return ~0.71% ('Explaining cryptocurrency returns: A prospect theory perspective', JIFMIM 2022; 1,573 coins, 2014-2020); high-minus-low MAX-decile weekly spreads are ~3.03% raw / ~1.99% risk-adjusted ('Lottery-like preferences and the MAX effect', Financial Innovation 2021) and >1.50%/week ('Speculation and lottery-like demand', JIFMIM 2021). All are NEGATIVE cross-sectional predictors: lottery-attractive coins are overpriced and subsequently underperform. (B) Divergence of opinion + short-sale constraints. Miller (1977, JF): when opinions diverge and pessimists cannot short, the marginal holder is the optimist, so price overshoots the mean valuation; overvaluation rises with disagreement and with how binding the short constraint is. Scheinkman-Xiong (2003, JPE): add overconfidence-driven disagreement and a RESALE OPTION — a buyer pays above his own fundamental valuation because he expects to resell to a more optimistic future buyer; this generates a bubble component plus high volume and high volatility in equilibrium. Garfinkel, Hsiao & Hu (2025, Financial Management 54(3):633-672) bring Miller to crypto: using abnormal volume as a disagreement proxy, high-disagreement coins under binding short constraints earn LOWER future returns, with higher order imbalance and asymmetric drops in buying vs selling — and, decisively, 'the effect of high disagreement disappears after a coin's margin trading is activated.'

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / DECAY MECHANISM. The CMA-relevant object is not a price level but a premium that DECAYS along two axes: (1) holder-base institutionalization (lottery-seeking retail replaced by diversified rational marginal holders shrinks lottery demand and the PT/MAX premium); (2) short/margin/options/borrow infrastructure deepening (lets pessimists express views, collapsing the Miller overvaluation and the Scheinkman-Xiong resale bubble). This is a contrarian, infrastructure-conditional decay absent from factor-regression (#10) and LPPLS. The honest signed implication for BTC is DOWNWARD: removing constraints and lottery demand lowers forward expected return.

HISTORICAL FIT / BTC-SPECIFIC CAVEAT (load-bearing). The alphas are concentrated in small, illiquid, low-price, costly-to-arbitrage coins and 'critically depend on harvesting extreme returns on small, illiquid, volatile coins' (Babiak & Bianchi, 'Extrapolation Bias and the Lottery Effect', SSRN 2024; consistent across the MAX papers, which find the low-price/small-cap concentration and limits-to-arbitrage amplification). Bitcoin is the OPPOSITE pole: largest, most liquid, most institutionalized, and now deeply two-sided shortable — CME futures (2017), IBIT options (trading since 19-Nov-2024, position limits expanded 2025), inverse/short ETFs (BITI), and an active basis-trade short base. Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu's own result — the disagreement premium vanishes once margin trading exists — implies BTC's behavioral overvaluation premium is largely already spent. So the family barely applies to BTC as a level model; its value is to explain WHY BTC's realized appreciation decayed (142->65->17%/yr) as constraints relaxed and the holder base matured, and to argue against any continued behavioral excess return.

FAILURE MODES. (1) Category error: a weekly cross-sectional ranking signal is not a 10-15yr level forecast; any CMA number is grafted on. (2) Sample fragility: short, bull-dominated 2014-2021 windows, weekly horizons, untested at decade scale; transaction costs may make the alphas unharvestable. (3) Misapplication to BTC: using an effect that lives in micro-caps to value the most liquid coin overstates relevance. (4) Risk-side silence: no native vol magnitude or cross-asset correlations. (5) Self-defeating: the mechanism predicts its own erosion, so it cannot underwrite a persistent BTC premium.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This family publishes NO multi-year BTC price or return forecast. Its on-record outputs are signed cross-sectional premia (the ~0.71%/SD PT effect; ~1.5-3%/week MAX spreads) and the qualitative Scheinkman-Xiong prediction of high volatility plus large volume during disagreement-driven bubbles. The only forward-looking CMA inference is structural and contrarian: the behavioral overvaluation premium decays toward zero as shorting/margin/options infrastructure deepens and the holder base institutionalizes — for Bitcoin, largely already realized — so a credible 10-15yr BTC CMA built with this lens sits at or below a de-premiumed maturing-risk-asset return (~8-12% nominal), with ~55-60% vol, ~0.45-0.55 growth-equity correlation, and a near-zero gold correlation that this preference-based framework, unlike the digital-gold narratives, makes no attempt to inflate.
