### #65 · Liquidity-Risk & Higher-Moment Priced Factors (Amihud Illiquidity, Co-Skewness / Downside-Tail Beta)

*Family: priced-higher-moment-factors · Source: Academia · Tier: Reject as engine · Overall 33*


**Explanation:** This family explains the cross-section of crypto returns with priced risks beyond market/size/momentum: an Amihud-illiquidity premium (illiquid coins earn more), a downside-tail-beta premium (Ang-Chen-Xing lineage), and a skewness premium (Harvey-Siddique lineage). Crypto's striking result is that skewness predictability is IDIOSYNCRATIC, not systematic coskewness as in equities, and that most anomalies live in the smallest 30-70% of coins. Key inputs: each coin's Amihud measure, downside beta, and (co)skewness, run through Fama-MacBeth/portfolio sorts. The framework yields no native CMA level; you measure Bitcoin's own loadings, assume forward factor premia, and translate. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the load-bearing mechanism is microstructure DECAY: as ETFs, custody and deep derivatives compress Bitcoin's Amihud illiquidity toward zero, any illiquidity premium it once earned shrinks. Bitcoin is the largest, most liquid, left-skewed coin — sitting at the low-premium end of every sort — so this lens implies BTC's risk-premium FROM these specific factors is small and falling, reinforcing the appreciation-decay path rather than a high level.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 2. Strong 25-yr equity pedigree (Amihud, Harvey-Siddique, Ang-Chen-Xing) gives high theoretical rigor, but the priced premia concentrate in tiny illiquid coins and vanish value-weighted, so BTC — the largest, most liquid coin — earns almost no excess return, gutting signal. Robustness is weak: the illiquidity premium is self-defeating as BTC's Amihud collapses with ETFs/custody, and the framework is silent on regime/halving/correlation shifts. It yields no native CMA level, requires per-coin microstructure/return panels, and any 10-15yr number is analyst-imposed, hurting data_ops.*


**Key drivers:** Amihud illiquidity measure (|return| / dollar volume) and its level/trend for each coin — Bitcoin's collapses toward zero as float deepens (ETFs, custody, derivatives), the core decay mechanism; Systematic liquidity beta (covariance of coin returns with market-wide liquidity shocks) — distinct from the liquidity LEVEL premium; the Pastor-Stambaugh-style risk channel; Downside beta / downside-tail beta (return covariance with the market conditional on down markets) — Ang-Chen-Xing lineage; in crypto the premium is positive but driven by limits-to-arbitrage, not pure risk aversion; Co-skewness (systematic skewness with the crypto market) vs idiosyncratic skewness — crypto predictability is IDIOSYNCRATIC (Chen-Liu), opposite to equities where systematic coskewness is priced (Harvey-Siddique +3.6%/yr); Market capitalization / float depth — anomalies concentrate in the smallest 30-70% of coins and largely vanish value-weighted; Bitcoin sits at the large-cap, low-premium extreme; Limits-to-arbitrage / mispricing intensity — premia widen when coins are hard to trade and shrink as arbitrage capital and liquidity arrive (post-ETF institutionalization); Sign of Bitcoin's own skew: large-cap coins are MORE left-skewed (negative skew) — under a negative-skewness-premium regime this argues for LOWER, not higher, BTC expected return


**Pros:** Grounds expected return in genuinely priced, theory-backed risks (illiquidity, downside tail, skewness) with a 25-year equity pedigree (Amihud 2002; Harvey-Siddique 2000; Ang-Chen-Xing 2006), not price-extrapolation or scarcity numerology; Supplies a real, mechanistic reason for appreciation DECAY specific to Bitcoin: as float deepens and Amihud illiquidity collapses, the illiquidity premium BTC can earn mechanically shrinks — a microstructure story the scarcity/network models lack; Cross-sectionally robust evidence: positive illiquidity premium (~25bps/week, Fitz 2021; Zhang-Li 2023 negative liquidity-return relation), positive downside-risk premium and a skewness premium all documented across hundreds of coins with Fama-MacBeth and portfolio sorts; Honest about crypto's distinctiveness — identifies that idiosyncratic (not systematic) skewness drives crypto, separating it cleanly from the equity coskewness story and from the behavioral lottery-MAX demand family; Directly portfolio-relevant: speaks to liquidity and tail covariances that matter for sizing BTC against equities/FI/gold, even if the level forecast is weak


**Cons:** The anomalies concentrate in tiny, illiquid coins and largely VANISH value-weighted or after excluding the smallest 30-70% (Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints, 2024) — Bitcoin, the largest and most liquid coin, sits exactly where these premia are smallest or absent, so the framework gives BTC almost NO extra expected return; Not a level/CMA model: it estimates per-unit cross-sectional factor premia, not a long-horizon price path. Any 10-15yr appreciation number is an analyst-imposed factor-premium assumption, not a model output; Self-defeating decay: the illiquidity premium relies on illiquidity, but Bitcoin's Amihud measure is collapsing toward zero with ETFs/custody/derivatives — the very maturation that makes BTC investable destroys the premium this lens would credit it with; Sign confusion / regime instability: crypto's downside-risk premium is POSITIVE (opposite to the usual safe-haven intuition) and explained by limits-to-arbitrage; the skewness premium is NEGATIVE and idiosyncratic-driven — both are fragile, sample-dependent, and may not be true risk premia but mispricing that arbitrages away; Short, overlapping samples (2014-2024) spanning few regimes, severe non-standard-errors / researcher-degrees-of-freedom problems (documented for crypto anomalies), and survivorship in the coin panel — premia may be data-mined; Silent on macro correlations and on Bitcoin's volatility level — it characterizes WHICH risks are priced cross-sectionally, not BTC's standalone vol or its co-movement with equities/FI/TIPS/gold, all of which must be imported

Net: a modest systematic risk premium plus residual liquidity/tail compensation, landing below the trailing-5y realized 17% and consistent with the cross-approach central (~8-12%). I anchor ~7-11%, toward the lower half because the specific premia this approach prices are exactly the ones Bitcoin is shedding. | ~4-8%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). Judgment; reflects a maturing mega-cap whose illiquidity-based excess return is decaying toward a small tail/liquidity-risk compensation. | ~50-60%/yr (JUDGMENT; framework silent on standalone vol). Anchored to realized trailing-5y ~57% with the floor held AT realized — the deep-float/ETF maturation that compresses the illiquidity premium also gently lowers vol, but the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence a floor below ~57%. Stays multiples of equities/gold. | ~+0.45 to +0.60 (JUDGMENT). The framework is cross-sectional and silent on macro betas, so anchored to realized trailing-5y +0.56, which rises with institutionalization. Notably, as BTC's idiosyncratic/illiquidity premia decay it behaves MORE like a systematic high-beta risk asset, reinforcing a strong equity tie. | ~+0.30 to +0.40 (JUDGMENT). Below growth-equity; tracks realized trailing-5y +0.37. | ~+0.10 to +0.25 (JUDGMENT). Low-positive via shared liquidity/discount-rate sensitivity; realized trailing-5y +0.19, drifting up as the marginal holder institutionalizes. | ~+0.20 to +0.35 (JUDGMENT). Slightly above nominal FI through a shared real-rate/liquidity channel; realized trailing-5y +0.30. | ~0.0 to +0.10 (JUDGMENT). This within-crypto factor framework supplies NO gold mechanism, and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). I hold the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band and explicitly reject any digital-gold reading — nothing in liquidity/skew pricing forces gold co-movement. |

**Sources:** Wei Zhang and Yi Li (International Journal of Finance & Economics) (2023) https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/ijfe.2431; Wei Zhang, Yi Li, Xiong Xiong, Pengfei Wang (Journal of Banking & Finance, vol. 133) (2021) https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378426621002053; Yan Chen and Yakun Liu (International Review of Financial Analysis / SSRN 4869652) (2024) https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4869652; Yakov Amihud (Journal of Financial Markets, vol. 5, pp. 31-56) (2002) https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1386418101000246; Campbell R. Harvey and Akhtar Siddique (Journal of Finance, vol. 55, pp. 1263-1295) (2000) https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/0022-1082.00247; Andrew Ang, Joseph Chen, Yuhang Xing (Review of Financial Studies, vol. 19, pp. 1191-1239) (2006) https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/19/4/1191/1580531


<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This family extends the canonical Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu three-factor (market/size/momentum) cross-section by adding SPECIFIC priced risks: (1) liquidity — Zhang & Li (2023, Int. J. Finance & Economics) use the Amihud (2002) measure (|return|/dollar volume) and find a negative liquidity-return relation (illiquid coins earn higher subsequent returns) via univariate/bivariate sorts and Fama-MacBeth, robust to alternative liquidity proxies; (2) downside risk — Zhang, Li, Xiong & Wang (2021, J. Banking & Finance 133) find a POSITIVE cross-sectional relation between downside beta (Ang-Chen-Xing lineage) and future returns; (3) skewness — Chen & Liu (2024, Int. Review of Financial Analysis) find a NEGATIVE skewness premium driven by IDIOSYNCRATIC skewness, explicitly contrasting with equities where SYSTEMATIC coskewness is priced (Harvey-Siddique 2000, coskewness premium ~3.6%/yr; Ang-Chen-Xing 2006, downside-beta premium ~6%/yr). The estimation object is per-unit factor premia on a coin panel; there is NO native asset-level CMA.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & MAGNITUDES. Fitz (2021, USU) reexamines 372 coins (Sep-2014 to May-2021) and finds a significant illiquidity premium of ~25bps/week, robust to weighting and model specification; the broader literature reports ~0.61%/month raw and ~0.44%/month four-factor-alpha high-minus-low illiquidity spreads. Crypto distinctives: large-cap coins are MORE left-skewed, small-cap more right-skewed; the negative skewness-return relation holds regardless of volatility (unlike equities, where volatility moderates it); limits-to-arbitrage explains why asymmetric-risk premia exceed left-tail premia at high arbitrage cost.

THE LOAD-BEARING CRITIQUE (why BTC gets little from this lens). 'Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints' (2024) and related work show size/volume/distress/illiquidity anomalies are 'concentrated in hard-to-trade assets' and 'critically depend on harvesting extreme returns on small, illiquid, and volatile coins' — coming SOLELY from the 30-70% smallest coins. For 13 of 14 anomalies the low-liquidity group earns the higher long-short return; mispricing intensifies 'when cryptocurrencies lose their asset liquidity.' Momentum is the exception (stronger in large/liquid coins). Bitcoin is the largest, most liquid, most left-skewed coin — the exact corner where illiquidity and idiosyncratic-skew premia are smallest or absent. This is the microstructure-DECAY mechanism made concrete: an Amihud-illiquidity premium requires illiquidity, but BTC's Amihud measure is collapsing toward zero with ETF/custody/derivatives float-deepening, so the premium BTC can earn shrinks toward nil over a 10-15yr horizon. Under a negative-skewness-premium regime, BTC's left skew argues for LOWER expected return, not higher.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. Fit is genuinely cross-sectional and replicated across hundreds of coins, but: (a) it does not produce a level — any BTC appreciation figure is an imposed factor-premium view; (b) the signs are unstable and partly explained by limits-to-arbitrage/mispricing rather than true risk compensation, so they should arbitrage away as the market matures (which is the decay thesis); (c) samples are short (2014-2024), overlapping, survivorship-prone, and crypto anomalies suffer documented 'non-standard errors' (large researcher-degrees-of-freedom dispersion across reasonable methodological choices); (d) the contradictory illiquidity findings — some studies find NO illiquidity premium and that return predictability diminishes in high-liquidity coins — directly imply BTC's premium is near-zero. There is no separate volatility or cross-asset-correlation output; those must be imported from realized data (trailing-5y vol ~57%; equity corr ~0.56; gold corr ~0).

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. Unlike S2F, Metcalfe, power-law, or gold-parity families, this academic literature publishes NO dated BTC price targets or multi-year appreciation forecasts produced via this method. It is descriptive cross-sectional asset pricing; the authors do not extrapolate a Bitcoin level. That absence is itself informative: practitioners have not weaponized liquidity/higher-moment pricing into hype targets, because the honest reading gives Bitcoin a SMALL and SHRINKING factor premium. The CMA contribution is therefore directional, not numeric — it supports the appreciation-DECAY thesis (forward nominal well below realized 17%, toward ~7-11%) and warns that the maturation making BTC institutionally investable simultaneously erodes the very illiquidity/idiosyncratic-skew compensation this lens would credit. Skeptical bottom line: this approach is best used to DISCIPLINE other models downward, not to manufacture a bullish BTC number.

</details>

### #66 · ETF-AUM Cointegration Elasticity & Inelastic-Markets Flow Multiplier

*Family: etf-flow-elasticity · Source: Academia · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 33*


**Explanation:** Bitcoin has no cashflow, so this approach prices it off the demand curve. Guliyev & Ahmadova (2025) estimate a long-run cointegrating elasticity of BTC price to spot-ETF net assets of ~1.32 (FMOLS; DOLS/CCR 1.28-1.35): a 1% rise in ETF AUM maps to ~1.32% higher price. Gabaix-Koijen (2021) supply the magnitude intuition: aggregate demand is inelastic (~-0.2), so $1 of permanent net inflow lifts market value ~$5 (range 3-8). To get a 10-15yr CMA you forecast cumulative ETF-AUM accumulation and multiply by a DECAYING elasticity. The honest reading forces hard decay: the 1.32 elasticity was fit on a 16-month, one-directional bull run where AUM and price rose together; cointegration is only 10%-significant and collapses if GBTC-conversion outflows are excluded; causality is partly reflexive (price rallies pull in flows). As the ETF stock saturates against a finite allocatable-capital pool, AUM growth decelerates and the elasticity compresses toward 1 and below. Net: a flow-amplified but steadily decaying appreciation path, not the historical level.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 4, orthogonality 2. Strong top-journal anchor (Gabaix-Koijen inelastic markets, ~5x) and correct I(1) estimators, but the operative 1.32 elasticity is fit on a 16-month single-regime bull, rejects no-cointegration only at 10%, and is contaminated by mechanical price->dollar-AUM reflexivity — so out-of-sample signal and regime robustness are low. ETF AUM is observable and refreshable (good data_ops), yet the level forecast is admitted judgment and the framework is silent on vol/tails/gold, adding little of the conditioning that gives a method its real CMA value beyond the shared decay anchor.*


**Key drivers:** Aggregate spot-ETF net assets (AUM) — the cointegrating regressor; its forecast accumulation path over 10-15yr is the primary input; Long-run price-to-AUM elasticity (~1.32 historical FMOLS) — must be decayed toward ~1.0 and below as the demand curve deepens and the reflexive bull-window fit unwinds; Gabaix-Koijen aggregate-market price-elasticity of demand (~-0.2) / inverse price-impact multiplier (~5x, range 3-8) — converts net dollar flow into permanent market-value shift; Market depth / float available for trading — multiplier shrinks as liquid float and arbitrage capacity grow (impact is depth-dependent: same flow moves price more on thin days); Reflexivity / feedback loop — price gains attract momentum inflows that further lift price (bidirectional causality the authors concede), inflating in-sample elasticity; Saturation of the allocatable-capital pool — finite institutional/retail wallet share for a 1-2% BTC allocation caps cumulative AUM, forcing flow (and thus appreciation) to decay; GBTC-conversion / structural-flow noise — early sample dominated by Grayscale outflows; relationship is unstable to their exclusion


**Pros:** Demand-side and cashflow-free by construction — appropriate for an asset with no dividends/earnings; prices BTC off an observable, refreshable institutional-flow variable rather than supply numerology (S2F) or pure time extrapolation; Anchored to a genuine, well-cited structural mechanism: Gabaix-Koijen inelastic-markets is a top-journal result with a transparent multiplier (~5x), and the cointegration estimators (FMOLS/DOLS/CCR) are the correct tools for I(1) series and converge tightly (1.28-1.35), giving robustness across endogeneity corrections; Naturally produces appreciation DECAY when honestly implemented: cumulative AUM must saturate against a finite allocatable-capital pool, so flow growth (and the elasticity itself) compress over a decade — the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA; Decomposable and falsifiable: you can stress the AUM path, the elasticity, and the multiplier separately, and mark realized BTC against the AUM-implied fair value; Ties BTC's price formation to the same flow-driven, inelastic-demand microstructure now documented for equities, making it portfolio-coherent and intuitively communicable to institutional allocators


**Cons:** The cointegration is statistically marginal and fragile: Guliyev-Ahmadova reject no-cointegration only at the 10% level (not 5%), on a 16-month, single-regime BULL sample where AUM and price mechanically rose together — exactly the spurious-trend trap the authors' own reviewers flagged ('very obvious on a small data set of bullish trend'). The 0.9248 level correlation is the classic two-trends artifact; Reverse/reflexive causality is unresolved and partly mechanical: a BTC price rise AUTOMATICALLY inflates the dollar AUM of ETF-held coins, so price->AUM contaminates the very regression used to claim AUM->price. The authors concede bidirectional feedback; the GBTC-outflow sensitivity (relationship goes insignificant when excluded) shows the estimate is not structurally stable; The 1.32 elasticity and the ~5x multiplier are NOT forward CMAs — neither paper publishes a multi-year return forecast. Building a 10-15yr appreciation requires forecasting cumulative ETF-AUM accumulation, which is itself the hardest unknown; the framework smuggles the entire answer into an assumed AUM path; Gabaix-Koijen's multiplier was estimated for the US EQUITY market; transplanting ~5x (or 3-8) to a younger, more liquid-relative-to-flow, globally-fungible BTC market is unvalidated — BTC's deep 24/7 spot/derivatives liquidity and elastic miner/long-term-holder supply likely make its demand curve FLATTER (smaller multiplier) than equities, biasing the CMA high; Flow is not permanent: ETF AUM can and does reverse (2026 saw far more volatile, two-sided flows); a multiplier calibrated on net accumulation overstates durable value if a large share of flow is hot/momentum capital that exits in drawdowns; Silent on volatility and on cross-asset correlations — both must be imported from realized data; the framework populates only the appreciation cell natively

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This is a demand-side structural CMA assembled from two published primitives that, individually, are NOT forecasts. (1) Guliyev & Ahmadova (2025, Ledger 10:154-172) estimate a long-run cointegrating elasticity of log-BTC price on log spot-ETF net assets. Using daily data 11-Jan-2024 to 16-May-2025, both series test as I(1) (ADF/PP), and FMOLS/DOLS/CCR — the appropriate efficient estimators for cointegrating vectors — yield a tightly clustered elasticity: FMOLS ~1.32, DOLS/CCR 1.28-1.35, all significant at 5% or better. Engle-Granger and Phillips-Ouliaris residual tests reject no-cointegration, but only at the 10% level. The raw level correlation of log-BTC and log-AUM is 0.9248. (2) Gabaix & Koijen (2021, NBER 28967) supply the magnitude logic: the aggregate market's price-elasticity of demand is small (~-0.2), so via a granular-IV identification, $1 of net flow into the market raises aggregate value by ~$5 (robustness range 3-8). The CMA combines them: forecast cumulative ETF-AUM accumulation over the horizon, convert AUM growth to price growth with a (decaying) elasticity, and optionally sanity-check the dollar magnitude with the inelastic-markets multiplier on net flow.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / QUOTES. The authors interpret 1.32 as 'a 1% increase in the total net assets of spot Bitcoin ETFs is associated with roughly a 1.32% increase in the market price of Bitcoin in the long run' and describe 'how initial ETF inflows could raise Bitcoin's price, which might then attract further inflows (a positive feedback loop).' They treat AUM as the long-run exogenous driver but 'acknowledge that such feedback effects mean the causality can be bidirectional.' Gabaix-Koijen: 'investing $1 in the stock market increases the market's aggregate value by about $5,' driven because 'households allocate capital to institutions, which are fairly constrained... with a mandate to maintain a fixed equity share.'

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The fit is in-sample over a 16-month, essentially one-directional bull run — precisely when a spurious two-trends correlation is most likely. The peer reviewers said so directly: '[the conclusion] seems very obvious to me on a small data set of bullish trend,' and the marginal 10%-only cointegration significance underlines fragility. Three structural failure modes: (a) Reflexive/mechanical reverse causality — a BTC price rise automatically inflates the dollar AUM of ETF-held coins, so price->AUM contaminates the regression; the authors concede this. (b) GBTC-conversion instability — the early sample is dominated by Grayscale outflows, and the authors report that EXCLUDING that period makes 'the estimated cointegration relationship... unstable and statistically insignificant,' i.e., the headline result leans on a one-off structural event. (c) Transplant risk on the multiplier — Gabaix-Koijen's ~5x is a US-equity number; BTC's deep 24/7 spot+derivatives liquidity and elastic long-term-holder/miner supply plausibly make its demand curve FLATTER, so a naive 5x overstates the permanent value impact of flow. Flow is also not durable: 2026 brought far more two-sided ETF flows, so a multiplier calibrated on net accumulation overstates value when a large share of inflow is hot money that exits in drawdowns.

WHY THE CMA MUST DECAY. The framework only yields a high forward return if cumulative ETF AUM keeps compounding fast AND the >1 elasticity persists. Neither survives scrutiny. AUM accumulation must decelerate as the ETF stock saturates against a finite allocatable-capital pool (a 1-2% BTC sleeve across institutions/retail is bounded). The 1.32 elasticity is a reflexive bull-window artifact and should be decayed toward 1.0 and below as the market deepens and arbitrage/derivatives elasticity grows. Honest construction therefore decays BOTH the AUM growth rate and the elasticity, producing a low-double-digit nominal appreciation (~9-13%) consistent with the realized decay path (142->65->17%/yr) and the cross-approach central (~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15). Volatility and all correlations are imported from realized data — the inelastic-markets mechanism if anything argues vol stays HIGH (steep demand curve = flow shocks move price hard), undercutting practitioner 'ETFs damped vol' claims.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. None. Critically, neither primary source publishes a multi-year BTC price target or CMA. Guliyev-Ahmadova explicitly disclaim forecasting: 'my goal is to document these structural demand-price relationships, rather than to propose a short-term trading signal or investment rule.' Gabaix-Koijen forecast nothing about BTC at all. So any 10-15yr number attached to this approach (including the synthesized ~9-13% above) is a constructed extrapolation, not an on-record forecast from the literature — which is the honest and load-bearing caveat for using it as a CMA building block.

</details>

### #67 · Equation-of-Exchange Velocity Network-Utility Valuation (Burniske MV=PQ)

*Family: monetary-utility-velocity · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Reject as engine · Overall 32*


**Explanation:** Burniske inverts the monetary identity MV=PQ to size the monetary base a cryptoeconomy needs: M = PQ/V. PQ is the network's "GDP" — the real on-chain transaction volume it settles (speculative exchange shuttling, ~30%+ of raw volume, is excluded). V is velocity, the float's annual turnover. Divide M by the circulating, non-hodled supply to get a Current Utility Value per coin; markets price the future, so you discount a chosen future-year utility value back at a steep 30-50% crypto discount rate. A 10-15yr BTC CMA emerges as expected return ≈ growth in real on-chain throughput (PQ) minus the drift in velocity, plus the decaying re-rating as a higher-adoption scenario becomes more probable. Two forces matter: PQ compounds as adoption rises but decelerates on an S-curve, and BTC velocity is at decade lows (>70% of supply dormant, ETF cold storage), which mechanically lifts M. The catch: velocity is empirically unstable and unforecastable, and the discount rate dominates the answer — so the framework is more disciplined story than reliable forecast.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 2. Theoretically the most "absolute"/bottom-up of the crypto models — it solves for a fair monetary base from modeled throughput and forces an explicit, one-lever-at-a-time adoption story, and uniquely makes falling velocity a first-class price mechanism (rigor=3). But its load-bearing inputs (V and the 30-50% discount rate) are empirically unforecastable: the arXiv test shows velocity fluctuates wildly with poor out-of-sample fit, and the answer is dominated by analyst discount-rate choice plus an unresolved infinite-recursion-of-expectations problem, gutting predictive power (signal=2). It offers no regime-change conditioning (silent on correlations, equity-corr rise, ETF-era shifts) and pivots on a parameter that breaks across regimes (robustness=2). Operationally it demands on-chain PQ scrubbing, velocity estimation, hodl-adjusted float, and subjective discount/scenario calibration — heavy and judgment-laden for a CMA process (data_ops=2).*


**Key drivers:** Real on-chain economic throughput PQ (the cryptonetwork 'GDP') — modeled bottom-up from resource price P (e.g. declining unit cost) and quantity Q via TAM x adoption S-curve x penetration, NOT raw on-chain volume (30%+ is exchange shuttling/speculation and is stripped out); Velocity V — the single most sensitive and central lever; turnover of the active float. Burniske derives BTC hybrid V~6.5 (2016) from ~54% hodlers + ~46% transactional, and a transactional V~14; forward V is the dominant unknown. Crucially, FALLING velocity (BTC at decade lows, >70% dormant) is a price TAILWIND under M=PQ/V; Hodl / dormant-coin fraction — coins held off-market (velocity 0) are removed from the float denominator, raising CUV per token; the SoV-vs-MoE tension lives inside the identity; Discount rate (30-50%, ~3-5x risky equities) applied to a single future utility value — economically the expected return; tiny changes swing the present price ~2x (30% vs 40%); Adoption-scenario probability / target transaction-share state the market believes BTC will occupy — price re-rates as belief climbs toward a ceiling (a decaying, one-time re-rating, not a perpetual growth rate); Circulating supply M_supply (near-deterministic 21M issuance schedule) — converts the required monetary base into a per-coin price


**Pros:** Genuinely 'absolute' / bottom-up: unlike NVT (a ratio) or S2F (supply-only), it solves for a fair monetary base from the network's OWN modeled economic throughput, and forces an explicit, auditable adoption story (P, Q, V, discount rate) you can stress one lever at a time; Makes velocity an explicit, first-class lever and captures a mechanism the other models miss: BTC's decade-low, still-falling velocity (HODL + ETF cold storage, >70% dormant) is a structural PRICE TAILWIND under M=PQ/V (lower V raises the required base) — a real, observable dynamic; Naturally produces appreciation DECAY: PQ growth decelerates on an adoption S-curve and the scenario re-rating is a one-time climb toward a ceiling, so the framework does not assume constant high returns forever — the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA; Grounded in standard monetary economics (equation of exchange) and refutable: Zochowski/Winton extended it (nth-order investors, Fair Token Value) and the arXiv 2024 paper tested it empirically, so it has a real critique-and-improvement literature rather than pure narrative


**Cons:** Velocity is empirically UNSTABLE and unforecastable — the load-bearing input. The arXiv (2024) empirical test finds V 'fluctuates dramatically' across coins and time, historical fits are poor, and forward predictions diverge substantially from realized prices ('better at post-hoc explanation than genuine forecasting'). The whole CMA pivots on a parameter the data says you cannot pin down; Severe circularity and discount-rate dominance: the answer is essentially the analyst's chosen 30-50% discount rate (a 30% vs 40% rate ~doubles the price), and 'future market prices themselves depend on further future expectations' (Burniske concedes the infinite-recursion-of-expectations problem is unresolved); PQ (the 'GDP') is badly contaminated and structurally leaking: raw on-chain volume overstates economic throughput ~3x (change outputs, self-spends, exchange shuttling), while real BTC activity increasingly migrates to Lightning/L2, exchange-internal ledgers and ETF custody that never touch the base chain — so the numerator is breaking exactly as institutionalization deepens; Conflates store-of-value and medium-of-exchange in one identity: the same falling velocity that boosts M as a 'tailwind' also signals BTC is NOT being used as a transactional network (the velocity 'problem' Zochowski debates) — so PQ-as-payments-GDP shrinks while the SoV reading dominates, and the framework cannot cleanly tell you which regime it is valuing; Burniske himself refuses to publish a BTC price target with it and disavowed his earlier (2015 ARK) ~$2,000/BTC equation-of-exchange estimate as methodologically flawed — the originator does not treat it as a reliable point-forecast engine; Silent on volatility and cross-asset correlations — it is a level/utility-value model, so every risk-and-correlation CMA cell must be imported from realized data or another framework


**Outputs (cited vs synthesized):**


| | Appr nom | Appr real | Vol | ρ GrEq | ρ VaEq | ρ FI | ρ TIPS | ρ Gold |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cited | n/a (source silent as an annualized rate). Burniske explicitly REFUSES to publish a BTC price target with the framework and disavowed his earlier 2015 ARK equation-of-exchange estimate (~$2,000/BTC) as methodologically flawed. The model outputs a discounted utility value per token; the only worked example is illustrative (INET token: 2028 future utility value $7.45 discounted at 40% over 10yr = $0.26 today; 53% current-utility / 47% speculative split). <details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Burniske's 2017 'Cryptoasset Valuations' (Medium) and Burniske & Tatar's 'Cryptoassets' (McGraw-Hill, 2017) reframe the Fisher equation of exchange MV=PQ as an absolute-valuation engine for assets with no cashflow. The pivot: 'A cryptoasset valuation is largely comprised of solving for M, where M = PQ/V. M is the size of the monetary base necessary to support a cryptoeconomy of size PQ, at velocity V.' PQ is the network's GDP — 'the on-chain transaction volume of its cryptoasset' — but Burniske strips speculation: 'Often 30%+ of a cryptoasset's on-chain transaction volume can be shuttling the asset between exchanges,' which is excluded from GDP. The float denominator also excludes hodled/bonded coins ('velocity of 0'). Procedure: (1) model P (resource unit price, often declining — INET assumed -16%/yr) and Q (TAM x adoption S-curve x penetration) to get future PQ; (2) choose V; (3) M = PQ/V; (4) CUV per token = M / non-hodled float; (5) discount a SINGLE future-year utility value to present at a steep crypto rate. His INET worked example: 2028 utility value $7.45 / (1.40)^10 = $0.26 rational 2018 price, of which 53% is current-utility and 47% speculative. Discount rate is 'expected rate of return,' 30-50%, '3-5x the discount rate used for risky equities' — and dominates: 30% gives $0.54 vs 40% gives $0.26 on the same asset.\n\nKEY RELATIONSHIPS. Forward return decomposes as PQ-growth + velocity-drift contribution + decaying scenario re-rating. The velocity term is what makes this distinct and currently topical: with V in the denominator, FALLING velocity is a price tailwind. CoinDesk (2025) reports BTC on-chain velocity at 'decade lows,' '>70% of BTC hasn't moved in over a year,' institutions ~12.8% of supply in cold storage — all of which mechanically raise the required monetary base M for any given PQ. Burniske's own BTC velocity anchors: hybrid V~6.5 in 2016 (from 54% hodlers + 46% transactional), transactional V~14.\n\nDISTINCTNESS. This is the bottom-up, dynamic sibling of digest #8 (QTM/MV=PT static identity). #8 plugs a single aggregate transaction-volume scenario (illicit / Visa-scale / all-electronic / world-GDP) and a single V to back out a price LEVEL. Burniske instead BUILDS PQ from the protocol's own resource economics and adoption S-curve and treats V as a decade-dynamic central lever, then discounts. It is not NVT (#3), which is a mean-reversion ratio that never solves for a fair M, and not Cagan structural money-demand.\n\nCRITIQUES (faithfully represented). Zochowski (Logos Network, 2018-19) — sympathetic but sharp — flags three flaws: the single-horizon assumption ('what if investors have different horizons?'), incomplete nth-order extensions ('why stop at 6 orders?'), and velocity opacity ('Velocity is still a somewhat opaque concept... without many satisfying answers'). His fixes: Contemporaneous/Present Utility Value and a 'Fair Token Value' = max PUV over all start-dates/horizons; a terminal rule (stop modeling once CUV-growth/liquid-supply-growth < 1+r). His #2 essay argues the 'velocity problem' (frictionless DLT -> high V -> value erodes) is overstated for PAYMENTS networks because PQ includes payment VALUE not just processing cost, and balances are rationally held (Venmo float, Visa V~500 still yields $31bn revenue, stablecoins V 20-50, USD M1 V~5.6). The decisive critique is the arXiv (2024) empirical test: velocity 'fluctuates dramatically' across coins and time, is not the stable parameter Burniske assumes, historical fits are poor, forward predictions 'diverge substantially from realized prices,' and the model is 'better at post-hoc explanation than genuine forecasting' — plus circular reasoning (assume stable V to justify a valuation that depends on unproven V).\n\nON-RECORD FORECASTS. Notably, Burniske REFUSES to publish a BTC price target with this framework, and disavowed his earlier 2015 ARK equation-of-exchange estimate (~$2,000/BTC) as methodologically flawed. There is no credible on-record 10-15yr BTC appreciation number produced by this method — its outputs are illustrative token examples (INET) and the implied return is simply the analyst's chosen 30-50% discount rate, which is the central circularity. FAILURE MODES: (1) velocity unforecastable; (2) discount-rate dominance / infinite expectations recursion (Burniske's own caveat); (3) PQ contamination (raw overstates ~3x) and off-chain leakage (Lightning/L2/ETF) breaking the numerator as institutionalization deepens; (4) SoV/MoE conflation — the same falling velocity that 'helps' price also says BTC isn't transacting, so payments-PQ shrinks. Net: a disciplined narrative and a genuinely useful lens on the velocity-decline tailwind, but not a reliable point-forecast engine; the honest 10-15yr CMA extrapolates BTC's appreciation DECAY (~9% nominal center), not its history.

</details>

### #68 · Treasury-Company Reflexive Demand Channel (mNAV Flywheel + Convertible Vol-Arb Loop)

*Family: treasury-reflexivity · Source: Asset manager · Tier: Context / cross-check · Overall 31*


**Explanation:** This treats BTC's price as set by a reflexive demand FLOW, not a fundamental level. When a treasury company (Strategy/MSTR) trades above 1x mNAV, it sells equity/0%-converts/preferreds above BTC-NAV and buys BTC at par, lifting BTC-per-share accretively and pulling float out of circulation. The engine underneath is convertible vol-arb: desks buy the converts and delta-hedge the stock; MSTR's ~106 implied vol makes the embedded option valuable at a 0% coupon, and gamma-hedging into rallies adds a self-reinforcing bid. In 2026 Strategy bought ~3x what all miners produced, so BTC grew "dependent on the buying machine." The loop reverses violently below 1x: accretive issuance stops, the gamma bid flips to selling, and thin cash plus a 2029-30 maturity wall risks forced BTC sales. For a 10-15yr CMA this implies a decaying appreciation as the premium normalizes toward 1x and the marginal float-removal flow fades, plus a fat left-tail from concentrated forced de-grossing — net a high-single-digit central return with elevated, asymmetric volatility.


*Scores — rigor 2, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 3, orthogonality 3. Reflexive-by-construction with no fundamental/equilibrium anchor, so it cannot derive a 10-15yr level — it's a decaying flow impulse masquerading as a valuation channel (rigor/signal low). Robustness is weak: ~76% single-entity concentration with a 2029-30 convert/preferred wall means the "channel" is really a bet on one balance sheet surviving a regime flip, and the mechanism itself is brand-new with no cross-cycle history. Data is observable in real time (mNAV, BTC/share, implied vol, issuance), giving decent data_ops, and its one genuine contribution is honestly shaping the LEFT tail and endogenous vol clustering — but as a CMA level method it is poor.*


**Key drivers:** mNAV premium (enterprise value / BTC-NAV); accretive issuance is only possible above 1x — VanEck: peaked ~2.6-2.8x late-2024, compressed to ~1.2x by Mar-2026, ~1-in-3 DATs now below 1x; BTC-per-share growth ('BTC yield') — the accretion metric the flywheel optimizes; each above-NAV raise that buys BTC at par increases it; Convertible volatility arbitrage / gamma feedback: vol-arb desks buy 0%-coupon converts and delta-hedge MSTR; extreme implied vol (~106 vs ~15 S&P, ~60 BTC) makes the embedded option valuable at 0% coupon and creates a self-reinforcing bid into rallies; Net DAT demand flow vs new supply: Strategy bought ~171k BTC in the first ~4.5 months of 2026 vs ~62k mined (~3x miner issuance); JPMorgan projects ~$30B of 2026 buying; Capital-markets dependence with no revolver: funding is 100% equity/convert/preferred issuance; thin cash; ~$8.25B converts + ~$10.3B preferreds; maturity/redemption wall 2029-2030; Concentration in one entity: Strategy holds ~76% of all treasury-company BTC (~818k BTC, ~4% of total supply); the channel is effectively a single-name flow; Latent forced-selling overhang / regime flip: below-1x premium + debt service + MSCI-exclusion risk (JPM: up to $8.8B index-driven forced sales) can trigger BTC liquidation and a reflexive 'spiral of doom'


**Pros:** Identifies a REAL, observable marginal-demand mechanism that no other approach in the set treats as a valuation channel — in 2026 a single treasury company's buying (~3x miner issuance) was visibly the dominant net flow supporting price, so the channel has genuine, dated price-impact evidence rather than only an in-sample fit; Honest about asymmetry: unlike scarcity/network/power-law models that are structurally bullish, this framework builds in a bearish regime flip (premium collapse → halted issuance → gamma-bid inversion → forced BTC selling), which correctly shapes the LEFT tail of a CMA rather than ignoring it; Mechanistically transparent and falsifiable in real time: mNAV, BTC-per-share, convertible terms, implied vol, and DAT net flows are all observable and refreshable, so the thesis can be marked against live data (VanEck, NYDIG, JPMorgan all publish the inputs); Explains BTC's elevated, fat-tailed volatility better than a fundamental-level model: forced de-grossing and vol-arb unwinds are an explicit endogenous source of crash risk and vol clustering, matching the realized ~57% vol floor


**Cons:** Reflexive and circular by construction: the premium that funds the buying depends on BTC's price, which depends on the buying — there is no fundamental anchor, so the channel can sustain ANY price on the way up and provides no equilibrium level, only a flow. It is a flow/timing mechanism masquerading as a valuation channel; deriving a 10-15yr level from it requires bolted-on assumptions about how the premium and flow decay; Single-entity concentration makes it fragile and non-diversifiable as a 'channel': ~76% of treasury BTC sits in one company with thin cash, no revolver, and a 2029-30 convertible/preferred wall. A CMA built on this is really a bet on one balance sheet surviving — Coinbase flags it as systemic risk; NYDIG's Cipolaro calls mNAV 'woefully deficient' for ignoring convert-refinancing and opco risk; The bid is self-limiting and decaying: as the premium normalizes toward 1x (already from ~2.7x to ~1.2x), accretive issuance slows and the marginal float-removal flow fades, so the very mechanism that drove past returns mechanically weakens — extrapolating its historical demand impulse overstates forward return; Vol-arb gamma support is symmetric and can violently invert: the same delta-hedging that bids the stock up sells it into weakness; below-1x, forced BTC selling and de-grossing can cascade ('spiral of doom', ~1-in-3 DATs already below NAV in 2026), so the channel injects crash risk it cannot itself arrest; Silent on cross-asset correlations and on a real appreciation rate — it produces a flow and a regime-flip risk, not native volatility or correlation numbers, all of which must be imported from realized data

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. This is a Soros-style reflexivity channel applied to BTC's MARGINAL DEMAND rather than its fundamental level. The unit of analysis is the leveraged digital-asset-treasury (DAT) company — overwhelmingly Strategy/MSTR. The load-bearing variable is mNAV (enterprise value ÷ BTC-NAV, where EV = common market cap + debt + preferred notional − cash; VanEck's definition). Above 1x, the firm issues equity, 0%-coupon convertibles, and preferreds at a premium and buys BTC at par, raising BTC-per-share ("BTC yield") accretively and permanently removing float. The CMA isn't a level but a flow: expected BTC return ≈ DAT net demand vs new issuance, scaled by how long the premium (and thus accretive issuance) persists, minus a latent forced-selling overhang on the downside.

THE PLUMBING (AMINA, VanEck). The deeper mechanism is convertible volatility arbitrage. Vol-arb desks buy MSTR's 0%-coupon converts and short/delta-hedge the equity; because MSTR's implied vol is extreme (~106 vs ~15 S&P, ~60 BTC), the embedded option is hugely valuable even at a 0% coupon — so MSTR raises ultra-cheap capital while the arb is profitable "regardless of direction." Gamma-hedging into rallies forces desks to BUY stock as it rises, a mechanical self-reinforcing bid that supports the premium and recycles into more BTC purchases. VanEck decomposes the premium into leverage + volatility + sentiment and notes MSTR "behaves like a call option on Bitcoin" via this recursive issue-and-buy loop. The premium has compressed from a ~2.6-2.8x late-2024 peak to ~1.2x by Mar-2026 (VanEck), i.e., a +112% premium to BTC+opco fair value — the tailwind is visibly fading.

HISTORICAL FIT / DEPENDENCY. The channel's strongest evidence is 2026 flow: Bloomberg ("Bitcoin Grows More Dependent on Michael Saylor's Buying Machine," 20-May-2026) reports Strategy bought ~171,238 BTC in the first ~4.5 months of 2026 vs ~62,000 mined network-wide — ~3x miner issuance — and that this single company "largely prevented a steeper fall" with BTC ~$77,500. Saylor's own framing: miners no longer set the price; "structured credit products now absorb every coin produced." Strategy holds ~818k BTC (~4% of total supply) and ~76% of ALL treasury-company BTC — so the "channel" is effectively a single-name flow.

FAILURE MODES (the honest core). (1) Circularity: the premium funds the buying, the buying lifts the price, the price lifts the premium — no fundamental anchor, so the channel can rationalize any price up and supplies no equilibrium level. (2) Self-limiting decay: as mNAV normalizes toward 1x, each raise removes less float; the very engine of past returns weakens. (3) Symmetric/inverting vol-arb: the gamma bid that levitates the stock sells into weakness; below 1x, accretive issuance halts and forced BTC selling can cascade. (4) Concentration + maturity wall: thin cash, no revolver, ~$8.25B converts + ~$10.3B preferreds, redemption wall 2029-2030 (Coinbase). NYDIG's Greg Cipolaro calls mNAV "woefully deficient" for ignoring convert-refinancing and opco risk. DL News ("spiral of doom," 2026): ~1-in-3 of 156 tracked DATs already below 1x mNAV, ~$112B BTC collectively; former-Goldman analyst Dom Kwok: if forced to sell shares at thin premiums, "Strategy could be forced to offload Bitcoin to cover its obligations." Coinbase explicitly flags the model as systemic risk; JPMorgan warned MSCI exclusion could trigger up to $8.8B of index-driven forced sales.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The channel publishes FLOW forecasts, not appreciation CMAs. JPMorgan (Panigirtzoglou): Strategy on pace for ~$30B of BTC buying in 2026, exceeding the ~$22B bought in each of 2024 and 2025. Saylor's stated ambition is 5-7% of total BTC supply (from ~4% today). VanEck stops short of a price forecast, instead arguing — per Sigel — that BTC "already has a lot of reflexivity, so there's no need to add leverage on top of it," i.e., even the bullish house is skeptical of the DAT model's durability. No source converts the flow into a 10-15yr annualized BTC return; that synthesis is mine.

WHY DISTINCT / CMA IMPLICATION. None of the 20 existing approaches treats a reflexive institutional demand-flow (or its convertible-financing plumbing) as the valuation channel — the closest, the LPPLS bubble-hazard and LTCMA approaches, model crash timing and portfolio assumptions, not the forced-buyer/seller flow itself. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA, this channel's real value is in SHAPING THE DISTRIBUTION, not pinning a central return: it justifies holding vol at/above the ~57% realized floor (endogenous de-grossing), a fat left tail (concentrated forced selling at the 2029-30 wall), and a tightened equity correlation (the marginal buyer is a leveraged equity vehicle, so BTC is MORE equity-like and NOT more gold-like via this mechanism). My synthesized central return (~6-10% nominal / ~3-7% real) sits at the low end of the cross-approach band precisely because a premium-dependent flow cannot compound at historical rates and carries a genuine reflexive-unwind probability mass.

### #69 · Lindy / Age-Conditioned Survival Adoption Premium

*Family: survival-adoption-premium · Source: Practitioner · Tier: Reject as engine · Overall 30*


**Explanation:** This treats accumulated survival as information, not magic. As Bitcoin ages without dying, a Bayesian observer holding uncertainty over its true (unknown) hazard rate down-weights the high-hazard worlds — Ord (2023) shows a uniform prior over constant hazards produces an effective survival curve with a Pareto tail (S(t)≈1/Kt) and a DECLINING observed hazard, even though nothing about the asset physically changed. Taleb's Antifragile frames the same thing as 'aging in reverse.' The CMA payoff is demand-side: a lower perceived ruin probability moves fiduciaries off zero allocation into 1-5% models, raising eligible capital, target weights, and price — an upward feedback, the inverse-sign of a fixed ruin haircut. Key inputs: BTC age (~17yr), the prior over hazard, and the survival-path return. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it implies the left-tail haircut SHRINKS over the horizon, but the honest version is sobering: the maximal-ignorance Gott prior assigns ~40% ruin over 12.5yr, far above the practitioner narrative — and the effect vanishes if hazard is bounded above zero.


*Scores — rigor 3, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 2. The Ord (2023) Bayesian-hazard machinery is genuinely rigorous and correctly yields a declining observed hazard plus a Gott base rate, so rigor earns a 3 — but it is fatally compromised by survivorship bias (Bitcoin is one survivor from a population >53% dead) and by illegitimately upgrading an evidential observer-side update into a causal physical-safety improvement that it then prices. Signal and robustness are weak: the honest math is bimodal and pessimistic (Gott ~42% ruin), it adds little conditioning beyond a static absorbing-zero point-mass that the fixed-haircut ruin row already captures, and it says nothing about the empirically load-bearing regime shifts (S2F break, rising +0.56 equity correlation, ETF-era flows). Data_ops is low because the payoff is judgment-driven demand-feedback with no clean operational input to a CMA pipeline.*


**Key drivers:** BTC network age t0 (~17yr from Jan-2009 genesis) — the sole input to the Gott/Lindy median-remaining-life = current-age estimate; The PRIOR over the unknown hazard rate k: uniform on [0,K] (Ord) or log-uniform ρ∝1/t (Gott) — the assumption that does all the work; Lindy holds only if k can be arbitrarily close to zero; Bayesian down-updating of perceived hazard as survival accumulates (S(t)≈1/Kt Pareto tail; effective λ(t)≈1/Kt² declining) — evidential, not causal; Eligible-capital / fiduciary-pool width: the demand feedback — lower perceived ruin moves pensions/endowments/insurers off zero toward 2-5% allocation models; Survival-path conditional return R_survival (borrowed from an adoption-S-curve / TAM / monetary model — Lindy is a wrapper, not a return model); Survivorship-bias discipline: >53% of listed coins dead (CoinGecko 2025); ElBahrawy net coin death rate ~1.04%/mo — the base rate that naive Lindy on the survivor ignores; Whether the true hazard is bounded away from zero (k>ε): if yes, the Pareto tail collapses to an exponential and the Lindy premium fades over time


**Pros:** Provides a rigorous Bayesian mechanism (Ord 2023) for WHY a survival premium can exist even with no physical change in the asset — the effective-hazard decline falls straight out of a uniform prior over an unknown constant hazard, so the 'BTC gets safer as it ages' intuition is not pure narrative; Correctly signed: it captures a real, observable demand feedback — accumulating survival genuinely has moved fiduciary allocation models off zero (2-5% institutional positions, ETF approval), which the fixed-haircut ruin row (#20) cannot represent because its hazard is static; Self-disciplining when done honestly: the same framework that delivers the premium also delivers the Gott base rate (~40% ruin over 12.5yr under maximal ignorance), forcing the user to confront that the survivor is one draw from a population that is >50% dead; Falsifiable structure: Lindy fails the moment the hazard is bounded above zero (k>ε) or rises faster than power-law — Ord gives explicit conditions, so the claim is testable rather than vibes; Naturally time-varying: unlike a fixed haircut, the survival weight S(T) updates as evidence accrues, so the framework cleanly absorbs new survival data and institutional adoption over the holding period


**Cons:** Survivorship bias is the fatal trap and the approach often commits it: applying Lindy to Bitcoin THE SURVIVOR ignores that it is one realization from a population where >53% of listed coins are dead (CoinGecko, Dec-2025) and net death rate ran ~1.04%/mo (ElBahrawy). Qiao Wang's critique: Lindy is 'true almost by definition' and useless once you have any information beyond age; Ord himself stresses the robustness increase is EVIDENTIAL, not CAUSAL — 'the change is in the observer, not the object.' There is no way to establish from BTC's single history that k can be arbitrarily small; It is a wrapper, not a valuation: you still must supply R_survival from another (often weak) model, and the demand-feedback channel adds reflexivity/circularity — rising price 'confirms' survival, which is invoked to justify the price; Says nothing native about volatility or correlations; every co-moment must be borrowed from realized data; Reaches the OPPOSITE conclusion to the absorbing-barrier camp (Taleb 2021, #20) from the identical survival record — the framework cannot adjudicate, it only exposes the analyst's prior

WHAT IT IS / MECHANISM. This is the demand-side, rising-weight inverse of the ruin-hazard row (#20). Both share the survival/hazard skeleton E[R]=S(T)*R_survival+(1-S(T))*(-100%), but the sign and feedback differ. #20 applies a FIXED extinction haircut. This approach makes the perceived hazard DECLINE with accumulated survival and lets that feed demand: as BTC ages, fiduciaries Bayesian-update their hazard estimate down, eligible capital widens (pensions/endowments/insurers move off zero into 2-5% allocation models), demand and price rise — an upward feedback. Two formalizations. Taleb (2012, Antifragile, pp.317-319): for 'non-perishables' (no hard lifespan cap) every period survived LENGTHENS expected remaining life — 'aging in reverse,' robustness proportional to life. Ord (2023, arXiv:2308.09045) supplies the rigorous Bayesian derivation and is the load-bearing source: with a uniform prior over an UNKNOWN but CONSTANT hazard k in [0,K], the effective survival curve is S(t)=(1/K)integral e^{-kt}dk=(1-e^{-Kt})/(Kt) -> 1/(Kt) for large Kt, a Pareto tail with exponent alpha=1, and effective hazard lambda(t)≈1/(Kt²) — DECLINING — purely because surviving to t is evidence against high-k worlds. Gott's Copernican variant (log-uniform prior rho∝1/t) gives the NARROW Lindy: median remaining life = current age, with the famous 95% CI T in [40/39·t0, 40·t0].

THE KEY RELATIONSHIP & SCRIPTED FIGURES. BTC age t0≈17.4yr (Jan-2009 genesis). Under Gott-hyperbolic S(t)=t0/t, the probability BTC survives the next H years is t0/(t0+H): H=10 -> 0.64; H=12.5 -> 0.58; H=15 -> 0.54. This is the CRUX and the most important honest finding: the maximal-ignorance Lindy prior is NOT bullish — it assigns ~40-46% ruin over a 10-15yr CMA horizon, vastly higher than Fidelity's 0.71%/yr (#20) or even a 3%/yr constant hazard (S(12.5)=0.69). Practitioners who say 'Lindy => Bitcoin is safe because it's old' are using the DIRECTION of the effect (hazard falls with age) while silently discarding the PRIOR that generates a fat ruin tail. Blended CMA: with R_survival≈11%/yr and S(12.5)≈0.58 (agnostic) you get E[cum]≈0.88, E[ann]≈5.2%; tightening the posterior to S≈0.81 (h_bar≈1.75%/yr, still above Fidelity) gives E[ann]≈8-10%. I center ~8.5% nominal.

CRITIQUES, FAITHFULLY. (1) Survivorship bias is the central failure mode and the approach routinely commits it. CoinGecko (Dec-2025): 53.2% of all listed tokens are dead; ElBahrawy et al. (2017, Royal Society Open Science) measured net coin death ~1.04%/month with a power-law market-share distribution reproduced by a birth-death model. Applying Lindy to Bitcoin-the-survivor conditions on the winner of a >50%-mortality lottery. Qiao Wang ('The Statistical Fallacy behind the Lindy Effect,' Crypto Words 2019): Lindy is 'a trivial statistical heuristic true almost by definition,' useless once you have ANY information beyond age, and 'intimately linked to survivorship bias.' (2) Ord's own caveat demolishes the demand-feedback story's strong form: the robustness increase is EVIDENTIAL not CAUSAL — 'There is an evidential increase in its robustness... but no causal increase. The change is in the observer, not the object.' A radioisotope of unknown half-life shows the same effect while being physically unchanged. Pricing BTC off an information update as if it were a physical safety gain is the error. (3) Prior-dependence: Ord proves Lindy FADES if k is bounded away from zero (k>epsilon) — the tail reverts to exponential. From BTC's single history you cannot establish that its hazard can be arbitrarily close to zero, so the Pareto tail is assumed, not earned. (4) It is a wrapper: R_survival must come from elsewhere, and the demand feedback adds reflexivity (rising price 'confirms' survival, invoked to justify price). (5) Opposite-conclusion problem: Taleb's absorbing-barrier argument (#20) and this Lindy reading start from the IDENTICAL survival record and reach opposite signs; the framework only exposes the prior.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Notably, NONE of the BTC-Lindy practitioner pieces produce a quantitative multi-year CMA. Crypto Research Report (Hays, 2021), Bitcoin Magazine ('Examining The Lindy Effect And Bitcoin'), Thesis.co and Shakepay all argue qualitatively ('survived ~13yr, strong network effects, will thrive long into the future') and supply only adoption datapoints (e.g. two-thirds of institutions with crypto exposure, Coalition Greenwich 2021; standard 2-5% fiduciary allocation models) — but NO survival probability, return forecast, or allocation-to-CMA mapping. The only rigorous numbers are the survival-math anchors above (Gott S, Ord's Pareto tail). This absence is itself a finding: the approach is used as a narrative tailwind, not a disciplined forecast — exactly the gap a credible CMA must close by pairing the rising-survival-weight intuition with the brutal Gott/CoinGecko base rate rather than the cherry-picked direction. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the defensible takeaway is: the left-tail haircut should SHRINK over the horizon as survival accrues (the legitimate contribution vs a fixed haircut), but it remains a real drag (~18-42% ruin mass depending on prior), so this approach LOWERS, not raises, the central forward return relative to survival-blind models — center ~8.5% nominal / ~6% real, vol ~65%, gold corr ~0.05.

### #70 · Square-Root Market-Impact Law (Metaorder Demand-to-Price Mechanism)

*Family: microstructure-impact · Source: Academia · Tier: Reject as engine · Overall 30*


**Explanation:** The square-root law says a buy program of size Q moves price by roughly Y*sigma*sqrt(Q/V): impact is concave, not linear. Donier & Bonart (2015) confirmed the exponent delta ~ 1/2 on over a million Bitcoin metaorders, spanning four decades of order size. The mechanism (Toth et al. 2011; Donier-Bouchaud LLOB) is that real liquidity is latent and thins out near the current price, so each extra dollar of net demand digs deeper into a sparse book. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this is the missing engine under every flow-based model: feed in projected cumulative net institutional inflow Q, and price scales as sqrt(Q). The key implication is automatic appreciation DECAY — once cumulative absorbed demand is large, doubling it lifts price only ~41%, so the headline 100x+ "Bitcoin multiplier" must shrink as the asset matures. This is the first-principles reason naive linear-flow targets (BofA 118x, Apollo 106x) overstate forward returns. It says nothing about volatility or cross-asset correlations directly; those are imported. It also assumes a forecastable demand path Q, which it cannot itself supply.


*Scores — rigor 4, signal 2, robustness 2, data-ops 2, orthogonality 2. Best-pedigreed micro-law in the BTC space (delta~1/2 confirmed on >1M metaorders, real latent-liquidity micro-foundation), and its concave sqrt(Q) shape is the structurally correct way to encode appreciation decay — hence high rigor. But it is not a self-contained CMA: it converts demand Q to price yet cannot forecast Q, so all 10-15yr return uncertainty is exiled into an unmodeled cumulative-inflow guess, and it supplies no level, no gold linkage, and an asset-agnostic tails/correlation story — so empirical signal for a decade horizon is weak. Robustness is low: calibrated at intraday-daily horizons with largely transient/uninformed impact, extrapolating a single-metaorder law to a decade super-metaorder ignores replenishment and regime change. Data_ops is poor in practice because the binding input (projected net institutional inflow path) is the hardest unobservable in the process.*


**Key drivers:** Cumulative net institutional demand Q over the horizon (the metaorder size) — the exogenous input the law converts to price; for a CMA this is the projected 10-15yr net inflow path, which the law itself does NOT forecast; Square-root exponent delta ~ 1/2 (empirically anchored on Bitcoin; Donier-Bonart) — the concavity parameter that forces appreciation decay; Order-unity prefactor Y (~0.5-1) calibrating impact magnitude per unit normalized flow; Volatility sigma — impact scales linearly in sigma, so higher BTC vol amplifies the price move per dollar of flow; Traded volume / liquidity V (the normalization) — deeper float and volume shrink impact; thinning liquid float (HODLing, ETF custody) raises it; Latent-liquidity profile shape near price (locally linear vanishing of supply/demand -> sqrt; the LLOB/Walrasian micro-foundation); Permanent vs transient impact fraction (~2/3 of peak impact tends to persist; the rest decays) — determines how much of demand-driven price gain is durable vs mean-reverting


**Pros:** Strongest empirical pedigree of any BTC valuation primitive: delta ~ 1/2 is confirmed across equities, futures, options AND Bitcoin (Donier-Bonart, >1M metaorders, four decades of size), with error bars below 0.01 in equity studies — a genuine near-universal law, not a curve fit to one BTC price history; Supplies appreciation DECAY from first principles: concavity (sqrt) means the marginal price response to cumulative demand falls automatically, so it is structurally the RIGHT shape for a maturing-asset CMA and a rigorous correction to the naive linear 100x+ 'Bitcoin multiplier'; Has a real micro-foundation (latent-liquidity / Walrasian double-auction theory; Donier-Bouchaud), not just a statistical regularity — it explains WHY impact is concave (liquidity vanishes near the price); Falsifiable and refreshable: Y, sigma, V are estimable from order-book/volume data and the law can be re-tested as the market matures; it also yields a tradeable liquidity/crash-risk measure (Donier-Bouchaud 'Why Do Markets Crash?'); Mechanically distinct from and complementary to higher-level flow/demand-clearing CMAs — it is the engine underneath them, so it disciplines any flow-based price target that would otherwise assume linearity


**Cons:** NOT a self-contained CMA: the law converts demand Q to price but cannot forecast Q. All the long-horizon return uncertainty is exiled into the projected cumulative-inflow path, which is exactly the hard, unmodeled part — the engine is rigorous, the fuel input is a guess; Calibrated and validated at intraday-to-daily metaorder horizons; extrapolating a single-metaorder impact law to a 10-15yr cumulative-demand 'super-metaorder' is a heroic stretch the original authors never endorsed — impact decay, liquidity replenishment and regime change over a decade are not captured by a static sqrt(Q); Impact is largely TRANSIENT: only ~2/3 (and on Bitcoin, per Donier-Bonart, an 'uninformed' component leading to 'almost complete long-term decay') of peak impact persists, so naive use overstates the permanent price gain from a given flow — durable appreciation requires the demand to be 'informed'/persistent, an assumption the law cannot certify; Parameters drift: Y, sigma and especially V (liquid float) are non-stationary; ETF custody and HODLing shrink V (amplifying impact) while deeper institutional books raise it — the net is ambiguous and the law gives no law of motion for V; Silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on all cross-asset correlations (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) — every distributional and portfolio-construction cell must be imported from realized data; it populates at most the appreciation channel; Reflexivity/endogeneity: sigma and V are themselves functions of price and flow, so the 'exogenous Q in, price out' framing is circular over long horizons; the same critique (price drives the inputs) that dogs S2F/NVT applies once you leave the intraday regime

WHAT IT IS. The square-root impact law is the most empirically robust object in all of market microstructure, and it is the mechanical engine that sits UNDER every flow-based BTC CMA — distinct from a higher-level demand-clearing simulator, which decides Q; this law decides how Q maps to price. Execute a metaorder of net size Q and price moves by I(Q) = Y * sigma * (Q/V)^delta, with delta empirically ~1/2 (concave), Y order-unity (~0.5-1), sigma volatility, V volume over the matching window. The concavity is the whole point: impact is sub-linear, so the marginal price response to cumulative demand falls as Q grows.\n\nBITCOIN EVIDENCE. Donier & Bonart (2015, arXiv:1412.4503; Market Microstructure & Liquidity) reconstructed >1,000,000 metaorders on Bitcoin/USD and found delta indistinguishable from 1/2 across four decades of order size — remarkable because Bitcoin in 2011-2014 had almost no arbitrageurs or designated market-makers, so the law cannot be an artifact of HFT. They further decompose order flow into 'informed' and 'uninformed' components, with the uninformed part leading to 'an almost complete long-term decay of impact.' This is the crucial caveat for a CMA: a large fraction of demand-driven price moves is TRANSIENT. Across other markets only ~2/3 of peak impact tends to persist (Bouchaud 2024).\n\nMECHANISM. Toth et al. (2011, Phys. Rev. X, 'Anomalous price impact and the critical nature of liquidity') introduced the latent-liquidity / 'epsilon-intelligence' picture: most liquidity is hidden and vanishes locally linearly around the current price, so a metaorder must consume progressively deeper, sparser book -> sqrt impact. Donier & Bouchaud (2015, 'From Walras' auctioneer to continuous-time double auctions', J. Stat. Mech.) generalized this into a dynamic supply/demand theory, empirically confirming on Bitcoin that supply and demand vanish QUADRATICALLY near the clearing price, which 'makes prices hypersensitive to small fluctuations.' This is the rigorous antithesis of Kyle (1985), whose linear lambda (delta=1) the data decisively reject.\n\nWHY IT BELONGS IN A BTC CMA. Practitioners already use a crude linear version: the 'Bitcoin multiplier.' Bank of America (2021) estimated ~$93M of net inflow moves BTC price ~1% (a 118x market-cap multiplier); Apollo Crypto (2024) computed ~106x from spot-ETF flows (with only ~30% flow/price correlation — itself a red flag). These linear multipliers are exactly what the square-root law CORRECTS: if price ~ sqrt(Q), the multiplier is not constant — it shrinks as cumulative absorbed demand and float grow. So the law is the first-principles reason a credible 10-15yr CMA must extrapolate BTC's appreciation DECAY rather than its level. Plug a compounding net-demand path into sqrt(Q) and even an aggressive demand CAGR is roughly halved into a high-single-digit price-appreciation contribution.\n\nON-RECORD FORECAST PRODUCED THIS WAY. The framework's one genuine ex-ante deliverable is a DOWNSIDE forecast, not an appreciation one: Donier & Bouchaud (2015, PLOS ONE, 'Why Do Markets Crash? Bitcoin Data Offers Unprecedented Insights') used Mt.Gox order-book liquidity (Dec-2011 to Jan-2014) to build three liquidity measures that predict the AMPLITUDE of a crash given a sell-imbalance — an early-warning liquidity-risk gauge. No multi-year BTC price target has ever been published from the pure impact law, which is honest: the authors never claimed it forecasts long-run returns.\n\nFAILURE MODES / SKEPTICISM. (1) The law converts demand to price but cannot forecast demand — all the CMA uncertainty is exiled into the unmodeled cumulative-inflow path Q. (2) It is calibrated at intraday-to-daily metaorder horizons; treating a decade of net demand as one giant 'super-metaorder' under a static sqrt(Q) ignores liquidity replenishment, the transient/decaying component, and regime change — a stretch the authors did not endorse. (3) Permanent impact is only a fraction of peak (Donier-Bonart's 'almost complete decay' for uninformed flow), so durable appreciation needs the demand to be persistent/'informed', which the law cannot certify. (4) Inputs sigma and V are non-stationary and endogenous to price/flow, reintroducing the same reflexivity that dogs S2F/NVT once you leave the intraday regime — ETF custody/HODLing shrink liquid float V (amplifying impact) while deeper institutional books raise it, net ambiguous. (5) The law is asset-agnostic and silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on all cross-asset correlations, so every distributional/portfolio cell (vol, growth/value-eq, FI, TIPS, gold) must be imported from realized data — and it supplies NO digital-gold linkage whatsoever, applying identically to gold and BTC without forcing co-movement (consistent with realized BTC-gold corr ~0). NET: a rigorous engine, an honest decay mechanism, but not a self-contained CMA — best used to discipline (square-root-haircut) any flow-based appreciation estimate and to flag liquidity-driven crash risk.

</details>

### #71 · Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law

*Family: scarcity-supply · Source: Crypto-native · Tier: Reject as engine · Overall 18*


**Explanation:** Stock-to-Flow values Bitcoin purely on monetary scarcity: it regresses log market value on the log stock-to-flow ratio (existing supply divided by annual new issuance), the same hardness metric used for gold and silver. PlanB's original fit (value proportional to SF^3.3, R squared about 0.95) and the cross-asset S2FX version (pooling BTC, gold and silver, treating halvings as discrete phase transitions, R squared about 0.997) both produce dated price targets, e.g. the $288k 2020-2024 cluster. Because issuance halves every four years, SF roughly doubles each halving, so the model mechanically projects roughly 10x (S2F) to 17x (S2FX) per step, implying ~78%/yr between halvings forever. For a 10-15yr CMA this is the model's fatal flaw: it is demand-blind, the regression is spurious (both series are non-stationary and fail cointegration), and it broke out-of-sample after 2021 (predicted ~$98k, BTC closed ~$57k). It also says nothing about volatility or correlations. Honest forward use discards the literal targets, imposes BTC's realized appreciation decay, and yields only a low-double-digit nominal anchor.


*Scores — rigor 1, signal 1, robustness 1, data-ops 5, orthogonality 1. Methodologically near-fatal: regressing non-stationary ln(price) on non-stationary, near-deterministic ln(SF) is a textbook spurious regression where SF is essentially time in disguise, so the high R-squared is artifactual and the coefficients meaningless (cointegration generally fails). It is demand-blind by construction and its own logic implies an absurd ~78%/yr forever, contradicting the dominant decay anchor. It already broke post-2021 and adds zero conditioning on tails/regime/correlation, so it fails regime change. The only strength is data_ops: the halving schedule and 21M cap are deterministic and trivially available, making the input itself zero-forecast-error and operationally effortless.*


**Key drivers:** Stock-to-flow ratio SF = circulating supply / annual new issuance (rises mechanically as block subsidy halves every ~210,000 blocks / ~4 years); Power-law exponent (~3.3 in original S2F) linking ln(SF) to ln(market value); Halving schedule — the deterministic, pre-programmed supply shock that doubles SF and drives ~10x value steps; Cross-asset anchoring: gold (SF~62) and silver (SF~22) market values used to pin the regression line and justify a 'monetary scarcity' premium for BTC as SF approaches/exceeds gold; Phase transitions / clusters (S2FX): treating each halving epoch as a regime with distinct properties, replacing time with SF as the independent variable; Absolute scarcity / 21M hard cap as the terminal narrative (SF → ∞ as issuance → 0)


**Pros:** Fully deterministic supply input: the halving schedule and 21M cap are known in advance, so SF is the rare financial variable with zero forecast error — attractive for a long-horizon CMA skeleton; Parsimonious and falsifiable: a single regressor produces explicit, dated price targets that can be checked (and have been); Captures a real economic intuition — that a credibly fixed, ungrowable supply supports a monetary 'hardness' premium (the same logic that makes gold a store of value); the Austrian/Mises critique even concedes SF can matter for a money's quality; Cross-asset framing (S2FX) at least disciplines the BTC fit against gold and silver rather than fitting BTC in isolation; Morillon & Chacon (2022), the first peer-reviewed treatment, find the in-sample fit is robust to early-assumption choices (not pure data-mining) and that dynamic out-of-sample accuracy improves over time


**Cons:** Spurious regression / non-stationarity: both ln(price) and ln(SF) are non-stationary, trending series, so the high R² is the textbook artifact of regressing one trend on another. Without cointegration the coefficients and R² are statistically meaningless (Burger, Bitcoinwords/WORDS review; has been shown cointegration generally does not hold); SF is a near-deterministic step function of time, so S2F is effectively price-regressed-on-time in disguise — it cannot distinguish scarcity from any other variable that trended up over 2010-2020; Demand-blind by construction: ignores adoption, liquidity, ETF flows, macro/real rates, regulation. Mises critique: scarcity (a subjective demand condition) is conflated with the mechanical SF ratio; price comes from marginal valuations, not a physical supply metric; Out-of-sample failure: PlanB's S2F/S2FX predicted >$100k for 2021-2022; BTC closed Nov-2021 ~$57k and bottomed <$16k in 2022. The model has traded materially below trend since 2021 (off by ~$130k at points). 'Floor model' walk-back further eroded credibility; Diminishing-returns problem: S2F implies a constant ~10x per halving forever (no decay), contradicting the clear empirical decay of BTC's growth rate (142%→65%→17%/yr) — the model is structurally too bullish at long horizons and its targets (e.g. $288k, $500k+, eventually multi-million) are unbounded; Even when the fit 'works', Morillon & Chacon show an S2F-timing strategy underperforms buy-and-hold — no economic value added; Says nothing about volatility or correlations — it is a price-level model only, so it cannot directly populate most CMA cells (vol, corr to equities/FI/TIPS/gold); S2FX 'phase transitions' have only ~4-6 data clusters; fitting a power law through 4 points (plus gold/silver) is gross overfitting and 'has not been replicated or reviewed' per PlanB himself
