<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

METHODOLOGY. Original S2F (PlanB, 2019): monthly data, OLS of ln(market value) on ln(SF). Reported fit ln(MV)=3.3·ln(SF)+14.6 → MV = e^14.6·SF^3.3, R²≈0.95, F-significance 2.3e-17. Because issuance halves ~every 4 years, SF roughly doubles each halving; exponent 3.3 → ~2^3.3 ≈ 10x market value per doubling. Post-2020-halving target ~$55k. S2FX (2020) 'removes time' and pools BTC with gold (SF~62) and silver (SF~22) plus four BTC monthly clusters interpreted as 'phase transitions'; reported R²≈0.997 across six points; next-cluster market value $5.5T → ~$288k/BTC at ~19M supply. PlanB himself flagged S2FX as 'a first step, not yet replicated or reviewed.'

HOW A CMA FALLS OUT. The model is a deterministic price-LEVEL forecaster: feed the known future SF path (2028/2032/2036 halvings) into the power law to get target prices, then back out an implied annualized appreciation. It is silent on volatility and on correlation to every other asset class — those cells cannot be populated from S2F at all and must be borrowed from realized data, which I do for the synthesized column.

THE CORE STATISTICAL INDICTMENT (this is the consensus academic/quant verdict, and I represent it as such, not as one side of a debate). Both ln(price) and ln(SF) are non-stationary I(1)-type trending series. Regressing one trend on another mechanically produces high R² and 'significant' coefficients with heavily autocorrelated residuals — the textbook spurious-regression result (Granger-Newbold). R² is not interpretable for non-stationary series. The defense is cointegration; multiple reviewers (Burger/Amdax via WORDS Bitcoin Journal Parts II & IV; numerous others) find cointegration generally does NOT hold, and that Engle-Granger/Johansen prerequisites are unmet. Crucially, SF is a near-deterministic step-function of TIME, so S2F is essentially 'price regressed on time' — it cannot identify scarcity as the cause versus any other quantity that trended up 2010-2020. PlanB failed to address serial correlation, which guts the predictive-power claim.

ECONOMIC INDICTMENT (Mises, Murphy & Newman 2022). The model conflates 'scarcity' (a subjective demand-side condition — insufficiency relative to wants) with the mechanical stock-to-flow RATIO. Price emerges from marginal buyers'/sellers' subjective valuations, not from a physical supply metric; there is 'no necessary relationship between price paid and physical supply.' They concede SF can bear on a money's QUALITY, but only insofar as actors subjectively value hardness — not as a deterministic price formula. So even the sympathetic Austrian read rejects S2F-as-price-model while granting S2F-as-monetary-narrative.

OUT-OF-SAMPLE FAILURE (decisive). S2F/S2FX 'worst case' ~$98k for Nov-2021; BTC closed ~$57k. 2022 model implied >$100k; BTC bottomed <$16k. Sustained sub-trend trade since 2021 (gap ~$130k at points; CryptoSlate/Protos). PlanB pivoted to a separate 'Floor Model' and walked back his own invalidation criterion — a classic unfalsifiability move. The peer-reviewed Morillon & Chacon (2022) is the most balanced source: in-sample robust and not pure data-mining, dynamic accuracy improves with data, BUT an S2F long/short timing strategy badly underperforms buy-and-hold — i.e., even if the level relationship has SOME signal, it adds no investable value.

DIMINISHING-RETURNS / DECAY (why this matters most for a 10-15yr CMA). S2F bakes in constant ~10x-per-halving growth with NO decay. The realized record flatly contradicts this: from this project's scripted empirical_anchor.json (Coinmetrics BRRNY monthly), nominal annualized appreciation is 142% full-window (2010-2026), 65% trailing-10y, 17% trailing-5y; vol 103%→69%→57%. The growth rate is clearly decaying as the asset matures and as base effects bite. A naive S2F CMA would extrapolate the level (huge) rather than the decaying rate (modest) — the single biggest reason not to use S2F output as a forward CMA. My synthesized nominal 12-18% extrapolates the DECAY curve and additionally removes the 'catch-up to gold's SF' tailwind (BTC's SF will exceed gold's within ~2 halvings, so the scarcity-premium re-rating that drove past returns largely exhausts).

CORRELATION NOTE. The S2FX thesis structurally predicts BTC should be valued on the same scarcity line as gold, implying high gold co-movement. Realized gold correlation is ~0 (-0.01 full / +0.03 10y / +0.045 5y). Meanwhile the correlation S2F denies should exist — to growth equities — is the one that has RISEN most (0.26→0.36→0.56), because real-world BTC trades as a liquidity-sensitive risk asset, not a demand-independent scarcity token. This is direct empirical evidence against the model's premise, and I weight the realized data over the model's implication in the synthesized correlations.

BOTTOM LINE. Treat S2F/S2FX as a NARRATIVE about monetary hardness, not as a CMA engine. Its only genuinely useful input — the deterministic, zero-error future SF path — is real, but the mapping from SF to price is spurious, demand-blind, decay-blind, and has failed out of sample. Use it (if at all) to justify a structural debasement-hedge premium in the qualitative thesis, never to set the appreciation number; borrow vol and all correlations from realized data.

### #72 · Logarithmic-Regression "Rainbow" Fair-Value Corridor

*Family: log-regression-corridor · Source: Crypto-native · Tier: Reject as engine · Overall 16*


**Explanation:** The Rainbow chart fits log(BTC price) to a logarithmic function of time — log10(price)=a·ln(time)−b — so the fair-value line bends DOWN even on a log scale, baking in diminishing returns as the network matures. Nine color bands, spaced ~0.5×–5× around that line, label sentiment zones (deep-blue "fire sale" to dark-red "bubble"); they are read as over/under-valuation, not price targets. For a CMA you extrapolate the central line: because instantaneous appreciation ≈ ln(10)·a/t, the model itself forecasts decay — roughly mid-30s %/yr at BTC's current ~17yr age sliding toward low-20s %/yr by ~2040. The corridor width substitutes for a volatility/dispersion view. Key inputs are just the fitted coefficients a, b and the fit window — there is no demand, supply, macro or cashflow input. The honest read: the authors call it a "meme chart… not investment advice," it has been recalibrated downward after breaking its own lower band (2022), and any 10-15yr number is a curve-extrapolation, not a forecast. It implies a decaying-but-still-high-double-digit nominal CAGR; volatility and all correlations must be imported from realized data.


*Scores — rigor 1, signal 2, robustness 1, data-ops 5, orthogonality 1. Zero economic anchor — fits log-price to ln(calendar time), a spurious co-trend with no value driver, and is silently re-parameterized whenever price escapes the band (V2/V3), making it descriptive and unfalsifiable rather than predictive (rigor 1, robustness 1). Its one virtue is the qualitatively-correct decay shape (ln(time) flattens trend even on log scale), which weakly echoes the realized 142->65->17%/yr decay anchor, but it adds no tail/regime/correlation conditioning and is silent on vol and gold-corr (signal 2). Trivial to run: two OLS coefficients on free public price data (data_ops 5).*


**Key drivers:** Time since genesis (ln of days/weeks since 2009) — the sole regressor; Fitted log-regression coefficients a (slope on ln time) and b (intercept), e.g. V1 a=2.9065 / b=19.493; Coin Bureau V2-style a=2.6521 / b=18.163 (weeks); R²≈0.95; 1/t appreciation decay AND log-scale flattening built into the ln(time) functional form (steeper deceleration than power-law-in-time); Band multipliers (~0.5× to ~5× the central line), evenly log-spaced, defining the corridor / dispersion; Fit-window and time-origin choices, plus periodic DOWNWARD recalibration (V2 after the Nov-2022 FTX break) — the retrofitting lever; Implicit adoption-S-curve narrative (diminishing returns as market cap expands) used to justify the flattening, but with no demand/macro variable


**Pros:** Encodes appreciation DECAY more aggressively than naive extrapolations: the ln(time) form flattens the trend even on a log scale, the qualitatively correct shape for a maturing, no-cashflow asset's forward CMA; Provides an explicit fair-value CORRIDOR rather than a point, which maps cleanly onto a CMA central case plus a dispersion/band view; Parameter-light, transparent and falsifiable: two coefficients fit by OLS on public price data, R²≈0.95 in-sample; deviations from the band are observable in real time; The single most widely cited, most accessible crypto-native fair-value band (Blockchaincenter, Bitcoin Magazine Pro, Coin Bureau, CoinGecko, Bitbo), so it shapes retail/practitioner expectations and is worth critiquing on its own terms; Authors are unusually honest about limits — explicit 'meme chart / not investment advice / no scientific basis / cannot predict price with a rainbow' disclaimers, which is more candor than S2F or Metcalfe marketing


**Cons:** No economic anchor whatsoever: calendar time is not a value driver. It fits a curve purely to past price — no supply, demand, adoption, macro, ETF-flow or cashflow input — so it is the most fundamentals-free model in the set (its own creators say it has 'no scientific basis'); Retrofitting / recalibration is the fatal critique: when BTC broke the lower band in the Nov-2022 FTX crash, the curve was RE-FITTED downward (V2, again in 2023). A 'fair value' line that is silently re-parameterized whenever price escapes it is descriptive, not predictive — it can never be falsified because it is moved to fit; Spurious-trend problem: log-price and ln(time) are both monotone trends; any rising series looks tight on a log-log/semi-log axis. The R²≈0.95 is an axis artifact (massive error compression), not evidence of a law — the same critique that sinks naive S2F/Metcalfe; Survivorship / single-path: fit to the one realized BTC history; it cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass, so it overstates expected return by ignoring the left tail; Lagging and band-breaking in BOTH directions: responds only to closing prices, overshoots tops/bottoms by 20-50%, and price has wicked outside both bands — so it is neither floor nor ceiling, just a loose attractor; Says nothing about volatility-as-a-statistic or any cross-asset correlation; the corridor width is a price-dispersion band, not an annualized return vol, and every correlation cell must be imported from realized data; Crypto marketing weaponizes it ('$1M by ~2037' style claims) in ways the careful authors disclaim; provenance of any forward number must be separated from the meme

<details><summary>Full notes</summary>

PROVENANCE & FORM. The Rainbow chart is a layering of two 2014 bear-market artifacts: BitcoinTalk user Trolololo's logarithmic-regression curve (22 Oct 2014) and Reddit user azop's humorous straight-line "rainbow" sentiment overlay. Rohmeo at Blockchaincenter merged them into the modern curved chart in 2019 and shipped the recalibrated V2 on 21 Nov 2022 after BTC fell below the V1 lower boundary in the FTX collapse. The load-bearing functional form is a regression of log(price) on ln(time): Blockchaincenter's V1 is quoted as y=2.9065·ln(x)−19.493; Coin Bureau quotes a V2-style log10(price)=2.6521·ln(weeks since 2009)−18.163 with R²≈0.95. This is the crucial distinction from #5 (Santostasi/Burger power-law-in-time), where log-price is LINEAR in log-time (a fixed exponent n≈5.6). Here log-price is CONCAVE in log-time — the ln(time) regressor bends the trend down even on the log axis, so the implied appreciation decays faster and the "fair value" flattens harder at long horizons. Nine bands, evenly log-spaced (~0.5× to ~5× the central line, each ~2× wide), supply the dispersion view. Several aggregators (Bitcoin Magazine Pro, Bitbo) actually publish a power-law variant log10(price)=a·log10(days)+b rather than the ln(time) form — the ecosystem is not internally consistent about whether it is log-regression-on-time or power-law-on-time, which itself is a tell that the curve is chosen for visual fit, not theory.

DECAY MATH FOR THE CMA. Under log10 P = a·ln(t) − b, d(ln P)/dt = ln(10)·a/t. With a≈2.6521 and t in weeks, at BTC's age ~905 weeks (~17.4yr) this is ~0.0067/week ≈ ~35%/yr; pushing t forward 15 years (~+780 weeks) drops it to ~22%/yr. So the central line forecasts a decaying nominal CAGR roughly in the low-20s%-to-mid-30s% band over a 2026-2041 window — the model self-generates decay, which is its one genuine virtue for a forward CMA. I anchor SYNTHESIZED nominal BELOW that (~16-22%) for retrofitting bias and tail risk.

RETROFITTING — THE CENTRAL CRITIQUE. The honest objection is not that the curve fits poorly but that it is MOVED whenever it fails. BTC broke the lower band in 2022; rather than falsify the framework, the slope/intercept were re-fit downward (V2 in Nov-2022, a further "maturing market / lower volatility" tweak in 2023). Coin Bureau notes the post-2021 trendline shifted ~15% and lower bands were extended to capture deeper drawdowns, "introducing subjectivity." A fair-value line that is silently re-parameterized each time price escapes it is descriptive, not predictive, and structurally un-falsifiable. Layer on the generic semi-log critique: log-price vs ln(time) are both monotone trends, and the log axis compresses error so massively that almost any rising series looks "tight" — the R²≈0.95 is an axis artifact, the same spurious-trend trap that sinks naive S2F and Metcalfe. The model also ignores demand, adoption, ETF flows, macro, and regulation entirely; its creators concede it has "no scientific basis" and call it a "meme chart." It is lagging (closing-price only, 20-50% overshoot at extremes), single-path (no left-tail mass), and breaks its own bands in both directions.

ON-RECORD FORWARD FIGURES. The careful authors publish NO dated multi-year price target — by design. The only concrete numbers are spot band snapshots (LBank, April-2026): Fire Sale ~$56k, BUY ~$75k, Accumulate ~$97k, Still Cheap ~$126k, with bands extended one halving cycle forward as "expected band ranges, not price predictions." Crypto marketing has nonetheless weaponized the corridor into "$1M floor by ~2037"-style claims (the same hype attached to the power-law corridor), which the Rainbow authors explicitly disclaim. The contrast with S2F is instructive and the LBank "broken models" piece makes it: S2F made hard dated predictions ($100k by 2021-23, $288k by 2024, ~$500k by 2025-26) that failed catastrophically against a ~$126k Oct-2025 peak; the Rainbow chart "survives" precisely BECAUSE it refuses to predict and recalibrates — durability via un-falsifiability, not accuracy. For a 10-15yr institutional CMA this is the worst of both worlds: it offers a decaying-trend shape that is qualitatively right but a level that is an extrapolated, periodically-massaged curve with no economic anchor, no native volatility, and no cross-asset correlation. I treat it as a sanity-check on the DECAY shape of appreciation, not as a source for the level, and import all vol/correlation cells from realized data.

</details>

## Cross-approach synthesis

### House view (analyst)
House view (10-15yr BTC CMA central): nominal appreciation ~8-12%/yr, real ~5-9%/yr; annualized volatility ~50-60% with the floor pinned at the realized trailing-5y ~57% (NOT below it); BTC-gold correlation ~0.0-0.15 (realized is ~0: -0.01 full, +0.03 10y, +0.045 5y); BTC-growth-equity correlation ~0.40-0.55 and RISING as ETF/institutional ownership deepens. The load-bearing point: this central estimate is driven by the empirical appreciation-DECAY anchor (annualized appreciation collapsing roughly 142% -> 65% -> 17%/yr across successive windows), not by any single valuation model. S2F/S2FX, power-law, Metcalfe, cost-of-production, M2-elasticity, TAM-substitution, DCF/moneyness, adoption-S-curve and the LTCMA frames all disagree on level and mechanism and several are statistically discredited out-of-sample; what they reliably supply is NARRATIVE (why scarcity, network, debasement or adoption might sustain a positive but fading drift), while the DATA supplies the numbers and the correlation profile. And the data's verdict is unambiguous: BTC behaves as a high-beta growth/risk asset, NOT as digital gold. Every gold-parity / TAM-substitution row carries the same internal contradiction — those theses need BTC and gold to co-move for BTC to inherit gold's monetary share, yet realized gold co-movement is ~0 — so the digital-gold correlation cell cannot be used to justify both the appreciation TAM and a diversification benefit. We therefore center forward returns on the decay anchor (mid-single to low-double-digit nominal, fading toward the high end of the equity-risk-premium range as the asset matures), keep vol at a ~50-60% band floored by realized ~57% rather than crediting unproven ETF-era compression, treat gold correlation as ~0 (modeling 0.0-0.15 only as an upper guardrail), and treat the rising growth-equity beta as the operative correlation for any portfolio math.


### Breadth assessment (completeness critic)
The field is now extraordinarily comprehensive - effectively exhaustive of the legitimate, decision-relevant mechanism space for a 10-15yr Bitcoin CMA. Across the ~73 listed approaches every major valuation 'engine' is represented: supply-scarcity (S2F, structural stock-flow, inelastic-markets), network-value (Metcalfe/NVT/Burniske/generalized-Metcalfe-logistic), cost/energy (production floor, thermoeconomic, security-budget), monetary/macro (M2 elasticity, QTM, Cagan/Jermann, FTPL, Triffin/dedollarization, eurodollar, hyperbitcoinization, debasement-CAGR), store-of-value TAM and cross-asset relative value, the full stochastic-process and tail toolkit (regime-switch/jump, rough vol, fractal/Hurst/ARFIMA, EVT/GPD, LPPLS, survival/ruin), the complete derivatives/risk-premium layer (RND/vol-surface, VRP/SVCJ, skew, perp-funding/carry, convenience-yield), equilibrium asset-pricing (consumption-CAPM/rare-disaster/ICAPM, rational-bubble OLG, game-theoretic security, Black-Litterman/implied-equilibrium inversion), the behavioral/narrative cluster, the modern demand-microstructure channels (ETF cointegration, discrete-access step-function, treasury-company flywheel, stablecoin float, square-root impact, on-chain flow), the ML/empirical-asset-pricing and nowcasting block, and the portfolio-construction/CMA-assembly machinery (LTCMA, LDI, entropy-pooling, CVaR, DCC-copula). Crucially, the framing already enforces the right discipline - extrapolating BTC's appreciation DECAY (142->65->17%/yr) rather than its level, and treating the academically-rejected hype models (naive S2F/Metcalfe/gold-parity, power-law) as cautionary rather than load-bearing. The five gaps I name are genuine DISTINCT mechanisms but second-order: a quantum/protocol-obsolescence existential hazard that uniquely loads the 2028-2040 left tail (the single most defensible addition); a Budish cost-to-attack security FLOOR (vs the field's security-as-cost/sustainability framings); a lost-coin EFFECTIVE-supply-attrition deflationary multiplier (the field models issuance but never supply decay); a realized-CPI Fisher-hedge test that specifically disciplines the TIPS/real-return cells; and an ESG-exclusion demand-suppression channel. None of these would materially move the honest cross-approach central estimate (~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15) - the quantum and Budish-floor items mainly widen and lower the tail, the lost-coin item is a modest upside tailwind, and the Fisher/ESG items reinforce the 'weak inflation hedge, regime-contingent institutional bid' read already embedded. Recommendation: add the quantum-obsolescence hazard and the Budish security-floor as full approaches (they carry distinct, citable academic/practitioner literature and change the tail), fold lost-coin attrition into the supply/inelastic-markets family as a sensitivity, and treat the Fisher-hedge and ESG items as refinements of the debasement and policy-cap approaches rather than standalone additions. With those, the field can be declared closed for a credible decade-plus BTC CMA."


### Known remaining families (identified, not yet deep-dived)

- **Quantum-Computing / Cryptographic-Obsolescence Existential-Hazard Discount** — DISTINCT mechanism, not a restatement of the field's abstract 'Survival/Ruin-Probability (Absorbing-Zero Hazard).' The generic ruin model treats failure as a featureless Poisson absorbing-zero event; the quantum/protocol-obsolescence channel is a SPECIFIC, partially-datable technological-displacement risk that loads on EXACTLY the 10-15yr CMA window. A cryptographically-relevant quantum computer (CRQC) is variously dated ~2028-2033 (the 'Quantum Doomsday Clock' ~Mar-2028; Bernstein 'real but manageable'), with ~6.9M BTC of exposed/reused public keys at risk (CoinDesk, Apr-2026; HRF) and Bitcoin lacking a coordinated post-quantum migration roadmap unlike Ethereum. For a decade-plus CMA this is the dominant left-tail term and a structural haircut to the discount rate: P(successful migration before CRQC) x conditional value + P(failure) x ~0. It also subsumes broader protocol-displacement risk (a technically-superior successor money) that NO current approach prices. Primary anchors: CoinDesk quantum-threat coverage (2026); Bernstein note (Apr-2026); Aggarwal et al. 'Quantum attacks on Bitcoin' (Ledger/PMC). Net CMA effect: lowers expected appreciation a few %/yr and fattens the absorbing-zero tail specifically in the 2028-2040 horizon.
- **Cost-to-Attack / 'Economic Limits' Security-Floor Lower Bound (Budish)** — DISTINCT from both 'Equilibrium/Game-Theoretic Security-Utility Pricing' (endogenous price-security fixed point) and 'Mining-Economics Security-Budget Sustainability' (whether the fee budget SUSTAINS security). This inverts the logic into a VALUATION FLOOR / no-double-spend incentive-compatibility bound: the network is only safe if the value extractable from a 51%/double-spend attack stays below the flow + stock cost of acquiring majority hashpower (~$10B hardware + energy in 2026 at ~950-990 EH/s). Eric Budish, 'The Economic Limits of Bitcoin and the Blockchain' (BFI/NBER) formalizes this as a hard collateral constraint linking transaction value, mining reward flow, and attack cost - implying a CEILING on safely-settleable value per block and a security-driven FLOOR on market cap. Distinct mechanism (security economics as a lower bound), distinct CMA implication (caps the credible 'settlement-network' utility term and ties long-run value to a declining post-subsidy fee budget). Not currently represented as a floor anywhere in the field.
- **Lost-Coin / Effective-Supply Attrition (Stochastic Deflationary Scarcity)** — DISTINCT supply-side mechanism the field omits: every existing supply approach (S2F, 'Structural Stock-Flow Demand-Clearing,' 'ETF-AUM Inelastic-Markets Multiplier') models ISSUANCE only - none model supply DECAY. Coins are permanently lost/dormant at ~3.3%/yr (CoinLedger/Crowdfund Insider 2025; est. 2.3-3.7M BTC, ~11-18% of cap already gone), and 'ancient'-coin dormancy (~566 BTC/day) now exceeds miner issuance (~450 BTC/day) - so EFFECTIVE float shrinks, making BTC net-deflationary post-2028. This is a separate price multiplier acting on the inelastic-supply curve: a shrinking liquid float amplifies any demand shock beyond what the issuance-only models assume. CMA relevance: a modest structural tailwind to appreciation and a higher demand-to-price elasticity, but with deep measurement uncertainty (lost is unobservable, and re-animation of 'lost' coins is a tail risk). Worth one approach because it changes the denominator the whole field divides market cap by.
- **Realized-Inflation / Fisher-Hedge Passthrough (CPI-Conditioned, Regime-Contingent)** — Partially overlaps the 'Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge' family but tests a DIFFERENT object: not money-SUPPLY growth, but whether BTC actually compensates REALIZED CPI inflation (the Fisher relation), which is the mechanism that should drive the BTC-TIPS correlation cell and the real-return CMA. The empirical literature is specifically informative and largely NEGATIVE: the Fisher/hedge property holds short-run but FAILS long-run, is CPI-specific (not PCE), concentrated in high-inflation/bull regimes, and present mainly PRE-institutionalization (Choi & Shin / MPRA 120477; ScienceDirect 2024). For a 10-15yr CMA this directly disciplines the TIPS and real-appreciation cells: BTC is at best a weak, regime-contingent inflation hedge, not a reliable one - a finding none of the supply/M2 approaches deliver because they test trend money, not realized inflation passthrough.
- **ESG / Carbon-Footprint Institutional-Exclusion Demand-Suppression Channel** — A distinct DEMAND-SIDE suppressor not captured by 'Official-Sector Policy-Endogenous Return Caps' (which is ban/repression/regulatory-capital) or 'Mining-Economics' (which is the supply/security side). Mechanism: ESG mandates, net-zero commitments, and carbon-disclosure rules structurally EXCLUDE proof-of-work BTC from a large pool of institutional capital regardless of return, shrinking the realizable TAM that every adoption/SoV approach assumes is fully addressable. Bitcoin energy use ~near all-time-high (Digiconomist; S&P Global Dec-2024; Cambridge CCAF), and the carbon-footprint trajectory (arXiv 2011.02612) keeps the issue live. CMA relevance: a haircut on the institutional-adoption term and a source of regime risk if carbon regulation tightens; weakest of the five and arguably a sub-case of policy caps, included only to round out the demand-suppression side the field under-weights.
